description: Treats symptoms of Parkinson's disease and restless legs syndrome by stimulating dopamine receptors in the brain.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and titrated by the prescriber based on response and tolerability; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term use for Parkinson's disease; may be used intermittently or long-term for restless legs syndrome as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce nausea.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
Do not stop abruptly without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden, uncontrollable sleep episodes (sleep attacks), even during activities like driving
New or worsening compulsive behaviors: gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping or eating
Fainting or severe low blood pressure
Hallucinations or severe confusion
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol and other sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine) - additive drowsiness and sleep-attack risk.
Ciprofloxacin can increase ropinirole levels - use caution.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting or severe confusion.
Call prescriber immediately for new compulsive behaviors or sudden sleep episodes; avoid driving until this risk is assessed.
self_monitoring: Monitor for excessive daytime sleepiness before driving.
Watch for new impulsive or compulsive behaviors and report them.
Track symptom control with prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up. Do not stop this medication abruptly without contacting the prescriber.

description: Treats symptoms of Parkinson's disease and restless legs syndrome by stimulating dopamine receptors in the brain.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and titrated by the prescriber based on response and tolerability; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term use for Parkinson's disease; may be used intermittently or long-term for restless legs syndrome as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food, consistently.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
Do not stop abruptly without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden, uncontrollable sleep episodes (sleep attacks), even during activities like driving
New or worsening compulsive behaviors: gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping or eating
Fainting or severe low blood pressure
Hallucinations or severe confusion
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol and other sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine) - additive drowsiness and sleep-attack risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting or severe confusion.
Call prescriber immediately for new compulsive behaviors or sudden sleep episodes; avoid driving until this risk is assessed.
self_monitoring: Monitor for excessive daytime sleepiness before driving.
Watch for new impulsive or compulsive behaviors and report them.
Track symptom control with prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up. Do not stop this medication abruptly without contacting the prescriber.

drug_class: Dopamine precursor/decarboxylase inhibitor combination (Parkinson's disease treatment)
description: The most effective treatment for the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease; levodopa is converted to dopamine in the brain, while carbidopa reduces side effects and increases the amount reaching the brain.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and titrated by the prescriber based on response and tolerability; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for Parkinson's disease.
directions_for_use: Take consistently, generally on an empty stomach unless nausea occurs, in which case take with a small non-protein snack.
High-protein meals can reduce absorption - space from protein-rich meals if directed.
Do not stop abruptly without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Use within 14 days of a nonselective MAOI
Suspicious, undiagnosed skin lesions (use with caution)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden sleep episodes or severe drowsiness
New or worsening compulsive behaviors: gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping
Hallucinations, confusion, or severe agitation
High fever, muscle rigidity, or confusion, especially after a missed dose or abrupt stop
Fainting or irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: High-protein meals and iron supplements can reduce absorption - separate timing as directed.
Avoid nonselective MAOIs; use caution with other dopaminergic OTC or herbal supplements.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for high fever/muscle rigidity/confusion, or for fainting/irregular heartbeat.
Call prescriber for new compulsive behaviors, hallucinations, or worsening involuntary movements.
self_monitoring: Track motor symptom control (tremor, stiffness, mobility) and timing of doses relative to symptoms.
Watch for new impulsive or compulsive behaviors.
Avoid abrupt discontinuation.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up. Do not skip doses or stop abruptly, since doing so can cause a serious withdrawal-like reaction; contact the prescriber if several doses are missed.

description: Provides local pain relief for postherpetic neuralgia (nerve pain after shingles) and other localized nerve or musculoskeletal pain by numbing the skin area.
typical_dosage: Apply up to 3 patches to the painful area once daily for up to 12 hours within a 24-hour period, then remove for 12 hours.
typical_duration: Used as needed/directed; reassess ongoing need periodically with prescriber.
directions_for_use: Apply to intact, dry skin over the painful area only.
Do not apply to broken, irritated, or inflamed skin.
Do not use heating pads over the patch.
Fold used patches in half, sticky sides together, and dispose of safely, away from children and pets.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from heat. Keep used and unused patches out of reach of children and pets - a used patch still contains enough lidocaine to be harmful if chewed or swallowed.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to lidocaine or amide-type anesthetics
Use over broken skin or open wounds
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of an allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Irregular heartbeat, dizziness, confusion, or ringing in ears (signs of systemic absorption/toxicity, especially with more than the recommended number of patches)
Numbness spreading beyond the application site
common_side_effects: Mild skin redness or irritation at application site
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not use with other topical products containing lidocaine, benzocaine, or other local anesthetics (e.g., some OTC sunburn or hemorrhoid creams) - risk of excess absorption and toxicity.
Avoid applying heat sources (heating pads) over the patch, which increases drug absorption.
action_if_adverse_effects: Remove the patch and seek emergency care for irregular heartbeat, confusion, ringing in ears, or an allergic reaction.
Call prescriber/pharmacist for persistent skin irritation.
self_monitoring: Check skin under the patch periodically for irritation.
Track the number of patches used per day to avoid exceeding the maximum.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally used on an as-needed or scheduled 12-hours-on/12-hours-off basis; if an application is missed, apply as soon as remembered and resume the regular schedule.

description: Numbs the skin before minor procedures such as needle sticks, IV placement, or minor skin procedures.
typical_dosage: Apply a thick layer to intact skin and cover with an occlusive dressing for at least 1 hour before a procedure, up to a maximum area/time directed by the prescriber.
typical_duration: Used as a single application before a procedure, as directed.
directions_for_use: Apply only to intact skin as directed, and cover with the provided occlusive dressing.
Do not apply to mucous membranes, eyes, or broken/irritated skin unless directed.
Wipe off the cream before the procedure begins, as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to lidocaine, prilocaine, or amide-type anesthetics
Infants under 12 months who are receiving methemoglobin-inducing agents
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of methemoglobinemia: bluish skin/lips, shortness of breath, fatigue, headache - seek emergency care
Signs of an allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Irregular heartbeat, dizziness, or confusion (systemic toxicity if used on large areas or for too long)
common_side_effects: Mild skin paleness, redness, or swelling at the application site
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not combine with other topical anesthetics (e.g., benzocaine-containing products) - increases risk of excess absorption and methemoglobinemia.
Use with caution alongside other medications that can cause methemoglobinemia (e.g., certain OTC benzocaine products).
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for bluish skin, difficulty breathing, or signs of allergic reaction.
Remove cream and notify provider if irritation is severe.
self_monitoring: Watch for unusual skin changes at the application site.
Follow the exact application time directed - longer than recommended application increases absorption risk.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as a single application before a scheduled procedure, not on a recurring schedule, so there is no missed dose to account for.

drug_class: Topical analgesic (TRPV1 agonist, derived from chili peppers)
description: Provides temporary relief of minor aches and pains of muscles and joints, and nerve pain such as after shingles, by depleting a pain-signaling chemical in nerve endings.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to the affected area up to 3-4 times daily as needed.
typical_duration: May be used regularly for ongoing pain; consistent daily use for 1-2 weeks is often needed for full effect.
directions_for_use: Wash hands thoroughly immediately after applying, or wear gloves, to avoid transferring to eyes/mucous membranes.
Do not apply to broken or irritated skin.
Do not bandage tightly or apply heat over the area.
A burning sensation is common initially and usually decreases with continued regular use.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to capsaicin or chili peppers
Use on broken, irritated skin, or near eyes/mucous membranes
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe burning, blistering, or skin ulceration
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Accidental eye contact causing severe pain or vision changes - flush eyes with water and seek care
common_side_effects: Burning, stinging, or redness at application site (usually decreases with continued use)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid using with other topical OTC products (e.g., menthol or methyl salicylate rubs) on the same area - can increase skin irritation.
Do not use heating pads over treated skin.
action_if_adverse_effects: Wash off with soap and water and seek care for severe reactions.
Flush eyes with water and seek care immediately if capsaicin contacts eyes.
self_monitoring: Watch the application site for excessive burning or skin breakdown.
Wash hands well after each application.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as needed for pain; there is no fixed schedule to miss.

description: Provides temporary relief of minor muscle and joint aches through a combination of numbing (lidocaine) and cooling/counterirritant (menthol) effects.
typical_dosage: Apply to the affected area up to 3-4 times daily as needed, per product labeling.
typical_duration: Short-term use for minor aches; see a doctor if pain persists beyond 7 days or worsens.
directions_for_use: Apply only to intact skin.
Wash hands after applying (unless the hands are the treated area).
Do not use with a heating pad or tight bandage over the area.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to lidocaine, menthol, or other product ingredients
Use on broken, irritated, or infected skin
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Severe skin burns or blistering
Signs of systemic toxicity with excessive or prolonged use over large areas: irregular heartbeat, confusion, dizziness
common_side_effects: Mild burning, tingling, or cooling sensation
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not use with other topical products containing lidocaine, menthol, or methyl salicylate on the same area - additive irritation/absorption risk.
Avoid combining with heating pads, which increase absorption and burn risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Remove the product and wash the area; seek care for signs of allergic reaction or systemic toxicity.
Stop use and see a doctor if pain persists beyond 7 days.
self_monitoring: Check the application site regularly for irritation or burns.
Limit use to the labeled area and frequency.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as needed for pain; there is no fixed schedule to miss.

drug_class: Nicotinic receptor partial agonist (smoking cessation aid)
description: Helps people quit smoking by reducing cravings and withdrawal symptoms and blunting the pleasurable effects of nicotine if smoking resumes.
typical_dosage: Started at a low dose and titrated up over the first week (commonly to 1 mg twice daily) per the prescriber's instructions, usually beginning about 1 week before the quit date.
typical_duration: Typically used for 12 weeks, sometimes extended for another 12 weeks if successful, as directed.
directions_for_use: Take after eating with a full glass of water to reduce nausea.
Set a quit date, usually about a week after starting.
Continue taking as directed even after quitting smoking.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Changes in mood or behavior: agitation, depressed mood, suicidal thoughts
New or worsening seizures
Signs of allergic reaction/angioedema: swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing, or severe skin reactions
New or worsening cardiovascular symptoms: chest pain, irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Nicotine replacement products (patch, gum, lozenge) used together may increase side effects like nausea and headache - do not combine unless directed by prescriber.
Alcohol may increase certain neuropsychiatric effects; use caution.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, severe allergic reaction, or seizure.
Call prescriber immediately for mood changes, agitation, or suicidal thoughts; stop the medication and seek guidance.
self_monitoring: Track mood and behavior changes, ideally with input from family or friends.
Track smoking urges and progress toward the quit date.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: Reduces nicotine withdrawal symptoms and cravings to help people quit smoking by delivering a steady, controlled dose of nicotine through the skin.
typical_dosage: Apply one patch daily, starting at a strength based on smoking history, then step down to lower strengths over about 8-10 weeks per product instructions.
typical_duration: Typically used for about 8-10 weeks in a step-down program.
directions_for_use: Apply to a clean, dry, hairless area of skin each morning; rotate application sites.
Remove old patch before applying a new one; do not wear more than one patch at a time unless directed.
Some formulations are removed at bedtime - follow product-specific instructions.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature. Keep used and unused patches away from children and pets - even used patches contain residual nicotine that can be harmful or fatal if ingested.
contraindications: Continuing to smoke, chew tobacco, or use other nicotine products while wearing the patch (risk of nicotine overdose)
Recent heart attack or serious/worsening heart disease (use with caution/medical supervision)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of nicotine toxicity: severe nausea/vomiting, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, weakness - especially if smoking continues while using the patch
Signs of allergic reaction: severe rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Chest pain or irregular heartbeat
common_side_effects: Skin redness or itching at application site
Vivid dreams or trouble sleeping (if worn overnight)
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not use with other nicotine-containing products (gum, lozenge, cigarettes, e-cigarettes) at the same time unless directed by a prescriber - risk of nicotine overdose.
Stopping smoking itself can change the levels of some other medications (e.g., certain antidepressants, insulin) - discuss any change in smoking status with a pharmacist or prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Remove the patch and seek care for signs of nicotine toxicity, chest pain, or allergic reaction.
Continue to avoid all tobacco/nicotine products while using the patch.
self_monitoring: Track skin reactions at rotating application sites.
Monitor cravings and withdrawal symptoms.
Confirm complete smoking cessation while using the patch.
missed_dose_instructions: If a patch application is missed for the day, apply a new one as soon as remembered and continue the regular daily schedule; do not apply two patches to make up for a missed one.

description: Reduces nicotine withdrawal symptoms and cravings to help people quit smoking by delivering nicotine through the lining of the mouth.
typical_dosage: One piece of gum or one lozenge every 1-2 hours as needed for cravings, not exceeding the labeled maximum per day, tapering down over about 12 weeks.
typical_duration: Typically used for up to 12 weeks as part of a quit program.
directions_for_use: For gum: chew slowly until a tingling sensation appears, then 'park' between the cheek and gum; repeat this chew-and-park cycle for about 30 minutes.
For lozenge: allow to dissolve slowly in the mouth; do not chew or swallow whole.
Avoid eating or drinking (especially acidic beverages like coffee, soda, or juice) for 15 minutes before and during use, as this reduces nicotine absorption.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from children and pets - can be harmful if ingested by children.
contraindications: Continued smoking or use of other nicotine products while using (risk of nicotine overdose)
Recent heart attack or serious/worsening heart disease (use with caution/medical supervision)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of nicotine toxicity: severe nausea/vomiting, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, weakness
Signs of allergic reaction: severe rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Mouth or throat irritation that is severe or persistent
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid acidic beverages (coffee, juice, soda) right before or during use - reduces nicotine absorption.
Do not use with other nicotine-containing products (patch, cigarettes, e-cigarettes) at the same time unless directed - risk of nicotine overdose.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of nicotine toxicity or allergic reaction.
See a dentist/doctor if jaw pain or mouth irritation is severe or persistent.
self_monitoring: Track the number of pieces used per day to stay within the labeled maximum.
Monitor cravings and taper use as directed over the program.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as needed for cravings; there is no fixed schedule to miss.

description: Prevents pregnancy by suppressing ovulation and altering cervical mucus and the uterine lining; may also be used to regulate menstrual cycles.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth at the same time every day, following the pack schedule without interruption.
typical_duration: Used continuously as long as contraception (or cycle regulation) is desired.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day to maintain effectiveness.
Start the next pack immediately after finishing the previous one, following the specific pack instructions.
Use a backup method (e.g., condoms) for the first 7 days if starting mid-cycle or if instructed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: History of blood clots (DVT/PE), stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected breast cancer or estrogen-dependent tumors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg pain/swelling, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, coughing up blood
Signs of stroke: severe headache, vision changes, weakness/numbness on one side, slurred speech
Severe abdominal pain (possible liver problem or blood clot)
Yellowing of skin/eyes (liver problem)
Severe leg pain or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception if combined.
Certain Rx antibiotics (e.g., rifampin) and some anticonvulsants can reduce effectiveness; confirm any new prescription with a pharmacist.
Smoking significantly increases the risk of serious cardiovascular side effects with this medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, stroke, or severe abdominal pain.
Call prescriber for persistent severe headaches, vision changes, or mood changes.
self_monitoring: Track menstrual cycle/bleeding patterns.
Monitor blood pressure periodically.
Do not smoke while taking this medication.
missed_dose_instructions: If one active pill is missed, take it as soon as remembered (even if it means taking two in one day) and continue the pack; if two or more are missed, follow the specific product instructions and use backup contraception - contact your prescriber or pharmacist for guidance.

description: Prevents pregnancy by suppressing ovulation and altering cervical mucus and the uterine lining; also commonly used to treat acne in appropriate patients.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth at the same time every day, following the pack schedule and taking tablets in the correct order without interruption.
typical_duration: Used continuously as long as contraception (or acne treatment) is desired.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day and in the order printed on the pack, since hormone amounts change through the cycle.
Start the next pack immediately after finishing the previous one.
Use a backup method (e.g., condoms) for the first 7 days if starting mid-cycle or if instructed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: History of blood clots (DVT/PE), stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected breast cancer or estrogen-dependent tumors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg pain/swelling, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, coughing up blood
Signs of stroke: severe headache, vision changes, weakness/numbness on one side, slurred speech
Severe abdominal pain (possible liver problem or blood clot)
Yellowing of skin/eyes (liver problem)
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception if combined.
Certain Rx antibiotics (e.g., rifampin) and some anticonvulsants can reduce effectiveness; confirm any new prescription with a pharmacist.
Smoking significantly increases the risk of serious cardiovascular side effects with this medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, stroke, or severe abdominal pain.
Call prescriber for persistent severe headaches, vision changes, or mood changes.
self_monitoring: Track menstrual cycle/bleeding patterns.
Monitor blood pressure periodically.
Do not smoke while taking this medication.
missed_dose_instructions: If one active pill is missed, take it as soon as remembered (even if it means taking two in one day) and continue the pack in the correct pill order; if two or more are missed, follow the specific product instructions and use backup contraception - contact your prescriber or pharmacist for guidance.

drug_class: Combined oral contraceptive (estrogen/progestin, with anti-mineralocorticoid activity)
description: Prevents pregnancy by suppressing ovulation and altering cervical mucus and the uterine lining; drospirenone also has a mild diuretic-like effect that can raise blood potassium.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth at the same time every day, following the pack schedule without interruption.
typical_duration: Used continuously as long as contraception is desired.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day to maintain effectiveness.
Start the next pack immediately after finishing the previous one, following the specific pack instructions.
Use a backup method (e.g., condoms) for the first 7 days if starting mid-cycle or if instructed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: History of blood clots (DVT/PE), stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected breast cancer or estrogen-dependent tumors
Kidney, liver, or adrenal disease that could impair potassium clearance
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg pain/swelling, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, coughing up blood
Signs of stroke: severe headache, vision changes, weakness/numbness on one side, slurred speech
Signs of high potassium: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
Severe abdominal pain or yellowing of skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium - drospirenone can raise blood potassium.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) taken regularly may further increase potassium retention when combined with drospirenone.
St. John's Wort can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception if combined.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, stroke, or high potassium (muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat).
Call prescriber for persistent severe headaches, vision changes, or mood changes.
self_monitoring: Track menstrual cycle/bleeding patterns.
Monitor blood pressure periodically.
Avoid potassium-rich supplements unless approved by prescriber; keep any scheduled potassium labs.
missed_dose_instructions: If one active pill is missed, take it as soon as remembered (even if it means taking two in one day) and continue the pack; if two or more are missed, follow the specific product instructions and use backup contraception - contact your prescriber or pharmacist for guidance.

description: Prevents pregnancy, primarily by thickening cervical mucus and sometimes suppressing ovulation; contains no estrogen, making it an option for those who cannot take estrogen (e.g., while breastfeeding or with clotting risk).
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth every day at the same time, with no placebo/hormone-free days.
typical_duration: Used continuously as long as contraception is desired.
directions_for_use: Take at the exact same time every day, within about a 3-hour window - timing is stricter than with combined pills.
Start a new pack immediately after finishing the previous one; there are no inactive pills.
Use a backup method for 48 hours if a pill is taken more than 3 hours late.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of an ectopic pregnancy: severe one-sided abdominal pain, especially if a period is missed
Signs of blood clot (less common than with estrogen-containing pills, but still possible): leg pain/swelling, chest pain, shortness of breath
Severe abdominal pain or yellowing of skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception if combined.
Certain Rx antibiotics (e.g., rifampin) and some anticonvulsants can reduce effectiveness; confirm any new prescription with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe abdominal pain or signs of blood clot.
Call prescriber for persistent irregular bleeding or mood changes.
self_monitoring: Track pill-taking times closely, since this pill has a narrow timing window.
Track menstrual/bleeding patterns.
missed_dose_instructions: If a pill is more than 3 hours late or missed, take it as soon as remembered and use a backup contraceptive method (e.g., condoms) for the next 48 hours; contact your prescriber or pharmacist if unsure.

description: Prevents pregnancy by releasing a steady, low dose of estrogen and progestin absorbed through the vaginal lining, which suppresses ovulation.
typical_dosage: Insert one ring into the vagina and leave in place continuously for 3 weeks, then remove for a 1-week ring-free break before inserting a new ring.
typical_duration: Used continuously in repeating 3-week-in/1-week-out cycles as long as contraception is desired.
directions_for_use: Insert and leave the ring in place for 21 days; exact positioning in the vagina is not critical for effectiveness.
Remove after 3 weeks and insert a new ring after a 7-day ring-free break.
If the ring is out of place for more than 3 hours, use backup contraception and follow product instructions.
storage_instructions: Follow pharmacy label storage instructions (some rings require refrigeration before dispensing); once dispensed, may generally be kept at room temperature until the labeled expiration date.
contraindications: History of blood clots (DVT/PE), stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected breast cancer or estrogen-dependent tumors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg pain/swelling, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, coughing up blood
Signs of stroke: severe headache, vision changes, weakness/numbness on one side, slurred speech
Severe abdominal pain or yellowing of skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception if combined.
Certain Rx antibiotics (e.g., rifampin) and some anticonvulsants can reduce effectiveness; confirm any new prescription with a pharmacist.
Avoid inserting spermicides/OTC vaginal products at the same time without checking compatibility with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, stroke, or severe abdominal pain.
Call prescriber for persistent vaginal irritation or discharge, or for severe headaches.
self_monitoring: Track the 3-week-in/1-week-out schedule to avoid gaps in protection.
Track menstrual cycle/bleeding patterns.
Do not smoke while using this medication.
missed_dose_instructions: If the ring is out of place for less than 3 hours, rinse with cool water and reinsert; if out for more than 3 hours, reinsert and use backup contraception for 7 days - contact your prescriber or pharmacist for guidance on adjusting the schedule.

description: Prevents pregnancy for 3 months per injection by suppressing ovulation; given as an intramuscular or subcutaneous injection by a healthcare provider.
dosage_forms: Injectable suspension (150 mg/mL IM; 104 mg/0.65 mL subcutaneous)
typical_dosage: One injection every 3 months (12-13 weeks), given by a healthcare provider.
typical_duration: Used long-term as ongoing contraception, with re-injection every 3 months.
directions_for_use: Return for a repeat injection every 3 months to maintain effectiveness; do not delay beyond the recommended window.
Use backup contraception if an injection is more than 1-2 weeks late, per provider guidance.
storage_instructions: Administered by a healthcare provider; between doses, keep any dispensed prefilled syringe at room temperature and protect from light and freezing.
contraindications: History of blood clots (use with caution - discuss with prescriber)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg pain/swelling, chest pain, shortness of breath
Severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Significant bone density loss with long-term use (discuss with prescriber if used more than 2 years)
Severe depression or mood changes
common_side_effects: Irregular bleeding or spotting, especially in the first several months
Delayed return to fertility after stopping
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product or supplement with a pharmacist.
Calcium and vitamin D supplementation may be recommended with long-term use due to bone density effects - discuss with prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or severe allergic reaction.
Call prescriber for irregular bleeding that is heavy or prolonged, or for mood changes.
self_monitoring: Track injection due dates to avoid gaps in protection.
Monitor weight and mood changes.
Discuss bone health with prescriber if used long-term.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact the prescriber's office to schedule the next injection as close to the 3-month mark as possible; if the injection is delayed, use backup contraception and consult the prescriber, since effectiveness can decrease.

description: Provides long-term pregnancy prevention (several years) by releasing a small, steady amount of progestin locally in the uterus, which thickens cervical mucus and thins the uterine lining; also used to treat heavy menstrual bleeding.
route: Intrauterine (device placed by a healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: One device placed in the uterus by a healthcare provider; provides continuous contraception for several years depending on the specific product - confirm replacement timing with prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, continuous use for the product's approved duration, then removed/replaced by a provider.
directions_for_use: Check for the device's strings periodically as instructed by your provider to confirm it remains in place.
Attend scheduled follow-up visits, especially soon after placement.
Contact provider if you cannot feel the strings or if you or a partner feels the hard plastic of the device.
storage_instructions: Administered and stored by a healthcare provider prior to placement; not self-administered or self-stored.
contraindications: Current pelvic infection or untreated sexually transmitted infection
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of pelvic infection: fever, severe pelvic pain, unusual discharge
Severe abdominal pain (possible perforation or expulsion)
Signs the device has moved or come out (cannot feel strings, partner feels hard plastic)
Heavy, prolonged bleeding
common_side_effects: Irregular spotting or bleeding, especially in the first few months
Lighter periods over time (may stop altogether)
Ovarian cysts (usually resolve on their own)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses, since the hormone acts mainly locally in the uterus; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) may help with cramping after placement if approved by your provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for fever with pelvic pain, severe abdominal pain, or heavy bleeding.
Contact provider if you cannot feel the device's strings or think it may have moved.
self_monitoring: Check for the device's strings periodically as instructed.
Track bleeding pattern changes.
Keep scheduled follow-up appointments.
missed_dose_instructions: There is no daily dose to miss; this device provides continuous protection until removed. Keep track of the recommended replacement date and schedule removal/replacement with your provider before it expires.

description: Prevents pregnancy after unprotected sex or contraceptive failure by delaying or preventing ovulation; most effective the sooner it is taken after intercourse, and does not work if pregnancy has already occurred.
typical_dosage: One 1.5 mg tablet by mouth as a single dose, taken as soon as possible (within 72 hours, though some benefit may occur up to 120 hours) after unprotected intercourse.
typical_duration: Single-use, one-time dose; not intended for regular or ongoing contraception.
directions_for_use: Take as soon as possible after unprotected sex - effectiveness decreases with time.
If vomiting occurs within 2 hours of taking the dose, contact a pharmacist or provider about whether to repeat the dose.
This does not protect against future acts of intercourse - use a regular contraceptive method going forward.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known pregnancy (does not terminate an existing pregnancy and will not work)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe lower abdominal pain 3-5 weeks after use (possible ectopic pregnancy) - seek care promptly
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
common_side_effects: Menstrual period changes (earlier or later than expected)
otc_and_other_interactions: Effectiveness may be reduced in individuals with a higher body weight; discuss options with a pharmacist.

Certain medications (e.g., some anticonvulsants, St. John's Wort, rifampin) can reduce effectiveness - a copper IUD or other prescription option may be a more effective alternative if using these medications regularly; ask a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Take a pregnancy test if your period is more than a week late.
Seek care for severe abdominal pain or signs of allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track menstrual cycle after use.
Take a pregnancy test if period is delayed by more than a week.
Consider starting or continuing a regular contraceptive method.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a single-dose, one-time medication used after unprotected intercourse, not a scheduled regimen, so there is no missed dose to account for.

description: An emergency contraceptive tablet taken after unprotected sex or contraceptive failure to prevent pregnancy; it is not intended for routine birth control and does not end an existing pregnancy.
typical_dosage: One 30 mg tablet taken as a single dose as soon as possible, and no later than 120 hours (5 days), after unprotected intercourse or contraceptive failure.
typical_duration: Single-dose, one-time use per episode.
directions_for_use: Take the single tablet as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse for best effectiveness.
Can be taken with or without food.
If vomiting occurs within 3 hours of taking the dose, contact prescriber about whether to repeat the dose.
Not for use as a regular birth control method.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known or suspected existing pregnancy (does not terminate a pregnancy)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe lower abdominal pain (rule out ectopic pregnancy, especially if pregnancy occurs after use)
Signs of an allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling, trouble breathing
common_side_effects: Menstrual period changes (earlier, later, or heavier than usual)
otc_and_other_interactions: Using a progestin-containing contraceptive (pills, patch, ring, implant, or IUD) within 5 days before or after ulipristal can make both methods less effective; use a barrier method (condoms) until the next period.
St. John's Wort and other strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce ulipristal's effectiveness.
Effectiveness may be reduced in women with a higher body weight/BMI - discuss options with a pharmacist or prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for severe lower abdominal pain or signs of an allergic reaction.
Take a pregnancy test if your period is more than a week late after taking this medication.
self_monitoring: Note the date taken and expected next menstrual period.
Start or resume regular contraception as directed - it does not provide ongoing pregnancy protection.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a one-time emergency dose, not a scheduled medication, so there is no missed dose to account for; take it as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse.

description: Replaces estrogen in the body to relieve menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, and to help prevent postmenopausal osteoporosis.
typical_dosage: 0.5-2 mg by mouth once daily, or one patch applied to the skin and changed once or twice weekly, using the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration needed.
typical_duration: Individualized; reassessed periodically by the prescriber, as ongoing use carries cumulative risks.
directions_for_use: Take tablets at the same time each day, with or without food.
Apply patches to clean, dry, hairless skin on the lower abdomen (avoid the waistline and breasts); rotate application sites.
Do not apply patches to skin exposed to direct sunlight.
storage_instructions: Store tablets at room temperature; store patches in their sealed pouch until use.
contraindications: History of breast cancer or other estrogen-sensitive cancer
Active or history of blood clots (DVT/PE) or stroke/heart attack
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Leg pain, swelling, or warmth (possible blood clot)
Chest pain, shortness of breath, or coughing up blood
Sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness on one side of the body, or slurred speech (possible stroke)
Yellowing of skin/eyes or severe abdominal pain (liver problems)
New breast lumps or abnormal vaginal bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can lower estradiol levels and reduce effectiveness.
May alter the effect of warfarin - clotting factor changes can affect INR and bleeding/clotting risk.
Can increase the amount of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine) needed - thyroid levels should be monitored.
Smoking significantly increases the risk of blood clots and stroke while taking estrogen.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for leg swelling/pain, chest pain, or sudden neurological symptoms.
Call the prescriber for new breast lumps, abnormal bleeding, or jaundice.
self_monitoring: Perform breast self-checks and keep up with recommended mammograms.
Report any abnormal vaginal bleeding to the prescriber.
Track hot flash frequency/severity to assess whether the dose is working.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. For patches, apply a new one as soon as remembered and resume the usual change schedule.

description: A mixture of estrogens used to relieve menopausal hot flashes and vaginal dryness and to help prevent postmenopausal osteoporosis.
typical_dosage: 0.3-1.25 mg by mouth once daily, or vaginal cream used as directed, at the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration needed.
typical_duration: Individualized; reassessed periodically by the prescriber, as ongoing use carries cumulative risks.
directions_for_use: Take tablets at the same time each day, with or without food.
If using vaginal cream, insert with the provided applicator as directed, typically at bedtime.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep vaginal cream tightly closed.
contraindications: History of breast cancer or other estrogen-sensitive cancer
Active or history of blood clots (DVT/PE) or stroke/heart attack
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Leg pain, swelling, or warmth (possible blood clot)
Chest pain, shortness of breath, or coughing up blood
Sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness on one side of the body, or slurred speech (possible stroke)
Yellowing of skin/eyes or severe abdominal pain (liver problems)
New breast lumps or abnormal vaginal bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can lower estrogen levels and reduce effectiveness.
May alter the effect of warfarin - clotting factor changes can affect INR and bleeding/clotting risk.
Can increase the amount of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine) needed - thyroid levels should be monitored.
Smoking significantly increases the risk of blood clots and stroke while taking estrogen.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for leg swelling/pain, chest pain, or sudden neurological symptoms.
Call the prescriber for new breast lumps, abnormal bleeding, or jaundice.
self_monitoring: Perform breast self-checks and keep up with recommended mammograms.
Report any abnormal vaginal bleeding to the prescriber.
Track hot flash frequency/severity to assess whether the dose is working.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A bio-identical progesterone capsule used with estrogen therapy to protect the uterine lining, or to treat lack of menstrual periods due to progesterone deficiency.
typical_dosage: 100-200 mg by mouth once daily, usually at bedtime, on the schedule directed by the prescriber.
typical_duration: Varies by indication - cyclic (part of each month) or continuous, per prescriber instructions.
directions_for_use: Take at bedtime because it can cause dizziness or drowsiness.
Take on an empty stomach unless your prescriber directs otherwise.
Do not use if you have a peanut allergy - this product is formulated with peanut oil.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Active or history of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected pregnancy (unless specifically directed by prescriber for pregnancy support)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Leg pain, swelling, or warmth (possible blood clot)
Sudden severe headache, vision changes, or weakness on one side of the body
Signs of a severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing
Yellowing of skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: Grapefruit juice may increase drug levels - use caution with regular consumption.
St. John's Wort may reduce effectiveness.
No significant OTC interactions expected beyond the above at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for leg swelling/pain, sudden neurological symptoms, or signs of severe allergic reaction.
Call the prescriber for persistent mood changes or abnormal bleeding.
self_monitoring: Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how this affects your alertness.
Report abnormal vaginal bleeding to the prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. Contact prescriber if you are unsure how a missed dose affects a specific treatment cycle.

drug_class: Selective estrogen receptor modulator (ovulation induction agent)
description: Stimulates the ovaries to release an egg (ovulation) and is used to help women with certain fertility problems become pregnant.
typical_dosage: 50 mg by mouth once daily for 5 days, usually starting on cycle day 3, 4, or 5, as directed by the prescriber.
typical_duration: Short courses per menstrual cycle, typically for no more than 3-6 cycles unless directed otherwise.
directions_for_use: Take at approximately the same time each day for the full 5-day course.
Contact the prescriber if a period does not occur before the next planned course.
Report any visual disturbances immediately and stop the medication.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Ovarian cysts not related to polycystic ovary syndrome
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Visual disturbances (blurring, spots, flashes) - stop the medication and call the prescriber right away
Severe pelvic/abdominal pain, bloating, or rapid weight gain (possible ovarian hyperstimulation)
Signs of a blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) are generally avoided around ovulation as they may interfere with egg release - discuss pain relief options with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop the medication and call the prescriber immediately for visual changes or severe pelvic pain.
Seek emergency care for signs of a blood clot.
self_monitoring: Track menstrual cycles and ovulation signs as instructed by your fertility team.
Watch for and report multiple-pregnancy risk factors or unusual bloating.
Attend scheduled ultrasounds/monitoring appointments.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on the same day; if a full day is missed, contact the prescriber about how to continue the course rather than doubling the dose.

description: Relaxes muscles in the prostate and bladder neck to improve urine flow in men with an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia).
typical_dosage: 0.4 mg by mouth once daily, approximately 30 minutes after the same meal each day; may be increased to 0.8 mg if needed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take about 30 minutes after the same meal each day for consistent absorption.
Swallow capsules whole - do not crush, chew, or open.
Rise slowly from sitting or lying down to reduce dizziness, especially with the first few doses.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in certain patients (discuss with prescriber)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting or severe dizziness on standing
Painful erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism)
Signs of a severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: PDE5 inhibitors for erectile dysfunction (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) can add to the blood-pressure-lowering effect and cause dizziness or fainting.
Inform any eye surgeon before cataract surgery - tamsulosin is linked to intraoperative floppy iris syndrome even after stopping the drug.
action_if_adverse_effects: Sit or lie down immediately if feeling dizzy or faint, and call the prescriber if it persists.
Seek emergency care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptoms to assess improvement.
Be cautious when driving or standing quickly until you know how this medication affects you.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time after the next meal; do not double up.

description: Shrinks prostate tissue to improve urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate (5 mg dose), or slows/reverses male pattern hair loss (1 mg dose).
typical_dosage: 1 mg by mouth once daily for hair loss, or 5 mg by mouth once daily for prostate enlargement, as prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy; benefits may take 3-6 months or longer to become noticeable.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not donate blood until at least 1 month (hair loss dose) or 6 months (prostate dose) after your last dose.
Women who are or may become pregnant should not handle broken or crushed tablets.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should not take or handle this medication (risk of birth defects in a male fetus)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening depression, mood changes, or thoughts of self-harm
Breast lumps, pain, discharge, or enlargement
Signs of a severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
This medication lowers PSA blood test results by about half - tell any clinician ordering a PSA test that you take finasteride.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call the prescriber promptly for mood changes, breast changes, or persistent sexual side effects.
Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptoms or hair growth over several months to assess benefit.
Report any mood changes to your prescriber.
Perform breast self-checks and report any lumps or tenderness.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Shrinks prostate tissue and improves urinary symptoms in men with an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia).
typical_dosage: 0.5 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy; benefits may take 3-6 months or longer to become noticeable.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow capsules whole - do not chew or open them.
Do not donate blood until at least 6 months after your last dose.
Women who are or may become pregnant should not handle leaking capsules.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should not take or handle this medication (risk of birth defects in a male fetus)
Known hypersensitivity to dutasteride or other 5-alpha reductase inhibitors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Breast lumps, pain, discharge, or enlargement
Signs of a severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
This medication lowers PSA blood test results by about half - tell any clinician ordering a PSA test that you take dutasteride.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call the prescriber promptly for breast changes or persistent sexual side effects.
Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptoms over several months to assess benefit.
Perform breast self-checks and report any lumps or tenderness.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Relaxes the bladder muscle to reduce urinary urgency, frequency, and leakage caused by an overactive bladder.
typical_dosage: 5 mg by mouth 2-3 times daily (immediate-release), or 5-30 mg once daily (extended-release), as directed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy, reassessed periodically for continued benefit.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food, at consistent times each day.
Swallow extended-release tablets whole - do not crush or chew.
Use sugar-free candy or sips of water for dry mouth.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Urinary retention or significant bladder outflow obstruction
Severe gastrointestinal motility disorders or GI obstruction
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Inability to urinate
Severe abdominal pain, constipation, or bloating
Confusion, hallucinations, or severe drowsiness (especially in older adults)
Eye pain or sudden vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other anticholinergic OTC products, such as diphenhydramine (Benadryl) or other sleep aids, increases dry mouth, constipation, drowsiness, and confusion risk.
Alcohol can increase drowsiness and dizziness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for inability to urinate or severe abdominal pain.
Call the prescriber for confusion, hallucinations, or worsening constipation.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptoms and bowel habits.
Use caution driving or operating machinery until you know how this affects alertness.
Stay well hydrated and manage constipation proactively (fiber, fluids).
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Relaxes the bladder muscle to reduce urinary urgency, frequency, and leakage caused by an overactive bladder.
typical_dosage: 5 mg by mouth once daily, may be increased to 10 mg once daily if needed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy, reassessed periodically for continued benefit.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food, swallowed with water.
Use sugar-free candy or sips of water for dry mouth.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Urinary retention or significant bladder outflow obstruction
Severe gastrointestinal motility disorders or GI obstruction
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Inability to urinate
Severe constipation or abdominal pain
Confusion or severe drowsiness (especially in older adults)
Irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other anticholinergic OTC products, such as diphenhydramine (Benadryl) or sleep aids, increases dry mouth, constipation, drowsiness, and confusion risk.
Can prolong the heart's QT interval - use caution combining with other QT-prolonging medications (e.g., ondansetron); discuss with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for inability to urinate or irregular heartbeat.
Call the prescriber for confusion or worsening constipation.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptoms and bowel habits.
Use caution driving or operating machinery until you know how this affects alertness.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

drug_class: Beta-3 adrenergic agonist for overactive bladder
description: Relaxes the bladder muscle to increase its storage capacity, reducing urinary urgency, frequency, and leakage.
typical_dosage: 25-50 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy, reassessed periodically for continued benefit.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow the tablet whole with water - do not crush, chew, or split it.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Severe liver or kidney impairment (dose adjustment or avoidance may be needed)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Significant increase in blood pressure
Inability to urinate
Signs of a severe allergic reaction: swelling of face/tongue/throat, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: This medication can raise blood levels of some other drugs, including metoprolol, by slowing their breakdown - report any new dizziness or unusually slow heartbeat.
Monitor blood pressure if taking OTC decongestants (e.g., pseudoephedrine), which can add to blood pressure elevation.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction or an inability to urinate.
Call the prescriber if home blood pressure readings are consistently elevated.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure periodically, especially early in treatment.
Track urinary symptoms to assess benefit.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Increases blood flow to treat erectile dysfunction and/or to relieve urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate.
typical_dosage: 10-20 mg taken as needed before sexual activity, or 2.5-5 mg once daily for ongoing use/BPH, as prescribed.
typical_duration: As-needed use before sexual activity, or long-term daily use for BPH symptoms/erectile dysfunction, depending on prescribed regimen.
directions_for_use: May be taken with or without food.
For as-needed use, take at least 30 minutes before anticipated sexual activity.
Do not take more than the prescribed amount in a 24-hour period.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Use of any nitrate medication (e.g., nitroglycerin) - can cause severe, life-threatening low blood pressure
Recent stroke, heart attack, or unstable heart disease
Severe liver or kidney impairment (dose adjustment or avoidance may be needed)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain or fainting during sexual activity - seek emergency care and avoid nitrates
Painful erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism)
Sudden decreased or lost vision in one or both eyes
Sudden decreased or lost hearing
otc_and_other_interactions: Alpha-blockers (e.g., tamsulosin) can add to blood-pressure-lowering effects and cause dizziness or fainting.
Do not combine with other PDE5 inhibitors (e.g., sildenafil, vardenafil).
Grapefruit juice may increase drug levels and side effects.
Alcohol can increase the risk of dizziness and low blood pressure.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, chest pain, or sudden vision/hearing loss.
Call the prescriber for persistent headache or flushing.
self_monitoring: Do not take if you have taken a nitrate medication recently - ask your prescriber how long to wait.
Report any vision or hearing changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: For as-needed use, there is no fixed schedule to miss - take only before sexual activity. For daily use, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip it and do not double up.

description: Increases blood flow to the penis to treat erectile dysfunction.
typical_dosage: 10 mg taken as needed approximately 60 minutes before sexual activity, adjusted between 5-20 mg based on response.
typical_duration: As-needed use before sexual activity; no more than once daily.
directions_for_use: Take about 60 minutes before anticipated sexual activity.
A high-fat meal may delay the onset of effect - consider taking on an empty stomach for faster results.
Do not take more than one dose per day.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Use of any nitrate medication (e.g., nitroglycerin) - can cause severe, life-threatening low blood pressure
Recent stroke, heart attack, or unstable heart disease
Known QT prolongation or use of Class IA/III antiarrhythmic medications
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain or fainting during sexual activity - seek emergency care and avoid nitrates
Painful erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism)
Sudden decreased or lost vision in one or both eyes
Sudden decreased or lost hearing
Irregular or rapid heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Alpha-blockers (e.g., tamsulosin) can add to blood-pressure-lowering effects and cause dizziness or fainting.
Do not combine with other PDE5 inhibitors (e.g., sildenafil, tadalafil).
Grapefruit juice may increase drug levels and side effects.
Alcohol can increase the risk of dizziness and low blood pressure.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, chest pain, or sudden vision/hearing loss.
Call the prescriber for irregular heartbeat or persistent dizziness.
self_monitoring: Do not take if you have taken a nitrate medication recently - ask your prescriber how long to wait.
Report any vision, hearing, or heart rhythm changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as needed before sexual activity; there is no fixed schedule to miss.

description: Numbs the lining of the urinary tract to relieve pain, burning, and urgency from a urinary tract infection; it treats symptoms only and does not treat the underlying infection.
typical_dosage: 95-200 mg by mouth up to 3 times daily after meals, generally for no more than 2 days.
typical_duration: Short-term use only, typically 2 days, alongside an antibiotic prescribed for the underlying infection.
directions_for_use: Take with or after food to reduce stomach upset.
Expect urine to turn orange or reddish-orange - this is normal and can stain clothing/contact lenses.
This does not replace antibiotic treatment for a urinary tract infection - see a prescriber if symptoms persist beyond 2 days.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Known G6PD deficiency (increased risk of hemolytic anemia)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice)
Bluish or grayish skin color, shortness of breath, or unusual fatigue (possible methemoglobinemia)
Signs of a severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Can interfere with urine and blood lab test results - tell your lab or clinician you are taking it.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for yellowing of skin/eyes or bluish skin color.
See a prescriber if urinary symptoms do not improve within 2 days.
self_monitoring: Do not use for more than 2 days without a prescriber evaluating the underlying infection.
Watch for improvement in burning/urgency symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as needed for urinary discomfort; if on a scheduled short course, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: A vitamin A-derived cream/gel applied to the skin to treat acne by increasing skin cell turnover and unclogging pores.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin (pea-sized for the face) layer to affected skin once daily, usually in the evening.
typical_duration: Ongoing use for weeks to months; full benefit may take 8-12 weeks.
directions_for_use: Wash and thoroughly dry the skin (wait 20-30 minutes after washing) before applying.
Apply a thin layer, avoiding the eyes, lips, and mucous membranes.
Use sunscreen daily and limit sun exposure - treated skin is more sensitive to sunburn.
Do not apply at the same time as benzoyl peroxide products; use them at different times of day if both are prescribed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from heat and light; keep tightly closed.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to tretinoin or other retinoids
Sunburned or eczematous skin at the application site
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe skin blistering, swelling, or crusting
Signs of a severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing
common_side_effects: Temporary worsening of acne in the first few weeks
otc_and_other_interactions: Using with benzoyl peroxide at the same time can inactivate tretinoin and increase skin irritation - apply at different times of day.
Other topical acne products (salicylic acid, alcohol-based astringents, medicated soaps) can add to dryness/irritation - introduce one product at a time.
Increased sun sensitivity - use sunscreen and limit sun/tanning bed exposure.
action_if_adverse_effects: Reduce application frequency or stop and call the prescriber for severe irritation, blistering, or swelling.
Seek care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Check skin for excessive redness, peeling, or irritation.
Track acne improvement over 8-12 weeks.
missed_dose_instructions: If an evening application is missed, simply apply at the next scheduled time; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: A gentler retinoid applied to the skin to treat acne by unclogging pores and reducing inflammation.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to affected skin once daily, usually in the evening.
typical_duration: Ongoing use for weeks to months; full benefit may take 8-12 weeks.
directions_for_use: Wash and dry the skin gently before applying.
Apply a thin layer, avoiding the eyes, lips, and mucous membranes.
Use sunscreen daily and limit sun exposure.
Can be combined with benzoyl peroxide, but introduce products gradually to minimize irritation.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from heat and light.
contraindications: Sunburned or eczematous skin at the application site
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe skin blistering, swelling, or crusting

description: A powerful oral vitamin A derivative used for severe, treatment-resistant nodular acne when other treatments have not worked.

storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.

Severe headache, vision changes, or nausea/vomiting (possible increased brain pressure)
Vision changes, especially trouble seeing at night
