typical_duration: Often long-term/ongoing, as directed by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take with food and a large glass of water to reduce stomach upset.
Swallow tablets whole; if unable to swallow, ask your pharmacist about dispersing in water/juice - do not crush or split on your own.
Take at the same time each day.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden weight gain, swelling of legs/face, or shortness of breath (fluid retention/heart problems)
Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Signs of GI bleeding or perforation: black/tarry stools, severe stomach pain
Signs of low blood counts/infection: fever, unusual bruising or bleeding
Severe rash or blistering skin reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice - can raise imatinib levels and toxicity.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can significantly lower imatinib levels and reduce effectiveness.
Azole antifungals such as fluconazole can increase imatinib levels/toxicity - discuss any antifungal need with your oncology team.
Imatinib can increase warfarin's blood-thinning effect - closer INR monitoring is needed if both are used.
Use acetaminophen cautiously and avoid excessive doses - combined liver stress risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for sudden swelling, breathing trouble, or signs of liver problems or bleeding.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled CBC (blood count) checks.
Keep scheduled liver function tests.
Track weight for sudden fluid retention.
Keep scheduled oncology follow-up labs to monitor treatment response.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered the same day unless it is close to the next dose - then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. Call your oncology team if you miss doses repeatedly.

description: A prodrug converted in the body to 5-fluorouracil, used to treat breast and colorectal cancers by interfering with cancer cell growth.
typical_dosage: Dosing is highly individualized based on body surface area, cancer type, and treatment protocol, and is set and adjusted by the oncology team - taken on a specific days-on/days-off cycle schedule that must be followed exactly.
typical_duration: Given in cycles (e.g., 14 days on, 7 days off) for a number of cycles determined by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take within 30 minutes after a meal, with water, exactly as scheduled.
Follow the exact days-on/days-off cycle schedule given by your oncology team - do not deviate.
Caregivers should wear gloves when handling tablets and wash hands afterward, since the drug is cytotoxic; avoid direct skin contact with broken or crushed tablets.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture, out of reach of children and pets.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Hand-foot syndrome: redness, pain, peeling, or blistering of palms/soles - report early
Severe diarrhea or vomiting leading to dehydration
Signs of low blood counts/infection: fever, unusual bruising or bleeding
Chest pain or irregular heartbeat (rare cardiac toxicity)
Severe mouth sores preventing eating or drinking
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly increases warfarin's blood-thinning effect - major bleeding risk; requires closer INR monitoring during and after treatment.
Avoid NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) when possible due to additive GI irritation/bleeding risk.
Folic acid or leucovorin-containing products can increase toxicity - use only if directed by your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Contact your oncology team promptly for hand-foot symptoms, severe diarrhea, or mouth sores so the dose can be adjusted.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled CBC and liver/kidney function checks.
Check hands and feet daily for redness, peeling, or blistering.
Track weight and hydration during periods of diarrhea/vomiting.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team about a missed dose rather than guessing - do not take an extra dose or change the cycle schedule on your own.

description: Modulates the immune system and blocks new blood vessel growth in tumors, used to treat multiple myeloma and certain other blood cancers.
typical_dosage: Dosing is highly individualized based on cancer type, cycle schedule, and lab values, and is set and adjusted by the oncology team - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Given in repeating cycles for a duration determined by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Do not open, break, or chew capsules; avoid contact with capsule contents if a capsule is damaged.
Take at the same time each day, with or without food, swallowed whole with water.
Available only through the restricted REVLIMID REMS program because of a serious birth-defect risk - follow all program requirements.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture, in the original packaging, out of reach of children and pets.
contraindications: Pregnancy (can cause severe, life-threatening birth defects)
Females who could become pregnant must use two reliable forms of contraception unless committing to abstinence; males must use condoms during and after treatment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Any suspicion of pregnancy - contact your prescriber and the REMS program immediately
Signs of a blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath - seek emergency care
Signs of low blood counts/infection: fever, unusual bruising or bleeding
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe skin reaction: blistering, peeling rash
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased risk of blood clots when combined with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (e.g., epoetin alfa, darbepoetin alfa) or estrogen-containing products.
Often combined with low-dose aspirin or an anticoagulant for clot prevention as part of the treatment plan - do not add or stop these without your oncology team's guidance.
NSAIDs may increase bleeding risk when platelet counts are low.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek emergency care for signs of a blood clot (leg swelling/pain, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath).
self_monitoring: Complete mandatory pregnancy tests as required by the REMS program if applicable.
Keep scheduled CBC checks.
Watch for and report new leg swelling, pain, or breathing difficulty right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team about a missed dose rather than guessing - do not double up, since dosing follows a specific cycle schedule.

description: Blocks proteins (CDK4/6) that drive cancer cell division, used with hormone therapy to treat certain hormone-receptor-positive breast cancers.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on treatment protocol and lab values, and is set and adjusted by the oncology team - taken on a specific days-on/days-off cycle schedule that must be followed exactly.
typical_duration: Given in repeating 28-day cycles (often 21 days on, 7 days off) for a duration determined by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day with food.
Swallow whole; do not chew, crush, or open capsules/tablets.
Follow the exact days-on/days-off cycle schedule given by your oncology team.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low white blood cell counts/infection: fever, chills, sore throat
New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (possible lung inflammation)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice - can raise palbociclib levels/toxicity.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as fluconazole or clarithromycin - can significantly increase toxicity.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can significantly reduce effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Contact your oncology team for new cough, shortness of breath, or signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled CBC checks before each cycle and periodically during the cycle.
Report new cough, fever, or shortness of breath promptly.
Keep scheduled liver function tests.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is vomited or missed, do not take an extra dose that day - resume the normal schedule the next day. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Blocks the effect of testosterone on prostate cancer cells, used to treat advanced prostate cancer.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by the oncology team, typically once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing therapy, as directed by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow whole; do not chew, dissolve, or open.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy (not indicated for use in females; can cause fetal harm)
History of seizures - use with extreme caution and prescriber discussion
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Seizure - seek emergency care immediately
Severe headache, confusion, or vision loss (possible posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, rare)
Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or shortness of breath (cardiovascular events)
Falls or fractures
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inducer - significantly reduces the effectiveness of many drugs, including warfarin, statins (simvastatin, atorvastatin), and sildenafil; discuss any new medication with your oncology team.
Avoid St. John's Wort - adds to the drug-level-lowering effect on other medications and offers no benefit here.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for a seizure, chest pain, or sudden vision/confusion changes.
Report new joint pain, falls, or high blood pressure readings to your oncology team.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure regularly.
Use fall-prevention precautions, especially in older adults.
Keep scheduled oncology follow-up labs.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered the same day; if it is the next day, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Blocks the body's production of testosterone-related hormones; used with low-dose prednisone to treat advanced prostate cancer.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by the oncology team; must be taken together with prednisone exactly as prescribed - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing therapy, as directed by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after a meal - food dramatically increases absorption and can cause excessive drug exposure.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
Take the prescribed dose of prednisone together with this medication exactly as directed - do not stop prednisone abruptly without medical guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy (not indicated for use in females; can cause fetal harm)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Signs of adrenal insufficiency if prednisone is stopped abruptly: weakness, dizziness, low blood pressure
Severe high blood pressure, swelling, or low potassium symptoms (muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat)
Chest pain or irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Must be taken with low-dose prednisone exactly as prescribed - stopping prednisone abruptly can cause adrenal insufficiency.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can reduce effectiveness via CYP3A4 induction.
May increase levels of drugs metabolized by CYP2D6; discuss all medications with your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for signs of liver problems, severe high blood pressure, or low potassium symptoms.
Never stop the accompanying prednisone dose without medical guidance - call your oncology team first.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled liver function tests.
Keep scheduled blood pressure and potassium level checks.
Continue taking prednisone exactly as directed alongside this medication.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and resume the normal schedule the next day - do not double up or take with food to make up for it. Continue taking prednisone as scheduled and contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Blocks testosterone's effect on prostate cancer cells; usually used together with a GnRH agonist (such as goserelin) to treat advanced prostate cancer.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by the oncology team, typically once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing therapy, as directed by the oncology team, usually alongside GnRH agonist therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
If also prescribed a GnRH agonist injection (such as goserelin), keep both medications on schedule.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Not indicated for use in females
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain
New or worsening cough or shortness of breath (rare lung inflammation)
Signs of heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases warfarin's blood-thinning effect - major bleeding risk; requires closer INR monitoring.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for signs of liver problems, breathing trouble, or heart failure symptoms.
Report unusual bruising or bleeding if taking warfarin together with this medication.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled liver function tests.
Keep any concurrent GnRH agonist injections on schedule.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it - do not double up. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Slows production of abnormal blood cells; used to treat certain blood cancers (such as chronic myeloid leukemia) and to reduce painful crises in sickle cell disease.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on body weight, condition being treated, and lab values, and is set and adjusted by the prescriber - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Often long-term/ongoing, with dose adjustments based on regular lab monitoring.
directions_for_use: Take with a full glass of water, at the same time each day.
Swallow capsules whole; if unable to swallow, ask your pharmacist about proper handling of the contents.
Caregivers should wear gloves and avoid direct skin contact when handling capsules or their contents, since this medication is cytotoxic; wash hands after handling.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture, out of reach of children and pets.
contraindications: Severe bone marrow suppression at baseline (per prescriber assessment)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood counts/infection: fever, unusual bruising or bleeding, severe fatigue
New skin ulcers or sores, especially on the legs - report to prescriber
New or worsening cough or shortness of breath (rare lung toxicity)
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive low blood counts when combined with other bone-marrow-suppressing medications (such as azathioprine or other chemotherapy).
Avoid live vaccines while on this medication - discuss vaccination timing with your care team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Report any new skin ulcers or sores to your prescriber promptly.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled CBC checks.
Inspect skin, especially legs, regularly for new sores or ulcers.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next dose - then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. Contact your prescriber about repeated missed doses.

description: Interferes with rapidly dividing cells; used at low weekly doses for autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and at higher, protocol-based doses for certain cancers.
route: Oral tablet or subcutaneous injection, depending on the product prescribed
typical_dosage: Dosing is highly individualized based on the condition being treated and is set by your prescriber. For autoimmune conditions it is often taken only ONCE PER WEEK, not daily - never take this medication daily unless specifically instructed, since dosing errors with this drug have caused fatal overdoses. For cancer treatment, dosing follows a specific oncology protocol.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing for autoimmune conditions; cycle-based for cancer treatment, as directed by the prescriber.
directions_for_use: Confirm with your pharmacist or prescriber exactly which day(s) of the week to take this medication if it is prescribed for an autoimmune condition - double-check before every dose.
Take folic acid supplementation on non-methotrexate days if prescribed, to help reduce side effects.
Avoid alcohol - increases liver toxicity risk.
Caregivers should wear gloves when handling tablets or preparing injections, since this medication is cytotoxic.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture, in the original container, well out of reach of children - accidental ingestion or dosing errors can be fatal.
contraindications: Significant kidney or liver impairment (per prescriber assessment)
Alcohol use disorder or significant liver disease
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood counts/infection: fever, unusual bruising or bleeding
Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (possible lung toxicity)
Severe mouth sores or stomach ulceration
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen, aspirin) can significantly increase methotrexate blood levels and toxicity, especially at higher doses - avoid or use only with close prescriber supervision.
Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim significantly increases methotrexate toxicity (both are folate antagonists) - this combination should be avoided.
Proton pump inhibitors (such as omeprazole) can reduce methotrexate clearance and raise levels, especially at higher doses.
Avoid alcohol due to additive liver toxicity risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for any unusual bleeding, bruising, or signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled CBC, liver function, and kidney function tests.
Report any fever or unusual bleeding immediately.
Double-check your dosing schedule (weekly vs. daily) with your pharmacist regularly.
missed_dose_instructions: For weekly dosing, contact your prescriber about a missed dose rather than guessing - do not take an extra dose or double up, and never take this medication more frequently than prescribed.

description: Blocks a protein (BTK) that certain blood cancer cells need to grow and survive, used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia and other lymphomas.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by the oncology team, typically once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Often long-term/ongoing, as directed by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Swallow whole with water at the same time each day.
Avoid grapefruit and Seville oranges.
Tell your oncology team and any surgeon/dentist about this medication before any surgery or procedure, since it may need to be paused.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serious bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in urine/stool, prolonged bleeding from a cut
Irregular heartbeat or palpitations (risk of atrial fibrillation)
Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat
Severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure
Signs of tumor lysis syndrome early in treatment (muscle cramps, nausea, decreased urination) - discuss risk with your care team
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit and Seville oranges - can significantly raise ibrutinib levels.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can significantly reduce effectiveness.

Strong azole antifungals (such as fluconazole) and macrolide antibiotics (such as clarithromycin) can significantly increase ibrutinib levels and toxicity - discuss any new prescription with your oncology team.
Increased bleeding risk when combined with warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel, or other blood thinners/antiplatelets - discuss any new OTC pain reliever or supplement with your care team before starting.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for palpitations, unusual bleeding, or uncontrolled high blood pressure.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled CBC checks.
Monitor blood pressure regularly.
Report new palpitations or irregular heartbeat promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible the same day; if it is missed by more than a normal dosing interval, skip it and resume the next scheduled dose - do not double up. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Blocks a mutated EGFR protein that drives growth in certain non-small cell lung cancers.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by the oncology team, typically once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Often long-term/ongoing, as directed by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow whole; if unable to swallow, ask your pharmacist about dispersing in water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (possible lung inflammation) - seek care promptly
Palpitations, dizziness, or fainting (possible QT prolongation/heart rhythm changes)
Signs of heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain
Signs of low blood counts/infection: fever, unusual bruising or bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid St. John's Wort - can significantly reduce effectiveness via CYP3A4 induction.
Use caution with other medications that can prolong the QT interval; review your full medication list with your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Contact your oncology team promptly for new cough, shortness of breath, or palpitations.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled heart function tests (echocardiogram) as ordered.
Report new cough or shortness of breath right away.
Keep scheduled CBC checks.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by less than 12 hours, take it as soon as remembered; if more than 12 hours have passed, skip it and resume the next scheduled dose - do not double up. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Blocks multiple proteins that support tumor blood vessel growth, used to treat kidney cancer and gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST).
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on cancer type and treatment protocol (often given on a cycle of weeks on/weeks off), and is set and adjusted by the oncology team - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Given in cycles for a duration determined by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow whole with water.
Follow the exact cycle schedule (weeks on/weeks off) given by your oncology team.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain
Severe or sudden high blood pressure - seek urgent care
Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Signs of bleeding, including GI or tumor-related bleeding
Signs of thyroid dysfunction: fatigue, weight change, feeling unusually cold or hot
Palpitations or fainting (possible QT prolongation)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice - can raise sunitinib levels.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can significantly reduce effectiveness.
Avoid strong azole antifungals (fluconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole) - can increase toxicity and QT prolongation risk.
Monitor blood pressure closely if also taking other blood-pressure-affecting medications (amlodipine, lisinopril, losartan, metoprolol).
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for signs of heart failure, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or bleeding.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure regularly, including at home.
Keep scheduled heart function tests (ejection fraction), thyroid function tests, and liver function tests.
Keep scheduled CBC checks.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and it is more than 12 hours until the next dose, take it as soon as remembered; otherwise skip it and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Blocks proteins involved in tumor blood vessel growth, used to treat advanced kidney cancer and certain soft tissue sarcomas.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by the oncology team, typically once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Often long-term/ongoing, as directed by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after a meal - food significantly increases absorption.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or break, since this increases absorption and toxicity risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, abdominal pain - seek care promptly
Severe or sudden high blood pressure - seek urgent care
Signs of heart problems: chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, swelling
Signs of bleeding or GI perforation: black/tarry stools, severe stomach pain
Signs of a blood clot: leg swelling/pain, sudden shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid acid-reducing medications - proton pump inhibitors (such as omeprazole) and H2 blockers substantially reduce pazopanib absorption since it needs stomach acid to dissolve properly; discuss any heartburn medication with your oncology team.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as fluconazole - can increase toxicity.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can significantly reduce effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for signs of liver problems, severe high blood pressure, or bleeding.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled liver function tests, especially early in treatment.
Monitor blood pressure regularly.
Keep scheduled heart function tests as ordered.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and resume the normal schedule the next day - do not double up or take it close to a meal to make up for it. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Blocks EGFR protein signaling to slow the growth of certain lung and pancreatic cancers.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by the oncology team, typically once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Often long-term/ongoing, as directed by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after food.
Take at the same time each day.
Do not smoke while on this medication - smoking significantly lowers drug levels; discuss smoking cessation support with your care team.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (possible lung inflammation) - seek care promptly
Severe diarrhea leading to dehydration
Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe stomach pain (rare GI perforation risk)
Eye pain, redness, or vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Acid-reducing medications (proton pump inhibitors such as omeprazole, and H2 blockers) can reduce erlotinib absorption - discuss any heartburn medication with your oncology team, since spacing or an alternative may be needed.
Smoking significantly lowers erlotinib blood levels.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
Erlotinib can increase warfarin's blood-thinning effect - closer INR monitoring is needed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Contact your oncology team promptly for new cough, shortness of breath, severe diarrhea, or eye symptoms.
self_monitoring: Watch for and report new cough or shortness of breath.
Keep scheduled liver function tests.
Track skin and eye changes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and resume the normal schedule the next day rather than doubling up. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Blocks the effect of testosterone on prostate cancer cells, used to treat advanced prostate cancer.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by the oncology team, typically once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing therapy, as directed by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow whole; do not chew, dissolve, or open.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Not indicated for use in females (can cause fetal harm)
History of seizures - use with caution and prescriber discussion
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Seizure - seek emergency care immediately
Severe rash (can require stopping the medication)
Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or shortness of breath (cardiovascular events)
Falls or fractures
Signs of low thyroid function: fatigue, weight gain, feeling cold
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inducer - significantly reduces the effectiveness of many drugs, including warfarin, statins (simvastatin, atorvastatin), sildenafil, and hormonal contraceptives; discuss any new medication with your oncology team.
Avoid St. John's Wort - adds to the drug-level-lowering effect on other medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for a seizure or chest pain.
Report new rash, falls, or high blood pressure readings to your oncology team.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure regularly.
Keep scheduled thyroid function tests.
Use fall-prevention precautions, especially in older adults.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered the same day; if it is the next day, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: Blocks testosterone's effect on prostate cancer cells, used to treat advanced prostate cancer, generally with less crossing into the brain than similar drugs in this class.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by the oncology team, typically taken twice daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing therapy, as directed by the oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take with food, which improves absorption.
Take doses at consistent, evenly spaced times as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Not indicated for use in females (can cause fetal harm)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or shortness of breath (cardiovascular events)
Signs of low blood counts: unusual bruising or bleeding, fever
Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine (rare)
Falls or fractures
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as fluconazole - may increase darolutamide levels/toxicity.
Avoid St. John's Wort - may reduce effectiveness.
May increase levels of statins (simvastatin, atorvastatin) - report new unexplained muscle pain to your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for chest pain, palpitations, or signs of a fall/fracture.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled CBC and liver function tests.
Monitor cardiovascular risk factors as directed by your oncology team.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered with food, then resume the normal schedule - do not double up to make up for a missed dose. Contact your oncology team about repeated missed doses.

description: A hormone therapy implant that lowers sex hormone (testosterone or estrogen) production, used to treat prostate cancer, certain breast cancers, and endometriosis.
dosage_forms: Subcutaneous implant (3.6 mg monthly; 10.8 mg every 3 months)
typical_dosage: Administered by a healthcare provider as a subcutaneous implant, typically every 1 or 3 months; the exact schedule is set by the oncology team - never delay or skip a scheduled injection without contacting the clinic.
typical_duration: Long-term, as directed by the oncology team; duration depends on the condition being treated.
directions_for_use: This medication is administered only by a healthcare provider as an implant placed under the skin of the abdominal wall.
Keep all scheduled injection appointments - do not delay.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled by the clinic/pharmacy; no home storage typically required.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a temporary symptom flare in the first weeks (worsening bone pain, urinary symptoms) - discuss with your prescriber
Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst/urination
Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or shortness of breath (cardiovascular risk, particularly with pre-existing heart disease)
Severe allergic reaction or injection site reaction
Signs of a bone fracture with long-term use
otc_and_other_interactions: May affect blood sugar control in people with diabetes - monitor glucose closely if also taking metformin, glipizide, or insulin.
Can affect heart rhythm (QT interval) - use caution with other medications that also affect heart rhythm; discuss your full medication list with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or signs of a severe allergic reaction.
Contact your care team for worsening bone pain or urinary symptoms in the first weeks of treatment.
self_monitoring: Keep the injection schedule exactly on time - contact the clinic immediately to reschedule if an appointment is missed.
Keep scheduled bone density scans with long-term use.
Monitor blood sugar closely if diabetic.
Keep scheduled blood pressure/cardiac risk monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: This is administered by a healthcare provider - contact the clinic immediately to reschedule if an appointment is missed, since delays can allow hormone levels to rebound and reduce treatment effectiveness.

description: Reduces the number of platelets made by the bone marrow; used to treat essential thrombocythemia and other conditions with excess platelet production.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on platelet counts and response, and is set and adjusted by the prescriber - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Often long-term/ongoing, with dose adjustments based on regular blood count monitoring.
directions_for_use: Take consistently, either always with or always without food, as directed.
If taking more than once daily, space doses evenly as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Significant heart disease (can worsen heart failure or arrhythmias)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath (heart problems) - seek care promptly
Signs of heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain
Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in urine/stool
Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Rebound high platelet counts if the medication is stopped abruptly - do not stop without prescriber guidance
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases bleeding risk when combined with aspirin, warfarin, clopidogrel, or NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen), since it also affects platelet function.
Avoid other medications that lower blood counts without prescriber guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, or signs of bleeding.
Do not stop this medication abruptly - contact your prescriber first, since platelet counts can rebound.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled platelet counts (CBC).
Keep scheduled heart function tests (echocardiogram) at baseline and periodically.
Monitor blood pressure and heart rate.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next dose; then skip it and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Contact your prescriber about repeated missed doses.

description: Suppresses the immune system to help prevent organ transplant rejection; sometimes used for certain autoimmune conditions.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on the type of transplant, lab values, and response, and is set and adjusted by your transplant team - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, for as long as the transplanted organ needs immunosuppression.
directions_for_use: Take consistently the same way relative to food each time, usually on an empty stomach, unless your transplant team directs otherwise.
Take exactly on schedule, usually twice daily about 12 hours apart.
Do not switch between different brands or formulations without your transplant team's approval, since absorption can differ.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy (significant risk of miscarriage and birth defects; a REMS program requires reliable contraception)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat - seek care immediately
Signs of low blood counts: unusual bruising or bleeding, pallor, severe fatigue
Signs of GI bleeding: black/tarry stools, vomiting blood
Confusion, vision changes, or new weakness (rare, serious brain infection risk - PML)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) when possible - increased GI and kidney risk.

Acid-reducing medications (proton pump inhibitors such as omeprazole, and antacids) can reduce mycophenolate absorption - take at a consistent time relative to these medications as directed by your transplant team.
Avoid live vaccines while on this medication.
Additive infection and low-blood-count risk with other immunosuppressants.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for unusual bleeding, confusion, or vision changes.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled CBC checks.
Keep all transplant clinic follow-ups and lab draws exactly on schedule.
Use reliable contraception as directed if of reproductive potential.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your transplant team about a missed dose rather than guessing - do not double up, since both too little and too much immunosuppression can be dangerous.

description: Suppresses the immune system to help prevent organ transplant rejection or to control certain autoimmune conditions.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on the condition being treated, body weight, and lab values, and is set and adjusted by your prescriber - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as directed by your transplant team or specialist.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce nausea.
Take at the same time(s) each day as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat - seek care immediately
Signs of low blood counts: unusual bruising or bleeding, fatigue, pallor
Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) when possible - increased GI and kidney risk.
Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim increases the risk of significant low blood counts when combined with azathioprine - use only with close monitoring if this combination is needed.
Additive low-blood-count risk with other bone-marrow-suppressing medications (such as hydroxyurea or mycophenolate).
Avoid live vaccines while on this medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for unusual bleeding, severe abdominal pain, or signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled CBC and liver function tests, especially early in therapy.
Keep scheduled skin cancer screening with long-term use.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your transplant team or prescriber about a missed dose rather than guessing - do not double up.

description: Suppresses the immune system to help prevent organ transplant rejection by blocking a cell-signaling pathway (mTOR).
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on blood trough drug levels and transplant type, and is set and adjusted by your transplant team - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed. This is a narrow-therapeutic-index medication requiring regular blood level checks.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, for as long as the transplanted organ needs immunosuppression.
directions_for_use: Take consistently either always with or always without food, as directed by your transplant team.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice at all times - it significantly raises drug levels.
If also taking cyclosporine, take sirolimus several hours apart from it exactly as instructed by your transplant team.
Do not crush tablets.
Tell any surgeon or dentist you take this medication before any procedure, due to effects on wound healing.
storage_instructions: Store as directed on the label (some formulations require refrigeration); protect from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat - seek care immediately
Signs of low blood counts: unusual bruising or bleeding
New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (possible lung toxicity)
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
Poor wound healing after any cut, surgery, or procedure
Signs of a blood clot: leg swelling/pain, sudden shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice entirely - large increase in drug levels.
Strong azole antifungals (such as fluconazole) significantly increase sirolimus levels - avoid or requires close monitoring/dose adjustment by your transplant team.
Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces sirolimus levels and raises rejection risk.
NSAIDs increase kidney injury risk when combined with sirolimus.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for new cough/shortness of breath, poor wound healing, or leg swelling.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood trough drug level checks exactly as instructed - this is critical due to the narrow therapeutic range.
Keep scheduled kidney function and cholesterol/triglyceride tests.
Keep all transplant clinic follow-up appointments.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your transplant team about a missed dose rather than guessing or doubling up - this medication has a narrow therapeutic range and dosing must be managed by your care team.

description: Blocks a cell-signaling pathway (mTOR) to either help prevent organ transplant rejection or slow the growth of certain cancers, depending on the reason it was prescribed.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on the reason for treatment (transplant rejection prevention or cancer treatment), blood trough levels, and lab values, and is set and adjusted by your transplant or oncology team - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing for transplant use; protocol-based duration for cancer treatment, as directed by your care team.
directions_for_use: Take consistently the same way relative to food each day, as directed.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
Do not crush or chew tablets unless specifically directed.
Tell any surgeon or dentist you take this medication before any procedure, due to effects on wound healing.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to everolimus or other mTOR inhibitors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat - seek care immediately
Severe mouth sores affecting eating or drinking
New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (possible lung inflammation)
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
Poor wound healing after any cut, surgery, or procedure
Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst/urination
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (such as fluconazole or clarithromycin) can significantly increase levels and toxicity - discuss any new prescription with your care team.
Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces levels and raises risk of rejection or reduced cancer control.
Monitor blood sugar closely if also taking metformin or glipizide, since everolimus can raise blood glucose.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever/signs of infection while on this medication, since low blood counts increase infection risk.
Seek care for new cough/shortness of breath, poor wound healing, or severe mouth sores.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood trough drug level checks if used for transplant.
Keep scheduled kidney function, blood glucose, and lipid panel tests.
Keep all clinic follow-up appointments and labs on schedule.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your transplant or oncology team about a missed dose rather than guessing or doubling up.

description: Blocks an enzyme (integrase) that HIV needs to multiply; used as part of a combination antiretroviral regimen to treat HIV infection.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on your specific antiretroviral regimen and is set by your HIV care provider - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as part of lifelong HIV treatment unless your provider changes the regimen.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day exactly as prescribed, as part of your combination regimen.

Separate from antacids or supplements containing calcium, iron, magnesium, or aluminum by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after - these significantly reduce absorption; taking with a calcium- or iron-containing meal is acceptable.
Do not skip doses or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with dofetilide (not applicable to drugs in this list, but relevant generally)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a rare but serious allergic/liver reaction: rash, fever, severe fatigue, yellowing skin/eyes - seek care immediately and stop the medication
New or worsening depression, anxiety, or thoughts of self-harm
Signs of liver problems: dark urine, abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly increases metformin blood levels, raising the risk of lactic acidosis - dose adjustment or closer monitoring of metformin is often needed; discuss with your prescriber before combining.
Calcium, iron, magnesium, and aluminum-containing antacids or supplements reduce dolutegravir absorption - separate dosing times as directed.
Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces dolutegravir levels and raises the risk of treatment failure and drug resistance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever, rash, or signs of liver problems - this can indicate a serious hypersensitivity reaction.
Report new mood changes to your HIV care provider.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Monitor blood glucose closely if also taking metformin.
Report new mood or sleep changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day. Do not skip or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider - missing doses can allow the virus to become resistant to treatment. Never take a break from antiretroviral therapy without medical guidance.

description: A two-drug combination tablet used as complete antiretroviral therapy to treat HIV infection in appropriate patients.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by your HIV care provider, typically one tablet once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as part of lifelong HIV treatment unless your provider changes the regimen.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day exactly as prescribed.
Separate from antacids or supplements containing calcium, iron, magnesium, or aluminum by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after.
Do not skip doses or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Hepatitis B co-infection without a concurrent hepatitis B treatment plan - stopping this medication can cause a severe hepatitis B flare
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a rare but serious allergic/liver reaction: rash, fever, severe fatigue, yellowing skin/eyes - seek care immediately
Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain with nausea/vomiting - seek care immediately
Worsening liver symptoms if hepatitis B co-infected, especially if this medication is stopped
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly increases metformin blood levels, raising the risk of lactic acidosis - discuss with your prescriber before combining.
Calcium, iron, magnesium, and aluminum-containing antacids or supplements reduce absorption - separate dosing times as directed.
Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces drug levels and raises the risk of treatment failure and drug resistance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever, rash, or signs of liver problems.
Never stop this medication abruptly if you have hepatitis B without your provider's guidance, due to flare risk.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Keep scheduled kidney function and, if applicable, hepatitis B monitoring.
Monitor blood glucose closely if also taking metformin.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day. Do not skip or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider - missing doses risks drug resistance, and stopping abruptly can cause a hepatitis B flare if co-infected.

description: A three-drug single-tablet regimen used as complete antiretroviral therapy to treat HIV infection.
dosage_forms: Tablet (abacavir 600 mg / dolutegravir 50 mg / lamivudine 300 mg)
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by your HIV care provider, typically one tablet once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as part of lifelong HIV treatment unless your provider changes the regimen.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day exactly as prescribed.
You must be tested for the HLA-B*5701 gene before starting - this identifies a high risk of a serious abacavir allergic reaction.
Separate from antacids or supplements containing calcium, iron, magnesium, or aluminum by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after.
Do not skip doses or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: HLA-B*5701-positive individuals (high risk of a serious, potentially fatal hypersensitivity reaction)
Hepatitis B co-infection without a concurrent treatment plan
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Abacavir hypersensitivity reaction: fever, rash, nausea, fatigue, or breathing symptoms - stop the medication and seek care immediately, and never restart it once this reaction is suspected, since restarting can be fatal
Signs of lactic acidosis or liver toxicity: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, yellowing skin/eyes
Signs of a rare but serious allergic reaction to dolutegravir: rash, fever, severe fatigue
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly increases metformin blood levels, raising the risk of lactic acidosis - discuss with your prescriber before combining.
Calcium, iron, magnesium, and aluminum-containing antacids or supplements reduce absorption - separate dosing times as directed.
Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces drug levels and raises the risk of treatment failure and drug resistance.
Limit alcohol - can increase abacavir levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately and stop the medication for fever, rash, or flu-like symptoms suggestive of a hypersensitivity reaction - do not restart without provider guidance.
Never stop this medication abruptly if you have hepatitis B without your provider's guidance, due to flare risk.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Keep scheduled liver function tests.
Monitor blood glucose closely if also taking metformin.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day. Do not skip or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider - missing doses risks drug resistance. If this medication is ever stopped due to a suspected allergic reaction, do not restart it without your provider's explicit guidance.

drug_class: Antiretroviral combination (integrase inhibitor + booster + 2 NRTIs, HIV)
description: A four-drug single-tablet regimen, including a booster (cobicistat) that raises blood levels of the other components, used as complete antiretroviral therapy to treat HIV infection.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by your HIV care provider, typically one tablet once daily with food - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as part of lifelong HIV treatment unless your provider changes the regimen.
directions_for_use: Take with food - this improves absorption.
Take at the same time every day.
Do not skip doses or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider.
Separate from antacids containing aluminum/magnesium by at least 2 hours.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Hepatitis B co-infection without a concurrent treatment plan - stopping can cause a severe hepatitis B flare
Concurrent use with many other drugs that depend on the same liver enzyme (CYP3A4) due to the cobicistat booster - review all medications with your HIV care provider and pharmacist
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of lactic acidosis or liver toxicity: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, yellowing skin/eyes - seek care immediately
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
Worsening liver symptoms if hepatitis B co-infected, especially if this medication is stopped
New or worsening bone pain (bone density loss with long-term use)
otc_and_other_interactions: The cobicistat booster is a strong inhibitor of drug-metabolizing enzymes and significantly raises levels of many medications: do not combine with simvastatin (major muscle toxicity/rhabdomyolysis risk) - a different statin at a reduced dose may be used instead per your prescriber.
Significantly increases sildenafil levels - dose reduction and caution are needed if combined.
Significantly increases alprazolam levels, raising sedation risk.
Avoid St. John's Wort - drastically reduces drug levels and raises the risk of treatment failure and resistance.
Significantly increases metformin levels - discuss with your prescriber before combining.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for signs of lactic acidosis, liver problems, or kidney problems.
Never stop this medication abruptly if you have hepatitis B without your provider's guidance.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Keep scheduled kidney function tests.
Keep scheduled bone density monitoring with long-term use.
Keep scheduled liver function tests.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day with food, unless it is close to the next dose. Do not skip or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider - missing doses risks drug resistance.

description: A three-drug single-tablet regimen used as complete antiretroviral therapy to treat HIV infection.
dosage_forms: Tablet (efavirenz 600 mg / emtricitabine 200 mg / tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg)
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by your HIV care provider, typically one tablet once daily at bedtime - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as part of lifelong HIV treatment unless your provider changes the regimen.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, preferably at bedtime - this reduces central nervous system side effects such as vivid dreams and dizziness.
Avoid high-fat meals around dosing time, since they can increase absorption to excessive levels.
Do not skip doses or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Hepatitis B co-infection without a concurrent treatment plan
Concurrent use with St. John's Wort (significantly reduces effectiveness)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening depression, anxiety, confusion, or thoughts of self-harm - seek care promptly
Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe rash or blistering skin reaction
Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not use St. John's Wort with this medication - it significantly reduces efavirenz levels, which can lead to treatment failure and drug resistance.

Strong inducer of drug-metabolizing enzymes - reduces the effectiveness of statins (simvastatin, atorvastatin), hormonal contraceptives, and other medications; discuss all medications with your HIV care provider.
Use caution with sedatives such as alprazolam due to additive central nervous system effects and altered drug levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for new mood changes, depression, or thoughts of self-harm.
Seek care for signs of liver problems or a severe rash.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Keep scheduled liver and kidney function tests.
Monitor mental health/mood, especially early in treatment.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day, ideally still at bedtime and away from a high-fat meal. Do not skip or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider - missing doses risks drug resistance.

description: Blocks the integrase enzyme HIV needs to multiply; used as part of a combination antiretroviral regimen to treat HIV infection.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by your HIV care provider, typically taken twice daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as part of lifelong HIV treatment unless your provider changes the regimen.
directions_for_use: Take twice daily at evenly spaced times, with or without food.
Do not skip doses or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe rash or blistering skin reaction (rare Stevens-Johnson syndrome) - seek care immediately
Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness (rare muscle toxicity)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
New or worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm
otc_and_other_interactions: Antacids containing aluminum or magnesium can reduce raltegravir absorption - separate dosing times if these are used.
Use caution with other muscle-toxic medications such as statins - report new muscle pain or weakness promptly.
Avoid St. John's Wort - may reduce raltegravir levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for a severe rash or muscle pain/weakness.
Seek care for signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Report muscle pain or weakness promptly.
Keep scheduled liver function tests.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose. Do not skip or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider - missing doses risks drug resistance.

description: Blocks an enzyme (protease) HIV needs to make new virus copies; usually given together with a boosting agent (ritonavir or cobicistat), as part of a combination antiretroviral regimen.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by your HIV care provider, and must be taken together with the prescribed booster medication (ritonavir or cobicistat) - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as part of lifelong HIV treatment unless your provider changes the regimen.
directions_for_use: Take with food - this significantly improves absorption.
Take exactly together with the prescribed booster medication (ritonavir or cobicistat) - never take darunavir without its booster.
Do not skip doses or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Use caution with a history of severe sulfa allergy (darunavir contains a sulfonamide component)
Concurrent use with many other drugs that depend on the same liver enzyme (CYP3A4) due to the booster - review all medications with your HIV care provider and pharmacist
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, especially with hepatitis B or C co-infection - seek care promptly
Severe skin reaction or rash (rare, can be serious) - seek care immediately
Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst/urination
Signs of a sulfa allergy reaction if applicable
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not combine with simvastatin or lovastatin - major risk of severe muscle toxicity (rhabdomyolysis); a different statin at a reduced dose (such as pravastatin or rosuvastatin) may be used instead per your prescriber.
Significantly increases sildenafil levels - dose reduction and caution are needed if combined.
Significantly increases alprazolam levels, raising sedation risk - use the lowest effective dose cautiously if combined.
Avoid St. John's Wort - drastically reduces darunavir levels and raises the risk of treatment failure and resistance.
May alter warfarin levels - closer INR monitoring is needed if combined.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for signs of liver problems or a severe rash.
Never stop darunavir or its booster medication separately without your provider's guidance.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Keep scheduled liver function, blood glucose, and lipid panel tests.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose, together with its booster medication, as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose. Do not skip or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider - missing doses risks drug resistance.

drug_class: Non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI, HIV antiretroviral)
description: Blocks an enzyme (reverse transcriptase) HIV needs to multiply; used as part of a combination antiretroviral regimen, typically for patients starting treatment with a lower viral load.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and set by your HIV care provider, typically one tablet once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as part of lifelong HIV treatment unless your provider changes the regimen.
directions_for_use: Take with a normal meal - absorption is significantly reduced if taken on an empty stomach or with only a protein drink.
Do not skip doses or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with proton pump inhibitors (such as omeprazole) - this combination is contraindicated because it drastically reduces rilpivirine absorption
High pretreatment viral load (an alternative regimen is generally chosen by the provider in this situation)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening depression, anxiety, or thoughts of self-harm - seek care promptly
Signs of liver toxicity: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe rash or allergic reaction
Palpitations or fainting (heart rhythm changes, more likely at higher-than-approved doses)
otc_and_other_interactions: CONTRAINDICATED with proton pump inhibitors such as omeprazole - drastically reduces absorption and risks treatment failure.
If an H2 blocker is needed, it must be taken 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine.
Antacids must be separated by at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine.
Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces levels and risks treatment failure/resistance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for new mood changes or thoughts of self-harm.
Seek care for signs of liver problems or a severe rash.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Monitor mood/depression symptoms.
Keep scheduled liver function tests.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and remembered within 12 hours, take it as soon as possible with food; if more than 12 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take the next dose with food at the regular time. Do not skip or stop this medication without talking to your HIV care provider - missing doses risks drug resistance.

description: Binds phosphate from food in the gut to lower blood phosphate levels in people with chronic kidney disease, especially those on dialysis.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on blood phosphate levels and is set and adjusted by your prescriber - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as long as needed to control phosphate levels.
directions_for_use: Take with meals - it will not work if taken between meals, since it needs to bind phosphate from food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
Take other oral medications at least 1 hour before or 3 hours after sevelamer, since it can bind and reduce their absorption.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe constipation or signs of bowel obstruction: no bowel movements, severe abdominal pain, vomiting - seek care promptly
Severe or worsening GI symptoms
otc_and_other_interactions: Can reduce absorption of ciprofloxacin, levothyroxine, and other oral medications if taken at the same time - separate dosing by several hours.
Review the timing of all your medications with your pharmacist, since sevelamer can broadly reduce absorption of drugs taken too close together.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for severe constipation, inability to have a bowel movement, or severe abdominal pain.
Contact your prescriber if stomach upset persists or worsens.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood phosphate level checks.
Keep scheduled calcium level checks.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and it is not taken with a meal or snack, skip it and take the next dose with your next meal as scheduled. Do not double the dose.

description: Binds excess potassium in the gut to lower blood potassium levels (hyperkalemia), often used in people with kidney disease or those taking certain heart/blood-pressure medications.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on blood potassium levels and is set and adjusted by your prescriber, typically once daily - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as long as needed to control potassium levels.
directions_for_use: Mix the powder with water and take with food once daily, exactly as directed.
Do not heat the mixture or take it dry.
Take other oral medications at least 3 hours before or 3 hours after patiromer, since it can bind and reduce their absorption.
storage_instructions: Store in the refrigerator; may be stored at room temperature for a limited time per the pharmacy label - check instructions and discard after the labeled date.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood magnesium: muscle cramps, weakness, irregular heartbeat - seek care
Severe constipation
Worsening swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces absorption of many oral medications, including levothyroxine and ciprofloxacin, if not properly time-separated (at least 3 hours apart) - review all medication timing with your pharmacist.
Often used alongside ACE inhibitors or ARBs (lisinopril, losartan) that can raise potassium - do not stop those medications without your prescriber's guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for muscle cramps, weakness, or irregular heartbeat (possible low magnesium).
Contact your prescriber for severe constipation.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood potassium and magnesium level checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the next dose at the regular scheduled time; do not double up. Contact your prescriber if you miss several doses in a row, since potassium levels may rise.

description: Binds excess potassium in the gut to treat high blood potassium (hyperkalemia).
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on blood potassium levels and is set and adjusted by your prescriber - often started with more frequent dosing, then reduced to a maintenance dose. Never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: May be used short-term to correct high potassium, or long-term as maintenance therapy, as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Mix with water and take exactly as directed, with or without food.
Separate other oral medications by at least 2 hours before or after, since this medication can reduce their absorption.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to sodium zirconium cyclosilicate
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening swelling (fluid retention, especially at higher doses) - report to prescriber
Signs of low blood potassium if overcorrected: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
Severe constipation
otc_and_other_interactions: Can reduce absorption of other oral medications if taken too close together - separate by at least 2 hours.
Often used with ACE inhibitors or ARBs (lisinopril, losartan) - do not stop those medications without your prescriber's guidance.
Contains sodium - discuss with your prescriber if you are also on a sodium-restricted diet.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for new or worsening swelling.
Seek care for muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood potassium level checks.
Watch for swelling or rapid weight gain.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the next dose as scheduled; do not double up. Contact your prescriber if several doses are missed.

description: An active form of vitamin D used to help control calcium and bone metabolism in people with chronic kidney disease or low parathyroid hormone levels.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on blood calcium, phosphate, and parathyroid hormone levels, and is set and adjusted by your prescriber - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as directed by your prescriber, with dose adjustments based on lab results.
directions_for_use: Take as directed, usually once daily.
Do not take extra vitamin D or calcium supplements without your prescriber's guidance, since this raises the risk of high blood calcium.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high calcium: nausea, vomiting, constipation, confusion, excessive thirst or urination, irregular heartbeat - seek care promptly
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid extra calcium-containing antacids or supplements (such as calcium carbonate) unless directed - raises risk of high blood calcium.
Use magnesium-containing antacids cautiously in kidney disease.
High blood calcium can increase the risk of side effects from certain heart medications - discuss your full medication list with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for confusion, irregular heartbeat, or persistent vomiting, which can signal high calcium.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood calcium, phosphate, and parathyroid hormone (PTH) level checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next dose; then skip it and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: Increases levels of a brain chemical (acetylcholine) involved in memory and thinking, used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease or Parkinson's disease dementia.
route: Oral or transdermal patch, depending on the product prescribed
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and started low, then slowly increased by the prescriber based on response and tolerability - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as directed by the prescriber.
directions_for_use: If taking capsules or solution, take with food to reduce nausea, in the morning and evening as directed.

If using the patch, apply to clean, dry, hairless skin on the back, chest, or upper arm; rotate application sites and do not reuse the same spot for at least 14 days; remove the old patch before applying a new one - never wear more than one patch at a time.
Wash hands after handling patches.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to rivastigmine or other carbamate derivatives
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe nausea, vomiting, or dehydration, especially when restarting after missed doses - seek care
Slow heart rate, dizziness, or fainting
Signs of GI bleeding: black/tarry stools, vomiting blood
Worsening of asthma or COPD symptoms
Seizure (rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid anticholinergic medications such as diphenhydramine - they directly oppose rivastigmine's effect and can worsen confusion.
May cause additive slow heart rate when combined with beta-blockers such as metoprolol - monitor pulse.
Increases stomach acid, raising GI bleeding risk when combined with NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) or aspirin.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for excessive nausea/vomiting, a very slow heart rate, or fainting.
Contact the prescriber before restarting after several missed doses.
self_monitoring: Watch for excessive nausea, vomiting, or unintended weight loss.
Monitor heart rate, especially if also taking a beta-blocker.
Caregivers should track cognitive and behavioral changes over time.
missed_dose_instructions: If more than a few doses in a row are missed, contact the prescriber before restarting rather than resuming the previous dose on your own - restarting at the prior dose after a gap can cause severe nausea and vomiting, and the prescriber may need to restart at a lower dose.

description: Increases levels of a brain chemical (acetylcholine) involved in memory and thinking, used to treat symptoms of mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's dementia.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and started low, then slowly increased by the prescriber based on response and tolerability - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as directed by the prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take with food, morning and evening for immediate-release forms, or once daily in the morning for extended-release capsules.
Drink adequate fluids while taking this medication.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Severe liver or kidney impairment (per prescriber assessment)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Slow heart rate, dizziness, or fainting - seek care
Severe nausea, vomiting, or dehydration, especially when restarting after missed doses
Signs of GI bleeding: black/tarry stools, vomiting blood
Seizure (rare)
Severe skin reaction (rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid anticholinergic medications such as diphenhydramine - they directly oppose galantamine's effect and can worsen confusion.
May cause additive slow heart rate when combined with beta-blockers such as metoprolol - monitor pulse.
Increases stomach acid, raising GI bleeding risk when combined with NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) or aspirin.

Contact the prescriber before restarting after several missed doses.

Monitor heart rate, especially if also taking a beta-blocker.
Caregivers should track cognitive and behavioral changes over time.
