description: A lab-made version of a hormone that stimulates the bone marrow to make red blood cells, used to treat anemia related to chronic kidney disease or certain cancer treatments.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on hemoglobin levels and body weight, and is set and adjusted by your prescriber based on regular lab monitoring - never adjust the dose yourself.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing for chronic kidney disease-related anemia, or for the duration of certain cancer treatments, as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Administered by injection as directed - may be given at a clinic/dialysis center or self-injected subcutaneously if trained to do so.
Do not shake the vial or prefilled syringe - shaking can deactivate the medication.
Let refrigerated medication warm slightly at room temperature before injecting, if instructed.
Rotate injection sites.
storage_instructions: Store in the refrigerator; do not freeze; protect from light.
contraindications: Known pure red cell aplasia caused by previous ESA therapy
Certain active cancers where increasing red blood cell mass is not appropriate, per oncology guidance
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath - seek emergency care (increased risk of clots, heart attack, and stroke)
Severe or sudden high blood pressure - seek urgent care
Seizure
Signs of a serious allergic reaction: rash, swelling, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased risk of blood clots when combined with lenalidomide, as sometimes used together in blood cancer treatment regimens - a clot-prevention plan is often needed per the oncology team.

Use caution with anticoagulants or antiplatelets (warfarin, apixaban, clopidogrel, aspirin) - not a direct drug interaction, but the combined clotting/bleeding risk should be monitored by your care team.
Effectiveness is reduced by iron deficiency - iron studies are often checked and iron supplementation may be needed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of a blood clot, severe high blood pressure, or a seizure.
Report new headaches or high blood pressure readings promptly.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled hemoglobin/hematocrit checks.
Monitor blood pressure regularly.
Keep scheduled iron studies.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber or dialysis/clinic team about a missed dose rather than making it up yourself, since dosing is individualized to lab results.

Keep scheduled iron studies.

description: Binds phosphate from food in the gut to lower blood phosphate in chronic kidney disease and also provides absorbable iron; used both as a phosphate binder and, in some patients, to treat iron deficiency anemia related to chronic kidney disease.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on blood phosphate or iron levels and is set and adjusted by your prescriber - never take a dose or schedule that differs from what was specifically prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term/ongoing, as long as needed to control phosphate or iron levels.
directions_for_use: Take with meals - it will not work as a phosphate binder if taken between meals.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
Take other oral medications at least 1 hour before or 3 hours after this medication, especially doxycycline and ciprofloxacin, since iron can significantly bind and reduce their absorption.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of iron overload with long-term high-dose use (rare) - monitor ferritin as scheduled
Severe constipation or signs of bowel obstruction: no bowel movements, severe abdominal pain, vomiting
Dark stools accompanied by severe abdominal pain (dark stools alone are expected with this medication)
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly reduces absorption of oral ciprofloxacin and other fluoroquinolone antibiotics, as well as levothyroxine and doxycycline, if taken together - separate dosing by several hours.
Avoid additional iron supplements unless directed - risk of iron overload.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for severe constipation, inability to have a bowel movement, or severe abdominal pain.
Contact your prescriber if stools remain unusually dark along with new abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood phosphate level checks.
Keep scheduled iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation).
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and not taken with a meal or snack, skip it and take the next dose with your next meal as scheduled. Do not double the dose.

description: A topical antiseptic solution used to help clean minor cuts, scrapes, and wounds and reduce the risk of infection.
typical_dosage: Apply a small amount directly to the affected area 1-3 times daily as needed for minor wound cleaning.
typical_duration: Short-term, occasional use for minor wound care; see a doctor if the wound does not improve within 7 days or shows signs of infection.
directions_for_use: Clean the wound area first if possible.
Apply a small amount directly onto the affected area; bubbling/foaming is normal and not a sign of a problem.
Rinse and pat the area dry after use.
For external use only.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original opaque (light-protective) container; discard if the solution no longer fizzes when applied, which indicates loss of potency.
contraindications: Do not use on deep or puncture wounds, serious burns, or animal bites without medical guidance
Do not apply to the eyes
Avoid prolonged, repeated use on the same wound (can delay healing)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling
Increased pain, redness, swelling, warmth, or pus at the wound site (possible infection)
Chemical burn or blistering with prolonged or repeated use
common_side_effects: Mild stinging or bubbling sensation at the site of application
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal topical use; avoid applying other topical antiseptics at the same time to the same area to reduce skin irritation.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and rinse the area with water if irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.
Seek medical care if signs of infection develop or the wound worsens.
self_monitoring: Check the wound daily for signs of healing versus infection.
Note any increased redness, swelling, warmth, or drainage.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for wound cleaning; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A topical antiseptic used to disinfect skin before minor procedures (such as injections) and to clean thermometers or minor skin surfaces; not intended for open wound cleaning.
typical_dosage: Apply to intact skin with a cotton ball or pad as needed to disinfect the surface before a minor procedure.
typical_duration: Occasional, as-needed use; not intended for ongoing daily use on the same area.
directions_for_use: Apply to intact (unbroken) skin only, using a cotton ball or gauze pad.
Allow the area to air dry before an injection or minor procedure.
Use in a well-ventilated area; avoid inhaling fumes.
Keep away from open flame - it is flammable.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in a tightly closed container away from heat, sparks, and open flame.
contraindications: Do not apply to open wounds, broken skin, or mucous membranes
Do not use near the eyes
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling
Chemical burn, blistering, or significant skin irritation
Signs of accidental ingestion or inhalation toxicity (confusion, difficulty breathing) - seek emergency care
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal topical use on intact skin; avoid combining with other flammable or irritating topical products on the same area.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and rinse the area with water if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
Seek emergency care for signs of ingestion or inhalation toxicity.
self_monitoring: Check treated skin for irritation, redness, or dryness with repeated use.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for skin disinfection; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A topical astringent stick used to stop minor bleeding from small nicks and cuts, such as shaving cuts.
typical_dosage: Moisten the tip and apply directly to the minor cut with gentle pressure for a few seconds as needed.
typical_duration: Single, occasional use per minor cut; see a doctor if bleeding does not stop within 10 minutes or the cut is large/deep.
directions_for_use: Wet the tip of the styptic pencil with water.
Apply directly to the bleeding nick or cut with light pressure.
Rinse the treated area after bleeding stops if desired.
Do not share the pencil between users (infection control).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in a dry place; keep the cap on between uses.
contraindications: Do not use on large, deep, or heavily bleeding wounds
Do not use on broken or irritated skin beyond the minor cut itself
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling
Bleeding that does not stop or worsens
Signs of infection at the site (increasing redness, pus, warmth)
common_side_effects: Temporary skin discoloration at the site
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal use; not intended for use in patients on blood thinners with more than trivial bleeding - seek direct pressure and medical advice instead.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use if irritation or allergic reaction occurs and rinse the area.
Seek medical care if bleeding does not stop or the wound appears infected.
self_monitoring: Confirm bleeding has stopped before resuming normal activity.
Watch the area for signs of infection over the following days.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for minor bleeding; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

brand_names: Generic OTC Sterile Saline Wound Wash
description: A sterile saltwater solution used to gently irrigate and cleanse minor wounds, cuts, and scrapes without stinging.
typical_dosage: Spray or pour directly onto the wound as needed to rinse away dirt and debris before dressing.
typical_duration: Short-term, as-needed use for wound cleaning; see a doctor if the wound does not improve within 7 days or shows signs of infection.
directions_for_use: Spray or irrigate directly onto the wound to flush away dirt and debris.
Pat the area dry with a clean cloth or gauze afterward.
Discard opened single-use containers after use if labeled as single-use.
For external use only.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep the nozzle/tip clean and avoid contamination between uses.
contraindications: Do not use on the eyes unless the product is specifically labeled as an eye wash
Known sensitivity to any listed ingredient
Do not use as a substitute for medical evaluation of deep or serious wounds
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling (uncommon)
Increased pain, redness, swelling, warmth, or pus at the wound site (possible infection)
common_side_effects: Generally well tolerated with minimal to no stinging
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant interactions expected with normal use; safe to use alongside most topical wound-care products such as antibiotic ointments.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
Seek medical care if signs of infection develop.
self_monitoring: Check the wound daily for signs of healing versus infection.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for wound cleaning; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A topical antifungal used to treat and prevent athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to the affected and surrounding skin twice daily.
typical_duration: Typically used for 2-4 weeks (athlete's foot may need up to 4-6 weeks); see a doctor if no improvement within 4 weeks.
directions_for_use: Wash and dry the affected area thoroughly before applying.
Apply a thin layer to the affected area and surrounding skin twice daily.
Continue using for the full recommended duration even if symptoms improve early.
Wash hands after application unless treating the hands.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from heat and open flame (sprays may be flammable).
contraindications: Do not use on broken, raw, or oozing skin without medical guidance
Not for use in children under 2 years without medical advice
Known sensitivity to tolnaftate or product ingredients
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, significant swelling
Worsening irritation, blistering, or spreading infection
common_side_effects: Mild stinging or irritation at the application site
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal topical use; minimal systemic absorption.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and wash the area if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
See a doctor if the infection worsens or does not improve after 4 weeks.
self_monitoring: Track improvement in itching, redness, and scaling.
Keep the area clean and dry between applications.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, apply as soon as remembered and resume the normal twice-daily schedule; do not double up.

description: A topical antifungal used to treat athlete's foot and help manage minor fungal nail and skin infections.
typical_dosage: Apply to the affected area(s) twice daily (morning and night).
typical_duration: Typically used for up to 4 weeks; see a doctor if no improvement within 4 weeks.
directions_for_use: Clean and dry the affected area before applying.
Apply a thin layer or use the applicator brush to cover the affected skin or nail twice daily.
Allow to dry before covering with socks or shoes.
Continue for the full recommended course.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, tightly closed, away from open flame.
contraindications: Do not use on broken, raw, or deeply cracked skin without medical guidance
Not for use in children under 2 years without medical advice
Known sensitivity to undecylenic acid or product ingredients
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, significant swelling
Worsening irritation, blistering, or spreading infection
common_side_effects: Mild burning or stinging at the application site
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal topical use; minimal systemic absorption.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and wash the area if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
See a doctor if the infection worsens or does not improve after 4 weeks.
self_monitoring: Track improvement in itching, redness, and scaling.
Keep feet clean, dry, and well-ventilated between applications.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, apply as soon as remembered and resume the normal twice-daily schedule; do not double up.

description: A medicated adhesive pad that softens and helps remove corns and calluses by breaking down thickened skin.
typical_dosage: Apply one pad directly over the corn or callus; replace every 48 hours as directed on the label.
typical_duration: Up to 14 days of use; see a doctor if the corn/callus does not improve or worsens.
directions_for_use: Wash and dry the foot before applying.
Center the medicated pad directly over the corn or callus, avoiding surrounding healthy skin.
Replace the pad every 48 hours as directed.
Soften and gently remove dead skin with a pumice stone between applications if directed on the label.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original packaging until ready to use.
contraindications: Do not use if diabetic or have poor circulation without a doctor's approval
Do not use on irritated, infected, or broken skin, moles, birthmarks, or warts with hair growing from them
Avoid contact with healthy surrounding skin, eyes, and mucous membranes
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling
Skin ulceration, significant pain, or signs of infection at the site
Signs of salicylate toxicity with excessive/improper use (ringing in ears, confusion) - rare with limited topical use
common_side_effects: Mild stinging at the application site
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant interactions expected with normal, limited use; avoid combining with other salicylate-containing topical products applied to the same or nearby skin, and use caution in patients on warfarin or other blood thinners if applying to large areas for prolonged periods.
action_if_adverse_effects: Remove the pad and wash the area if irritation, pain, or allergic reaction occurs.
See a doctor if the area becomes infected or does not improve.
self_monitoring: Check surrounding skin for irritation with each pad change.
People with diabetes should inspect feet daily for any skin changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Used on a pad-replacement schedule (about every 48 hours) rather than a dose schedule; if a pad change is missed, replace it as soon as remembered.

drug_class: Topical oral anesthetic (local anesthetic, ester type)
description: A topical numbing gel applied to the gums or mouth to temporarily relieve pain from toothaches, canker sores, minor dental irritation, or teething (age restrictions apply).
typical_dosage: Apply a small amount to the affected area up to 4 times daily as needed, not more often than every 4 hours.
typical_duration: Short-term, as-needed use; see a dentist/doctor if pain persists beyond 7 days.
directions_for_use: Apply a small amount directly to the affected gum or mouth tissue with a clean fingertip or cotton swab.
Do not exceed 4 applications per day.
Do not eat or chew gum immediately after application (numbing effect and risk of biting the cheek/tongue).
Not for use in children under 2 years old (FDA warning regarding methemoglobinemia).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tightly closed and out of reach of children.
contraindications: Known sensitivity to benzocaine or other 'caine' local anesthetics
Do not use for teething without consulting a pediatrician
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of methemoglobinemia: pale/gray/blue-colored skin, lips, or nail beds, shortness of breath, fatigue, rapid heart rate - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling of the mouth/throat, difficulty breathing
Persistent numbness or worsening pain
common_side_effects: Temporary numbness or tingling of the mouth/tongue
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive risk of methemoglobinemia when combined with other oxidizing drugs, including sulfa antibiotics such as sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim - use caution and avoid excessive or frequent application.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for bluish/gray skin discoloration or breathing difficulty (possible methemoglobinemia).
Stop use and seek care for signs of allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track pain relief and duration of numbness.
Watch for any unusual skin color changes, especially in children.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for pain relief; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: An anticavity mouth rinse used daily to help strengthen tooth enamel and reduce the risk of cavities.
typical_dosage: Rinse with 10 mL for 1 minute once daily, typically at bedtime, then spit out.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing daily use as part of routine dental hygiene.
directions_for_use: Swish 10 mL (or as directed) around the mouth for 1 minute.
Spit out completely - do not swallow.
Do not eat, drink, or rinse the mouth with water for 30 minutes after use.
Not for use in children under 6 years old unless directed by a dentist.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, tightly closed, out of reach of children.
contraindications: Children under 6 years of age (risk of swallowing and fluorosis)
Known sensitivity to fluoride or rinse ingredients
Do not use if unable to reliably spit out the rinse
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of fluoride overdose/ingestion (nausea, vomiting, stomach pain) - contact poison control if swallowed in large amounts
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, mouth swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal use; avoid using at the same time as other high-concentration fluoride products to prevent excess fluoride exposure.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and rinse the mouth with water if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
Contact poison control or seek care if a large amount is swallowed.
self_monitoring: Confirm the rinse is spit out fully, especially when used by children.
Report persistent mouth irritation to a dentist.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily rinse is missed, simply resume the normal schedule the next day; do not double the dose.

description: A diluted hydrogen peroxide solution used as a mouth rinse to help cleanse minor mouth irritations, such as canker sores or after minor dental procedures.
typical_dosage: Mix as directed on the label (often diluted with water), swish in the mouth for about 1 minute up to 4 times daily, then spit out.
typical_duration: Short-term use, no more than 7 days unless directed by a dentist/doctor.
directions_for_use: Dilute with water if not pre-diluted, per label instructions.
Swish in the mouth for about 1 minute.
Spit out completely - do not swallow.
Do not use full-strength (undiluted) hydrogen peroxide in the mouth.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original opaque container away from light; discard if the solution no longer fizzes.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, mouth or throat swelling
Worsening mouth pain, white patches, or signs of infection
Accidental swallowing of a large amount - contact poison control
common_side_effects: Mouth or tongue irritation with frequent use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal use; avoid combining with other oral antiseptic rinses at the same time to reduce irritation.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and rinse the mouth with plain water if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
Contact poison control or seek care if a significant amount is swallowed.
self_monitoring: Track improvement of mouth irritation; see a dentist if it persists beyond 7 days.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for mouth irritation; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A saliva-substitute product (rinse, spray, or gel) used to relieve dry mouth (xerostomia) by moisturizing and lubricating the mouth.
typical_dosage: Use as needed to relieve dry mouth symptoms, such as before meals, speaking, or at bedtime.
typical_duration: Can be used long-term as needed for chronic dry mouth; see a dentist/doctor if dry mouth is severe, persistent, or accompanied by mouth sores.
directions_for_use: Spray, swish, or apply gel to the mouth and tongue as needed.
For rinses, swish for about 1 minute and spit out or swallow per label instructions (many are safe to swallow in small amounts).
May be used before meals or speaking to ease dryness.
Follow product-specific instructions, as formulations vary (rinse vs. spray vs. gel).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, tightly closed.
contraindications: Known sensitivity to any product ingredient
Persistent or severe dry mouth should be evaluated by a dentist or doctor rather than managed with OTC products alone
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, mouth or throat swelling (uncommon)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal use; safe to use alongside most oral medications and other dental hygiene products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
self_monitoring: Track whether dry mouth symptoms improve; note any new mouth sores, which should be evaluated by a dentist.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for dry mouth relief; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: Ear drops that combine a mild analgesic (antipyrine) and a local anesthetic (benzocaine) to temporarily relieve minor ear pain and inflammation.
typical_dosage: Instill drops to fill the ear canal (typically 2-4 drops) up to 3 times daily as needed or as directed.
typical_duration: Short-term use only; see a doctor if ear pain persists beyond 48 hours or worsens.
directions_for_use: Warm the bottle slightly in the hand before use (cold drops can cause dizziness).
Tilt the head to the side and instill the directed number of drops into the ear canal.
Keep the head tilted or place a cotton plug in the ear for a few minutes after instilling.
Do not touch the dropper tip to the ear or any surface.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, tightly closed, away from light.
contraindications: Known sensitivity to benzocaine, antipyrine, or other 'caine' anesthetics
Discharge or drainage from the ear (may indicate perforation or infection requiring evaluation)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of methemoglobinemia: pale/gray/blue skin color, shortness of breath, fatigue - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, severe itching in or around the ear
Worsening ear pain, fever, or new drainage
common_side_effects: Temporary stinging or burning on instillation
Mild, brief dizziness if drops are cold
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive risk of methemoglobinemia when combined with other oxidizing drugs, including sulfa antibiotics such as sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim, though risk is low with limited otic use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of allergic reaction or methemoglobinemia.
See a doctor if pain worsens or new ear drainage develops.
self_monitoring: Track pain relief and duration.
Watch for new drainage, fever, or hearing changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for ear pain; if on a scheduled regimen, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

drug_class: Multi-symptom cold/flu combination (analgesic/antipyretic + cough suppressant + expectorant)
description: A combination product that relieves fever, body aches, cough, and chest congestion associated with the common cold or flu.
typical_dosage: Follow label directions; typically 1-2 doses every 4-6 hours as needed, not exceeding the maximum daily acetaminophen dose (usually 3000-4000 mg/day from all sources combined).
typical_duration: Short-term use, typically no more than 7 days for cough/cold symptoms or 3 days for fever, unless directed by a doctor.
directions_for_use: Read the label carefully to confirm the acetaminophen dose per serving and avoid double-dosing with other acetaminophen products.
Take with water; may be taken with or without food.
Do not take with alcohol.
Do not use with other cough/cold or fever products containing the same active ingredients.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture; keep liquid forms tightly capped.
contraindications: Taking an MAOI (e.g., phenelzine, selegiline) within the last 14 days
Known sensitivity to acetaminophen, dextromethorphan, or guaifenesin
Chronic alcohol use (increases risk of liver injury with acetaminophen)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing of the skin/eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual fatigue - seek care immediately
Signs of serotonin syndrome when combined with other serotonergic drugs: agitation, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity, tremor - seek emergency care
Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Contains acetaminophen - avoid combining with other acetaminophen-containing products (including hydrocodone/acetaminophen) to prevent exceeding the maximum daily dose and risking liver injury.
Chronic use with warfarin can increase bleeding risk (INR) - monitor closely if used regularly for more than a couple of days.
Dextromethorphan can cause serotonin syndrome when combined with MAOIs, tramadol, or SSRIs/SNRIs (e.g., sertraline, escitalopram) - avoid combination, especially with MAOIs.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek emergency care for signs of liver injury, serotonin syndrome, or severe allergic reaction.
Do not exceed labeled maximum daily dose or combine with other products containing the same ingredients.
self_monitoring: Track total daily acetaminophen intake from all sources.
Track symptom improvement; see a doctor if fever or cough does not improve within the labeled duration.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally used as needed for symptoms; if on a scheduled regimen, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: An antihistamine used to relieve sneezing, runny nose, itchy/watery eyes, and other symptoms of allergies or the common cold.
typical_dosage: 4 mg by mouth every 4-6 hours as needed, not to exceed 24 mg in 24 hours (adult dosing; lower for children per label).
typical_duration: Short-term or intermittent use for allergy/cold symptoms; see a doctor if symptoms persist beyond 7 days.
directions_for_use: Take by mouth with or without food.
Use caution when driving or operating machinery due to drowsiness.
Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
Do not exceed the labeled maximum daily dose.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture.
contraindications: Difficulty urinating due to an enlarged prostate (without medical guidance)
Known sensitivity to chlorpheniramine or other antihistamines
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
Confusion, difficulty urinating, or severe dizziness, especially in older adults
Rapid or irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation and CNS depression with alcohol, alprazolam, tramadol, hydrocodone/acetaminophen, gabapentin, and other sedating medications - use caution and avoid combining when possible.
Additive anticholinergic and sedative effects with other antihistamines (e.g., diphenhydramine) - avoid duplicate therapy.
MAOIs (phenelzine, selegiline) can intensify and prolong the anticholinergic and sedative effects of antihistamines - avoid combination.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of severe allergic reaction or significant confusion/urinary retention.
Contact a prescriber if sedation is excessive or symptoms do not improve.
self_monitoring: Track drowsiness level, especially before driving.
Older adults should monitor for confusion, dizziness, or falls.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for allergy/cold symptoms; if on a scheduled regimen, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: A topical antihistamine cream used to temporarily relieve itching and pain from minor skin irritations, insect bites, and rashes such as poison ivy.
typical_dosage: Apply to the affected area up to 3-4 times daily as needed.
typical_duration: Short-term use, generally no more than 7 days; see a doctor if the condition worsens or does not improve.
directions_for_use: Apply a thin layer to the affected area; do not apply to large areas of skin.
Avoid applying to broken, blistered, or oozing skin.
Wash hands after application unless treating the hands.
Do not use with a heating pad or occlusive bandage over the area.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture.
contraindications: Chickenpox or measles (avoid use without medical guidance)
Use on large areas of skin, deep or puncture wounds, or serious burns
Known sensitivity to diphenhydramine or other antihistamines
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, significant swelling, difficulty breathing
Signs of significant systemic absorption with heavy/prolonged use over large areas: confusion, severe drowsiness, rapid heartbeat - seek care
common_side_effects: Mild stinging or burning at the application site
otc_and_other_interactions: With heavy or prolonged use over large areas of skin, diphenhydramine can be absorbed systemically and add to sedation from oral sedating medications (e.g., oral diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, hydrocodone/acetaminophen) - avoid combining oral and topical diphenhydramine and use caution with other sedatives.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of allergic reaction or significant systemic sedation.
See a doctor if the rash or irritation worsens or does not improve.
self_monitoring: Limit the area of skin treated and the duration of use.
Watch for excessive drowsiness, especially in children or older adults.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for itching/irritation; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A balanced liquid nutrition drink providing calories, protein, vitamins, and minerals, used to supplement or replace meals for people with poor appetite or increased nutritional needs.
typical_dosage: 1-3 servings (bottles/cans) daily as a meal replacement or supplement, or as directed by a healthcare provider or dietitian.
typical_duration: Can be used short-term (illness recovery) or long-term for ongoing nutritional support, as directed.
directions_for_use: Shake well before opening.
Drink as a meal replacement or between meals as a supplement.
Refrigeration may improve taste but is not required for unopened containers.
Follow any specific guidance from a doctor or dietitian regarding frequency, especially for diabetes or kidney disease.
storage_instructions: Store unopened containers at room temperature; refrigerate opened containers and use within the time specified on the label (typically 24-48 hours).
contraindications: Galactosemia or known milk protein allergy (check specific product formulation)
Severe swallowing difficulty without appropriate texture modification (consult a doctor/speech therapist)
Certain metabolic or kidney conditions requiring restricted protein, electrolytes, or fluid without medical guidance
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling, difficulty breathing
Significant blood sugar changes in people with diabetes
Signs of fluid overload in people with kidney or heart failure (swelling, shortness of breath)
common_side_effects: Mild stomach upset or loose stools, especially if introduced quickly
otc_and_other_interactions: Contains vitamin K; large or inconsistent changes in intake can affect INR control in people taking warfarin - aim for consistent daily intake and inform the prescriber managing warfarin therapy.
Contains sugar/carbohydrates that can affect blood glucose in people using metformin, glipizide, or insulin - monitor blood sugar and choose a diabetes-specific formulation if advised by a provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of allergic reaction.
Contact a provider if blood sugar or fluid status becomes difficult to control.
self_monitoring: Track daily caloric/nutritional intake if used for weight management or illness recovery.
People with diabetes should monitor blood glucose after starting or changing intake.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as a dietary supplement rather than on a strict dosing schedule; simply resume normal intake if a serving is missed.

description: A naturally occurring compound taken as a dietary supplement, often used by people on statin therapy or for general antioxidant support, though evidence for benefit is limited.
typical_dosage: 30-200 mg by mouth once daily, or as directed on the product label.
typical_duration: Can be used long-term as a general supplement; discuss ongoing use with a prescriber, especially if taking warfarin.
directions_for_use: Take with a meal containing some fat to improve absorption.
Take at the same time each day for consistency.
Inform all prescribers and pharmacists about use of this supplement.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Known sensitivity to CoQ10 or product ingredients
Use caution and consult a prescriber if taking warfarin or other anticoagulants
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling (uncommon)
Signs of reduced anticoagulant effect in patients on warfarin (unexpected clotting/bruising changes) - report to prescriber
common_side_effects: Insomnia if taken late in the day
otc_and_other_interactions: May reduce the effectiveness of warfarin (structurally similar to vitamin K), potentially lowering INR and increasing clotting risk - use only with prescriber knowledge and closer INR monitoring.
No significant negative interaction with statins (atorvastatin, simvastatin); some patients use CoQ10 to help offset statin-related muscle discomfort, though evidence is limited.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and consult a prescriber if unusual bruising, bleeding, or clotting symptoms occur while on warfarin.
Stop use for signs of allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Patients on warfarin should have INR checked after starting, stopping, or changing the dose of CoQ10.
Report all supplement use to the pharmacist and prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A moisturizing cream containing ceramides used to hydrate skin and help restore and maintain the skin's natural protective barrier, often used for dry skin or eczema-prone skin.
typical_dosage: Apply to clean, dry (or slightly damp) skin once or twice daily, or as needed for dryness.
typical_duration: Can be used long-term as part of routine skin care.
directions_for_use: Apply to clean skin, ideally within a few minutes of bathing to lock in moisture.
Massage gently until absorbed.
Avoid applying to broken or actively infected skin unless directed by a doctor.
Reapply as needed throughout the day for dryness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from direct sunlight.
contraindications: Known sensitivity to any product ingredient
Do not apply to open wounds or actively infected skin without medical guidance
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, significant swelling (uncommon)
common_side_effects: Mild stinging on freshly irritated skin
Rare mild breakouts in acne-prone individuals depending on formulation
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected; safe to use alongside most other topical medications, though it should generally be applied after (not before) prescription topical treatments unless directed otherwise.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
self_monitoring: Track skin hydration and any new irritation or breakouts.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for skin moisturizing; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A topical product that helps protect the skin from sunburn and reduces the risk of skin cancer and premature skin aging caused by UV radiation.
typical_dosage: Apply generously to exposed skin 15-30 minutes before sun exposure; reapply at least every 2 hours and after swimming, sweating, or towel drying.
typical_duration: Used as needed with any sun exposure; ongoing use as part of routine skin protection.
directions_for_use: Apply generously to all exposed skin before going outdoors.
Reapply at least every 2 hours, and immediately after swimming or heavy sweating.
Use in combination with shade, protective clothing, and sunglasses for best protection.
Check the expiration date; sunscreen effectiveness declines over time.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; avoid extreme heat (e.g., a hot car), which can reduce effectiveness.
contraindications: Known sensitivity to sunscreen active ingredients (e.g., oxybenzone) or inactive ingredients
Do not apply to broken or irritated skin
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, significant swelling
Severe skin irritation or blistering (rare)
common_side_effects: Mild skin irritation or stinging, especially around the eyes
Occasional acne flare with heavier formulations
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal topical use; particularly useful (and often recommended) for patients taking photosensitizing medications such as sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim, ciprofloxacin, or tetracyclines, which increase sunburn risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and wash off if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
Seek care for a severe or worsening skin reaction.
self_monitoring: Reapply on schedule during prolonged sun exposure.
Watch for new skin irritation with a new product/formulation.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed with sun exposure; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss - simply reapply when next exposed.

description: A topical astringent used to relieve minor skin irritation, itching, and discomfort, commonly used for hemorrhoids, minor skin irritation, or as a soothing skin toner.
typical_dosage: Apply to the affected area up to 6 times daily as needed, or after each bowel movement if used for hemorrhoidal/anal itching.
typical_duration: Short-term or as-needed use; see a doctor if symptoms persist beyond 7 days.
directions_for_use: Clean and dry the area before applying.
Gently wipe or pat the pad/liquid onto the affected area.
Discard pads after single use; do not flush pads unless labeled flushable.
For external use only.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep the container or pad package closed between uses.
contraindications: Do not use on broken skin, deep wounds, or actively bleeding areas beyond minor hemorrhoidal irritation without medical guidance
Known sensitivity to witch hazel or product ingredients
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, significant swelling
Rectal bleeding that is new, heavy, or persistent - see a doctor
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal topical use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and rinse the area if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
See a doctor for new, heavy, or persistent rectal bleeding.
self_monitoring: Track symptom relief; note any bleeding, worsening pain, or lack of improvement.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for irritation; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A topical cream applied to the anal area to temporarily shrink swollen hemorrhoidal tissue and relieve associated pain, burning, and itching.
typical_dosage: Apply to the affected external area up to 4 times daily, such as morning, night, and after each bowel movement.
typical_duration: Short-term use, typically no more than 7 days; see a doctor if symptoms persist, bleeding occurs, or a lump or protrusion does not improve.
directions_for_use: Clean and dry the area gently before applying.
Apply a small amount externally to the affected area; use the applicator only if directed for internal use.
Wash hands before and after application.
Do not exceed the labeled maximum number of applications per day.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from excessive heat.
contraindications: Use with an MAOI (e.g., phenelzine, selegiline) - risk of severe hypertensive reaction
Uncontrolled high blood pressure, heart disease, or thyroid disease without medical guidance
Known sensitivity to phenylephrine, pramoxine, or product ingredients
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of hypertensive crisis: severe headache, chest pain, rapid heartbeat, vision changes - seek emergency care, especially if taking an MAOI
Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, significant swelling, difficulty breathing
Rectal bleeding, or a lump/mass that does not improve
common_side_effects: Mild burning or stinging on application
otc_and_other_interactions: Phenylephrine is a sympathomimetic; combining with MAOIs (phenelzine, selegiline transdermal) can cause a severe hypertensive crisis - avoid this combination entirely, similar to the caution with oral decongestants such as pseudoephedrine.

May reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect of antihypertensives (e.g., lisinopril, losartan, metoprolol, amlodipine) with more than minimal/occasional use - use the lowest effective amount for the shortest time.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of hypertensive crisis, especially if taking an MAOI.
Stop use and seek care for signs of severe allergic reaction or new/worsening rectal bleeding.
self_monitoring: Track symptom improvement; see a doctor if no improvement within 7 days.
Monitor blood pressure if using regularly and taking blood pressure medication.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for hemorrhoidal symptoms; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: An adsorbent supplement marketed for relief of gas and upset stomach; it is a different, medically supervised product/dose when used as an emergency antidote for poisoning.
typical_dosage: Follow label directions, typically 500-1000 mg by mouth as needed for gas/upset stomach, taken with a full glass of water.
typical_duration: Short-term, occasional use; see a doctor if gas or stomach upset is frequent or persistent.
directions_for_use: Take with a full glass of water.
Separate from all other oral medications, supplements, and vitamins by at least 2 hours (before or after) since activated charcoal can reduce their absorption.
Do not use as a substitute for emergency poisoning treatment without medical direction - call Poison Control or 911 for suspected poisoning.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in a tightly closed container away from moisture.
contraindications: Suspected bowel obstruction or decreased bowel motility
Not a substitute for professional treatment of suspected poisoning or overdose
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of bowel obstruction: severe abdominal pain, bloating, inability to pass stool or gas - seek care
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling (uncommon)
Black stools are expected and not a cause for concern on their own, but should not be confused with signs of GI bleeding if other symptoms are present
otc_and_other_interactions: Can significantly reduce the absorption and effectiveness of many oral medications, including levothyroxine, warfarin, acetaminophen, and most other oral drugs, if taken at or near the same time - always separate activated charcoal from other oral medications by at least 2 hours.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of bowel obstruction or allergic reaction.
Contact a pharmacist if unsure how to properly space other medications around charcoal use.
self_monitoring: Track timing of activated charcoal relative to other medications to ensure adequate spacing.
Report any severe abdominal pain or inability to pass stool/gas.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for gas/upset stomach; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: An enzyme supplement taken to help digest lactose (milk sugar) and reduce gas, bloating, and diarrhea in people with lactose intolerance.
typical_dosage: Take 1-2 tablets/caplets with the first bite of dairy food, or as directed on the label; dosing can be adjusted based on the amount of dairy consumed.
typical_duration: Used as needed with dairy consumption; can be used long-term for chronic lactose intolerance.
directions_for_use: Take with the first bite or sip of a dairy-containing food or beverage.
May take additional tablets for larger or higher-fat dairy meals per label guidance.
Chew chewable forms thoroughly before swallowing.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture.
contraindications: Known sensitivity to lactase enzyme or product ingredients
Not intended to treat milk protein allergy (different from lactose intolerance)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling (rare)
common_side_effects: Generally well tolerated; rare mild stomach upset
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected; lactase enzyme is not systemically absorbed and is safe to take alongside other medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use if an allergic reaction occurs.
self_monitoring: Track whether gas, bloating, or diarrhea improve with dairy consumption when taken as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed with dairy consumption; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss - simply take with the next dairy-containing meal.

description: A dietary supplement containing live beneficial bacteria used to support digestive health and may help reduce symptoms such as gas, bloating, or diarrhea in some people.
typical_dosage: 1 capsule (or as directed on the label) once daily, with or without food.
typical_duration: Can be used long-term for ongoing digestive support; discuss use with a doctor if being taken for a specific medical condition.
directions_for_use: Take once daily, generally with a meal to improve survival through stomach acid.
If also taking antibiotics, separate the probiotic dose from the antibiotic dose by at least 2 hours for best effectiveness.
Follow specific storage instructions (some products require refrigeration).
storage_instructions: Store as directed on the label - some formulations require refrigeration to keep bacteria viable, while others are shelf-stable at room temperature.
contraindications: Severely weakened immune system, critical illness, or central venous catheter without medical guidance (rare risk of bloodstream infection)
Known sensitivity to any product ingredient
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling (uncommon)
Fever or signs of infection in immunocompromised individuals - seek care promptly
common_side_effects: Mild gas or bloating, especially when first starting
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant harmful drug interactions expected; however, antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim) can reduce probiotic bacterial viability if taken at the same time - separate doses by at least 2 hours for best effect.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of allergic reaction.
Immunocompromised patients should contact a doctor promptly if fever or signs of infection develop while using probiotics.
self_monitoring: Track digestive symptom improvement over 1-2 weeks of consistent use.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A topical ointment applied to the chest, neck, or back to temporarily relieve cough and congestion symptoms associated with the common cold through its cooling, vapor-releasing action.
typical_dosage: Apply a thick layer to the chest, neck, and back up to 3 times daily as needed, especially before bedtime.
typical_duration: Short-term use during cold symptoms, typically up to 7 days; see a doctor if cough persists or worsens.
directions_for_use: Apply a thick layer to the chest, neck, and/or back - do not apply to the face, nostrils, or under the nose.
Do not cover with a tight bandage; loose clothing is fine.
Do not heat the product (e.g., in a microwave) or add to hot water for inhalation.
Not for use in children under 2 years old.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from heat and open flame.
contraindications: Application to the face, nostrils, broken skin, or wounds
Known sensitivity to menthol, camphor, or other ingredients
History of asthma without checking with a doctor first (strong vapors may trigger symptoms in some individuals)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, significant swelling
Signs of camphor toxicity if accidentally ingested: seizures, vomiting, confusion - seek emergency care immediately
Worsening cough or breathing difficulty
common_side_effects: Local skin irritation or burning sensation
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected with normal topical use; minimal systemic absorption when used as directed on intact skin.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and wash off if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
Seek emergency care immediately if the product is swallowed.
self_monitoring: Track cough and congestion symptom relief; see a doctor if symptoms do not improve or worsen.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for cold symptoms; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A topical cream used to temporarily relieve minor aches and pains of muscles and joints, such as from arthritis, backache, or strains.
typical_dosage: Apply to the affected area up to 3-4 times daily as needed.
typical_duration: Short-term or intermittent use; see a doctor if pain persists beyond 7 days or worsens.
directions_for_use: Apply to clean, dry, intact skin over the painful area.
Massage gently until absorbed.
Wash hands after application unless treating the hands.
Do not use with a heating pad or tight bandage over the treated area.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture.
contraindications: Known sensitivity or allergy to aspirin or other salicylates
Application to broken, irritated, or wounded skin
Use with a heating pad (increases absorption and risk of burns/toxicity)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, significant swelling, difficulty breathing
Signs of salicylate toxicity with excessive use: ringing in the ears, nausea, confusion, rapid breathing - seek care
common_side_effects: Mild skin irritation or warming/burning sensation
otc_and_other_interactions: Topical salicylate can be absorbed into the bloodstream, especially with extensive or prolonged use, and may add to the bleeding risk of warfarin or other blood thinners (e.g., apixaban, aspirin, clopidogrel) - use the smallest effective area and duration, and use extra caution in patients on anticoagulants.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and wash the area if irritation or allergic reaction occurs.
Seek care for signs of salicylate toxicity, especially with extensive use.
self_monitoring: Limit the area of skin treated and monitor for irritation.
Patients on blood thinners should watch for unusual bruising or bleeding.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for pain relief; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A thick, petrolatum-based ointment used to relieve dryness, burning, and irritation of the eyes, typically applied at bedtime due to temporary blurring of vision.
typical_dosage: Apply a small (about 1/4 inch) ribbon into the lower eyelid at bedtime, or as needed for eye dryness.
typical_duration: Can be used long-term as needed for dry eye symptoms; see an eye doctor if symptoms persist or worsen.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Pull down the lower eyelid and apply a small ribbon of ointment inside the lid.
Blink gently to spread the ointment; vision may be blurred temporarily, so use mainly at bedtime.
Do not touch the tip of the tube to the eye or any surface.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep the cap tightly closed and discard per label instructions after opening (commonly 3 months).
contraindications: Known sensitivity to petrolatum, mineral oil, or other ointment ingredients
Use with contact lenses unless the product specifically states it is safe for use with lenses
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: significant eye redness, swelling, itching
Eye pain, changes in vision, or persistent blurred vision that does not clear
Signs of eye infection: discharge, significant redness, light sensitivity
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected; when using other eye drops at the same time, apply this ointment last since it can slow the absorption of other eye medications applied afterward - space other eye drops at least 10 minutes before this ointment.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of allergic reaction or infection.
See an eye doctor for persistent vision changes or eye pain.
self_monitoring: Track dryness symptom relief and any vision changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for eye dryness; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A sterile isotonic solution used to rinse and flush the eyes to help remove loose foreign material, air pollutants, or other irritants, and to relieve minor eye irritation.
typical_dosage: Rinse the affected eye(s) with the solution as needed using the eyecup or by flushing directly, per label directions.
typical_duration: Short-term, as-needed use; see an eye doctor if irritation persists beyond 24-48 hours or vision changes occur.
directions_for_use: Tilt the head back and gently flush the eye with the solution, or use the provided eyecup per label instructions.
Blink several times during irrigation.
Do not touch the tip of the applicator to the eye or any surface.
Discard the eyecup or applicator per label instructions to avoid contamination.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; discard per the label's after-opening timeframe.
contraindications: Known sensitivity to any product ingredient
Do not use to treat a penetrating eye injury or chemical burn without seeking emergency care first
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, significant redness, discharge, or vision changes that do not improve after rinsing
Signs of a foreign object still present after irrigation
Chemical exposure to the eye - seek emergency care and continue rinsing with plain water/saline while awaiting care
common_side_effects: Mild, temporary stinging or blurred vision immediately after use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant drug interactions expected; safe to use before other eye drops or ointments as an initial rinse.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care if eye pain, redness, or vision changes persist after rinsing.
Seek emergency care for chemical exposure to the eye.
self_monitoring: Track whether irritation improves after use; note any vision changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Used as needed for eye irritation; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

generic_name: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine, bivalent prefusion F (RSVpreF)
drug_class: Vaccine (RSV prefusion F protein, bivalent, recombinant)
description: Helps protect adults 60 and older, and pregnant individuals (to protect infants after birth), against lower respiratory tract disease caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or other healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: One 0.5 mL intramuscular injection; timing individualized based on age, pregnancy status, and current CDC/ACIP recommendations.
typical_duration: One-time vaccination per current guidance; repeat dosing recommendations may change over time.
directions_for_use: Administered as a single injection in the upper arm by a pharmacist or healthcare provider.
Bring your vaccination record so timing with other vaccines (e.g., flu, COVID-19) can be coordinated.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled under refrigeration by the pharmacy/clinic; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) to a previous dose or any vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: difficulty breathing, swelling of face/throat, hives, rapid heartbeat - seek emergency care immediately
New weakness, tingling, or difficulty walking (Guillain-Barré-type symptoms reported rarely) - seek care promptly
common_side_effects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for injection site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated.
Tell the pharmacist about immunosuppressant use (e.g., prednisone, tacrolimus) as it may reduce the vaccine response.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your provider for new weakness/tingling after vaccination.
Report persistent or worsening injection site reactions to the pharmacy.
self_monitoring: Watch the injection site for a few days for worsening redness or swelling.
Monitor temperature if fever develops.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a one-time (or provider-scheduled) vaccination; contact the pharmacy or your provider to reschedule if a planned dose is missed.

generic_name: Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) conjugate vaccine
description: Protects infants and young children (and certain at-risk adults) against invasive disease caused by Haemophilus influenzae type b, including meningitis and epiglottitis.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or other healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: Series of doses per the routine childhood immunization schedule (typically at 2, 4, 6, and 12-15 months), or a single dose in certain at-risk adults per current guidelines.
typical_duration: Completed per the recommended immunization schedule.
directions_for_use: Administered as an injection in the thigh or upper arm by a healthcare provider.
Bring the vaccination record to each visit so the series stays on schedule.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled under refrigeration by the clinic/pharmacy; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or any vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
High fever or unusual, prolonged crying/fussiness in an infant
common_side_effects: Injection site redness, swelling, or tenderness
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; acetaminophen may be used for fever/discomfort per pediatrician guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Call the pediatrician for high fever or persistent inconsolable crying.
self_monitoring: Watch the injection site for a couple of days.
Track the immunization schedule to keep the series on time.
missed_dose_instructions: If a scheduled dose in the series is missed, contact the provider to resume the series as soon as possible - the series does not need to be restarted from the beginning.

generic_name: Tetanus toxoid, reduced diphtheria toxoid, and acellular pertussis vaccine (Tdap)
description: Protects against tetanus, diphtheria, and whooping cough (pertussis); recommended for adolescents, adults needing a booster, and during each pregnancy.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or other healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: One 0.5 mL intramuscular injection, with a booster (often Td or Tdap) recommended every 10 years or after certain wounds.
typical_duration: Booster typically every 10 years, or once each pregnancy.
directions_for_use: Administered as a single injection in the upper arm.
Tell the pharmacist if this is for wound care/tetanus prophylaxis, routine booster, or pregnancy.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled under refrigeration by the pharmacy/clinic; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or any component
Encephalopathy within 7 days of a previous pertussis-containing vaccine not attributable to another cause
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
High fever or significant arm swelling extending past the nearest joint
common_side_effects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Call your provider for high fever or marked arm swelling.
self_monitoring: Watch the injection site for a few days.
Keep a record of vaccination date for future booster timing.
missed_dose_instructions: This is typically a one-time booster or series dose; contact the pharmacy/provider to reschedule if a planned dose is missed.

drug_class: Vaccine (RSV prefusion F protein, adjuvanted, recombinant)
description: Helps protect adults 60 and older (and certain younger high-risk adults) against lower respiratory tract disease caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or other healthcare provider)
dosage_forms: Single-dose vial with adjuvant suspension, reconstituted for injection
typical_dosage: One 0.5 mL intramuscular injection; timing individualized per current CDC/ACIP recommendations.
typical_duration: One-time vaccination per current guidance; repeat dosing recommendations may change over time.
directions_for_use: Administered as a single injection in the upper arm by a pharmacist or healthcare provider.
Bring your vaccination record so timing with other vaccines can be coordinated.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled under refrigeration by the pharmacy/clinic; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or any vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: difficulty breathing, swelling of face/throat, hives, rapid heartbeat - seek emergency care immediately
New weakness, tingling, or difficulty walking (Guillain-Barré-type symptoms reported rarely) - seek care promptly
common_side_effects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for injection site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated.
Tell the pharmacist about immunosuppressant use (e.g., prednisone, tacrolimus) as it may reduce the vaccine response.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your provider for new weakness/tingling after vaccination.
self_monitoring: Watch the injection site for a few days for worsening redness or swelling.
Monitor temperature if fever develops.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a one-time (or provider-scheduled) vaccination; contact the pharmacy or your provider to reschedule if a planned dose is missed.

description: Protects against invasive meningococcal disease (meningitis, sepsis) caused by Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B; recommended for adolescents/young adults and certain high-risk individuals.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or other healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: 2-dose series given at least 1 month apart (schedule may differ for high-risk individuals); does not substitute for MenACWY vaccination.
typical_duration: Series completed per current ACIP guidance; booster timing individualized for ongoing risk.
directions_for_use: Administered as an injection in the upper arm.
Complete the full series on schedule for full protection.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled under refrigeration by the pharmacy/clinic; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or any vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
High fever or severe headache with stiff neck (evaluate promptly to distinguish from actual meningococcal disease)
common_side_effects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Call your provider for high fever, severe headache, or neck stiffness.
self_monitoring: Watch the injection site for a few days.
Track the 2-dose series schedule.
missed_dose_instructions: If the second dose in the series is delayed, get it as soon as possible - do not restart the series from the beginning.

description: A live attenuated tuberculosis vaccine used in select high-risk settings, and also instilled into the bladder by a urologist as immunotherapy for early-stage bladder cancer (non-muscle-invasive) to reduce recurrence.
route: Intradermal injection (TB prevention) or intravesical instillation via urinary catheter (bladder cancer immunotherapy, administered in a clinic setting)
dosage_forms: Lyophilized powder for reconstitution (injection or intravesical instillation)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist/urologist; bladder cancer regimens typically involve weekly instillations for 6 weeks (induction) with maintenance courses over 1-3 years.
typical_duration: Individualized per treatment plan; one-time for TB vaccination, multi-year for bladder cancer maintenance therapy.
directions_for_use: Administered only by a trained healthcare provider in a clinic setting.
For bladder instillation: follow post-procedure voiding and hygiene precautions given by your care team (e.g., sitting to urinate for 6 hours after, disinfecting the toilet with bleach solution).
storage_instructions: Stored and handled by the pharmacy/clinic as a hazardous biologic; not for home storage. As a live organism, it requires special handling precautions.
contraindications: Immunocompromised states (e.g., high-dose steroids, chemotherapy, HIV, on strong immunosuppressants) - live vaccine risk
Active urinary tract infection or gross hematuria (for intravesical use)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever above 103°F, chills, or symptoms of BCG sepsis (an infection from the live organism) - seek emergency care immediately
Blood in urine that is heavy/persistent, severe bladder pain, or inability to urinate (bladder use)
Signs of disseminated infection: persistent high fever, joint pain, cough
common_side_effects: Burning/urgency with urination and mild blood in urine (bladder use)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid concurrent antibiotics (especially fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin) around the time of bladder instillation, as they can inactivate the live BCG organism - follow your urology team's specific timing instructions.
Immunosuppressants (prednisone, methotrexate, tacrolimus) can blunt effectiveness and increase infection risk - discuss with your care team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for high fever, chills, or signs of systemic infection.
Contact your urologist for severe bladder pain or heavy bleeding.
Do not take antibiotics around treatment days unless directed by your care team.
self_monitoring: Track temperature after each instillation/injection.
Report urinary symptoms that worsen or persist beyond 48 hours.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your urologist or the clinic to reschedule a missed instillation/vaccination as soon as possible.

drug_class: Kinase inhibitor (ALK inhibitor) - oral targeted oncology therapy
description: Used to treat ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), either after surgery or for advanced/metastatic disease.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; taken with food, typically twice daily.
typical_duration: Ongoing as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take with food to improve absorption.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush.
Take at consistent times each day.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original container, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, right-upper abdominal pain - seek care promptly
New or worsening shortness of breath, cough, or fever (possible lung inflammation/pneumonitis) - seek care promptly
Muscle pain or weakness with dark urine (possible severe muscle injury)
Slow heart rate, dizziness, or fainting (bradycardia)
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole at higher doses, some antifungals) can raise blood levels and increase toxicity - report all new prescriptions to your specialty pharmacist.
St. John's Wort can significantly lower drug levels and reduce effectiveness - avoid.
Grapefruit and grapefruit juice may alter drug levels for many of these agents - ask your pharmacist about your specific medication.
Report use of acid-reducing medications (e.g., omeprazole) to your oncology team, as they may affect drug absorption for some agents in this class.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncology team promptly for new breathing symptoms, signs of liver problems, or muscle pain.
Do not stop or adjust the dose without your oncologist's guidance.
self_monitoring: Scheduled liver function tests and complete blood counts as ordered.
Report new bruising, bleeding, or unusual fatigue.
Watch for shortness of breath.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and it is more than 6 hours until the next dose, take it as soon as remembered; otherwise skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

drug_class: Kinase inhibitor (ALK inhibitor) - oral targeted oncology therapy
description: Used to treat ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; often started at a lower dose for the first 7 days, then increased if tolerated.
typical_duration: Ongoing as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, or fever - especially in the first week (possible early-onset lung inflammation) - seek care immediately
Very high blood pressure, severe headache, or vision changes
Slow heart rate, dizziness, or fainting (bradycardia)
Vision changes or blurred vision
Muscle pain or weakness with dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole at higher doses, some antifungals) can raise blood levels and increase toxicity - report all new prescriptions to your specialty pharmacist.
St. John's Wort can significantly lower drug levels and reduce effectiveness - avoid.
Grapefruit and grapefruit juice may alter drug levels for many of these agents - ask your pharmacist about your specific medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek prompt medical attention for new breathing problems, especially during the first week of treatment.
Contact your oncology team for any concerning new symptoms.
self_monitoring: Blood pressure checks as directed.
Scheduled liver function and CK (muscle enzyme) labs.
Eye exams if vision changes occur.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

drug_class: Kinase inhibitor (ROS1/NTRK inhibitor) - oral targeted oncology therapy
description: Used to treat ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer and certain NTRK gene fusion-positive solid tumors.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically once or twice daily with or without food.
typical_duration: Ongoing as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush.
Take at consistent times each day.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening shortness of breath, cough, or fever (possible lung inflammation)
Dizziness, confusion, changes in speech or coordination (nervous system effects)
Muscle pain or weakness with dark urine
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole at higher doses, some antifungals) can raise blood levels and increase toxicity - report all new prescriptions to your specialty pharmacist.
