self_monitoring: Monthly pregnancy testing if applicable (REMS program requirement).
Periodic hemoglobin/hematocrit and liver function checks.
Track weight for fluid retention.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered that day; if not remembered until the next day, skip the missed dose - do not double up.

description: Used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) to improve exercise capacity and delay clinical worsening.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; typically started at 62.5 mg twice daily and increased to a maintenance dose after 4 weeks.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Take twice daily, morning and evening, with or without food.
Only available through a restricted distribution program (REMS) due to liver toxicity and birth defect risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with cyclosporine or glyburide
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, nausea - seek care promptly (monthly liver tests required)
Rapid weight gain or swelling of legs/ankles
Signs of anemia: unusual fatigue, pale skin
otc_and_other_interactions: Effective contraception required due to birth defect risk; hormonal contraceptives alone may be less reliable due to drug interaction - discuss backup methods with your specialist.
Contraindicated with cyclosporine (large increase in bosentan levels) and glyburide (increased liver toxicity risk).
May reduce levels of warfarin and other CYP substrates - monitor INR closely if on warfarin.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your specialist promptly for signs of liver problems, swelling, or fatigue.
Keep all scheduled monthly liver function tests.
self_monitoring: Monthly liver function tests (REMS requirement).
Monthly pregnancy testing if applicable.
Periodic hemoglobin checks.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up.

description: Used with ritonavir and other antiretroviral medications to treat HIV-1 infection in treatment-experienced patients.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your HIV specialist; always given with low-dose ritonavir to boost levels, typically twice daily with food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of a complete antiretroviral regimen.
directions_for_use: Take with food.
Take exactly as prescribed with ritonavir - do not take tipranavir alone.
Do not skip doses; missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
storage_instructions: Store capsules in the refrigerator until dispensed, then may be kept at room temperature for a limited time per pharmacy label; oral solution requires refrigeration - do not freeze.
contraindications: Concurrent use with certain statins (e.g., simvastatin) due to severe interaction risk
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue - seek care promptly
Signs of intracranial bleeding: severe headache, confusion, weakness on one side (rare but serious, particularly with other risk factors)
Rash with fever or blistering (severe skin reaction)
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with simvastatin (greatly increased statin levels, rhabdomyolysis risk) - atorvastatin dose adjustments may be needed under specialist supervision.
Reduces the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives - use an additional barrier method.
St. John's Wort significantly reduces drug levels and can cause treatment failure/resistance - avoid.
Interacts with many other medications through CYP enzyme pathways - always check with your HIV pharmacist before starting anything new, including OTC products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your HIV specialist promptly for signs of liver problems or severe rash.
Do not stop this medication on your own - stopping can lead to drug resistance.
self_monitoring: Scheduled liver function tests and lipid panels.
Regular HIV viral load and CD4 count monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered with food and ritonavir; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. Never stop this medication without talking to your HIV specialist.

description: Used with other antiretroviral medications to treat HIV-1 infection.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your HIV specialist; typically once daily with food, often boosted with ritonavir or cobicistat.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of a complete antiretroviral regimen.
directions_for_use: Take with food to improve absorption.
Take at the same time each day.
Do not skip doses - missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with proton pump inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole) in treatment-naive patients - reduces atazanavir absorption significantly
Concurrent use with simvastatin or lovastatin
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Yellowing of the skin/eyes (jaundice is common and often expected/benign with this drug due to elevated bilirubin, but new severe abdominal pain or worsening jaundice should be reported)
Signs of irregular heartbeat: palpitations, dizziness, fainting (PR interval prolongation)
Signs of new or worsening diabetes
Signs of gallstones: severe right-upper abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole) - significantly reduces absorption and can cause treatment failure; if an acid reducer is truly needed, only famotidine at a specific separated dosing time as directed by your HIV specialist is generally used, and never a PPI.
Contraindicated with simvastatin/lovastatin due to markedly increased statin levels and rhabdomyolysis risk; atorvastatin may be used at a reduced, specialist-directed dose.
Reduces the effectiveness of some hormonal contraceptives - discuss additional contraception.
St. John's Wort significantly reduces drug levels - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your HIV specialist for palpitations, severe abdominal pain, or worsening jaundice.
Do not start any new OTC medication, especially antacids/acid reducers, without checking with your HIV pharmacist first.
self_monitoring: Regular HIV viral load and CD4 count monitoring.
Periodic liver function, bilirubin, and lipid panel checks.
ECG if you have risk factors for heart rhythm problems.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered with food; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. Never stop this medication without talking to your HIV specialist.

drug_class: Antiviral - nucleotide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor
description: Used to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adults with evidence of active liver disease.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; typically 10 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy; do not stop without your specialist's guidance, as stopping can cause a severe flare of hepatitis.
directions_for_use: Take once daily, with or without food.
Do not stop this medication suddenly - discuss any planned discontinuation with your specialist.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe fatigue, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain with rapid breathing (rare but serious lactic acidosis) - seek emergency care
Worsening liver function after stopping the drug (severe hepatitis flare) - contact your specialist promptly if the medication is stopped for any reason
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid other nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., prolonged NSAID use such as ibuprofen/naproxen) - can increase kidney toxicity risk.
Report all new medications to your specialist given kidney function considerations.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of lactic acidosis.
Contact your specialist immediately if you stop this medication for any reason, due to hepatitis flare risk.
self_monitoring: Scheduled kidney function tests and hepatitis B viral load monitoring.
Liver function tests as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up. Contact your specialist if you miss multiple doses.

drug_class: Antiviral - nucleoside analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor
description: Used to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adults and children with evidence of active viral replication.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; typically 0.5-1 mg once daily on an empty stomach.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy; do not stop without your specialist's guidance, as stopping can cause a severe flare of hepatitis.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach (at least 2 hours after a meal and 2 hours before the next meal).
Do not stop this medication suddenly.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe fatigue, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain with rapid breathing (rare but serious lactic acidosis) - seek emergency care
Worsening liver function after stopping the drug (severe hepatitis flare) - contact your specialist promptly if therapy is interrupted
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; report all new medications, especially other antivirals, to your specialist.
Alcohol may increase liver strain - discuss safe limits with your specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of lactic acidosis.
Contact your specialist immediately if this medication is stopped for any reason.
self_monitoring: Scheduled liver function tests and hepatitis B viral load monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on an empty stomach; if close to the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up. Contact your specialist if you miss multiple doses.

description: Used to treat and prevent Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) in patients who cannot tolerate other therapies, and to treat babesiosis.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically taken with food once or twice daily depending on indication.
typical_duration: Course length varies by indication - from a few weeks (babesiosis) to ongoing prophylaxis while immunocompromised.
directions_for_use: Take with a fatty meal to significantly improve absorption.
Shake the oral suspension well before each use.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; do not freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe rash, fever, or blistering (serious skin reaction)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Rifampin and certain other medications significantly reduce atovaquone levels - report all medications to your prescriber.
Take with food; absorption is poor on an empty stomach.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for severe rash or signs of liver problems.
Do not skip doses if using for infection prevention (prophylaxis).
self_monitoring: Complete the full course as directed.
Report new rash or fever.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose with food as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to prevent and treat malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum.
typical_dosage: For prevention: one tablet daily starting 1-2 days before travel, daily during travel, and for 7 days after returning. For treatment: individualized, set by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Prevention: for the duration of travel plus 7 days after return. Treatment: a short course (typically 3 days) as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day with food or a milky drink to improve absorption and reduce stomach upset.
For prevention, start before travel and continue for the full 7 days after leaving the malaria-risk area, even if you feel well.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to atovaquone or proguanil
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe rash, mouth sores, or blistering (rare severe skin reaction)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Fever or symptoms of malaria despite taking this medication - seek prompt medical evaluation
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not take with rifampin, which reduces effectiveness significantly.
Metoclopramide and tetracycline can reduce absorption/levels.
Take with food to reduce nausea and improve absorption.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for severe rash or persistent vomiting (which could prevent absorption and increase malaria risk).
Seek prompt care for fever during or after travel despite taking this medication.
self_monitoring: Complete the full prophylaxis course, including the 7 days after leaving the risk area.
Watch for fever for at least several weeks after travel.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if vomiting occurs within an hour of a dose, a repeat dose may be needed - contact your prescriber or pharmacist for guidance.

description: Used for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults.
route: Subcutaneous injection (self-administered with a prefilled pen/syringe)
typical_dosage: 70 mg or 140 mg injected subcutaneously once monthly, per your prescriber's direction.
typical_duration: Ongoing preventive therapy; your prescriber will periodically reassess whether it continues to help.
directions_for_use: Inject into the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm once monthly.
Allow the pen/syringe to reach room temperature (about 30 minutes) before injecting.
Rotate injection sites.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze. May be stored at room temperature for up to 7 days if needed. Protect from light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing, hives - can occur days after injection
Severe constipation with abdominal pain (rare but reported, sometimes requiring hospitalization)
New or worsening high blood pressure
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected.
Use a fiber supplement/stool softener and stay hydrated if constipation develops; report severe or worsening constipation to your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your prescriber for severe constipation or new high blood pressure.
self_monitoring: Keep a headache diary to track migraine frequency/severity.
Monitor blood pressure if you have hypertension risk factors.
Track bowel habits.
missed_dose_instructions: Give the missed dose as soon as remembered, then resume monthly dosing from that date; contact your prescriber with questions.

description: Used to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness due to narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea, or shift work disorder.
typical_dosage: 150-250 mg by mouth once daily in the morning (or 1 hour before a shift for shift work disorder).
typical_duration: Long-term as directed by your prescriber, with periodic reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take in the morning to avoid interfering with nighttime sleep.
May be taken with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to armodafinil or modafinil
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe rash, blistering, or mouth sores (rare but serious skin reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome) - seek care immediately
Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling, difficulty breathing
Chest pain, irregular heartbeat
New or worsening depression, anxiety, or thoughts of self-harm
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly reduces the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives (including combined oral contraceptives) - use an additional non-hormonal method during use and for one month after stopping.
Can alter levels of warfarin - monitor INR closely if used together.
May reduce the effectiveness of other CYP3A4-metabolized medications; check with your pharmacist before starting new prescriptions.
Avoid combining with other stimulants without medical guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care immediately for severe rash or signs of allergic reaction.
Contact your prescriber for chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or mood changes.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate periodically.
Track sleep quality and daytime alertness.
Report new skin rash immediately.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and it is still morning/well before bedtime, take it as soon as remembered; otherwise skip it to avoid interfering with sleep - do not double up.

description: Used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar I disorder (manic or mixed episodes), as sublingual tablets or a transdermal patch.
route: Sublingual (under the tongue) or transdermal patch
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; sublingual tablets typically twice daily, patch applied once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term maintenance therapy as directed by your prescriber.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling of face/tongue/throat, difficulty breathing/swallowing - seek emergency care immediately
High fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, irregular heartbeat/sweating (possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care
Uncontrollable muscle movements of the face/tongue/limbs (tardive dyskinesia)
New or worsening depression or suicidal thoughts (boxed warning in children/young adults)

Increased risk of low blood pressure/dizziness when combined with blood pressure medications (e.g., lisinopril, amlodipine, metoprolol).
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or neuroleptic malignant syndrome symptoms.
Contact your prescriber for uncontrollable movements or mood changes.
self_monitoring: Track weight, blood sugar, and cholesterol periodically.
Watch for and report abnormal movements.
Monitor mood, especially early in treatment.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next dose; then skip it - do not double up. For the patch, apply a new patch as soon as remembered and resume the daily replacement schedule.

description: Used to treat chorea associated with Huntington's disease and tardive dyskinesia in adults.

Swallow tablets whole; do not chew or crush.

Concurrent use with an MAOI, or within 14 days of stopping one
Concurrent use with tetrabenazine or valbenazine

High fever, muscle stiffness, confusion (possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome)
Signs of irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation)
Difficulty swallowing
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with other CNS depressants (diphenhydramine, alprazolam, opioids, alcohol).

Report new abnormal movements or worsening chorea.
Periodic ECG if risk factors for QT prolongation exist.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to treat major depressive disorder in adults, combining a rapid-acting NMDA receptor antagonist with a norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor.

Current or recent (within 14 days) use of an MAOI
Concurrent use with other bupropion-containing products

Signs of serotonin syndrome when combined with other serotonergic drugs: agitation, fast heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity

Significant increase in blood pressure or heart rate

Contact your prescriber promptly for mood changes, agitation, or signs of serotonin syndrome.
Do not stop abruptly without discussing with your prescriber.

Track mood, especially in the first weeks of treatment or after dose changes.
Avoid other OTC dextromethorphan products.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up or take extra tablets to make up for a missed dose.

description: Used with other medications to treat partial-onset (focal) seizures in adults and children.

Severe drowsiness, difficulty breathing, or extreme incoordination
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with other CNS depressants (diphenhydramine, alprazolam, opioids like tramadol/hydrocodone, alcohol).
Rifampin can significantly reduce brivaracetam levels - report use to your neurologist.
Use caution with other seizure-threshold-lowering medications.

Seek care for severe rash, fever, or breathing difficulty.
Never stop this medication abruptly.

Track mood and behavior changes.
Avoid driving until seizure control is established and you know how the medication affects you.

description: Used to treat hyperprolactinemia (elevated prolactin), Parkinson's disease, acromegaly, and (as Cycloset) to improve blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes.

Contact your prescriber for new compulsive behaviors or persistent dizziness.

Prolactin level monitoring if used for hyperprolactinemia.
Blood sugar monitoring if used for diabetes (Cycloset).

description: Used to treat Parkinson's disease symptoms and to control drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms (e.g., muscle stiffness, tremor) caused by antipsychotic medications.

Contact your prescriber for confusion, hallucinations, or severe constipation.

Older adults and caregivers should monitor for confusion or memory changes.
Stay cool and hydrated in hot weather.

description: Used to treat Parkinson's disease and drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms, and to treat levodopa-induced dyskinesia.

Swelling of the legs/ankles or a lace-like purplish skin discoloration (livedo reticularis)

Sudden worsening of Parkinson's symptoms with fever/confusion after stopping the medication

Use caution with other dopaminergic medications; report all Parkinson's medications to your pharmacist.

Track mental status changes, especially in older adults.
Kidney function monitoring (dose is renally adjusted).

description: Used to treat symptoms of depression, including depression accompanied by anxiety or agitation.

Acute recovery phase after a heart attack

Periodic ECG if you have cardiac risk factors.
Report any abnormal involuntary movements.
