description: Used to treat hyperprolactinemia (elevated prolactin levels), including prolactin-secreting pituitary tumors.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically 0.25-1 mg taken twice weekly.
typical_duration: Long-term as directed, with periodic reassessment and prolactin level checks; some patients can eventually taper off under supervision.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce nausea.
Take on the same two days each week as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Shortness of breath, chest pain, or swelling of legs (rare heart valve or lung fibrosis effects with long-term/high-dose use)
Severe headache, vision changes, or fainting
New compulsive behaviors (gambling, hypersexuality) - report to your prescriber
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive low blood pressure effects with blood pressure medications (lisinopril, losartan, amlodipine, metoprolol).
Avoid combining with other ergot derivatives.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for shortness of breath, chest pain, or swelling.
Report new compulsive behaviors.
self_monitoring: Periodic prolactin level checks.
Echocardiogram monitoring may be recommended with long-term, higher-dose use.
Blood pressure checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered with food; if close to the next scheduled dose, skip it - do not double up.

description: Used along with other antiemetic medications to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy or surgery.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically a 3-day regimen (e.g., 125 mg on day 1, 80 mg on days 2 and 3) around each chemotherapy cycle, combined with other antiemetics.
typical_duration: Short courses taken around each chemotherapy cycle, or a single dose before surgery.
directions_for_use: Take exactly on the schedule provided by your oncology team, typically starting about an hour before chemotherapy.
May be taken with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with pimozide (significant interaction risk)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Severe fatigue or signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives - use an additional non-hormonal method during the treatment cycle and for one month after.
Can affect warfarin levels - INR should be monitored closely around each treatment cycle.
Interacts with many CYP3A4-metabolized medications; check with your oncology pharmacist before taking any new medication, including OTC products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncology team for severe or persistent side effects, or if nausea/vomiting is not controlled.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track nausea/vomiting control and report if inadequate.
INR monitoring if also on warfarin.
missed_dose_instructions: This is taken on a specific schedule around chemotherapy - contact your oncology pharmacy if a dose is missed rather than guessing on timing.

drug_class: Fumarate (Nrf2 pathway activator) - disease-modifying therapy for multiple sclerosis
description: Used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your neurologist; typically started at a lower dose and increased after 7 days to a twice-daily maintenance dose, taken with food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your neurologist.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce flushing and stomach upset.
Swallow capsules whole; do not crush, chew, or open them or sprinkle on food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to monomethyl fumarate or dimethyl fumarate
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection, especially unusual/prolonged infections (rare risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, a serious brain infection) - report new confusion, weakness, vision changes, or personality changes immediately
Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling, difficulty breathing, hives
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe or persistent abdominal pain (rare bowel-related events)
otc_and_other_interactions: Taking non-enteric-coated aspirin about 30 minutes before a dose (if approved by your neurologist) may reduce flushing.
Additive risk of low white blood cell counts with other immunosuppressants (e.g., methotrexate) - report all medications to your neurologist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your neurologist promptly for new neurologic symptoms, confusion, or vision changes.
Report persistent abdominal pain or signs of infection.
self_monitoring: Scheduled complete blood counts (white blood cell counts) and liver function tests.
Watch for and report any new or unusual neurologic symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up unless directed by your neurologist.

description: A rescue inhaler combining a short-acting bronchodilator with an inhaled corticosteroid, used as-needed for quick relief of asthma symptoms and to reduce the risk of asthma exacerbations.
typical_dosage: 2 inhalations as needed for symptoms, not to exceed the maximum daily inhalations directed by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Used as-needed on an ongoing basis for asthma symptom relief, alongside any prescribed maintenance therapy.
directions_for_use: Shake well before each use.
Use a spacer if directed to improve delivery.
Rinse mouth with water after use to reduce oral thrush risk from the inhaled steroid component.
Carry with you at all times for quick relief.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; avoid extreme heat or freezing. Do not puncture or expose to flame.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to albuterol or budesonide
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening shortness of breath despite use, or needing to use it much more often than usual - seek prompt medical evaluation, asthma may be worsening
Chest pain or rapid/irregular heartbeat
Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling, hives, difficulty breathing (paradoxical bronchospasm)
common_side_effects: Oral thrush/hoarseness (rinse mouth after use to reduce risk)
otc_and_other_interactions: Beta-blockers (e.g., metoprolol) can blunt the effect of the albuterol component and worsen bronchospasm.
Other stimulant-containing OTC decongestants (e.g., pseudoephedrine) may increase heart rate/jitteriness when combined.
Increased risk of low potassium when combined with diuretics.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe difficulty breathing or chest pain.
Contact your prescriber if you are needing this rescue inhaler more often than usual - this signals your asthma may not be well controlled.
self_monitoring: Track how often the rescue inhaler is needed and report increased use to your prescriber.
Rinse mouth after each use.
Know how to recognize worsening asthma symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a rescue/as-needed inhaler, not a scheduled medication - use it when needed for symptoms per your asthma action plan.

description: Used as a long-term, twice-daily maintenance nebulizer treatment for bronchospasm associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
typical_dosage: One 15 mcg vial nebulized twice daily (morning and evening), about 12 hours apart.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing maintenance therapy; not for acute rescue use.
directions_for_use: This is a maintenance medication - use on a fixed twice-daily schedule, not as a rescue inhaler for sudden symptoms.
Use only with a nebulizer as directed; do not mix with other medications in the nebulizer unless approved.
Keep a fast-acting rescue inhaler (e.g., albuterol) on hand for sudden symptoms.
storage_instructions: Store vials in the refrigerator or at room temperature per pharmacy label, protected from light; use each vial immediately after opening the foil pouch and discard unused solution.
contraindications: Use as monotherapy for asthma without a concurrent inhaled corticosteroid (boxed warning - increased risk of asthma-related death)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat
Worsening breathing symptoms despite use - this is not a rescue medication; use your rescue inhaler and seek care
Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling, hives, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Beta-blockers (metoprolol) can blunt effectiveness and worsen bronchospasm.
Diuretics may increase risk of low potassium when combined.
Other sympathomimetic decongestants (pseudoephedrine) may increase heart rate/jitteriness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain or severe difficulty breathing.
Contact your prescriber if symptoms worsen despite regular use.
self_monitoring: Track symptom control and rescue inhaler use.
Monitor heart rate if you notice palpitations.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not use more than 2 doses (30 mcg) in 24 hours.

description: Used as a once-daily maintenance treatment to control and prevent asthma symptoms.
typical_dosage: 1 inhalation once daily, at the same time each day.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing maintenance therapy; not for acute rescue use.
directions_for_use: This is a maintenance medication - it does not relieve sudden symptoms; keep a rescue inhaler (e.g., albuterol) on hand.
Rinse mouth with water (do not swallow) after each use to reduce the risk of oral thrush/hoarseness.
Do not shake the inhaler before use.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, keep the cover closed when not in use, and protect from moisture.
contraindications: Primary treatment of status asthmaticus or other acute asthma episodes requiring intensive measures
Known hypersensitivity to fluticasone furoate or milk proteins (dry powder inhalers may contain lactose)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening breathing symptoms or need for more frequent rescue inhaler use - seek prompt evaluation
Vision changes (risk of glaucoma/cataracts with long-term use)
Signs of adrenal suppression: unusual fatigue, weakness, especially when stopping or during illness/stress
Signs of pneumonia in patients with COPD (if used off-label): fever, increased mucus, worsening cough
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can increase systemic corticosteroid exposure and side effects - report all new prescription medications to your pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber if asthma symptoms worsen or your rescue inhaler use increases.
Report vision changes for an eye exam.
self_monitoring: Rinse mouth after each use and check for oral thrush.
Track frequency of rescue inhaler use.
Periodic eye exams with long-term use.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used as a twice-daily maintenance treatment for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) to reduce exacerbations and improve breathing.
typical_dosage: 2 inhalations twice daily, about 12 hours apart.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing maintenance therapy; not for acute rescue use.
directions_for_use: Shake well before each use.
This is a maintenance medication - keep a fast-acting rescue inhaler on hand for sudden symptoms.
Rinse mouth with water after use to reduce oral thrush risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; avoid extreme heat or freezing. Do not puncture or expose to flame.
contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma or urinary retention (due to the anticholinergic/glycopyrrolate component - use with caution)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening shortness of breath, chest tightness, or needing more rescue inhaler use than usual
Chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat
Eye pain, blurred vision, or halos around lights (possible narrow-angle glaucoma)
Difficulty urinating
Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling, hives, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive anticholinergic effects with diphenhydramine (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation), especially in older adults.
Beta-blockers (metoprolol) may blunt the bronchodilator effect.
Increased risk of low potassium when combined with diuretics.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe difficulty breathing, chest pain, or eye pain with vision changes.
Contact your prescriber if your rescue inhaler use increases.
self_monitoring: Track symptom control and rescue inhaler frequency.
Rinse mouth after each use.
Report urinary difficulty.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up (do not take more than 2 inhalations twice daily).

description: A long-acting injectable form of aripiprazole used to treat schizophrenia in adults. Aristada Initio is a single-dose formulation used to help start therapy quickly, alongside the first dose of regular Aristada and a short course of oral aripiprazole.
route: Intramuscular injection, administered by a healthcare provider (gluteal or deltoid muscle)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically given once every 4, 6, or 8 weeks depending on the specific dose/formulation used.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing maintenance therapy as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Administered only by a trained healthcare provider - do not self-inject.
Keep all scheduled injection appointments; do not let doses lapse beyond the recommended window.
A short course of oral aripiprazole is often required when starting therapy - take exactly as directed.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled by the pharmacy/clinic under refrigeration or controlled room temperature; not for home storage.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: High fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, irregular heartbeat/sweating (possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care
Uncontrollable muscle movements of the face/tongue/limbs (tardive dyskinesia)
New or worsening depression or suicidal thoughts
Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst/urination
Difficulty controlling body temperature in hot weather
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with alcohol, opioids (tramadol, hydrocodone/acetaminophen), and benzodiazepines (alprazolam).
Strong CYP2D6/3A4 inhibitors or inducers can significantly affect levels - report all new prescription and OTC medications to your pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for symptoms of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
Contact your prescriber for abnormal movements or mood changes.
self_monitoring: Track weight, blood sugar, and cholesterol periodically.
Keep all scheduled injection visits.
Report abnormal movements.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber's office promptly to reschedule if an injection appointment is missed - going too long without a dose can reduce effectiveness and may require restarting an oral supplementation course.

description: Used to treat severe psoriasis in adults.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your dermatologist; typically 25-50 mg once daily with the main meal.
typical_duration: Individualized, set by your dermatologist; often continued for months with periodic reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take with food (a meal containing fat improves absorption).
Effective contraception is required starting 1 month before treatment, during treatment, and for 3 YEARS after stopping due to prolonged teratogenic risk.
Avoid donating blood during treatment and for 3 years after stopping.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy or plans to become pregnant within 3 years of stopping (severe birth defect risk)
Concurrent use with methotrexate or tetracyclines
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening depression or suicidal thoughts
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Severe headache, vision changes, or nausea/vomiting (possible increased intracranial pressure)
Bone or joint pain (possible bone changes with long-term use)
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with tetracycline antibiotics (increased risk of intracranial pressure) and methotrexate (increased liver toxicity risk).
Alcohol must be strictly avoided during treatment and for 2 months after stopping - alcohol converts acitretin to a longer-acting, more teratogenic compound (etretinate).
Vitamin A supplements should be avoided due to additive toxicity risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your dermatologist promptly for mood changes, signs of liver problems, or bone/joint pain.
Strictly avoid alcohol and use reliable contraception as directed.
self_monitoring: Scheduled liver function tests and lipid panels.
Monthly pregnancy testing if applicable.
Periodic bone health assessment with long-term use.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose with food as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to relieve inflammation and itching from corticosteroid-responsive skin conditions such as eczema and dermatitis.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to the affected area 2-3 times daily.
typical_duration: Short-term use, typically no more than 2-3 weeks unless directed otherwise by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Apply a thin layer and rub in gently.
Do not use on the face, groin, or underarms unless specifically directed.
Do not cover with an occlusive dressing (e.g., plastic wrap) unless instructed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Untreated skin infection at the application site
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of skin infection developing under treatment: increased redness, warmth, pus
Significant skin thinning, stretch marks, or visible blood vessels with prolonged use
Signs of systemic absorption with overuse: unusual fatigue, weight changes (rare with appropriate use)
common_side_effects: Burning or stinging at application site
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected with appropriate topical use.
Avoid applying other topical products to the same area at the same time unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact your prescriber if the area appears infected or skin thinning develops.
Do not use longer than directed.
self_monitoring: Monitor the treated area for improvement or signs of thinning/irritation with prolonged use.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered and resume the regular schedule; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: Used to treat dry, scaly skin (xerosis) and certain thickened skin conditions such as ichthyosis or keratosis pilaris.
typical_dosage: Apply to affected skin twice daily.
typical_duration: Ongoing as needed for dry skin/keratosis, or short-term as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Apply to clean, dry skin and rub in gently.
Avoid applying to broken, irritated, or sunburned skin.
Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to lactic acid or ammonium lactate
Use on broken or infected skin
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe burning, stinging, or redness that worsens with use
Signs of allergic skin reaction: hives, significant swelling
common_side_effects: Mild burning or stinging on application, especially on broken skin
otc_and_other_interactions: May increase skin sensitivity to other topical products applied to the same area.
Increases sun sensitivity of treated skin - use sunscreen on exposed treated areas.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact your prescriber or pharmacist if significant irritation or an allergic reaction develops.
self_monitoring: Monitor skin for improvement in dryness/scaling and for irritation.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered and resume the regular twice-daily schedule; do not double up.

drug_class: Retinoid X receptor (RXR) agonist - oral oncology retinoid
description: Used to treat cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) that has not responded to at least one other systemic treatment.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist/dermatologist, based on body surface area; typically taken once daily with a meal.
typical_duration: Long-term as directed, with periodic reassessment of response.
directions_for_use: Take with a meal to improve absorption.
Effective contraception is required for females of reproductive potential due to significant birth defect risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of pancreatitis: severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting (related to elevated triglycerides) - seek care promptly
Signs of very high triglycerides
Signs of hypothyroidism: fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain (very common - most patients need thyroid hormone supplementation)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Gemfibrozil significantly increases bexarotene levels - avoid combining.
Vitamin A supplements should be avoided due to additive toxicity risk.
Levothyroxine dose often needs to be started or increased due to bexarotene-induced hypothyroidism - your prescriber will monitor thyroid levels closely.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for severe abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis).
Contact your prescriber for symptoms of low thyroid function or vision changes.
self_monitoring: Scheduled triglyceride, cholesterol, liver function, thyroid function, and complete blood count testing - required regularly during therapy.
Monthly pregnancy testing if applicable.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose with food as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to treat active, mild to moderate ulcerative colitis and to help maintain remission.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your gastroenterologist; typically 2-3 capsules three times daily.
typical_duration: Course length individualized - active flares typically treated for 8-12 weeks; may be continued longer for maintenance.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food, at evenly spaced times.
Swallow capsules whole, or open and sprinkle on applesauce if unable to swallow whole, per your pharmacist's instructions.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to salicylates or aminosalicylates
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening of colitis symptoms (bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, fever) shortly after starting - rare paradoxical reaction; contact your prescriber
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
Signs of allergic reaction or severe rash
Signs of pericarditis/myocarditis (rare): chest pain, shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: May slightly increase the effect of anticoagulants like warfarin - monitor INR if used together.
No significant interaction with common OTC pain relievers, but check with your pharmacist before regular NSAID use given underlying colitis.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your gastroenterologist if colitis symptoms worsen after starting, or for signs of kidney problems.
Report new chest pain or shortness of breath.
self_monitoring: Periodic kidney function tests.
Track bowel symptoms and report worsening.
Report new joint or chest symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to treat pruritus (itching) associated with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC) and Alagille syndrome, primarily in pediatric patients.
dosage_forms: Capsule (including capsule contents that can be sprinkled on soft food for young children)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist, based on body weight; typically once daily in the morning before breakfast.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Give in the morning, about 30 minutes before the first meal of the day.
If unable to swallow the capsule, it may be opened and the contents sprinkled on soft food per pharmacist instructions - do not chew the beads.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of worsening liver function: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, easy bruising - seek care promptly
Severe or persistent diarrhea leading to dehydration
Significant, unexplained weight loss
common_side_effects: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency (A, D, E, K) with prolonged use
otc_and_other_interactions: May reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) - supplementation and monitoring may be needed as directed by your specialist.
Bile acid binding resins (e.g., cholestyramine) may reduce this drug's effectiveness if taken together - separate dosing as directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your specialist promptly for signs of worsening liver function or persistent diarrhea.
Report significant weight loss.
self_monitoring: Scheduled liver function tests.
Fat-soluble vitamin level monitoring.
Track growth/weight in children.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and give the next dose at the regular time the following morning - do not double up.

description: Used to relieve itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis (eye allergies).
typical_dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) twice daily.
typical_duration: Used as needed during allergy seasons/exposure, or as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Tilt head back, pull down the lower eyelid, and instill the drop without touching the eye/eyelid with the dropper tip.
Remove contact lenses before instilling; wait at least 10 minutes before reinserting.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, keep tightly closed.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe eye pain, significant vision changes, or worsening redness (possible eye infection or other condition) - seek prompt evaluation
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected.
Avoid using with other eye drops within several minutes to prevent washout - space out different eye medications by at least 5 minutes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact your prescriber for severe eye pain, vision changes, or worsening symptoms.
self_monitoring: Track symptom relief; if no improvement in a few days, contact your prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Use the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to treat bacterial conjunctivitis (pink eye) caused by susceptible bacteria.
typical_dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily, 4-12 hours apart, for 7 days.
typical_duration: Short course, typically 7 days; complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
directions_for_use: Shake well before use.
Wash hands before use; avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye.
Do not wear contact lenses while symptoms of infection are present.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to besifloxacin or other fluoroquinolones
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: significant swelling, rash, difficulty breathing
Worsening eye redness, pain, or vision changes despite treatment - may indicate a resistant infection or other condition
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; avoid using with other eye drops within several minutes to prevent washout.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber if symptoms do not improve within a few days or worsen.
Seek care for signs of allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Complete the full 7-day course even if the eye feels better sooner.
Watch for symptom improvement.
missed_dose_instructions: Use the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up. Complete the full course as prescribed.

description: The ophthalmic form is used to lower elevated eye pressure in ocular hypertension and open-angle glaucoma; the oral tablet form is used to treat high blood pressure.
typical_dosage: Ophthalmic: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) twice daily. Oral: individualized, set by your prescriber, typically once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: For eye drops: shake suspension well; wash hands before use; press gently on the inner corner of the eye for 1-2 minutes after instilling to reduce systemic absorption.
For tablets: take at the same time each day; do not stop abruptly.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Severe asthma or COPD with bronchospasm
Severe bradycardia (slow heart rate) or certain heart block
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Very slow heart rate, dizziness, or fainting
Wheezing or difficulty breathing (even with the eye drop form, some medication is absorbed systemically)
Signs of worsening heart failure: shortness of breath, swelling, rapid weight gain
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive effects with other blood-pressure or heart-rate-lowering medications (amlodipine, metoprolol, lisinopril).
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) may blunt the blood-pressure-lowering effect of the oral form.
Do not stop abruptly - can cause rebound high blood pressure or chest pain.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for very slow heart rate, dizziness, or breathing difficulty.
Do not stop this medication abruptly without medical guidance.
self_monitoring: Home blood pressure and heart rate checks (oral form).
Regular eye pressure checks (ophthalmic form).
Report new wheezing or shortness of breath.
missed_dose_instructions: Take/use the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to lower elevated eye pressure in ocular hypertension and open-angle glaucoma.
typical_dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) two to three times daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Shake well before use.
Wash hands before use; avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye.
If using more than one eye drop product, space them at least 5 minutes apart.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Severe kidney impairment (relative caution due to sulfonamide component)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic/sulfonamide reaction: rash, hives, difficulty breathing, severe skin reaction
Significant eye pain or vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive effect with oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors if used together (not typically combined).
No significant interactions with common OTC medications expected; use caution in patients with sulfa allergies.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for significant eye pain or vision changes.
Seek care for signs of an allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Regular eye pressure checks as scheduled by your ophthalmologist.
missed_dose_instructions: Use the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to treat urinary retention caused by an underactive bladder (not due to a physical blockage).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically 10-50 mg two to four times daily.
typical_duration: As directed by your prescriber; may be short-term (e.g., postoperative/postpartum) or longer-term.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals) to reduce nausea, unless directed otherwise.
Take at consistent times as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Severe bradycardia or low blood pressure
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe abdominal pain or cramping
Wheezing or difficulty breathing
Fainting, very slow heart rate, or severe flushing
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Effects are blocked by anticholinergic drugs such as diphenhydramine - avoid combining.
Additive cholinergic effects (cramping, diarrhea) with other cholinergic medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for severe cramping, wheezing, or fainting.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptoms and bladder emptying.
Report severe GI symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to treat high blood pressure and certain irregular heart rhythms (ventricular arrhythmias).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically 200-800 mg per day, given once or twice daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time(s) each day, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly - taper as directed to avoid rebound high blood pressure or chest pain.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Severe bradycardia or certain heart block without a pacemaker
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Very slow heart rate, dizziness, or fainting
Signs of worsening heart failure: shortness of breath, swelling, rapid weight gain
Wheezing or difficulty breathing
Chest pain if the medication is stopped abruptly
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can blunt the blood-pressure-lowering effect.
Additive effects with other blood-pressure/heart-rate-lowering medications (amlodipine, lisinopril, metoprolol).
Do not stop abruptly.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for very slow heart rate, dizziness, or breathing difficulty.
Never stop this medication abruptly.
self_monitoring: Home blood pressure and pulse checks.
Report any new shortness of breath or swelling.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: Used to treat symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), such as difficulty urinating and weak urine stream.
typical_dosage: 10 mg by mouth once daily, taken after the same meal each day.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take after the same meal each day for consistent absorption.
Swallow the tablet whole; do not crush, chew, or split.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with liver/kidney impairment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting or severe dizziness, especially when standing up quickly (orthostatic hypotension)
Prolonged, painful erection (priapism) - seek emergency care
Fast or irregular heartbeat
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive low blood pressure/dizziness with other blood pressure medications (lisinopril, losartan, amlodipine, metoprolol) and with sildenafil/tadalafil.
Inform your surgeon/eye surgeon if planning cataract surgery - can cause intraoperative floppy iris syndrome.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for a prolonged erection.
Contact your prescriber for fainting or severe dizziness.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
self_monitoring: Monitor for dizziness, especially with position changes.
Track urinary symptom improvement.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time with a meal the following day - do not double up.

description: Used as an inhaled mucolytic to thin and loosen thick mucus in chronic bronchopulmonary conditions (e.g., cystic fibrosis, COPD, bronchiectasis), and (as effervescent tablets, Cetylev) as an oral antidote for acetaminophen overdose.
route: Oral inhalation via nebulizer, or oral (effervescent tablets for antidote use)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; nebulized mucolytic use typically 3-4 times daily. Antidote dosing is a specific weight-based regimen used under direct medical supervision.
typical_duration: Ongoing for chronic mucus-clearance use as directed; antidote use is a short, defined course managed by a medical team.
directions_for_use: For inhalation: use with a nebulizer as directed; a foul (rotten-egg) sulfur smell is normal.
Rinse mouth and wash face after nebulizer use, as it may leave a sticky residue.
Oral antidote use should only be taken exactly as directed by the treating medical team.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; once opened, inhalation solution should generally be used within the timeframe on the label and discarded if discolored.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Wheezing or worsening difficulty breathing after a nebulizer treatment (bronchospasm) - seek prompt evaluation
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling, difficulty breathing
Nausea/vomiting that prevents keeping oral antidote doses down - contact the treating medical team immediately
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected with inhaled mucolytic use.
Activated charcoal (used for other overdose scenarios) can reduce absorption of oral acetylcysteine if given together - timing is managed by the treating medical team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop nebulizer treatment and contact your prescriber if wheezing/bronchospasm occurs - a bronchodilator may be needed beforehand for future doses.
For antidote use, follow the treating medical team's instructions exactly.
self_monitoring: Track mucus clearance and breathing symptoms with chronic use.
Antidote use is monitored by the medical team with blood testing.
missed_dose_instructions: For chronic nebulizer use, take the missed dose as soon as remembered and resume the regular schedule - do not double up. Oral antidote dosing must follow the treating medical team's exact schedule.

description: Used to lower elevated homocysteine levels in patients with homocystinuria, a rare inherited metabolic disorder.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your metabolic specialist, based on body weight; typically mixed with water, juice, formula, or food and taken twice daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Measure the exact dose with the provided scoop.
Dissolve completely in the recommended amount of liquid or soft food and take right away.
Do not put dry powder directly in the mouth - dissolve first.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, tightly closed, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe headache, confusion, or vision changes (rare reports of elevated brain pressure/cerebral edema) - seek care promptly
Signs of severe allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected.
Taken alongside other homocystinuria therapies (e.g., vitamin B6/B12, folic acid) as directed by your specialist - do not adjust the overall regimen on your own.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your specialist for severe headache, confusion, or vision changes.
Report persistent GI upset.
self_monitoring: Scheduled plasma homocysteine and methionine level monitoring.
Track growth/development in children as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Give the missed dose as soon as remembered; if close to the next scheduled dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up. Contact your specialist if doses are missed frequently.

description: Used to treat moderate to severe infections such as streptococcal infections (e.g., strep throat) and other susceptible bacterial infections, particularly in children, combining a rapid-acting and a long-acting penicillin component.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber, based on weight and infection; usually given as a single intramuscular injection (or occasionally as a short series).
typical_duration: Often a single injection; your prescriber will advise if additional doses are needed.
directions_for_use: Administered only by a trained healthcare provider into a large muscle (e.g., buttock or thigh).
Tell the provider about any prior penicillin allergy before the injection.
Stay at the pharmacy/clinic for observation for a period after the injection as directed, in case of an allergic reaction.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled by the pharmacy/clinic under refrigeration; not for home storage.
contraindications: Known allergy to penicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing, wheezing - seek emergency care immediately (patients are often observed on-site for this reason)
Severe injection site pain, numbness, or signs of nerve injury
Severe diarrhea (possible C. difficile infection) developing during or after treatment
common_side_effects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Probenecid can increase and prolong penicillin blood levels if taken together.
Tell your pharmacist about any other antibiotic allergies before receiving this injection.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of a severe allergic reaction, which can occur quickly after the injection.
Contact your prescriber for severe injection site pain or persistent diarrhea.
self_monitoring: Remain for observation at the pharmacy/clinic as directed after the injection.
Watch the injection site over the following days.
missed_dose_instructions: If this is part of a multi-dose series and an appointment is missed, contact the prescriber's office promptly to reschedule.

description: Used to treat certain infections requiring sustained antibiotic levels, most notably syphilis, and for long-term prevention of rheumatic fever recurrence and certain streptococcal infections.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber, based on the condition being treated; syphilis treatment may involve one or a series of weekly injections depending on disease stage.
typical_duration: Ranges from a single injection to a series of weekly injections (e.g., 1-3 weeks) depending on the condition.
directions_for_use: Administered only by a trained healthcare provider into a large muscle (e.g., buttock or thigh) - this medication is never given intravenously.
Tell the provider about any prior penicillin allergy before the injection.
Keep all scheduled follow-up injection appointments if part of a multi-week series.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled by the pharmacy/clinic under refrigeration; not for home storage.
contraindications: Known allergy to penicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing, wheezing - seek emergency care immediately
Fever, chills, headache, or muscle aches within 24 hours of a syphilis treatment injection (Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction) - typically mild and short-lived, but notify your provider
Severe injection site pain or numbness
common_side_effects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Probenecid can increase and prolong penicillin blood levels if taken together.
Tell your pharmacist about any other antibiotic allergies before receiving this injection.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
Contact your prescriber if fever/flu-like symptoms after a syphilis treatment injection are severe or prolonged.
self_monitoring: Remain for observation at the pharmacy/clinic as directed after the injection.
Keep all follow-up injection appointments if part of a series.
Follow-up blood testing (e.g., RPR titers) as directed to confirm treatment response for syphilis.
missed_dose_instructions: If part of a multi-week series, contact the prescriber's office immediately to reschedule a missed dose - delays can reduce treatment effectiveness, especially for syphilis.

description: Used as part of a combination antibacterial regimen to treat lung infections caused by Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) in adults who have not responded to prior therapy.
route: Oral inhalation via a specific nebulizer system (Lamira)
typical_dosage: 590 mg once daily, nebulized using the specific Lamira nebulizer system provided with this medication - no substitute nebulizer should be used.
typical_duration: Individualized, set by your specialist; typically continued for up to 12 months after cultures become negative, as part of a multi-drug regimen.
directions_for_use: Use only with the Lamira nebulizer system provided - other nebulizers are not validated for this product.
Shake the vial gently before use.
Sit upright during treatment; treatment takes about 14 minutes.
This medication is used alongside other oral antibiotics prescribed for MAC lung disease - take all medications in your regimen as directed.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze. May be stored at room temperature for a limited time before use per product labeling - ask your specialty pharmacist for specifics.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to amikacin or other aminoglycosides
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Coughing up blood - seek emergency care
New or worsening shortness of breath, wheezing, or chest tightness during or after treatment (bronchospasm/hypersensitivity pneumonitis)
Hearing changes, ringing in the ears, or dizziness/balance problems (ototoxicity - a known risk with aminoglycosides even when inhaled)
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid other inhaled or systemic ototoxic or nephrotoxic medications when possible (e.g., other aminoglycosides) - discuss all medications with your specialist.
Use a fast-acting bronchodilator before treatment if you have a history of bronchospasm, as directed by your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop treatment and contact your specialist promptly for hearing changes, significant shortness of breath, or coughing up blood.
Report any new balance problems immediately.
self_monitoring: Scheduled hearing tests (audiograms) periodically during therapy.
Scheduled kidney function tests.
Track sputum cultures as directed to assess treatment response.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered that day; if a full day is missed, skip it and resume the normal daily schedule the next day - do not double up.

description: Ophthalmic drops are used to dilate the pupil and temporarily paralyze eye focusing for eye exams, treatment of certain inflammatory eye conditions (uveitis/iritis), amblyopia therapy, and low-dose off-label use for myopia control in children. Oral/sublingual drops are also used to reduce excessive drooling (sialorrhea) in certain neurologic conditions.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber, based on the indication and concentration prescribed (concentrations and frequency vary widely by use, from daily low-dose myopia-control drops to occasional use before eye exams).
typical_duration: Varies widely by indication - from a single use before an eye exam to daily long-term use for myopia control or drooling management.
directions_for_use: For eye drops: wash hands before use; instill as directed and press gently on the inner corner of the eye afterward to reduce systemic absorption.
Expect blurred near vision and light sensitivity after ophthalmic use - sunglasses may help; use caution with driving or activities requiring near vision.
For oral/sublingual use in drooling management, follow your prescriber's exact dosing schedule.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to atropine or belladonna alkaloids
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, significant vision loss, or halos around lights (possible angle-closure glaucoma) - seek emergency care
Confusion, agitation, flushing, very dry mouth, rapid heartbeat, or fever (signs of anticholinergic toxicity, especially in young children with accidental ingestion or overuse) - seek emergency care
Difficulty urinating
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive anticholinergic effects with diphenhydramine (dry mouth, confusion, urinary retention), especially in older adults or young children.
Use caution combining with other medications that increase heart rate.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for eye pain with vision loss, or signs of anticholinergic toxicity.
Keep out of reach of children - accidental ingestion of eye drops can be serious.
self_monitoring: Use sunglasses and avoid tasks requiring sharp near vision while pupils are dilated.
Track response to therapy (e.g., myopia progression, drooling control) as directed by your prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Use/take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it - do not double up.

description: A combined hormonal birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy; also used to help regulate menstrual cycles and reduce menstrual cramps/acne in some patients. Available in a couple of common dose strengths marketed under different brand/generic names.
dosage_forms: Tablet (28-day pack: active hormone tablets plus placebo/reminder tablets)
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth at the same time every day, following the order in the pack (typically 21 active tablets followed by 7 placebo tablets, though pack structures vary by brand).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as long as contraception/cycle regulation is desired.
directions_for_use: Take one tablet at the same time every day, in the order specified on the pack, to maintain effectiveness and cycle control.
Start a new pack immediately after finishing the previous one, without a break, unless directed otherwise.
Use a backup contraceptive method for the first 7 days if starting the pack for the first time or restarting after a gap.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture, in the original pack.
contraindications: Smoking (especially age 35+) combined with this medication - increased risk of serious cardiovascular events
History of blood clots (DVT/PE), stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected breast cancer or other estrogen-sensitive cancer
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain/warmth, sudden shortness of breath, chest pain - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of stroke: sudden weakness/numbness, trouble speaking, severe headache, vision changes - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, severe abdominal pain, dark urine
Severe migraine or new migraine with aura - contact your prescriber, this medication may need to be stopped
otc_and_other_interactions: Enzyme-inducing medications significantly reduce contraceptive effectiveness - this includes rifampin, certain anticonvulsants, and St. John's Wort; use an additional barrier method if any of these are needed.
Armodafinil and other CYP3A4-inducing wakefulness agents can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use a backup method.
Some antibiotics and antifungals may modestly affect levels; discuss with your pharmacist if starting a new antibiotic course.
Increased risk of blood clots when combined with other estrogen-containing products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or stroke.
Contact your prescriber promptly for severe headache, new migraine with aura, or signs of liver problems.
Stop smoking - discuss cessation support with your pharmacist/prescriber.
self_monitoring: Track cycle/bleeding pattern.
Home blood pressure checks periodically.
Perform routine breast self-awareness and attend recommended cancer screenings.
Report new severe headaches or leg swelling right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If one active pill is missed, take it as soon as remembered (even if it means taking two pills the same day) and continue the pack on schedule. If two or more active pills are missed, follow the specific missed-pill instructions in the package labeling or call your pharmacist/prescriber, and use a backup contraceptive method for at least 7 days.

description: A combined hormonal birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy, with a biphasic dosing pattern that includes a short interval of low-dose estrogen-only tablets instead of placebo tablets to help reduce breakthrough bleeding and hormone withdrawal symptoms.
dosage_forms: Tablet (28-day pack: active combination tablets, low-dose estrogen tablets, and placebo tablets in sequence)
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth at the same time every day, following the exact order in the pack.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as long as contraception is desired.
directions_for_use: Take one tablet at the same time every day, in the exact order printed on the pack - the sequence of different tablet colors/doses matters for this product.
Start a new pack immediately after finishing the previous one.
Use a backup contraceptive method for the first 7 days if starting for the first time or restarting after a gap.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture, in the original pack.
contraindications: Smoking (especially age 35+) combined with this medication - increased risk of serious cardiovascular events
History of blood clots (DVT/PE), stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected breast cancer or other estrogen-sensitive cancer
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain/warmth, sudden shortness of breath, chest pain - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of stroke: sudden weakness/numbness, trouble speaking, severe headache, vision changes - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, severe abdominal pain, dark urine
Severe migraine or new migraine with aura - contact your prescriber, this medication may need to be stopped
common_side_effects: Slightly higher reported risk of blood clots with desogestrel-containing pills compared to some other progestins - discuss your individual risk factors with your prescriber
otc_and_other_interactions: Enzyme-inducing medications significantly reduce contraceptive effectiveness - this includes rifampin, certain anticonvulsants, and St. John's Wort; use an additional barrier method if any of these are needed.
Armodafinil and other CYP3A4-inducing wakefulness agents can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use a backup method.
Some antibiotics and antifungals may modestly affect levels; discuss with your pharmacist if starting a new antibiotic course.
Increased risk of blood clots when combined with other estrogen-containing products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or stroke.
Contact your prescriber promptly for severe headache, new migraine with aura, or signs of liver problems.
Stop smoking - discuss cessation support with your pharmacist/prescriber.
self_monitoring: Track cycle/bleeding pattern.
Home blood pressure checks periodically.
Perform routine breast self-awareness and attend recommended cancer screenings.
Report new severe headaches or leg swelling right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If one active pill is missed, take it as soon as remembered (even if it means taking two pills the same day) and continue the pack on schedule. If two or more active pills are missed, follow the specific missed-pill instructions in the package labeling or call your pharmacist/prescriber, and use a backup contraceptive method for at least 7 days.

description: A combined hormonal birth control pill taken in an extended 91-day cycle (84 active hormone tablets followed by 7 low-dose estrogen tablets instead of placebo), resulting in a period only about every 3 months instead of monthly. Available in a standard-dose (Seasonique-type) and lower-dose (LoSeasonique-type) strength depending on the specific product dispensed.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth at the same time every day, continuously through the full 91-day pack, then starting the next pack immediately.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as long as contraception is desired.
directions_for_use: Take one tablet at the same time every day, in the exact order printed on the pack, without a break between packs.
Expect a period only about once every 3 months (during the low-dose estrogen tablet week); breakthrough spotting is common, especially in the first few cycles.
Use a backup contraceptive method for the first 7 days if starting for the first time or restarting after a gap.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture, in the original pack.
contraindications: Smoking (especially age 35+) combined with this medication - increased risk of serious cardiovascular events
History of blood clots (DVT/PE), stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected breast cancer or other estrogen-sensitive cancer
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain/warmth, sudden shortness of breath, chest pain - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of stroke: sudden weakness/numbness, trouble speaking, severe headache, vision changes - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, severe abdominal pain, dark urine
Severe migraine or new migraine with aura - contact your prescriber, this medication may need to be stopped
common_side_effects: Irregular/unscheduled spotting, especially during the first few cycles of use
otc_and_other_interactions: Enzyme-inducing medications significantly reduce contraceptive effectiveness - this includes rifampin, certain anticonvulsants, and St. John's Wort; use an additional barrier method if any of these are needed.
Armodafinil and other CYP3A4-inducing wakefulness agents can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use a backup method.
Some antibiotics and antifungals may modestly affect levels; discuss with your pharmacist if starting a new antibiotic course.
Increased risk of blood clots when combined with other estrogen-containing products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or stroke.
Contact your prescriber promptly for severe headache, new migraine with aura, or signs of liver problems.
Stop smoking - discuss cessation support with your pharmacist/prescriber.
self_monitoring: Track cycle/bleeding pattern.
Home blood pressure checks periodically.
Perform routine breast self-awareness and attend recommended cancer screenings.
Report new severe headaches or leg swelling right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If one active pill is missed, take it as soon as remembered (even if it means taking two pills the same day) and continue the pack on schedule. If two or more active pills are missed, follow the specific missed-pill instructions in the package labeling or call your pharmacist/prescriber, and use a backup contraceptive method for at least 7 days.

description: Treats schizophrenia and depressive episodes associated with bipolar I or II disorder (used alone or with other mood medications).
typical_dosage: 42 mg by mouth once daily with food, unless your prescriber directs otherwise.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take once daily with food.
Swallow capsule whole; do not crush or chew.
Do not stop suddenly without talking to your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Increased suicidal thoughts/behavior, especially in young adults - seek care immediately
High fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, irregular heartbeat/sweating (neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care
Uncontrollable muscle movements of face/tongue/limbs (tardive dyskinesia) - contact prescriber
Increased risk of death in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning) - not approved for this use
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or other CNS depressants - use caution.
Avoid alcohol, which increases sedation.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers can significantly change lumateperone levels - tell your prescriber about all new medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for neuroleptic malignant syndrome symptoms or suicidal thoughts.
Contact prescriber for abnormal movements or persistent sedation.
self_monitoring: Watch for mood changes or suicidal thoughts, especially early in treatment.
Track for unusual movements.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted cancer therapy used for symptomatic or progressive medullary thyroid cancer that cannot be surgically removed.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (available only through a restricted REMS program due to QT prolongation risk).
typical_duration: Individualized; continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablet whole; if unable to swallow, follow your pharmacist's instructions for dispersing in water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Uncorrected low magnesium, potassium, or calcium
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting, palpitations, or very fast/irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation/torsades de pointes risk) - seek emergency care
Severe diarrhea, rash (including Stevens-Johnson syndrome), or shortness of breath (possible lung inflammation) - seek care
Signs of stroke or heart problems
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid other QT-prolonging drugs such as ondansetron, azithromycin, and certain antipsychotics unless directed by your oncologist.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., St. John's Wort) which can reduce effectiveness.
NSAIDs and diarrhea medications may be used cautiously under oncologist guidance for symptom management.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting or irregular heartbeat.
Contact your oncologist for severe diarrhea or rash.
self_monitoring: Baseline and periodic ECG monitoring is required.
Electrolyte (magnesium, potassium, calcium) and thyroid function labs as scheduled.
Blood pressure checks.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by less than 12 hours, take it as soon as remembered; if more than 12 hours late, skip it and resume the next day - do not double up.

description: Eye drops that lower elevated pressure inside the eye in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) twice daily, or as directed by your eye doctor.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use; avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye.
Press gently on the inner corner of the eye (nasolacrimal occlusion) for 1-2 minutes after instilling to reduce systemic absorption.
Wait at least 5 minutes between this and other eye drops.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep bottle tightly closed.
contraindications: Severe bradycardia, heart block, or decompensated heart failure
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Wheezing or trouble breathing (can occur even from eye drops) - seek care
Very slow heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting - seek care
Eye pain, vision changes, or signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive effects with oral beta-blockers (e.g., metoprolol) can cause excessive slowing of heart rate/blood pressure.
Use caution with other medications that lower heart rate or blood pressure.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for breathing trouble or fainting.
Contact your eye doctor for persistent eye irritation.
self_monitoring: Periodic eye pressure checks with your eye doctor.
Monitor pulse if you have heart conditions.
missed_dose_instructions: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; do not double up.

description: An inhaled antibiotic used to improve respiratory symptoms in people with cystic fibrosis whose lungs are colonized with Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
dosage_forms: Solution for nebulization (single-use vials with diluent ampules)
typical_dosage: 75 mg by nebulizer three times daily, at least 4 hours apart, in repeating 28-day-on/28-day-off cycles as directed by your specialist.
typical_duration: Cyclical long-term therapy (28 days on, 28 days off), as directed by your pulmonologist/CF specialist.
directions_for_use: Use only with the Altera nebulizer system provided with this medication.
Mix the vial contents with the provided diluent immediately before use; do not use if not fully dissolved.
Use a bronchodilator before each dose if part of your regular regimen, as directed.
storage_instructions: Store unopened vials in the refrigerator; may be kept at room temperature for up to 28 days. Protect from light. Do not freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Wheezing, chest tightness, or difficulty breathing after a dose - seek care
Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, dizziness - seek emergency care
Coughing up blood
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; minimal systemic absorption with inhaled use.
Use bronchodilators as directed if you experience wheezing after dosing.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for breathing difficulty or allergic reaction.
Report persistent cough or wheezing to your specialist.
self_monitoring: Track lung function/symptoms as directed by your CF care team.
Report new respiratory symptoms promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered, keeping at least 4 hours between doses; do not double up.

description: An oral antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as respiratory tract, ear, and skin infections.
typical_dosage: 250-500 mg by mouth every 8 hours, or as directed, for the length of the prescribed course.
typical_duration: Short-term course, typically 7-10 days as prescribed.
directions_for_use: Take at evenly spaced intervals.
May be taken with or without food; food may reduce stomach upset.
Complete the full course even if you feel better.
storage_instructions: Store capsules at room temperature. Refrigerate reconstituted suspension and discard after 14 days.
contraindications: Use caution with severe penicillin allergy (cross-reactivity possible)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe or persistent watery/bloody diarrhea (possible C. difficile colitis) - seek care
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing - seek emergency care
Unusual bruising or bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: May enhance the effect of warfarin, increasing bleeding risk - monitor INR closely if used together.

action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber for severe diarrhea or rash.
self_monitoring: Watch for improvement of infection symptoms.
Report diarrhea that is severe or bloody.

description: An oral antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections including ear infections, throat infections, and urinary tract infections.

Complete the full course even if symptoms improve.

Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing - seek emergency care

Carbamazepine levels may be increased when combined with cefixime.

Contact prescriber for severe diarrhea.
self_monitoring: Watch for improvement of infection symptoms.

description: An oral antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections of the respiratory tract, ears, sinuses, and skin.

Complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
storage_instructions: Store tablets at room temperature. Refrigerate reconstituted suspension and discard after 14 days.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe or persistent watery/bloody diarrhea (possible C. difficile colitis) - seek care
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing - seek emergency care

Probenecid can increase cefprozil blood levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber for severe diarrhea or rash.
self_monitoring: Watch for improvement of infection symptoms.

drug_class: Bile acid (gallstone dissolution / bile acid synthesis disorder therapy)

directions_for_use: Take exactly as directed, usually divided into two daily doses.
Take consistently with regard to food as instructed by your pharmacist.

Seek emergency care for severe abdominal pain or jaundice.
self_monitoring: Periodic liver function tests.
Follow-up imaging to monitor gallstone dissolution as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A prescription antimicrobial mouth rinse used to reduce plaque and treat gingivitis.
route: Oral (topical, mouth rinse - do not swallow)
typical_dosage: Rinse with 15 mL (one capful) undiluted for 30 seconds twice daily, morning and evening, after brushing.
typical_duration: Short-term course as directed by your dentist, often up to 6 months.
directions_for_use: Do not swallow; spit out after rinsing.
Do not rinse with water or eat/drink immediately afterward.
Avoid use with certain toothpaste ingredients (sodium lauryl sulfate) close in time, which can cause staining.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: swelling of mouth/throat, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care
Severe mouth irritation or ulceration

Seek emergency care for swelling or difficulty breathing.
self_monitoring: Watch for improvement in gum health; report worsening gingivitis to your dentist.
Monitor for tooth staining.
missed_dose_instructions: Rinse as soon as remembered and continue your regular twice-daily schedule; do not double up.

description: Used to prevent and treat malaria caused by susceptible organisms, and sometimes for certain autoimmune conditions.
typical_dosage: Individualized based on indication (treatment vs. prevention) and body weight, set by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Short-term for malaria treatment; weekly dosing for prevention starting before travel and continuing after return, as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
For malaria prevention, start dosing before travel and continue for the full period directed after leaving the risk area.

contraindications: Known retinal or visual field changes from 4-aminoquinoline drugs
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Vision changes or blurred vision (retinal toxicity with long-term use) - seek care
Irregular heartbeat, palpitations, or fainting (QT prolongation) - seek emergency care
Signs of severe allergic reaction or muscle weakness
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive QT-prolongation risk with azithromycin and other QT-prolonging drugs.
Antacids and kaolin-containing products can reduce absorption - separate dosing by several hours.
May increase digoxin levels if used together.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for irregular heartbeat or fainting.
Contact prescriber for vision changes.
self_monitoring: Periodic eye exams for long-term use.
Report vision changes promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat psychotic disorders, severe behavioral problems, and severe nausea/vomiting or intractable hiccups.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber based on indication; often started low and titrated.
typical_duration: Varies by indication; long-term for psychiatric conditions, short-term for nausea/hiccups.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as directed.
Avoid prolonged sun exposure - this drug increases sun sensitivity.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: High fever, muscle rigidity, confusion, irregular heartbeat/sweating (neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care
Uncontrollable muscle movements (tardive dyskinesia) - contact prescriber
Irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation) - seek emergency care
Signs of low white blood cell count: fever, sore throat, infection - seek care
Increased risk of death in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning) - not approved for this use
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or other CNS depressants.
Additive QT prolongation with ondansetron and other QT-prolonging drugs.
Additive anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation, confusion) with diphenhydramine.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for neuroleptic malignant syndrome or irregular heartbeat.
Contact prescriber for abnormal movements.
self_monitoring: Watch for abnormal movements and mood changes.
Periodic blood counts and ECG as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Replaces a missing bile acid in patients with bile acid synthesis disorders and certain peroxisomal disorders, supporting fat and vitamin absorption.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist based on body weight and response.
typical_duration: Lifelong, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with food.
Capsules may be opened and mixed with food for patients who cannot swallow capsules, per your pharmacist's instructions.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue - seek care
Worsening diarrhea or peptic ulcer symptoms
otc_and_other_interactions: Bile acid sequestrants (colestipol, cholestyramine) reduce absorption - avoid taking together; separate dosing significantly if both are needed.
Aluminum-based antacids may bind cholic acid and reduce absorption.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your specialist for persistent diarrhea or GI symptoms.
Seek care for signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Periodic liver function tests and monitoring of fat-soluble vitamin levels as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food; if close to the next dose, skip it and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: Treats fungal skin infections (ringworm, athlete's foot, yeast infections of the skin) and fungal nail infections.
typical_dosage: Apply to affected skin twice daily, or apply nail lacquer once daily to affected nails as directed.
typical_duration: Skin infections typically 2-4 weeks; nail lacquer therapy often continues for up to 48 weeks.
directions_for_use: Clean and dry the area before application.
For nail lacquer, apply evenly over the entire nail and 5 mm of surrounding skin; remove with alcohol weekly as directed.
Continue for the full course even if symptoms improve.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from heat and open flame (nail lacquer is flammable).
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, severe itching, swelling - seek care
Severe local irritation or burning
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; minimal systemic absorption with topical use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact your prescriber for severe irritation or allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Watch for improvement of the infection; report worsening or spreading of symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered and resume your regular schedule; do not double up.

description: A two-drug combination tablet used with other antiretroviral medications to treat HIV-1 infection.

typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day.
Take with other antiretroviral medications exactly as prescribed.
Do not skip doses; missed doses can lead to drug resistance.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain with nausea/vomiting - seek emergency care
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine - seek care
Decreased urination or bone pain (kidney or bone effects with long-term tenofovir use) - contact prescriber
Worsening of hepatitis B if you also have that infection and stop this medication - do not stop without medical supervision

Avoid other tenofovir- or lamivudine-containing products to prevent double-dosing.

Seek emergency care for lactic acidosis symptoms.

Kidney function and bone density monitoring as scheduled.
Track adherence closely.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule - do not double up.

description: Lowers parathyroid hormone, calcium, and phosphorus levels in secondary hyperparathyroidism (chronic kidney disease on dialysis) and treats hypercalcemia in parathyroid carcinoma.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist and adjusted based on lab values (typically starting 30 mg once daily and titrated).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with food or shortly after a meal.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, chew, or divide.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Blood calcium level below the lower limit of normal
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low calcium: muscle cramps/spasms, numbness/tingling around mouth or in fingers, seizures - seek care promptly
Severe nausea/vomiting
Fainting or very slow heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin or fluconazole can raise cinacalcet levels, increasing risk of low calcium - dose adjustment may be needed.
Additive risk of low calcium when combined with other calcium-lowering therapies.
