Periodic parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the next dose at the regular scheduled time with food; do not double up to make up for a missed dose.

description: An oral solution taken before a colonoscopy to cleanse the colon so your doctor can see the bowel lining clearly.
typical_dosage: Two doses (typically the evening before and morning of the procedure) as specifically directed by your prescriber's bowel-prep instructions.
typical_duration: One-time use for procedure preparation.
directions_for_use: Follow your prescriber's exact timing instructions - this is critical for an adequate bowel prep.
Drink the required amount of clear liquids after each dose as instructed.
Stay near a bathroom, as this will cause frequent, watery bowel movements.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of dehydration: severe dizziness, very dark urine, little/no urination - seek care
Severe abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or signs of an irregular heartbeat (electrolyte disturbance) - seek emergency care
Seizures (rare, related to fluid/electrolyte shifts)

Oral medications may not be well absorbed during bowel prep - take other oral medications at least 1 hour before starting this product.

Contact prescriber if unable to complete the prep due to vomiting.

Confirm bowel movements are clear/light yellow before the procedure as instructed.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a one-time procedure preparation - if a dose is missed or not completed, contact your prescriber's office promptly, as your procedure may need to be rescheduled.

description: Used with other medications to treat seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.

Contact prescriber for suicidal thoughts or worsening mood.

Track seizure frequency/response to therapy.

description: Used to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and sometimes depression.

missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

Track anxiety/seizure symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: A newer oral treatment for schizophrenia in adults, working through muscarinic (not dopamine) receptors.

Severe nausea/vomiting

description: An inhaled/nebulized antibiotic used off-label in cystic fibrosis and other chronic lung infections to control resistant gram-negative bacteria such as Pseudomonas.

Use with the specific nebulizer device recommended by your care team.

Numbness/tingling around the mouth or in extremities, or muscle weakness (neurotoxicity) - contact prescriber

description: Eye drops that lower elevated eye pressure in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension when a single agent is not sufficient.

typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.

Wait at least 5 minutes between this and other eye drops.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Wheezing or trouble breathing - seek care

Contact your eye doctor for persistent eye irritation.

description: A once-daily single-tablet regimen used to treat HIV-1 infection in appropriate patients.

Do not skip doses; missed doses can lead to drug resistance.

Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort, carbamazepine, phenytoin)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue - seek care
Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain with nausea/vomiting - seek emergency care

Worsening of hepatitis B if you also have that infection and stop this medication

Seek emergency care for signs of severe liver problems or lactic acidosis.

Liver and kidney function labs as scheduled.
Track adherence closely - missed doses risk resistance.

description: An oral targeted therapy for chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma and follicular lymphoma after prior treatments.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (typically 25 mg by mouth twice daily, adjusted based on tolerability).
typical_duration: Individualized; continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serious infection: fever, chills, cough, sore throat - seek care promptly (boxed warning)
Severe or bloody diarrhea/colitis - seek care (boxed warning)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine (boxed warning) - seek care
Shortness of breath, cough (possible lung inflammation) - seek care
Severe rash or blistering (boxed warning: skin reactions)
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as fluconazole or clarithromycin can raise duvelisib levels and toxicity risk - avoid or use with close monitoring.
Avoid St. John's Wort and other strong CYP3A4 inducers, which reduce effectiveness.
Live vaccines should be avoided due to immunosuppression - discuss any vaccination with your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncologist immediately for fever, severe diarrhea, or rash.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Frequent blood counts and liver function tests, especially during the first several months.
Report new infections, diarrhea, or skin changes promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If more than 6 hours have passed since the missed dose, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy used in combination with vemurafenib to treat BRAF-mutated melanoma that has spread or cannot be surgically removed.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist as part of a 28-day cycle (typically 60 mg once daily for 21 days, then 7 days off).
typical_duration: Individualized; continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
Follow the on/off cycle schedule exactly as prescribed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe bleeding - seek emergency care
Vision changes, eye pain (possible retinal detachment) - seek care promptly
Signs of heart problems: shortness of breath, swelling, irregular heartbeat (decreased heart pumping function) - seek care
Severe skin reactions, rash, or new skin lesions - contact prescriber
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin or fluconazole can raise cobimetinib levels and toxicity risk - avoid or use with close monitoring.
Increased sun sensitivity - use sun protection; avoid combining with other photosensitizing drugs when possible.
Increased bleeding risk when combined with warfarin, apixaban, or aspirin.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncologist for vision changes, rash, or signs of heart problems.
Seek emergency care for severe bleeding or breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Periodic eye exams, echocardiograms, and liver function tests as directed.
Use sunscreen and protective clothing due to photosensitivity.
missed_dose_instructions: If more than 4 hours have passed since the missed dose, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up.

description: Replaces digestive enzymes for people whose pancreas doesn't make enough of them (e.g., cystic fibrosis, chronic pancreatitis, pancreatic surgery), helping digest fats, proteins, and carbohydrates.
typical_dosage: Individualized dose based on body weight and fat intake, set by your specialist; taken with meals and snacks.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy taken with every meal/snack.
directions_for_use: Take with meals and snacks, not on an empty stomach.
Swallow capsules whole with plenty of fluid; do not crush or chew the enzyme beads.
If unable to swallow capsules, they may be opened and sprinkled on a small amount of acidic soft food per your pharmacist's instructions - do not mix into an entire meal or hold in the mouth.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture and heat.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to pork protein (pancrelipase is pork-derived)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe abdominal pain, especially in patients with cystic fibrosis (rare bowel narrowing/fibrosing colonopathy with very high doses) - seek care
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care
Joint pain or swelling (rare gout-like symptoms from elevated uric acid)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; take consistently with each meal for best effect.
Iron supplements may be less well absorbed if taken at the same time - separate dosing if possible.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for severe abdominal pain or persistent GI symptoms.
Seek emergency care for allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track weight, stool consistency, and nutritional status.
Report abdominal pain, especially if severe or new.
missed_dose_instructions: This medication is taken with each meal/snack - if a dose is missed, simply take the next dose with your next meal or snack; do not double up.

description: Treats invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis, serious fungal infections.
route: Oral (also available IV for hospital use)
typical_dosage: Loading dose then maintenance dosing set by your specialist (commonly 372 mg by mouth every 8 hours for 6 doses, then 372 mg once daily).
typical_duration: Individualized, often weeks to months, guided by your infectious disease specialist and clinical response.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food.
Swallow capsules whole; do not crush, chew, or open.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort) or strong inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, certain HIV medications)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue - seek care
Signs of severe allergic/infusion-related reaction (for IV form)
Irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases levels of tacrolimus and cyclosporine (CYP3A4 inhibition) - significant dose reduction and closer monitoring of these drugs is typically required.
Avoid St. John's Wort, which can reduce isavuconazole levels and effectiveness.
May interact with other CYP3A4-metabolized medications - tell your prescriber about all medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for signs of liver problems.
Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Periodic liver function tests.
Levels of concomitant tacrolimus/cyclosporine should be monitored closely if used together.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: A combination birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy.
dosage_forms: Tablet (28-day pack: 21 active tablets + 7 inactive tablets)
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth at the same time each day, following the pack sequence.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as long as contraception is desired.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day to maintain effectiveness.
Start a new pack immediately after finishing the previous one.
Use a backup contraceptive method for the first 7 days if starting mid-cycle.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: History of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden severe headache, one-sided weakness - seek emergency care
Severe abdominal pain (possible liver or gallbladder problem) - seek care
Vision changes or migraine with aura - contact prescriber
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception if taking together.
Certain antibiotics and antifungals may affect effectiveness in some patients; discuss with your pharmacist.
May reduce effectiveness of lamotrigine (not on this list) and be affected by seizure medications - discuss all medications with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or stroke.
Contact prescriber for severe abdominal pain or vision changes.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure periodically.
Track menstrual bleeding patterns.
Report calf pain/swelling or chest pain promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If one active pill is missed, take it as soon as remembered (even if it means taking two pills in one day), then continue the pack as usual. If two or more active pills are missed, follow package instructions and use backup contraception for 7 days; consider emergency contraception if unprotected sex occurred.

description: Used to treat certain cancers (including lymphomas and leukemias) and severe autoimmune conditions (such as lupus nephritis) by suppressing rapidly dividing cells.
route: Oral (also available IV for infusion administration)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist/rheumatologist based on body weight, blood counts, and indication.
typical_duration: Individualized treatment course or cycles, determined by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach unless your prescriber says otherwise; if it upsets your stomach, may be taken with food.
Drink plenty of fluids and urinate frequently, especially the day of and day after dosing, to reduce bladder irritation.
Handle tablets with care; caregivers should avoid direct contact with crushed tablets or bodily fluids for a period after dosing per your pharmacist's counseling.
Effective contraception is required during treatment and for a period afterward - this drug can cause fetal harm and may affect fertility.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep away from children and pets.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Blood in urine, painful urination (hemorrhagic cystitis) - seek care promptly
Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat (from low white blood cells) - seek care immediately
Unusual bruising or bleeding (low platelets)
Signs of severe allergic reaction
Shortness of breath or cough (rare lung toxicity)
Increased long-term risk of secondary cancers and infertility - discuss with your specialist
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other immunosuppressants (tacrolimus, cyclosporine) increases infection risk - used together only under close specialist supervision.
Live vaccines should be avoided during treatment due to immunosuppression.
NSAIDs may increase bleeding/GI risk when platelet counts are low - use acetaminophen for pain when possible and confirm with your care team.
Allopurinol and certain other drugs can increase toxicity - review all medications with your oncology pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of infection, severe bleeding, or allergic reaction.
Contact your specialist for blood in urine or painful urination.
self_monitoring: Frequent blood counts (white cells, platelets) during treatment.
Urinalysis to monitor for bladder irritation.
Report fever immediately - it can signal a medical emergency during chemotherapy.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your specialist's office for guidance on a missed dose - do not take a double dose on your own.

description: Used as part of a multi-drug regimen to treat active tuberculosis, particularly drug-resistant TB, when other medications cannot be used.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist as part of a combination TB regimen (commonly 250 mg once or twice daily, adjusted based on blood levels).
typical_duration: Long-term course (often many months), determined by your infectious disease specialist as part of a full TB regimen.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed and always in combination with your other TB medications - never stop or skip doses without medical guidance.
Take with food if it upsets your stomach.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Seizures - seek emergency care
Severe confusion, depression, suicidal thoughts, or psychotic symptoms - seek care immediately
Signs of peripheral neuropathy: numbness, tingling, or weakness in hands/feet - contact prescriber
otc_and_other_interactions: Alcohol increases the risk of seizures and should be avoided.
Additive CNS effects (drowsiness, confusion) with alprazolam, tramadol, diphenhydramine, or other CNS depressants.
Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) is often prescribed alongside cycloserine to reduce neurologic side effects - take as directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for seizures.
Contact your specialist immediately for confusion, depression, or suicidal thoughts.
self_monitoring: Periodic blood level monitoring of cycloserine.
Watch closely for mood or neurologic changes and report them promptly.
Kidney function monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up. Never stop your TB regimen without your specialist's guidance.

description: Reduces cystine accumulation in cells for patients with nephropathic cystinosis, a rare metabolic disorder.
typical_dosage: Individualized dose based on body surface area, set by your specialist, typically given every 6 hours.
typical_duration: Lifelong, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or after meals, at evenly spaced intervals as directed.
Introduce gradually per your specialist's titration schedule to reduce GI side effects.
Capsules may be opened and contents sprinkled on food for those who cannot swallow, per pharmacist instructions.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe skin rash or blistering - seek care
Severe abdominal pain or GI bleeding (rare ulceration) - seek care
Unusual bruising or bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; take consistently apart from meals for best absorption.
Antacids may be used to help with stomach upset if recommended by your specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your specialist for persistent GI symptoms or rash.
Seek emergency care for severe abdominal pain or bleeding.
self_monitoring: Periodic white blood cell counts and monitoring of cystine levels as directed by your specialist.
Track growth in children.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: Eye drops used to reduce corneal cystine crystal accumulation in patients with cystinosis.
typical_dosage: One drop in each eye every waking hour, or as directed by your ophthalmologist.
typical_duration: Lifelong, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use; avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye.
Shake well before use if directed by the label.
Wait at least 5-10 minutes between this and other eye drops.
storage_instructions: Store in the refrigerator; protect from light. Discard per the expiration timeline noted on the pharmacy label once opened.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe eye pain, redness not resolving, or vision changes - seek care
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; minimal systemic absorption with ophthalmic use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your ophthalmologist for persistent eye pain, redness, or vision changes.
self_monitoring: Periodic eye exams to monitor corneal crystal accumulation.
Report worsening eye symptoms promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered and resume your regular hourly schedule during waking hours; do not double up.

description: Improves walking speed in adults with multiple sclerosis.
typical_dosage: 10 mg by mouth twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for as long as it provides benefit.
directions_for_use: Take exactly 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, chew, or split.
Do not take more than 2 tablets in 24 hours or more than 1 tablet at a time.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Seizures - seek emergency care (risk increases with higher doses or kidney impairment)
Signs of severe allergic reaction
Severe dizziness or balance problems leading to falls
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other drugs that lower the seizure threshold when possible.
NSAIDs and other drugs affecting kidney function may increase dalfampridine levels and seizure risk - use caution, especially with ibuprofen or naproxen in patients with reduced kidney function.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for seizures.
Contact prescriber for dizziness, falls, or urinary symptoms.
self_monitoring: Periodic kidney function tests, especially before starting and if risk factors change.
Track walking ability/benefit from the medication.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time, keeping at least 12 hours between doses - do not double up or take extra tablets.

description: Treats chronic spasticity from conditions such as spinal cord injury, stroke, cerebral palsy, or multiple sclerosis. An IV form is also used to treat malignant hyperthermia in hospitals.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically started low (25 mg once daily) and gradually increased based on response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic spasticity.
directions_for_use: Take with food if it upsets your stomach.
Avoid alcohol.
Use caution with tasks requiring alertness until you know how this affects you.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Should not be used where spasticity is needed to sustain function (e.g., some ambulation)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, right upper abdominal pain - seek care (boxed warning for hepatotoxicity)
Severe weakness or difficulty breathing - seek care
Signs of severe allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with alprazolam, tramadol, diphenhydramine, or alcohol.
Avoid use with other drugs known to affect the liver when possible - discuss with your prescriber.
Estrogen-containing products may increase risk of liver toxicity in some patients.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for signs of liver problems or significant weakness.
Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction or breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Periodic liver function tests, especially during the first months of treatment.
Track muscle spasticity symptoms and functional status.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used orally to treat leprosy and dermatitis herpetiformis, and to prevent Pneumocystis pneumonia in immunocompromised patients; a topical gel form treats acne.
typical_dosage: Individualized by indication, set by your prescriber (oral doses commonly 50-100 mg daily).
typical_duration: Long-term therapy for chronic conditions; duration varies by indication.
directions_for_use: Take oral tablets at the same time each day.
For topical gel, apply a thin layer to clean, dry skin as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Severe G6PD deficiency (increased risk of hemolytic anemia)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of hemolytic anemia: unusual fatigue, pale skin, yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine - seek care
Signs of methemoglobinemia: bluish skin/lips, shortness of breath, headache - seek emergency care
Severe skin reaction (rash, blistering, peeling) - seek emergency care
Signs of liver problems
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim increases the risk of hemolysis and methemoglobinemia - use together only with close monitoring if directed by your prescriber.
Rifampin can lower dapsone levels and reduce effectiveness.
NSAIDs and other drugs affecting blood cells should be used cautiously - report any unusual bruising.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for bluish skin color or severe skin reactions.
Contact prescriber for signs of anemia.
self_monitoring: G6PD level checked before starting.
Periodic complete blood counts, especially in the first months.
Liver function tests as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

generic_name: Diphtheria, tetanus, and acellular pertussis (DTaP) vaccine
otc_or_rx: Rx (administered by a qualified immunizer, e.g., pharmacist or clinician)
description: A vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis (whooping cough), primarily used for the infant/childhood immunization series.
dosage_forms: Injectable suspension (single-dose vial or prefilled syringe)
typical_dosage: Given as a series per the recommended childhood immunization schedule, administered by a qualified immunizer.
typical_duration: Series of doses per the immunization schedule; booster doses (e.g., Tdap) given later in adolescence/adulthood.
directions_for_use: Administered only by a trained healthcare professional or pharmacist - not self-administered.
Bring vaccination records to each visit to stay on schedule.
Mild soreness at the injection site and low-grade fever are expected; use a cool compress and acetaminophen as directed for comfort.
storage_instructions: Must be refrigerated (36-46F) by the administering facility; do not freeze.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component
Encephalopathy within 7 days of a previous pertussis-containing vaccine not attributable to another cause
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing, dizziness - seek emergency care
High fever (over 105F), persistent crying for 3+ hours, or seizures - seek care
Significant swelling of the entire injected limb
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for injection-site discomfort or fever per your provider's guidance; routine preventive use before vaccination is generally not recommended as it may blunt immune response.
Immunosuppressant medications may reduce vaccine effectiveness - discuss timing with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your provider for high fever or prolonged crying/irritability.
self_monitoring: Monitor for fever and injection site reaction for 24-48 hours after vaccination.
Keep track of the immunization schedule for follow-up doses.
missed_dose_instructions: If a scheduled dose in the series is missed, contact your provider or pharmacist to reschedule as soon as possible - the series does not need to be restarted from the beginning.

description: An oral targeted therapy for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and certain types of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist, typically once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or split.
Do not take antacids or acid-reducing medications close to dosing time (see interactions).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/vomit, coughing up blood - seek emergency care
Shortness of breath, cough, chest pain, or swelling (possible fluid around the lungs/heart or pulmonary hypertension) - seek care
Signs of severe infection due to low white blood cells - seek care
Irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation)
otc_and_other_interactions: Proton pump inhibitors such as omeprazole significantly reduce dasatinib absorption and should be avoided; if acid suppression is needed, discuss antacid timing (separated by several hours) or H2 blockers with your oncologist.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin can increase dasatinib levels and toxicity risk.
Increased bleeding risk with warfarin, apixaban, or aspirin.
Additive QT prolongation risk with ondansetron and other QT-prolonging drugs.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of bleeding, severe breathing trouble, or irregular heartbeat.
Contact your oncologist for fever or unusual swelling.
self_monitoring: Frequent blood counts, especially early in treatment.
Periodic chest X-ray/echocardiogram if breathing symptoms develop.
Report unusual bruising or bleeding.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy used in combination with low-dose chemotherapy for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults who cannot tolerate intensive chemotherapy.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (commonly 100 mg once daily as part of a combination regimen).
typical_duration: Individualized; continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, split, or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy (causes severe birth defects/fetal death) - effective contraception required for patients of reproductive potential and their partners
Blood or plasma donation during and for a period after treatment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, fainting (QT prolongation) - seek emergency care
Muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness with dark urine (possible rhabdomyolysis) - seek care promptly
Signs of pregnancy while on treatment - contact prescriber immediately
Signs of infection (low blood counts are common with combination chemotherapy)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) - can raise glasdegib levels and QT prolongation risk.
Additive QT prolongation risk with ondansetron and other QT-prolonging drugs.
Avoid St. John's Wort, which can reduce effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting or irregular heartbeat.
Contact your oncologist for muscle pain/weakness or suspected pregnancy.
self_monitoring: Baseline and periodic ECG monitoring, along with electrolyte checks.
Pregnancy testing before and during treatment as directed.
Frequent blood counts.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and vomiting occurs, do not repeat the dose - wait and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double up.

description: Removes excess iron from the body in patients who receive frequent blood transfusions or have certain iron overload conditions.
typical_dosage: Individualized dose based on body weight and ferritin levels, set by your specialist; typically once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy, monitored with regular iron level testing.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach or with a light meal, at the same time each day, as directed for your specific product.
Do not take with aluminum-containing antacids.
Follow your pharmacist's instructions for dispersing tablets in water/juice if using the dispersible form.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: High-risk myelodysplastic syndromes with advanced disease (for certain uses)
Poor performance status/very short life expectancy
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of GI ulceration or bleeding: black/tarry stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain - seek care (boxed warning)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine - seek care (boxed warning)
Decreased urination or swelling (kidney injury) - contact prescriber (boxed warning)
Signs of severe allergic reaction or skin rash
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) increase the risk of GI ulceration/bleeding when combined with this drug - avoid if possible; use acetaminophen for pain instead.
Aspirin and other antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs (warfarin, apixaban, clopidogrel) further increase bleeding risk.
Aluminum-containing antacids should not be taken at the same time.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for signs of GI bleeding, liver problems, or kidney injury.
Contact your specialist for persistent nausea, vomiting, or rash.
self_monitoring: Regular kidney function, liver function, and ferritin level labs as directed.
Monthly weight checks in children.
Periodic hearing and eye exams for long-term use.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: Used to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy in patients age 2 and older.
typical_dosage: Individualized dose based on body weight, set by your specialist, typically once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop suddenly - your prescriber will taper the dose if stopping.
Shake oral suspension well before each use and use the provided dosing device.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat (immune suppression) - seek care
Severe mood changes, depression, or unusual behavior - contact prescriber
Significant vision changes (cataracts, glaucoma with long-term use) - seek care
Signs of adrenal insufficiency if stopped abruptly: severe fatigue, weakness, low blood pressure - seek care
Bone pain or fractures with long-term use
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid live vaccines during treatment due to immune suppression.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) increase risk of stomach irritation/ulcers when combined with steroids - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) can increase deflazacort levels/side effects.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for signs of infection, mood changes, or vision changes.
Seek emergency care for signs of adrenal crisis if a dose is missed for an extended period or during illness.
self_monitoring: Growth (height/weight) tracking in children.
Bone density and eye exams periodically with long-term use.
Blood sugar and blood pressure monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up. Do not stop abruptly without medical guidance.

description: A once-daily single-tablet regimen used to treat HIV-1 infection in appropriate patients.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily, with or without food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day.
Do not skip doses; missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort, carbamazepine, phenytoin)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine - seek care
Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain with nausea/vomiting - seek emergency care
Decreased urination or bone pain (kidney/bone effects with long-term tenofovir use)
Worsening of hepatitis B if you also have that infection and stop this medication
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort must be avoided - can cause loss of viral control and resistance.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) may increase kidney-related side-effect risk with the tenofovir component.
Avoid other doravirine-, lamivudine-, or tenofovir-containing products to prevent double-dosing.
action_if_adverse_effects: Do not stop or skip doses on your own - contact your HIV specialist about side effects.
Seek emergency care for signs of lactic acidosis.
self_monitoring: Periodic HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Kidney function and bone density monitoring as scheduled.
Track adherence closely.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule - do not double up.

description: An oral antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections; also used off-label to treat SIADH-related low sodium levels.
typical_dosage: 150 mg four times daily or 300 mg twice daily, for the length of the prescribed course (dosing for SIADH is individualized).
typical_duration: Short-term course for infections (typically 7-14 days); longer-term, individualized dosing when used for SIADH.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals or dairy products.
Avoid lying down for 30 minutes after taking a dose.
Avoid prolonged sun exposure - this drug increases sun sensitivity.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture; discard expired medication (degraded tetracyclines can be harmful).
contraindications: Children under 8 years (can cause permanent tooth discoloration)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe headache and vision changes (rare increased brain pressure) - seek care
Severe or persistent diarrhea (possible C. difficile colitis) - seek care
Signs of severe allergic reaction or severe skin reaction (sun-related blistering) - seek emergency care
Signs of low sodium being over-corrected: confusion, severe weakness (when used for SIADH) - seek care
otc_and_other_interactions: Can enhance the effect of warfarin, increasing bleeding risk - monitor INR closely if used together.
Calcium, iron, and antacid products reduce absorption significantly - separate dosing by several hours.
May reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives - discuss backup contraception with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction or severe headache with vision changes.
Contact prescriber for severe diarrhea.
self_monitoring: Watch for improvement of infection symptoms.
Sodium levels monitored closely if used for SIADH.
Use sun protection.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat depression.
typical_dosage: Individualized; often started at 25-100 mg daily and gradually adjusted by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy; full benefit may take several weeks.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Do not stop suddenly - taper as directed by your prescriber.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Use within 14 days of an MAO inhibitor
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Increased suicidal thoughts/behavior, especially in young adults - seek care immediately
Irregular heartbeat, chest pain, or fainting - seek emergency care
Seizures
Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity - seek emergency care
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures with tramadol; increased risk of serotonin syndrome with sertraline/escitalopram - use combinations only with medical supervision.
St. John's Wort can cause dangerous serotonin syndrome and should be avoided.
Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, or other CNS depressants.
Additive anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention) with diphenhydramine.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for suicidal thoughts, seizures, or serotonin syndrome symptoms.
Contact prescriber for persistent side effects.
self_monitoring: Watch for mood changes, especially early in treatment.
Periodic ECG may be recommended, particularly in older adults or those with heart disease.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat diabetes insipidus (reduces excessive urination/thirst), bedwetting in children, and certain bleeding disorders (mild hemophilia A/von Willebrand disease).
typical_dosage: Individualized by indication, set by your prescriber (tablets commonly 0.1-0.2 mg at bedtime for bedwetting; other regimens for diabetes insipidus).
typical_duration: Varies by indication; long-term for diabetes insipidus, often nightly for bedwetting.
directions_for_use: Take tablets consistently with regard to food as directed.
For nasal spray, prime the pump before first use per the package instructions; clear nasal congestion before dosing for best absorption.
Limit fluid intake around dosing time as directed by your prescriber to reduce the risk of low sodium/water retention.
storage_instructions: Store tablets at room temperature. Nasal spray: store at room temperature or refrigerate per product label; do not freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low sodium (hyponatremia): headache, nausea, confusion, seizures - seek emergency care
Significant decrease in urination with swelling
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: SSRIs (sertraline, escitalopram) increase the risk of low sodium when combined with desmopressin - monitor closely.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can potentiate the antidiuretic (water-retaining) effect, increasing risk of hyponatremia.
Avoid excessive fluid intake around dosing time.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for confusion, severe headache, or seizures (possible low sodium).
Contact prescriber for persistent nasal congestion or reduced effect.
self_monitoring: Periodic sodium level checks, especially when starting or adjusting dose.
Track urine output and fluid intake as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Treats inflammation and itching from corticosteroid-responsive skin conditions such as eczema and psoriasis.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to the affected area once or twice daily, as directed.
typical_duration: Short-term use, typically no more than 2-4 weeks, unless otherwise directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Apply a thin layer only to affected skin; avoid the face, groin, and underarms unless specifically directed.
Do not use with occlusive dressings (bandages/plastic wrap) unless instructed.
Wash hands after application unless hands are the treated area.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep away from open flame (spray/gel may be flammable).
contraindications: Untreated skin infection at the application site
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of skin infection: increasing redness, pus, warmth - seek care
Significant skin thinning, stretch marks, or easy bruising with prolonged use - contact prescriber
Signs of systemic absorption with extensive/prolonged use: unusual fatigue, weight changes (rare with appropriate use)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected with appropriate topical use; minimal systemic absorption unless used over large areas or for prolonged periods.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact your prescriber for signs of infection or skin thinning.
self_monitoring: Watch for improvement of the treated condition.
Limit duration of use as directed to avoid skin thinning.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered and resume your regular schedule; do not double up.

description: Used with clobazam and valproate to treat seizures associated with Dravet syndrome in patients age 6 months and older.
typical_dosage: Individualized dose based on body weight, set by your neurologist, given with food in divided doses.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with food; do not take with dairy products, carbonated beverages, or caffeine/theophylline-containing products.
Do not stop suddenly - can worsen seizures; taper as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Increased seizure frequency or new seizure types - contact neurologist
Severe drowsiness, confusion, or difficulty walking (ataxia) - seek care
Signs of low white blood cell/platelet counts: fever, unusual bruising - seek care
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases levels of clobazam and can increase sedation - dose adjustments of clobazam are often needed when starting stiripentol.
Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or other CNS depressants.
Avoid caffeine and theophylline-containing products, which may interact.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your neurologist for increased seizures, confusion, or unsteady walking.
Seek care for signs of low blood counts.
self_monitoring: Periodic blood counts and liver function tests.
Track seizure frequency and type.
Monitor weight/appetite, especially in children.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: An oral antibiotic used to treat infections caused by staphylococcus bacteria, including certain skin infections.
typical_dosage: 125-500 mg by mouth every 6 hours, for the length of the prescribed course.
typical_duration: Short-term course, typically 7-14 days as prescribed.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals, for best absorption.
Complete the full course even if you feel better.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing - seek emergency care
Severe or persistent watery/bloody diarrhea (possible C. difficile colitis) - seek care
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: May decrease the effectiveness of warfarin (enzyme induction), reducing INR - monitor closely if used together.
May reduce effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives - discuss backup contraception with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber for severe diarrhea or liver-related symptoms.
self_monitoring: Watch for improvement of infection symptoms.
Report severe or bloody diarrhea.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Treats Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (C. diff colitis).
typical_dosage: 200 mg by mouth twice daily for 10 days, or as directed by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Short-term course, typically 10 days as prescribed.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food.
Complete the full course even if diarrhea improves before finishing.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing - seek emergency care
Worsening or persistent diarrhea despite treatment - contact prescriber
Signs of GI bleeding: blood in stool
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; minimal systemic absorption with oral use.
Avoid taking anti-diarrheal medications (e.g., loperamide) without checking with your prescriber, as they may mask treatment response.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber if diarrhea worsens or does not improve.
self_monitoring: Track bowel movement frequency and consistency.
Report fever or worsening abdominal pain.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Relieves mild to moderate pain and inflammation from conditions such as osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.
typical_dosage: 250-500 mg by mouth every 8-12 hours, as directed by your prescriber; use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed.
typical_duration: Short-term for acute pain; may be used longer-term for chronic arthritis under medical supervision.
directions_for_use: Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset.
Do not crush or chew tablets.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Right before or after heart bypass surgery
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of GI bleeding: black/tarry stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain - seek care
Chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side, slurred speech (cardiovascular risk) - seek emergency care
Swelling, rapid weight gain, or decreased urination (kidney effects)
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases bleeding risk with other NSAIDs, aspirin, warfarin, clopidogrel, or apixaban.
Can reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect of lisinopril/losartan and stress the kidneys.
Combined with sertraline or escitalopram increases GI bleeding risk.
Significantly raises acetaminophen blood levels - use caution if combined.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of GI bleeding, chest pain, or kidney-related swelling.
Do not exceed the prescribed dose or combine with other NSAIDs.
self_monitoring: Watch for stomach pain or dark stools.
Periodic kidney function tests with long-term use.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Treats acute migraine headache attacks, with or without aura.
typical_dosage: One spray in each nostril, repeated after 15 minutes for a total of 4 sprays per migraine attack, not to exceed the maximum weekly dose directed by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Used as needed for acute migraine attacks; not for daily/preventive use.
directions_for_use: Prime the nasal spray device before first use per instructions.
Do not blow your nose for a period after use.
Do not use more than directed - overuse can cause medication-overuse headache and ergot toxicity.
storage_instructions: Store in the refrigerator or as directed on the label; protect from light. Do not freeze.
contraindications: Coronary artery disease/history of heart attack
Use with certain strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., some antifungals, macrolide antibiotics)
Use within 24 hours of a triptan medication
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain, numbness/coldness in fingers or toes, or leg pain with walking (vasospasm/reduced blood flow) - seek emergency care
Signs of stroke or heart attack
Severe or worsening headache despite treatment
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not use within 24 hours of sumatriptan or other triptans - increased risk of prolonged vasospasm.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, fluconazole) can dangerously increase levels and vasospasm risk - avoid combination.
Avoid other vasoconstricting medications (e.g., certain decongestants) unless approved by your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, numbness/coldness in extremities, or signs of stroke.
Contact prescriber if migraines are not adequately controlled.
self_monitoring: Track frequency of migraine attacks and medication use to avoid overuse.
Report any numbness, coldness, or pain in the hands/feet.
missed_dose_instructions: This medication is used as needed for migraine attacks, not on a fixed schedule; there is no 'missed dose' - use only when a migraine occurs, following the maximum dose limits provided by your prescriber.

brand_names: Dimethyl Fumarate Starter Pack (Tecfidera Starter Pack)
description: An oral disease-modifying therapy for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis.
typical_dosage: Starter pack titration to 120 mg twice daily for 7 days, then increased to the maintenance dose of 240 mg twice daily, as directed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce flushing and stomach upset.
Swallow capsules whole; do not crush, chew, or sprinkle contents on food.
Taking non-enteric-coated aspirin 30 minutes before a dose (if approved by your prescriber) may reduce flushing.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection, especially unusual or severe (rare risk of PML - progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy - with low lymphocyte counts): confusion, vision changes, weakness - seek care immediately
Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe or persistent abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other immunosuppressants (tacrolimus, cyclosporine, methotrexate) may increase infection risk - use together only under close specialist supervision.
Non-enteric-coated aspirin may be used before dosing (per prescriber guidance) to reduce flushing.
Live vaccines should generally be avoided during treatment - discuss with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your neurologist promptly for new neurologic symptoms or signs of infection.
Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Periodic complete blood counts (lymphocytes) required throughout treatment.
Liver function tests periodically.
Report new or worsening neurologic symptoms right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is within 4 hours of the next dose - then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to control diarrhea by slowing intestinal movement.
typical_dosage: 2 tablets (or 10 mL liquid) by mouth four times daily initially, then reduced to the lowest effective dose, as directed by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Short-term use for acute diarrhea; not intended for long-term use.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as directed; do not exceed the recommended dose.
Stay well hydrated while experiencing diarrhea.
Avoid alcohol and other sedating substances while taking this medication.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep out of reach of children (overdose in children can be fatal).
contraindications: Diarrhea caused by certain bacterial infections (e.g., pseudomembranous colitis) or poisoning
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Slowed or difficult breathing, extreme drowsiness - seek emergency care, especially in children or when combined with other sedatives
Severe abdominal distension or bloating (possible toxic megacolon)
Signs of severe allergic reaction
Diarrhea that worsens or contains blood/mucus - stop use and contact prescriber
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation and respiratory depression risk with tramadol, hydrocodone/acetaminophen, alprazolam, or other CNS depressants.
Additive anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation) with diphenhydramine.
MAO inhibitors may cause a hypertensive crisis if combined - avoid this combination.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for breathing difficulty or extreme drowsiness.
Stop use and contact prescriber if diarrhea worsens or contains blood.
self_monitoring: Track diarrhea frequency and hydration status.
Discontinue and seek care if no improvement within 48 hours.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally used as needed/short-term for diarrhea; if on a scheduled regimen, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: Used to maintain normal heart rhythm in patients with atrial fibrillation/flutter and to convert these arrhythmias to normal rhythm; only dispensed by specially certified pharmacies due to serious arrhythmia risk.
typical_dosage: Individualized dose based on kidney function and QT interval, determined and adjusted by your cardiologist; treatment is initiated in a hospital setting with cardiac monitoring.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy once a safe dose is established.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, to maintain consistent blood levels.
Never change your dose or restart after missing doses without contacting your cardiologist first - restarting requires re-hospitalization for monitoring in most cases.
Avoid grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Congenital or acquired long QT syndrome
Severe kidney impairment (creatinine clearance below 20 mL/min)

Concurrent use with verapamil, cimetidine, trimethoprim (alone or with sulfamethoxazole), ketoconazole, itraconazole, prochlorperazine, megestrol, dolutegravir, or hydrochlorothiazide-containing products - contraindicated due to dangerously increased dofetilide levels/QT prolongation
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, palpitations, dizziness, or fainting (torsades de pointes risk) - seek emergency care immediately
Chest pain or shortness of breath - seek emergency care
Signs of heart failure: swelling, sudden weight gain, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: CONTRAINDICATED with sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim - dramatically increases dofetilide levels via inhibition of renal elimination, causing life-threatening QT prolongation.
Additive QT prolongation risk with ondansetron and other QT-prolonging drugs.
Avoid grapefruit juice.
Tell every prescriber and pharmacist you take dofetilide before starting ANY new medication, including OTC products - many common drugs are contraindicated.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for irregular heartbeat, fainting, or chest pain.
Never restart this medication after missing several doses without contacting your cardiologist - re-monitoring is required.
self_monitoring: Periodic ECG and kidney function monitoring as directed - this is essential and non-negotiable for safe use.
Check with a pharmacist before starting any new medication, including OTC drugs and supplements.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time - do not double up. If several doses in a row are missed, contact your cardiologist before resuming, as re-evaluation of your QT interval may be required.

description: Increases platelet counts in adults with chronic liver disease before a scheduled procedure, and in adults with chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who have had an insufficient response to other treatments.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist based on indication and baseline platelet count.
typical_duration: Short-term course before a procedure (chronic liver disease); long-term, ongoing therapy for ITP.
directions_for_use: Take with food.
Follow the exact schedule provided by your specialist, especially for pre-procedure dosing.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, one-sided weakness - seek emergency care
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine - seek care
Severe headache
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased risk of blood clots when combined with other clot-forming risk factors; use caution with hormonal medications or other pro-thrombotic drugs.
No significant OTC interactions expected; discuss all new medications with your specialist given the platelet-raising effect.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot.
Contact your specialist for signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Frequent platelet count monitoring, especially when starting or adjusting dose.
Report leg swelling, chest pain, or shortness of breath immediately.
missed_dose_instructions: For pre-procedure short courses, contact your specialist's office promptly if a dose is missed, since exact timing before the procedure matters. For ongoing ITP therapy, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

drug_class: Tricyclic antidepressant (low-dose form used for insomnia)
description: Used at low doses to treat insomnia (difficulty staying asleep) and at higher doses to treat depression/anxiety.
typical_dosage: For insomnia: 3-6 mg by mouth within 30 minutes of bedtime. For depression, individualized higher doses set by your prescriber.
typical_duration: For insomnia, short-term use is generally recommended, though longer use may be directed by your prescriber; for depression, long-term ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: For insomnia, take within 30 minutes of bedtime and do not take within 3 hours of a meal.
Do not take unless you can devote a full night (7-8 hours) to sleep.
Do not stop suddenly if used long-term for depression - taper as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Use within 14 days of an MAO inhibitor
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Increased suicidal thoughts/behavior, especially in young adults (higher-dose use) - seek care immediately
Irregular heartbeat, chest pain (higher doses) - seek emergency care
Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity - seek emergency care
Severe daytime drowsiness or sleep-related behaviors (sleepwalking, sleep-driving)
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased risk of serotonin syndrome and seizure risk with tramadol; increased risk of serotonin syndrome with sertraline/escitalopram.
Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, or alcohol - avoid combining, especially at insomnia doses.
St. John's Wort can cause dangerous serotonin syndrome and should be avoided.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for serotonin syndrome symptoms or irregular heartbeat.
Contact prescriber for severe daytime sedation or unusual sleep behaviors.
self_monitoring: Watch for excessive daytime drowsiness.
Monitor mood if used for depression, especially early in treatment.
missed_dose_instructions: For insomnia use, do not take if fewer than 7-8 hours of sleep time remain - just skip that dose. For scheduled dosing (depression), take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; do not double up.

description: Treats secondary hyperparathyroidism in patients with chronic kidney disease, including those on dialysis.
typical_dosage: Individualized dose set by your nephrologist, adjusted based on parathyroid hormone and calcium levels.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not take other vitamin D supplements unless directed by your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high calcium: nausea, vomiting, constipation, confusion, muscle weakness, excessive thirst/urination - seek care
Irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Calcium-containing antacids or supplements can increase the risk of high calcium levels when combined with this medication.
Magnesium-containing antacids should be avoided in patients on dialysis due to risk of high magnesium levels.
Digoxin toxicity risk is increased if calcium levels become elevated - use caution.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your nephrologist for symptoms of high calcium.
Seek emergency care for irregular heartbeat or severe confusion.
self_monitoring: Frequent calcium, phosphorus, and parathyroid hormone (PTH) labs, especially when starting or adjusting dose.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Treats nausea and vomiting associated with cancer chemotherapy that hasn't responded to other treatments, and stimulates appetite in patients with AIDS-related weight loss.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber based on indication (e.g., before and after chemotherapy for nausea, or before meals for appetite).
typical_duration: Short-term around chemotherapy cycles, or longer-term for appetite stimulation as directed.
directions_for_use: Take as directed relative to meals or chemotherapy timing.
Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how this affects you.
Avoid alcohol, which increases sedation.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep in a secure location due to misuse potential.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to cannabinoids or sesame oil (capsule form)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Rapid heartbeat, chest pain - seek care
Severe mood changes, hallucinations, or confusion - contact prescriber
Seizures (rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with alprazolam, tramadol, diphenhydramine, or alcohol.
May increase heart rate - use caution with other stimulant medications.
Additive CNS effects with sertraline or other centrally acting medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for significant mood changes or rapid heartbeat.
Seek emergency care for seizures or chest pain.
self_monitoring: Track nausea/appetite response to treatment.
Watch for mood or cognitive changes, especially when starting or increasing dose.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Treats symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension (a drop in blood pressure on standing) caused by certain nervous system disorders.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist, typically taken three times daily with the last dose at least 3 hours before bedtime.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food.
Take the last daily dose several hours before bedtime to reduce nighttime high blood pressure.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying and monitor blood pressure as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe headache, chest pain, or confusion (possible high blood pressure, especially when lying down) - seek care
Signs of allergic reaction
Fainting or worsening dizziness
common_side_effects: High blood pressure (especially when lying down)
otc_and_other_interactions: Use caution combining with other blood-pressure-raising medications or decongestants.
May interact with drugs affecting dopamine or norepinephrine pathways - discuss all medications with your specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your specialist for severe headache or high blood pressure symptoms while lying down.
Seek emergency care for chest pain or confusion.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure both sitting/standing and lying down, especially at night, as directed.
Track dizziness/fainting episodes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Treats moderate to severe hot flashes associated with menopause and helps prevent postmenopausal osteoporosis, in women with a uterus (the bazedoxifene component protects the uterine lining without added progestin).
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily, with or without food.
typical_duration: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals; re-evaluated periodically by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day.
Swallow tablet whole; do not crush or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: History of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected breast cancer or estrogen-dependent cancer
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden severe headache, one-sided weakness - seek emergency care
Abnormal vaginal bleeding - contact prescriber
Signs of gallbladder disease: abdominal pain, nausea
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce estrogen levels and effectiveness while increasing breakthrough bleeding.
NSAIDs are generally compatible but combined use with anticoagulants (warfarin, apixaban) further increases clot-related risks already associated with estrogen therapy.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or stroke.
Contact prescriber for abnormal vaginal bleeding.
self_monitoring: Periodic blood pressure checks.
Routine breast and gynecologic exams as recommended.
Report new bleeding patterns.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: A maintenance inhaler used to control asthma symptoms; not for acute/rescue relief of sudden breathing problems.
typical_dosage: 2 inhalations twice daily (morning and evening), strength individualized by your prescriber based on asthma severity.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing maintenance therapy.
directions_for_use: Use on a regular schedule, not for sudden symptoms - keep a fast-acting rescue inhaler (e.g., albuterol) on hand for acute symptoms.
Rinse mouth with water and spit after each use to prevent oral thrush.
Shake well before each use and prime as directed if new or unused for a while.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; do not puncture or expose the canister to high heat.
contraindications: Primary treatment of status asthmaticus or acute asthma episodes requiring intensive measures
Should not be used as monotherapy without an inhaled corticosteroid component being appropriate for the patient
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening asthma symptoms or increased use of rescue inhaler - contact prescriber (boxed warning: LABAs may increase risk of asthma-related death)
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing immediately after use - seek emergency care
White patches in the mouth (thrush)
Rapid heartbeat, tremor, or chest pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Beta-blockers (metoprolol) can reduce the effectiveness of the formoterol component and should be used cautiously together.
Additive cardiac stimulation with other stimulant or decongestant medications.

Rinse mouth after each use and watch for oral thrush.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: A self-injectable biologic used to treat moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (eczema) in adults and adolescents.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing, dizziness - seek emergency care
Eye pain, redness, or vision changes (conjunctivitis is common; report if severe or persistent) - contact prescriber
Signs of infection: fever, unusual fatigue

Contact prescriber for eye symptoms or signs of infection.
self_monitoring: Track skin/eczema improvement.
Report new or worsening eye symptoms promptly.
Watch for signs of infection.
missed_dose_instructions: Take/administer the missed dose as soon as remembered, then resume your regular injection schedule; contact your specialist if uncertain about timing. Do not double up.

description: Lowers blood pressure by relaxing blood vessels.

typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness, especially with the first doses.

Do not use with an ACE inhibitor (e.g., lisinopril) in most patients due to increased risk of kidney problems, low blood pressure, and high potassium

Signs of high potassium: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
Decreased urination or significant swelling (kidney effects)

Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium unless directed by your prescriber.

Call prescriber for signs of high potassium or reduced urination.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure at home if recommended.
Periodic kidney function and potassium labs.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

drug_class: Angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB)/thiazide-like diuretic combination

Stay adequately hydrated unless your prescriber directs fluid restriction.

Do not use with an ACE inhibitor (e.g., lisinopril) in most patients

Signs of dehydration or significant dizziness/fainting

Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium unless directed.

Call prescriber for signs of electrolyte imbalance or severe dizziness.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure at home if recommended.
Periodic kidney function, sodium, and potassium labs.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Increases platelet production in chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), certain cases of hepatitis C-associated thrombocytopenia, and severe aplastic anemia.

Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot.
self_monitoring: Frequent platelet counts and liver function tests, especially when starting or adjusting dose.
Periodic eye exams with long-term use.
Complete blood counts as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

Severe dizziness or falls, especially in elderly patients
Signs of a severe allergic reaction/DRESS syndrome: rash, fever, swollen glands
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased sedation with diphenhydramine or alcohol.
May reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives at higher doses - use a backup method.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for aggressive/violent behavior or suicidal thoughts.
Contact prescriber for severe dizziness/falls.
Do not stop abruptly.
self_monitoring: Monitor mood and behavior changes closely (family/caregiver involvement recommended).
Track seizure frequency.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next bedtime dose; then skip. Do not double up.

description: Replaces antibodies in patients with immune deficiencies, or modulates the immune response in certain autoimmune/inflammatory conditions.
route: Intravenous infusion (often via home infusion nursing)
typical_dosage: Individualized based on body weight and indication, set by your specialist and infused on a scheduled basis (e.g., every 3-4 weeks).
typical_duration: Long-term maintenance therapy per your specialist.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare professional (often a home infusion nurse) via IV infusion.
A pre-medication (such as acetaminophen or an antihistamine) may be given to reduce infusion reactions per protocol.
storage_instructions: Store per product-specific instructions (varies by brand); protect from freezing.
contraindications: History of severe (anaphylactic) reaction to immune globulin
IgA deficiency with antibodies against IgA
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling, chest pain, stroke symptoms - increased risk especially with rapid infusion
Signs of kidney injury: decreased urination, swelling
Aseptic meningitis symptoms: severe headache, stiff neck, fever
Severe allergic/anaphylactic reaction during infusion
Signs of hemolysis: fatigue, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Can interfere with the effectiveness of live vaccines for several months after infusion - discuss vaccine timing with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, severe allergic reaction, or severe headache with stiff neck.
Report decreased urination.
self_monitoring: Kidney function tests periodically if at risk.
Monitor for infusion reactions.
Track symptom control.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your specialist's office to reschedule the infusion as soon as possible.

description: Protects against HPV types that cause most cervical, anal, and other cancers, as well as genital warts.
typical_dosage: A 2- or 3-dose series depending on age at first dose, per current CDC schedule, administered by a pharmacist/clinician.
typical_duration: Completed vaccination series per schedule.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare professional at recommended intervals.
Complete the full series for full protection.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate at 36-46°F (2-8°C), protected from light; do not freeze (pharmacy storage).
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component (including yeast)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) - seek emergency care immediately
Fainting can occur after injection (observe for 15 minutes)
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for post-vaccination soreness or fever; no significant drug interactions.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of anaphylaxis.
Sit or lie down if feeling faint after vaccination.
self_monitoring: Watch the injection site and general symptoms for 15-30 minutes after vaccination.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your pharmacy/provider to schedule the next dose as soon as possible if delayed - the series does not need to restart.

description: Treats bacterial conjunctivitis (pink eye).
typical_dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) every 2 hours while awake (up to 8 times/day) for the first 1-2 days, then 2-4 times daily for the remainder of the course, per label/prescriber.
typical_duration: Short course, typically about 7 days.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use; avoid touching the dropper to the eye.
Remove contact lenses before use and do not wear them during treatment of an active infection.
Complete the full course.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protected from light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: eye swelling, severe redness/itching
Worsening eye pain or vision changes
Signs of secondary infection
common_side_effects: Unpleasant taste if it drains into the throat
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic OTC interactions expected given minimal systemic absorption.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber if there is no improvement in a few days or if symptoms worsen.
self_monitoring: Monitor eye symptoms for improvement.
Complete the full course even if feeling better.
missed_dose_instructions: Use as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip and resume the regular schedule.

generic_name: Polyethylene glycol 3350 with electrolytes (bowel preparation solution)
description: Used to cleanse the colon before a colonoscopy or other bowel procedure, taken orally and self-administered at home.
dosage_forms: Powder for oral solution (mixed with water to a specified volume, e.g., 4 liters)
typical_dosage: Per prescriber/procedure instructions - typically mix the entire contents with water to the labeled volume and drink the prescribed amount (often 8 oz every 10-15 minutes), starting at a specific time before the procedure; may be a split-dose regimen (evening before and morning of the procedure).
