typical_duration: A single bowel-prep course before the scheduled procedure.
directions_for_use: Follow the exact timing instructions given by your prescriber/procedure center.
Refrigerate the mixed solution and drink chilled through a straw to improve palatability if allowed.
Stay near a bathroom once drinking begins.
Continue clear liquids as directed and stop solid food as instructed before the prep.
storage_instructions: Store the powder at room temperature before mixing; once mixed, refrigerate and use within the timeframe specified on the label (typically 48 hours).
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of dehydration: dizziness, decreased urination
Signs of an allergic reaction
Severe abdominal pain or bloating
Chest pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Take other oral medications at least 1 hour before starting the prep, as absorption of other drugs may be reduced during bowel cleansing.
Follow your prescriber's instructions about which regular medications to hold or take on prep day.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for severe abdominal pain, chest pain, or signs of severe dehydration.
Contact the procedure center with questions about timing.
self_monitoring: Track fluid intake and urination to avoid dehydration.
Ensure the full prep is completed for an effective procedure.
missed_dose_instructions: Not applicable in the usual sense - if you cannot complete the prep as directed, contact your procedure center/prescriber promptly since the procedure may need to be rescheduled.

description: Treats certain RET-altered non-small cell lung cancer and thyroid cancers.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist, typically taken once daily on an empty stomach.
typical_duration: Continued as directed by your oncologist until disease progression or unacceptable side effects.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal), swallowed whole, at the same time daily.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: None absolute; caution in patients with interstitial lung disease
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis: new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, fever
High blood pressure
Signs of liver toxicity
Severe bleeding events
Signs of tumor lysis syndrome
Irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation)
Impaired wound healing - hold before surgery
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid acid-reducing medications (antacids, H2 blockers, proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole) close to dosing time - they can reduce absorption; discuss timing with your oncology team.
Grapefruit juice may increase levels - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for new/worsening shortness of breath or cough.
Report high blood pressure readings to your oncology team.
self_monitoring: Home blood pressure monitoring.
Periodic liver function tests.
Report new respiratory symptoms promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on an empty stomach if possible; if close to the next dose, skip it. Do not double up.

description: Treats certain EGFR mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist, typically 250 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as directed by your oncologist until disease progression or unacceptable side effects.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time daily, with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of interstitial lung disease: new/worsening cough, shortness of breath, fever
Signs of severe liver toxicity
Severe abdominal pain (possible GI perforation)
Severe diarrhea/dehydration
New eye pain or vision changes (corneal problems)
otc_and_other_interactions: Acid-reducing medications (antacids, H2 blockers like famotidine, proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole) can reduce absorption/effectiveness - avoid or time carefully with your oncology team.
St. John's Wort significantly reduces effectiveness - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for new/worsening shortness of breath or severe abdominal pain.
Report persistent diarrhea to your oncology team promptly.
self_monitoring: Periodic liver function tests.
Monitor for respiratory symptoms.
Report vision changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose (within 12 hours); then skip. Do not double up.

drug_class: Beta-3 adrenergic agonist for overactive bladder
description: Treats symptoms of overactive bladder, including urgency, frequency, and urge incontinence.
typical_dosage: 75 mg once daily, with or without food.
typical_duration: Long-term, as needed for symptom control, per your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day.
Swallow whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Difficulty urinating (urinary retention), especially in patients with bladder outlet obstruction
Significant increase in blood pressure (uncommon)
otc_and_other_interactions: Caution with other anticholinergic OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine), which may compound urinary retention risk in susceptible patients.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for difficulty urinating or significant blood pressure changes.
self_monitoring: Track bladder symptom improvement.
Monitor blood pressure periodically if hypertensive.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip. Do not double up.

description: Prevents organ transplant rejection and treats certain autoimmune conditions (such as severe rheumatoid arthritis or psoriasis).
typical_dosage: Highly individualized based on transplant type, body weight, and blood levels; set and closely monitored by your transplant specialist.
typical_duration: Long-term, often lifelong for transplant recipients.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time(s) each day consistently.
Use the same brand/product every time - do not switch products without prescriber approval.
Be consistent with taking it with or without food.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protected from light; once opened, use oral solution within the time specified on the label.
contraindications: Abnormal kidney function requiring dose adjustment
Concurrent use with certain interacting medications
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Boxed warning: increased risk of serious infections and certain cancers (including lymphoma and skin cancers) due to immunosuppression
Signs of kidney toxicity: decreased urination, swelling
High blood pressure
Signs of neurotoxicity: tremor, seizures, confusion
Signs of liver toxicity
otc_and_other_interactions: Grapefruit juice significantly increases drug levels - avoid.
NSAIDs increase kidney toxicity risk.
St. John's Wort significantly reduces effectiveness and risks transplant rejection - avoid.
Many other significant drug interactions exist - always check with your pharmacist before adding any medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for signs of infection (fever, chills), decreased urination, or significant blood pressure elevation.
Never switch cyclosporine products/brands without prescriber approval.
Do not stop without your transplant team's guidance.
self_monitoring: Regular blood level monitoring (essential).
Kidney function and blood pressure monitoring.
Watch for signs of infection.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip. Do not double up. Contact your transplant team promptly if a dose is missed - never stop this medication without medical guidance.

description: Treats certain EGFR mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist, typically 40 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as directed by your oncologist until disease progression or unacceptable side effects.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal), at the same time daily.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe diarrhea/dehydration
Signs of interstitial lung disease: new/worsening cough, shortness of breath
Severe skin reactions: blistering, peeling
Signs of liver toxicity
New eye pain or vision changes (corneal problems)
Signs of heart failure: shortness of breath, swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Acid-reducing medications (antacids, H2 blockers, proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole) can reduce absorption - discuss timing with your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for new/worsening shortness of breath, severe diarrhea with dehydration signs, or severe skin blistering.
Report persistent diarrhea early to your oncology team.
self_monitoring: Periodic liver and kidney function tests.
Monitor hydration status.
Report vision changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered if more than 12 hours until the next dose; otherwise skip it. Do not double up.

drug_class: Immunomodulator - disease-modifying therapy for multiple sclerosis
description: Reduces relapse frequency in relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis.
dosage_forms: Prefilled syringe (20 mg/mL daily, or 40 mg/mL three times weekly)
typical_dosage: 20 mg once daily or 40 mg three times weekly (at least 48 hours apart), per your prescriber - do not mix up the two strengths/schedules.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing disease-modifying therapy.
directions_for_use: Allow the syringe to reach room temperature before injecting.
Rotate injection sites (abdomen, thighs, hips, upper arms).
Do not reuse needles/syringes.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate at 36-46°F (2-8°C); may be stored at room temperature (up to 77°F) for up to 30 days if needed, protected from light. Do not freeze.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to glatiramer acetate or mannitol
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Immediate post-injection reaction: flushing, chest tightness, palpitations, anxiety, trouble breathing shortly after injection - usually transient but seek care if severe or prolonged
Signs of severe allergic reaction
Chest pain
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions (redness, pain, swelling; occasionally skin dimpling with long-term use)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain/tightness that doesn't resolve quickly or signs of severe allergic reaction after injection.
Rotate injection sites to reduce skin changes.
self_monitoring: Monitor injection sites for skin changes over time.
Track relapse frequency/symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Inject as soon as remembered; do not double up. Resume the regular schedule.

description: Treats certain brain tumors and Hodgkin lymphoma, taken orally at home between clinic visits.
typical_dosage: Individualized based on body surface area, set by your oncologist, typically given as a single dose repeated every 6 weeks.
typical_duration: Cyclical dosing per your oncologist's treatment plan, with blood count monitoring between doses.
directions_for_use: Take as a single dose exactly as directed by your oncologist, usually on an empty stomach with an antiemetic pre-medication.
Do not take more often than prescribed - delayed bone marrow suppression can accumulate.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and out of children's reach; capsule size/color may vary by dose - check that capsules match your prescription.
contraindications: Significantly decreased blood counts at the time of a planned dose (requires blood count check before each dose)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of delayed, cumulative bone marrow suppression: unusual bruising/bleeding, fever, signs of infection, fatigue - can occur weeks after a dose
Signs of lung toxicity: shortness of breath, dry cough, with cumulative doses
Signs of liver or kidney toxicity
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid live vaccines during treatment.
Avoid other bone-marrow suppressing OTC/Rx products unless directed by your oncologist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek prompt care for fever, signs of infection, unusual bruising/bleeding, or new shortness of breath.
Keep all scheduled blood count appointments before each dose.
self_monitoring: Blood counts checked before each dose (mandatory).
Periodic lung and kidney function tests per your oncologist.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team - do not take a missed dose without specific instructions, as dosing intervals are carefully spaced for safety.

description: Emergency treatment for severe low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) in people with diabetes who are unable to safely take sugar by mouth.
route: Subcutaneous/intramuscular injection (auto-injector or prefilled syringe) or intranasal
typical_dosage: One dose given at the first signs of severe hypoglycemia if the person cannot safely eat or drink, per your prescriber's action plan; call 911/emergency services after administration.
typical_duration: Used as needed for emergencies; keep available at all times if at risk for severe low blood sugar.
directions_for_use: Caregivers/family should be trained on use in advance.
Inject into the outer thigh, buttock, or upper arm per device instructions.
Turn the unconscious person on their side after administration (they may vomit upon waking).
Give oral carbohydrate once the person can swallow safely.
Seek emergency medical care after every use.
storage_instructions: Store per specific product instructions - some at room temperature; protect from light and heat. Check the expiration date regularly. Do not freeze.
contraindications: Certain rare tumor-related contraindications (pheochromocytoma, insulinoma) - not relevant to standard emergency use
severe_side_effects_seek_care: This medication IS the emergency treatment; seek emergency care if the person does not respond within 15 minutes of administration
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant interaction concerns given its emergency single-use nature.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call 911 if the person does not become responsive within 15 minutes, then give a second dose if available and directed.
Always seek follow-up medical evaluation after a severe hypoglycemia episode.
self_monitoring: Check the expiration date regularly.
Ensure caregivers/family know how and when to use it.
Keep glucose monitoring supplies available.
missed_dose_instructions: Not applicable - used only as needed for emergency severe hypoglycemia.

description: Reduces excessive drooling/saliva production and can be used to treat certain other conditions such as excessive sweating, as directed by a prescriber.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber, typically taken a few times daily.
typical_duration: Ongoing as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach (30-60 minutes before meals) for best absorption unless directed otherwise.
Take at consistent times.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction
Difficulty urinating (urinary retention)
Severe constipation or signs of bowel obstruction
Rapid heartbeat
Signs of overheating/heat intolerance (reduced sweating can increase heat stroke risk)
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased anticholinergic effects (confusion, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention) when combined with diphenhydramine or other anticholinergic OTC products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for inability to urinate, severe constipation, or signs of overheating/heat stroke.
Contact prescriber for eye pain (possible angle-closure glaucoma).
self_monitoring: Monitor for urinary retention or constipation.
Avoid overheating, especially in hot weather.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip. Do not double up.

drug_class: Combination antidiabetic - SGLT2 inhibitor + DPP-4 inhibitor
description: Improves blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes.
typical_dosage: One tablet once daily in the morning, with or without food, as directed by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day.
Maintain adequate hydration.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of ketoacidosis (can occur even with normal blood sugar): nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fatigue, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care
Signs of dehydration/low blood pressure, especially in elderly patients
Signs of a serious genital/perineal infection (Fournier's gangrene): severe pain or swelling in the genital area
Signs of pancreatitis: severe abdominal pain
New bone fractures or joint pain
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs may increase kidney risk.
Combining with other diabetes medications increases low blood sugar risk - monitor closely.
Stay well hydrated, especially with hot weather or illness (discuss sick-day dosing with prescriber).
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of ketoacidosis or severe genital pain/swelling.
Contact prescriber for signs of dehydration or recurrent infections.
self_monitoring: Home blood glucose monitoring.
Periodic kidney function tests.
Watch for genital/urinary infection symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip. Do not double up or take an extra dose.

description: Treats neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated plexiform neurofibromas in adults and children.
typical_dosage: Individualized based on body surface area, set by your specialist, generally taken twice daily on an empty stomach.
typical_duration: Continued as directed by your specialist based on response and tolerability.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after eating), twice daily about 12 hours apart.
Swallow capsules whole (do not open).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protected from moisture.
contraindications: None absolute; caution with pre-existing heart or eye conditions
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of heart failure/left ventricular dysfunction: shortness of breath, swelling, fatigue - requires periodic heart function monitoring
Signs of eye toxicity (retinal vein occlusion or retinal detachment): vision changes, eye pain
Severe skin reactions
Severe diarrhea/dehydration
Signs of elevated liver enzymes
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid starting any new medication without checking with your specialist given the complexity of this therapy.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek prompt care for vision changes, shortness of breath/swelling, or severe skin reactions.
Report persistent diarrhea.
self_monitoring: Periodic echocardiogram and eye exams (required).
Liver function tests.
Monitor skin and GI symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered if the next dose is not due soon (generally skip if within a few hours of the next dose); do not double up. Contact your specialist with questions.

description: Prevents nausea and vomiting associated with chemotherapy or radiation therapy.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - typically taken before chemotherapy and for a period afterward, or one patch applied prior to chemotherapy that lasts up to 7 days.
typical_duration: Short-term, around chemotherapy/radiation cycles.
directions_for_use: Take the oral tablet before chemotherapy as directed.
For the patch, apply to clean, dry, hairless skin on the upper outer arm at least 24 hours before chemotherapy and remove at least 24 hours after chemo completion (can be worn up to 7 days).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to granisetron or other 5-HT3 antagonists
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction
Irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation), especially with other QT-prolonging drugs
Signs of serotonin syndrome when combined with other serotonergic drugs (rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other serotonergic OTC products (high-dose dextromethorphan) increases serotonin syndrome risk.
Caution with other QT-prolonging medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for irregular heartbeat, severe constipation, or signs of allergic reaction (patch site reaction).
self_monitoring: Monitor nausea control.
Watch the patch site for skin reactions.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally used around chemotherapy sessions per a specific schedule - contact your oncology team if a dose is missed rather than taking one independently.

description: A purified human plasma protein given by injection twice weekly to prevent swelling attacks (hereditary angioedema) in people whose bodies do not make enough functional C1 esterase inhibitor.
dosage_forms: Lyophilized powder for subcutaneous injection (reconstituted with provided diluent)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist - commonly 60 international units/kg injected subcutaneously twice weekly, about 3-4 days apart.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing prophylaxis against hereditary angioedema attacks.
directions_for_use: Reconstitute exactly as trained by your care team using the supplied transfer device and diluent.
Inject into the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm, rotating sites.
Complete self-administration training with a healthcare provider before injecting at home.
Do not use if the solution is cloudy or contains particles.
storage_instructions: Store refrigerated; may be kept at room temperature for a limited time per the package insert. Protect from light. Use reconstituted product promptly per instructions.
contraindications: Known severe hypersensitivity (including anaphylaxis) to C1 esterase inhibitor products
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a blood clot: swelling, pain, redness in a limb, chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden severe headache - seek care immediately
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, wheezing, dizziness
Severe headache or vision changes (rare hypersensitivity reactions)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; this is a plasma protein replacement rather than a metabolized small-molecule drug.
Discuss with your prescriber before starting any new hormonal medications, as estrogen-containing products can independently trigger angioedema attacks.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for facial or throat swelling, trouble breathing, or signs of a blood clot.
Report persistent injection site reactions or new symptoms to your specialist.
self_monitoring: Keep a log of angioedema attacks and injection dates/sites.
Watch for and report signs of blood clots, especially with other clotting risk factors.
Attend follow-up visits for clinical response assessment.
missed_dose_instructions: Give the missed dose as soon as possible and resume the twice-weekly schedule; contact your prescriber if more than one dose is missed.

description: A very strong steroid cream, ointment, or lotion used short-term for stubborn inflammatory skin conditions like psoriasis and severe eczema that have not responded to weaker steroids.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to affected skin once or twice daily; do not exceed 50 g/week and do not use for more than 2 consecutive weeks unless directed by prescriber.
typical_duration: Short-term treatment (typically up to 2 weeks) due to high potency; long-term continuous use is avoided.
directions_for_use: Apply a thin film only to affected areas; rub in gently.
Wash hands after application unless hands are the treated area.
Do not use on the face, groin, or underarms, and avoid occlusive dressings/bandaging unless directed.
Do not use with other topical steroids at the same time unless instructed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tube/container tightly closed and away from children.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to halobetasol or other corticosteroids
Untreated skin infections at the application site
Use on large body surface areas or under occlusion without medical supervision
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of skin thinning, stretch marks, or easy bruising with prolonged use
Signs of systemic absorption: unusual tiredness, weight gain, rounded face (rare, with overuse)
Signs of skin infection at the treated site: increasing redness, warmth, pus
common_side_effects: Burning or stinging at application site
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC oral medication interactions expected since absorption is primarily local; avoid applying other topical products (e.g., other steroids, retinoids) to the same area at the same time without guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact your prescriber if you notice skin thinning, worsening irritation, or signs of infection.
Do not exceed the prescribed duration or amount - overuse increases risk of skin and systemic side effects.
self_monitoring: Track how long you have been using the medication; do not exceed 2 weeks without follow-up.
Check treated skin regularly for thinning or irritation.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered; if close to the next application, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: A vaccine that protects against hepatitis A virus infection, given as an injection, often administered by pharmacists for routine immunization or travel protection.
typical_dosage: A 2-dose series given 6-12 months apart (adult and pediatric formulations differ); individualized, set by your immunization provider.
typical_duration: 2-dose primary series; provides long-term (likely lifelong) immunity once completed.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider or pharmacist into the upper arm muscle.
Complete both doses of the series for full protection.
Bring your vaccination record to ensure the second dose is given on schedule.
storage_instructions: Stored refrigerated by the administering provider/pharmacy; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose of hepatitis A vaccine or any vaccine component (including neomycin)
Moderate to severe acute illness (vaccination should be postponed until recovery)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing, dizziness - seek emergency care immediately
High fever or unusual behavior changes after vaccination
common_side_effects: Soreness, redness, or swelling at the injection site
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used as needed for injection site soreness or fever after vaccination unless otherwise contraindicated.
Immunosuppressive medications (e.g., prednisone, methotrexate, tacrolimus) may reduce the vaccine's effectiveness; timing may need to be coordinated with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of anaphylaxis.
Report persistent high fever or unusual symptoms to your provider.
self_monitoring: Keep track of your vaccination dates to ensure the second dose is completed on time.
Watch the injection site for a few days for worsening redness or swelling.
missed_dose_instructions: If the second dose is delayed, it does not need to be restarted from the beginning - schedule it as soon as possible with your provider.

description: An injectable blood thinner used to prevent or treat blood clots; may be self-administered subcutaneously at home for clot prevention or used under medical supervision.
route: Subcutaneous injection (home use); intravenous (hospital/clinical setting only)
dosage_forms: Injectable solution (single-dose or multi-dose vials, prefilled syringes)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber based on indication and lab monitoring (e.g., low-dose subcutaneous injections for clot prevention).
typical_duration: Varies by indication - from short-term prevention after surgery to longer-term therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Inject subcutaneously into the abdomen, rotating sites, exactly as trained by your care team.
Do not rub the injection site after administration.
Do not adjust your dose without checking with your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from light unless otherwise directed; do not use if solution is discolored or contains particles.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in urine/stool, coughing up blood, prolonged bleeding from cuts - seek care immediately
Signs of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia: new clot symptoms (leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath) or unexplained low platelet counts
Severe headache, weakness, or vision changes (possible bleeding)
common_side_effects: Mild bleeding/bruising elsewhere on the body
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, and other NSAIDs unless directed - increased bleeding risk.
Increased bleeding risk when combined with other anticoagulants/antiplatelets (warfarin, apixaban, clopidogrel).
Herbal supplements like St. John's Wort and high-dose fish oil may further increase bleeding risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of serious bleeding or new clot symptoms.
Report any unusual bruising or bleeding to your prescriber promptly.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled blood tests (platelet counts, and aPTT if applicable).
Watch for and report unusual bruising or bleeding.
Use a soft toothbrush and electric razor to minimize bleeding risk.
missed_dose_instructions: Take/administer as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; contact your prescriber for guidance rather than doubling up.

description: A 2-dose hepatitis B vaccine given one month apart, commonly administered in pharmacies for adults needing hepatitis B protection.
typical_dosage: 2 doses given at least 4 weeks apart in adults 18 years and older; individualized, set by your immunization provider.
typical_duration: 2-dose primary series providing long-term protection.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider or pharmacist into the upper arm muscle.
Complete both doses at least 4 weeks apart for full protection.
Bring your vaccination record to your second appointment.
storage_instructions: Stored refrigerated by the administering provider/pharmacy; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose of any hepatitis B vaccine or vaccine component
Moderate to severe acute illness (postpone until recovery)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
High fever or unusual symptoms after vaccination
common_side_effects: Injection site soreness, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used as needed for injection site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated.
Immunosuppressive medications (e.g., prednisone, methotrexate, tacrolimus) may reduce vaccine effectiveness; timing may need to be coordinated with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of anaphylaxis.
Report persistent high fever or unusual symptoms to your provider.
self_monitoring: Track your vaccination dates to complete the 2-dose series on schedule.
Watch the injection site for a few days for worsening symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: If the second dose is delayed beyond 4 weeks, it does not need to be restarted - schedule it as soon as possible with your provider.

description: An oral antibiotic used to treat intestinal infections caused by certain parasites, such as intestinal amebiasis.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - commonly 25-35 mg/kg/day in divided doses with meals for 5-10 days depending on the infection.
typical_duration: Short course, typically 5-10 days.
directions_for_use: Take with meals to improve tolerability.
Complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
Drink plenty of fluids while taking this medication.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of hearing changes (ringing in ears, hearing loss) - though rare with oral use due to minimal absorption
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling - rare with oral use
Severe or persistent diarrhea, especially with blood or mucus (possible C. difficile infection)
otc_and_other_interactions: May enhance the effect of oral anticoagulants like warfarin by altering gut flora and vitamin K absorption - monitor INR closely.
Avoid other nephrotoxic or ototoxic medications when possible.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop and contact your prescriber for severe diarrhea, hearing changes, or signs of kidney problems.
Seek care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track bowel symptoms and confirm resolution with follow-up stool testing as directed.
Report any hearing changes or decreased urination.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food; if close to the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used long-term to manage autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and lupus, and to prevent or treat malaria.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - commonly 200-400 mg by mouth daily for autoimmune conditions, in divided doses.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for autoimmune conditions; short courses for malaria prevention/treatment.
directions_for_use: Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset.
Take at the same time(s) each day for autoimmune indications.
Do not stop abruptly without consulting your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Long-term use in children (weight-based dosing caution)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Vision changes, blurred vision, or difficulty seeing in dim light - seek prompt eye evaluation (risk of retinal toxicity with long-term use)
Irregular heartbeat, palpitations, or fainting (rare cardiac effects, especially with QT-prolonging combinations)
Signs of low blood sugar: shakiness, sweating, confusion
Unusual muscle weakness (rare myopathy)
otc_and_other_interactions: Antacids (aluminum/magnesium hydroxide) can reduce absorption - separate dosing by at least 4 hours.
May increase the blood-sugar-lowering effect of diabetes medications like glipizide or insulin - monitor for hypoglycemia.
Combining with other QT-prolonging medications (e.g., ondansetron, certain antibiotics) increases risk of heart rhythm problems.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek prompt care for vision changes or irregular heartbeat.
Report new muscle weakness or unusual symptoms to your prescriber.
self_monitoring: Get a baseline and then annual (or as directed) eye exam to screen for retinal toxicity.
Check blood sugar more frequently if also taking diabetes medications.
Report any vision changes immediately, even between scheduled exams.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A self-injectable medication used to treat acute attacks of hereditary angioedema (sudden swelling episodes) in adults.
typical_dosage: 30 mg injected subcutaneously into the abdomen at the onset of an angioedema attack; a second dose may be given if symptoms persist, per your prescriber's instructions (up to 3 doses in 24 hours).
typical_duration: As-needed for acute hereditary angioedema attacks; not a daily maintenance medication.
directions_for_use: Inject into the skin of the abdomen at the first sign of an attack.
Use a different injection site if a repeat dose is needed.
Complete self-injection training with your care team before using at home.
Seek emergency care if the attack involves the throat/airway, regardless of self-treatment.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protected from light; do not refrigerate or freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Throat/airway swelling, difficulty breathing or swallowing - call 911 immediately, this is a medical emergency regardless of treatment
Attack symptoms that do not improve or worsen after treatment
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions (redness, swelling, burning, itching - very common)
otc_and_other_interactions: May blunt the blood-pressure-lowering effect of ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) transiently; monitor blood pressure.
No significant OTC interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Always seek emergency care for throat or airway swelling, even after self-injecting.
Contact your prescriber if attacks are becoming more frequent or severe.
self_monitoring: Keep a log of angioedema attacks, triggers, and treatments used.
Always carry your emergency supply and know when to seek emergency care regardless of self-treatment.
missed_dose_instructions: Not applicable - this is an as-needed rescue medication used only during an acute attack, not on a fixed schedule.

description: An oral targeted cancer medication used to treat certain types of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), especially forms resistant to other treatments.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist based on response and side effects.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your oncologist, with regular reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food, exactly as prescribed.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
Do not stop or change the dose without talking to your oncology team.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep out of reach of children and pets.
contraindications: Use caution or avoid in patients with significant cardiovascular disease without close monitoring (boxed warning for arterial occlusion)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clots or arterial occlusion: chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side, slurred speech, vision loss, leg pain/swelling - seek emergency care immediately (boxed warning)
Signs of heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Signs of infection: fever, chills (from low blood counts)
Unusual bleeding or bruising
Severe abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) which can increase ponatinib levels and toxicity - discuss all new medications with your oncology team first.
St. John's Wort can reduce ponatinib effectiveness and should be avoided.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) may increase bleeding risk if platelet counts are low.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for any signs of blood clot, stroke, or heart attack.
Contact your oncology team promptly for fever, unusual bleeding, or signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled blood counts, liver function tests, and cardiovascular monitoring (blood pressure checks).
Monitor blood pressure at home if directed.
Report new symptoms promptly to your oncology team.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on the same day; if a full day is missed, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule the next day. Do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: An oral targeted therapy for adults with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that has a specific IDH2 gene mutation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly taken once daily; requires IDH2 mutation testing before starting.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy as directed by your oncology team, with regular reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or split.
Attend all scheduled monitoring visits, especially in the first 3 months (risk of differentiation syndrome).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and heat.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of differentiation syndrome: fever, cough, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain, swelling - seek immediate medical care (boxed warning, can be fatal if untreated)
Signs of tumor lysis syndrome: muscle cramps, weakness, decreased urination, nausea
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea leading to dehydration
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers, including St. John's Wort, which can reduce effectiveness.
Discuss all new prescription and OTC medications with your oncology team before starting, given the risk of differentiation syndrome requiring close monitoring.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek immediate medical care for fever, cough, or shortness of breath, especially in the first 3 months of treatment.
Contact your oncology team promptly for persistent nausea, vomiting, or signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled blood counts and liver function monitoring.
Weigh yourself regularly and report rapid weight gain or new swelling immediately.
Report new respiratory symptoms right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed or vomited, take the next dose at the regular scheduled time the next day - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: Eye drops used to prevent and treat pain and inflammation after cataract surgery.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) once daily, starting the day before surgery and continuing for a period directed by your eye surgeon (commonly through 2 weeks post-op).
typical_duration: Short-term, around the time of cataract surgery, as directed by your ophthalmologist.
directions_for_use: Shake well before use.
Wash hands before instilling drops; avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or any surface.
Wait at least 5 minutes between this and other eye drops.
Do not wear contact lenses during treatment unless approved by your eye doctor.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep the bottle tightly closed.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to nepafenac or other NSAIDs
Active or history of significant corneal disease (increased risk of corneal problems)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, redness, or vision changes that worsen - seek prompt evaluation (possible corneal problems)
Signs of eye infection: increasing discharge, severe redness
Delayed wound healing at the surgical site
otc_and_other_interactions: Minimal systemic absorption, so significant oral drug interactions are unlikely; however, combining with other topical NSAID or corticosteroid eye drops should be coordinated with your eye surgeon.
Use with other eye drops (e.g., antibiotic drops after surgery) as directed, spacing administration by several minutes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your eye surgeon promptly for worsening pain, redness, or vision changes.
Stop use and seek care for signs of infection or allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled post-operative eye exams.
Track your vision and report any sudden changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; then skip the missed dose. Do not double up.

description: An older-generation antidepressant also used for conditions like bedwetting (enuresis) in children and certain chronic pain syndromes.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - commonly starting at a low dose and gradually titrated based on response and tolerability.
typical_duration: Long-term for depression/chronic conditions; may be shorter courses for bedwetting.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, often in the evening due to sedation.
Do not stop abruptly - taper as directed by your prescriber to avoid withdrawal symptoms.
Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture, light, and children.
contraindications: Use with or within 14 days of MAO inhibitors (e.g., phenelzine)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Increased thoughts of suicide, especially in young adults (boxed warning) - seek immediate help
Irregular heartbeat, chest pain, or fainting
Severe confusion, hallucinations, or high fever with muscle rigidity (possible serotonin syndrome)
Signs of urinary retention or severe constipation
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other sedating OTC products like diphenhydramine - increased drowsiness and anticholinergic effects (confusion, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention).
Combining with tramadol or SSRIs (sertraline, escitalopram) increases the risk of serotonin syndrome.
Avoid St. John's Wort - risk of serotonin syndrome and reduced antidepressant effect.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, irregular heartbeat, fainting, or signs of serotonin syndrome.
Contact your prescriber immediately for worsening mood or suicidal thoughts.
self_monitoring: Monitor mood and report worsening depression or suicidal thoughts right away, especially when starting or changing doses.
Report constipation, urinary difficulty, or dizziness with standing.
Periodic ECG monitoring may be recommended, especially with pre-existing heart conditions.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A topical cream that stimulates the immune system to treat genital/perianal warts, actinic keratosis, and certain superficial skin cancers.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - commonly applied a few times per week (e.g., 3 times weekly for warts) and left on for a specified time before washing off.
typical_duration: Varies by indication, typically several weeks (e.g., up to 16 weeks for warts).
directions_for_use: Apply a thin layer to the affected area before bedtime, exactly as directed; leave on for the prescribed time (often 6-10 hours), then wash off with mild soap and water.
Wash hands before and after application.
Avoid sexual contact while the cream is on the skin (for genital wart treatment).
Do not use occlusive dressings unless directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; discard single-use packets after opening.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to imiquimod or cream components
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe local skin reactions: significant redness, swelling, blistering, or ulceration - contact your prescriber
Flu-like symptoms (fever, chills, muscle aches) - may occur with immune stimulation and usually resolve, but report if severe
Signs of skin infection at the application site
common_side_effects: Redness, itching, or burning at the application site
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic OTC drug interactions expected due to minimal absorption; avoid using other topical products on the treated area unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for severe local reactions or if symptoms do not improve.
Stop use and seek care for signs of secondary skin infection.
self_monitoring: Track your application schedule and the appearance of treated lesions.
Report lack of improvement or worsening symptoms at follow-up visits.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered, then resume your regular schedule; do not apply twice in one day to make up for a missed application.

description: A vaccine used both before exposure (for travelers, veterinarians, animal handlers) and after a potential rabies exposure (bite or scratch from an animal that may carry rabies) to prevent rabies infection.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your provider - pre-exposure series is typically 2-3 doses; post-exposure prophylaxis is typically 4 doses over about 2 weeks, given with rabies immune globulin if not previously vaccinated.
typical_duration: Short series (days to weeks) depending on pre- or post-exposure indication.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider into the deltoid (upper arm) muscle.
Complete the entire series on schedule - post-exposure prophylaxis is time-critical and must not be missed or delayed.
Seek care immediately after any animal bite or scratch, even before confirming vaccine need.
storage_instructions: Stored refrigerated by the administering provider; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component (post-exposure prophylaxis has no absolute contraindications given the fatal nature of untreated rabies)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
Neurological symptoms (rare): numbness, tingling, weakness
common_side_effects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used as needed for injection site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated.
Chloroquine and related antimalarials may reduce the immune response if given for pre-exposure prophylaxis; inform your provider of antimalarial use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of anaphylaxis.
Report unusual neurological symptoms to your provider promptly.
self_monitoring: Keep strict track of your dosing schedule, especially for post-exposure prophylaxis - missed or delayed doses can compromise protection.
Report the animal bite/exposure to local health authorities as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your provider immediately if a scheduled dose is missed, especially during post-exposure prophylaxis - do not skip or delay doses in this series.

description: An oral medication used to treat leishmaniasis, a parasitic infection transmitted by sandflies, affecting the skin or internal organs.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber, typically weight-based dosing over a 28-day course.
typical_duration: 28-day course as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce nausea.
Complete the entire 28-day course even if symptoms improve.
Use effective contraception during treatment and for 5 months after the last dose (risk of birth defects).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Women who could become pregnant and are not using effective contraception
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of pregnancy while taking this medication - contact your prescriber immediately
Severe vomiting or diarrhea leading to dehydration
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine
Signs of Stevens-Johnson syndrome: severe rash, blistering, peeling skin
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; take antiemetics as directed if nausea is severe.
Avoid other nephrotoxic medications when possible; discuss all medications with your prescriber given kidney/liver monitoring needs.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Contact your prescriber for persistent vomiting, diarrhea, or signs of organ toxicity.
self_monitoring: Attend scheduled kidney and liver function tests during treatment.
Confirm you are using effective contraception before and during treatment.
Track symptom improvement and attend follow-up visits to confirm cure.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. Contact your prescriber if multiple doses are missed.

description: An inhaled powder used as needed by people with Parkinson's disease to quickly treat sudden 'OFF' episodes (when oral levodopa/carbidopa temporarily wears off).
dosage_forms: Inhalation powder capsules (42 mg) for use with the provided inhaler
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your neurologist - commonly 2 capsules (84 mg) inhaled at the onset of OFF symptoms, up to 5 times per day as needed.
typical_duration: Used as-needed alongside your regular oral Parkinson's medication regimen.
directions_for_use: Use only with the inhaler device provided; do not swallow the capsules.
Load the capsule into the inhaler exactly as trained and inhale deeply per instructions.
Continue taking your regular oral carbidopa/levodopa medication as prescribed - this is an add-on, not a replacement.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original blister packaging; protect from moisture; discard the inhaler after 14 days of use.
contraindications: Asthma, COPD, or other chronic lung disease (risk of bronchospasm) without close monitoring
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden shortness of breath, wheezing, or cough (risk of bronchospasm, especially with lung disease)
New or worsening hallucinations, confusion, or unusual behavior changes
Sudden episodes of falling asleep during daily activities
Fainting or severe dizziness with standing
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid use with MAO inhibitors like phenelzine (risk of hypertensive crisis).
Antipsychotics and metoclopramide can reduce effectiveness of levodopa-based therapy.
High-protein meals close to dosing may reduce absorption/effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek prompt medical care for breathing difficulty or wheezing.
Contact your neurologist for new hallucinations, confusion, or worsening symptoms.
self_monitoring: Track the frequency and severity of OFF episodes and how well this medication helps.
Monitor breathing, especially if you have underlying lung disease - your prescriber may check lung function periodically.
Watch for signs of impulse control changes or excessive daytime sleepiness.
missed_dose_instructions: This is an as-needed medication used only during OFF episodes - there is no daily missed-dose schedule to follow.

description: A self-injectable growth-factor replacement used in children with severe primary insulin-like growth factor-1 deficiency to promote growth.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your pediatric endocrinologist based on body weight, given twice daily shortly before or after a meal/snack.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy until growth plates close or as directed by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Inject subcutaneously into the upper arm, thigh, buttock, or abdomen, rotating sites.
Give shortly before or after a meal or snack - do not administer if the child is unable to eat, due to risk of low blood sugar.
Complete injection training with your care team before administering at home.
storage_instructions: Store refrigerated; do not freeze. Protect from light. Discard vial per the manufacturer's in-use timeframe after first puncture.
contraindications: Active or suspected tumor (growth factors can promote tumor growth)
Known hypersensitivity to mecasermin or its components (contains benzyl alcohol - avoid in neonates)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe low blood sugar: sweating, shakiness, confusion, seizure - seek care immediately, especially if a dose is given without food
Signs of increased pressure in the brain: severe headache, vision changes, vomiting
Enlarged tonsils causing sleep apnea/breathing problems in children
Unusual lumps or rapid growth of any tissue
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions (redness, swelling, lipohypertrophy with repeated use in the same site)
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases the blood-sugar-lowering effect of diabetes medications (e.g., glipizide, insulin) - monitor for hypoglycemia closely.
Always give with food to reduce hypoglycemia risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe hypoglycemia or increased intracranial pressure.
Contact your specialist for new lumps, breathing problems during sleep, or lack of expected growth response.
self_monitoring: Monitor for signs of low blood sugar around dosing times, especially if a meal is skipped.
Attend all scheduled growth measurements and follow-up visits.
Rotate injection sites and check for skin changes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and it is not possible to eat afterward, skip that dose - do not inject without food. Resume the normal schedule at the next scheduled dose; do not double up.

description: A once-daily inhaled long-acting bronchodilator used for the maintenance treatment of COPD to help keep airways open.
dosage_forms: Dry powder inhaler (62.5 mcg per actuation)
typical_dosage: One inhalation (62.5 mcg) once daily, at the same time each day.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing maintenance therapy for COPD - not for acute symptom relief.
directions_for_use: Use at the same time every day for maintenance treatment; not a rescue inhaler for sudden breathing problems.
Do not shake the inhaler; follow the device's specific loading and inhalation technique.
Rinse mouth after use if desired (not required, but can reduce dry mouth).
Keep the inhaler dry; do not exhale into the mouthpiece.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep the inhaler cover closed when not in use; discard 6 weeks after opening the foil tray or when the dose counter reads 0.
contraindications: Severe hypersensitivity to milk proteins (contains lactose) or umeclidinium
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden worsening of breathing after use (paradoxical bronchospasm) - stop use and seek care immediately
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling
New or worsening eye pain, blurred vision, or halos around lights (possible narrow-angle glaucoma)
Difficulty urinating (possible urinary retention, especially with prostate enlargement)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other anticholinergic inhalers (e.g., ipratropium) unless directed - additive anticholinergic side effects.
Diphenhydramine and other anticholinergic OTC products (sleep aids, some cold medicines) can add to dry mouth, urinary retention, and constipation risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for sudden worsening breathing, chest tightness, or allergic reaction.
Contact your prescriber for eye pain, vision changes, or urinary difficulty.
self_monitoring: Track your breathing symptoms and rescue inhaler use; report increasing rescue inhaler need to your prescriber.
Check the dose counter on the inhaler regularly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if close to the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not use two doses at once.

description: An oral medication used to treat tardive dyskinesia (involuntary movements) and chorea associated with Huntington's disease.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - commonly started at 40 mg once daily and titrated up based on response and tolerability.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take once daily at the same time, with or without food.
Swallow capsules whole.
Do not stop or change your dose without consulting your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening depression, thoughts of suicide, or unusual mood changes - seek care promptly (increased risk in Huntington's disease patients)
Irregular heartbeat, palpitations, or fainting (QT prolongation risk)
Signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome: high fever, severe muscle stiffness, confusion
Difficulty swallowing, drowsiness affecting daily activities
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other sedating medications/OTC sleep aids like diphenhydramine - additive drowsiness.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) can increase valbenazine levels; dose adjustment may be needed.
Combining with other QT-prolonging medications (e.g., ondansetron) may increase risk of heart rhythm changes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for irregular heartbeat, fainting, or severe mood changes.
Contact your prescriber before starting new medications, especially strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
self_monitoring: Track movement symptom improvement and any new mood changes.
Report excessive drowsiness that interferes with daily activities.
Attend follow-up visits, especially early in treatment or after dose changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

drug_class: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor
description: An oral targeted cancer medication used, often in combination with immunotherapy, to treat advanced renal cell carcinoma (kidney cancer).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly started at 5 mg twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, and adjusted based on tolerability.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy as directed by your oncology team, with regular reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food, exactly as prescribed.
Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water.
Do not change your dose without talking to your oncology team.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and heat.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clots, heart attack, or stroke: chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side, slurred speech - seek emergency care immediately
Uncontrolled high blood pressure or hypertensive crisis symptoms (severe headache, vision changes)
Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/urine, coughing up blood
Signs of a hole forming in the stomach/intestine (GI perforation): severe abdominal pain
Signs of thyroid problems: fatigue, weight changes, cold intolerance
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, including clarithromycin and fluconazole - can significantly increase axitinib levels and toxicity.
St. John's Wort can reduce axitinib effectiveness and should be avoided.
NSAIDs may increase bleeding risk when platelet counts are low - use acetaminophen for pain when possible, as directed by your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of blood clot, stroke, heart attack, or severe bleeding.
Contact your oncology team for uncontrolled blood pressure, severe abdominal pain, or signs of thyroid/liver problems.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure at home regularly and report elevated readings.
Attend all scheduled blood counts, thyroid function, and liver function tests.
Watch for and report hand-foot skin changes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than a few hours, skip it and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: An oral combination medication used to treat myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML), allowing decitabine to be taken by mouth instead of by IV infusion.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly one tablet once daily on days 1-5 of each 28-day cycle.
typical_duration: Repeating 28-day cycles as directed by your oncology team, continued as long as clinically beneficial.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach - at least 2 hours after and no less than 2 hours before a meal.
Take at the same time each day for the 5 scheduled days of each cycle.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, split, or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to decitabine, cedazuridine, or components
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat (from low white blood cell counts) - seek care promptly
Unusual bleeding or bruising (from low platelet counts)
Severe fatigue or shortness of breath (from low red blood cell counts/anemia)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid live vaccines during treatment due to immune suppression.
Discuss all new OTC and prescription medications with your oncology team given the risk of low blood counts and infection.
NSAIDs may increase bleeding risk when platelet counts are low - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for fever, signs of infection, or significant bleeding/bruising.
Contact your oncology team for severe fatigue or shortness of breath.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled blood counts, especially before each new cycle.
Watch for and report fever, unusual bruising, or bleeding right away.
Track appetite, weight, and energy levels between visits.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, contact your oncology team for guidance rather than doubling up - do not take an extra dose to make up for a missed one.

description: An oral targeted therapy used to treat myelofibrosis, a bone marrow disorder, to help reduce spleen size and symptoms.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly 400 mg once daily on an empty stomach.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, on an empty stomach if possible (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal) to reduce nausea variability, or as directed.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush.
Anti-nausea medication may be prescribed before starting, given high rates of nausea/vomiting.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency (boxed warning for risk of serious encephalopathy) - must be corrected before starting
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of Wernicke's encephalopathy: confusion, unsteady walking, vision changes - seek emergency care immediately (boxed warning)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine
Signs of GI bleeding: black/tarry stools, vomiting blood
Signs of infection: fever, chills (from low blood counts)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) - can increase fedratinib levels and toxicity.
St. John's Wort can reduce fedratinib effectiveness and should be avoided.
Discuss thiamine (vitamin B1) status and supplementation with your oncology team before and during treatment.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for confusion, unsteady walking, or vision changes.
Contact your oncology team for persistent nausea/vomiting, signs of liver problems, or infection.
self_monitoring: Have thiamine levels checked before starting and periodically during treatment, per your oncology team.
Attend all scheduled blood counts and liver function tests.
Track weight and hydration status given high rates of GI side effects.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on the same day; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: A once-monthly long-acting injectable antipsychotic given by a healthcare provider to treat schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a healthcare provider)
dosage_forms: Extended-release injectable suspension (39, 78, 117, 156, or 234 mg prefilled syringe)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your psychiatric prescriber - typically started with specific initiation doses on day 1 and day 8, then a monthly maintenance dose in the deltoid or gluteal muscle.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing monthly maintenance therapy as directed by your psychiatric provider.
directions_for_use: Administered only by a healthcare provider - do not attempt to self-inject.
Keep all scheduled monthly injection appointments; missing appointments can allow symptoms to return.
Continue any other prescribed oral medications as directed until your provider says otherwise.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled by the administering pharmacy/clinic; not for home storage.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to paliperidone or risperidone
Increased mortality risk in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning - not approved for this use)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome: high fever, severe muscle stiffness, confusion, irregular heartbeat - seek emergency care immediately
Uncontrollable movements of the face/tongue/limbs (tardive dyskinesia)
Irregular heartbeat or fainting (QT prolongation)
Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision
New or worsening thoughts of suicide
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine) - additive drowsiness.
Combining with other QT-prolonging medications (e.g., ondansetron) increases risk of heart rhythm changes.
Alcohol can increase sedation and impair judgment/coordination.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or severe heart rhythm changes.
Contact your psychiatric provider for new abnormal movements, significant weight gain, or worsening mood.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled monthly injection appointments without delay.
Monitor weight, blood sugar, and cholesterol periodically as directed.
Report any unusual movements or mood changes to your care team.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber's office as soon as possible to reschedule if you miss a scheduled injection appointment - do not wait until your next planned date, as timing affects drug levels.

description: A long-acting antipsychotic injection given every 3 months by a healthcare provider to treat schizophrenia, for patients already stabilized on the once-monthly formulation for at least 4 months.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a healthcare provider)
dosage_forms: Extended-release injectable suspension (273, 410, 546, or 819 mg prefilled syringe)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your psychiatric prescriber based on your prior monthly (Invega Sustenna) dose; given once every 3 months in the deltoid or gluteal muscle.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing maintenance therapy given every 3 months as directed.
directions_for_use: Administered only by a healthcare provider - do not attempt to self-inject.
Only used after being adequately treated with the once-monthly formulation for at least 4 months.
Keep all scheduled quarterly injection appointments - this medication remains in the body for a long time, so timing matters.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled by the administering pharmacy/clinic; not for home storage.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to paliperidone or risperidone
Increased mortality risk in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning - not approved for this use)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome: high fever, severe muscle stiffness, confusion, irregular heartbeat - seek emergency care immediately
Uncontrollable movements of the face/tongue/limbs (tardive dyskinesia)
Irregular heartbeat or fainting (QT prolongation)
Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision
New or worsening thoughts of suicide
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine) - additive drowsiness.
Combining with other QT-prolonging medications (e.g., ondansetron) increases risk of heart rhythm changes.
Alcohol can increase sedation and impair judgment/coordination.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or severe heart rhythm changes.
Contact your psychiatric provider for new abnormal movements, significant weight gain, or worsening mood.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled quarterly injection appointments without delay - because the effects last a long time, both missed doses and any side effects can persist for months.
Monitor weight, blood sugar, and cholesterol periodically as directed.
Report any unusual movements or mood changes to your care team.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber's office promptly to reschedule if you miss a scheduled injection appointment - because of the long duration of action, your provider will give specific instructions based on how late the dose is.

description: The longest-acting antipsychotic injection available, given twice a year by a healthcare provider to treat schizophrenia, for patients already stabilized on the monthly or 3-month formulation.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a healthcare provider)
dosage_forms: Extended-release injectable suspension (1092 mg or 1560 mg prefilled syringe)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your psychiatric prescriber based on your prior paliperidone palmitate dose; given once every 6 months in the gluteal muscle.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing maintenance therapy given twice yearly as directed.
directions_for_use: Administered only by a healthcare provider - do not attempt to self-inject.
Only used after being adequately treated with the 1-month or 3-month formulation.
Keep all scheduled semi-annual injection appointments - this medication remains in the body for many months.
storage_instructions: Stored and handled by the administering pharmacy/clinic; not for home storage.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to paliperidone or risperidone
Increased mortality risk in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning - not approved for this use)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome: high fever, severe muscle stiffness, confusion, irregular heartbeat - seek emergency care immediately
Uncontrollable movements of the face/tongue/limbs (tardive dyskinesia)
Irregular heartbeat or fainting (QT prolongation)
Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision
New or worsening thoughts of suicide
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine) - additive drowsiness.
Combining with other QT-prolonging medications (e.g., ondansetron) increases risk of heart rhythm changes.
Alcohol can increase sedation and impair judgment/coordination.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or severe heart rhythm changes.
Contact your psychiatric provider for new abnormal movements, significant weight gain, or worsening mood.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled twice-yearly injection appointments without delay - side effects and drug levels can persist for many months given the very long duration of action.
Monitor weight, blood sugar, and cholesterol periodically as directed.
Report any unusual movements or mood changes to your care team.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber's office promptly to reschedule if you miss a scheduled injection appointment - your provider will give specific instructions, as the very long duration of action makes precise timing important.

description: A vaccine that protects against poliovirus infection, given as part of the routine childhood immunization schedule and to some adult travelers.
typical_dosage: Given as a 4-dose series in childhood per the routine immunization schedule, or as directed for adult travelers; individualized, set by your provider.
typical_duration: Completed per the childhood immunization schedule (doses at 2, 4, 6-18 months, and 4-6 years) or per travel recommendations for adults.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider into the arm or thigh muscle.
Follow the recommended immunization schedule for on-time doses.
Bring immunization records to each visit.
storage_instructions: Stored refrigerated by the administering provider; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose, or to neomycin, streptomycin, or polymyxin B
Moderate to severe acute illness (postpone until recovery)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
High fever or unusual symptoms after vaccination
common_side_effects: Injection site redness, swelling, or soreness
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used as needed for injection site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated.
Immunosuppressive medications (e.g., prednisone, methotrexate, tacrolimus) may reduce vaccine effectiveness; timing may need to be coordinated with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of anaphylaxis.
Contact your provider for high fever or unusual symptoms.
self_monitoring: Track your (or your child's) vaccination dates to complete the series on schedule.
Watch the injection site for a few days for worsening symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is delayed, it does not need to be restarted from the beginning - schedule the next dose as soon as possible with your provider.

description: An oral targeted cancer medication used in combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant to treat certain PIK3CA-mutated, hormone receptor-positive breast cancers.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly 9 mg once daily, used as part of a combination regimen with other cancer medications.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy as directed by your oncology team, with regular reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
Take alongside your other prescribed combination cancer medications exactly as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision, fruity breath odor - seek care promptly (hyperglycemia is common and can be serious)
Signs of severe skin reaction or rash with blistering
Signs of lung inflammation (pneumonitis): new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, fever
Severe or persistent diarrhea leading to dehydration
Signs of stomatitis: mouth sores/pain affecting eating
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) - can increase inavolisib levels and toxicity.
St. John's Wort can reduce inavolisib effectiveness and should be avoided.
Blood sugar should be monitored closely if also taking diabetes medications like glipizide or metformin.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for signs of high blood sugar, breathing changes, or severe skin reactions.
Contact your oncology team for persistent diarrhea, mouth sores, or fatigue.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood sugar as directed by your oncology team, especially in the first weeks of treatment.
Attend all scheduled blood counts and other monitoring tests.
Check your mouth regularly for sores and report eating difficulty.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is within 12 hours of the next dose - then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

drug_class: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel blocker (heart rate lowering agent)
description: An oral medication used to reduce heart rate and hospitalization risk in certain patients with chronic heart failure or stable symptomatic coronary artery disease.
