typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your cardiologist - commonly started at 5 mg twice daily with meals and adjusted based on heart rate response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your cardiologist.
directions_for_use: Take with meals to improve absorption.
Take exactly as prescribed twice daily; do not skip doses.
Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how this medication affects your vision (can cause temporary visual brightness changes).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Sick sinus syndrome, sinoatrial block, or 3rd-degree AV block unless a functioning pacemaker is present
Resting heart rate below 60 beats per minute before treatment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Very slow heart rate (bradycardia): dizziness, fainting, extreme fatigue - seek care promptly
Irregular heartbeat or palpitations (risk of atrial fibrillation)
Vision changes: temporary flashes of light or brightness (phosphenes) - report if bothersome or persistent
common_side_effects: Luminous visual phenomena (phosphenes, temporary brightness in vision)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors including clarithromycin, itraconazole, and certain antifungals - significantly increases ivabradine levels and bradycardia risk.
Fluconazole (a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor) can increase ivabradine levels - use with caution and monitor heart rate.
Combining with other heart-rate-lowering medications like metoprolol increases the risk of excessive bradycardia.
Grapefruit juice can increase ivabradine levels and should be avoided.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for fainting, very slow heart rate, or irregular heartbeat.
Contact your cardiologist about bothersome visual changes or before starting any new medication.
self_monitoring: Check your pulse/heart rate periodically at home as directed.
Report symptoms of very slow heart rate (dizziness, fainting) right away.
Attend all scheduled cardiology follow-up visits.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with a meal unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: An oral medication used to reduce the risk of relapse in children and adults with high-risk neuroblastoma who have already had a response to prior multi-agent treatment.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist based on body surface area, typically taken twice daily.
typical_duration: Extended maintenance therapy, often for up to 2 years, as directed by your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food, exactly as prescribed.
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew unless directed for a child unable to swallow whole tablets.
Attend all scheduled hearing tests during treatment.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Hearing changes or hearing loss - seek prompt evaluation (requires regular hearing monitoring)
Signs of low blood counts: fever, unusual bruising/bleeding, severe fatigue
Severe or persistent diarrhea or vomiting leading to dehydration
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions are well established; discuss all new medications with your oncology team given the need for close monitoring.
Avoid other ototoxic medications when possible, given the risk of hearing changes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncology team promptly for hearing changes, fever, or unusual bleeding.
Seek care for severe dehydration from diarrhea or vomiting.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled hearing (audiometry) tests before and during treatment.
Attend all scheduled blood count monitoring.
Track diarrhea/vomiting frequency and hydration status.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose; then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: A vaccine used to prevent disease caused by chikungunya virus, typically given to adults traveling to or living in areas where chikungunya is common.
typical_dosage: A single dose administered by a healthcare provider; individualized, set by your travel medicine or immunization provider.
typical_duration: Single-dose vaccination; timing before travel should be discussed with your provider (at least 2 weeks before potential exposure).
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider into the upper arm muscle.
Plan vaccination at least 2 weeks before travel to an at-risk area to allow immunity to develop.
Discuss your full health history with your provider, as this is a live vaccine.
storage_instructions: Stored refrigerated/frozen by the administering provider; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
Severe joint pain, high fever, or symptoms resembling a chikungunya-like illness after vaccination (reported in some recipients, especially older adults) - seek care if severe
New or worsening heart problems after vaccination (rare reports)
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used as needed for post-vaccination fever or discomfort unless otherwise contraindicated.
Immunosuppressive medications (e.g., prednisone, methotrexate, tacrolimus) may reduce vaccine effectiveness and increase risk since this is a live vaccine - discuss timing with your provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your provider for severe joint pain, high fever, or new cardiac symptoms after vaccination.
self_monitoring: Monitor for fever, joint pain, or unusual symptoms for the first couple of weeks after vaccination, especially if you are 60 or older.
Keep a record of your vaccination date for future travel documentation.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a single-dose vaccine; if travel plans change, discuss timing with your provider - no repeat dosing schedule applies.

description: A vaccine given to travelers to certain parts of Asia to protect against Japanese encephalitis, a mosquito-borne viral brain infection.
typical_dosage: A 2-dose series given 28 days apart (adults); individualized, set by your travel medicine provider, completed at least 1 week before travel.
typical_duration: 2-dose primary series; a booster may be recommended after 1 year for continued risk.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider into the upper arm muscle.
Complete both doses at least 1 week before potential exposure/travel.
Bring your vaccination record to your second appointment.
storage_instructions: Stored refrigerated by the administering provider; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component
Moderate to severe acute illness (postpone until recovery)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately, including delayed reactions up to several days after vaccination
High fever or unusual symptoms after vaccination
common_side_effects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used as needed for injection site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated.
Immunosuppressive medications (e.g., prednisone, methotrexate, tacrolimus) may reduce vaccine effectiveness; timing may need to be coordinated with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of allergic reaction, even if delayed by several days.
Contact your provider for high fever or unusual symptoms.
self_monitoring: Track your vaccination dates to complete the 2-dose series on schedule before travel.
Watch for delayed allergic reactions for up to 10 days after vaccination, as advised by your provider.
missed_dose_instructions: If the second dose is delayed, it does not need to be restarted from the beginning - schedule it as soon as possible with your provider, ideally still before travel.

description: An oral targeted medication used to treat myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera, and chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) by reducing overactive immune/bone marrow signaling.
dosage_forms: Tablet (5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg, 20 mg, 25 mg)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist based on indication, blood counts, and kidney/liver function.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed, with regular reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food, exactly as prescribed.
Swallow tablets whole; if unable to swallow, may be given via nasogastric tube per specific instructions from your care team.
Do not stop this medication abruptly - stopping suddenly can cause a serious withdrawal-like flare of symptoms; taper only as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serious infection: fever, chills, cough, burning with urination - seek care promptly (increased infection risk, including tuberculosis reactivation and shingles)
Signs of a blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath
Signs of new skin cancers: unusual moles or skin lesions
Unusual bleeding or bruising
Sudden worsening of myelofibrosis symptoms after stopping the medication
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) - significantly increases ruxolitinib levels and side effect risk; dose adjustment is often needed.
St. John's Wort can reduce ruxolitinib effectiveness and should be avoided.
NSAIDs may increase bleeding risk when platelet counts are low - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for signs of infection, blood clot, or significant bleeding.
Contact your specialist before stopping this medication - abrupt discontinuation can cause serious symptom flare.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled blood counts, especially when starting or changing doses.
Watch for and report signs of infection promptly.
Have regular skin checks for new or changing skin lesions.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up, and never stop abruptly without consulting your specialist.

description: A combination tablet for type 2 diabetes that pairs sitagliptin (which increases insulin release after meals) with metformin (which reduces glucose production by the liver).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - commonly one tablet twice daily with meals, based on current sitagliptin and metformin doses.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for type 2 diabetes management.
directions_for_use: Take with meals to reduce stomach upset and improve blood sugar control.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
Continue diet and exercise recommendations from your care team.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: History of severe allergic reaction (including anaphylaxis) to sitagliptin
Use around the time of procedures requiring IV contrast dye (temporary hold required)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, difficulty breathing, severe tiredness, unusual stomach discomfort - seek emergency care immediately (rare but serious with metformin)
Signs of pancreatitis: severe abdominal pain radiating to the back, persistent nausea/vomiting
Signs of severe allergic reaction or skin reaction (rash, blistering) - associated with sitagliptin
Joint pain that is severe or disabling (reported with DPP-4 inhibitors)
otc_and_other_interactions: Alcohol increases the risk of lactic acidosis with metformin - avoid excessive alcohol use.
Combining with other diabetes medications (e.g., glipizide) increases the risk of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia).
Iodinated contrast dye used in some imaging studies requires temporarily stopping this medication - inform your radiology team you take this medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of lactic acidosis or severe allergic reaction.
Contact your prescriber for severe abdominal pain or joint pain.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed by your prescriber and keep a log.
Attend scheduled kidney function and vitamin B12 level checks (metformin can lower B12 with long-term use).
Watch for and report signs of low blood sugar if taking other diabetes medications.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: An extended-release combination tablet for type 2 diabetes that pairs sitagliptin with an extended-release form of metformin, taken once daily.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - commonly one or two tablets once daily with the evening meal, based on current sitagliptin and metformin doses.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for type 2 diabetes management.
directions_for_use: Take once daily with the evening meal.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, cut, or chew extended-release tablets.
It is normal to notice the tablet shell in the stool - the medication has already been absorbed.
Continue diet and exercise recommendations from your care team.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: History of severe allergic reaction (including anaphylaxis) to sitagliptin
Use around the time of procedures requiring IV contrast dye (temporary hold required)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, difficulty breathing, severe tiredness, unusual stomach discomfort - seek emergency care immediately (rare but serious with metformin)
Signs of pancreatitis: severe abdominal pain radiating to the back, persistent nausea/vomiting
Signs of severe allergic reaction or skin reaction (rash, blistering) - associated with sitagliptin
Joint pain that is severe or disabling (reported with DPP-4 inhibitors)
otc_and_other_interactions: Alcohol increases the risk of lactic acidosis with metformin - avoid excessive alcohol use.
Combining with other diabetes medications (e.g., glipizide) increases the risk of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia).
Iodinated contrast dye used in some imaging studies requires temporarily stopping this medication - inform your radiology team you take this medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of lactic acidosis or severe allergic reaction.
Contact your prescriber for severe abdominal pain or joint pain.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed by your prescriber and keep a log.
Attend scheduled kidney function and vitamin B12 level checks (metformin can lower B12 with long-term use).
Watch for and report signs of low blood sugar if taking other diabetes medications.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food on the same day unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule the next day. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted cancer medication used to treat certain B-cell cancers, including mantle cell lymphoma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia, especially after prior BTK inhibitor therapy.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly 200 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy as directed by your oncology team, with regular reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew.
Do not change your dose without talking to your oncology team.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serious infection: fever, chills, cough - seek care promptly
Unusual bleeding or bruising
Irregular heartbeat, palpitations, or fainting (risk of atrial fibrillation)
Signs of tumor lysis syndrome: muscle cramps, weakness, decreased urination
New or worsening shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) - can increase pirtobrutinib levels and toxicity.
St. John's Wort can reduce pirtobrutinib effectiveness and should be avoided.
Increased bleeding risk when combined with anticoagulants (warfarin, apixaban) or antiplatelets (clopidogrel, aspirin) - discuss all medications with your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for signs of infection, significant bleeding, or irregular heartbeat.
Contact your oncology team for new shortness of breath or unusual symptoms.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled blood counts and cardiac monitoring.
Watch for and report signs of infection or unusual bruising/bleeding.
Check your pulse periodically if you have a history of heart rhythm problems.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on the same day; if it is the next day, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: A topical solution applied to the toenails or fingernails to treat fungal nail infections (onychomycosis).
typical_dosage: Apply to the entire affected nail surface, nail bed, and under the tip of the nail once daily.
typical_duration: Typically 48 weeks of daily use, as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Apply once daily to clean, dry nails, covering the entire nail surface, folds, nail bed, and under the nail tip.
Allow to dry before putting on socks or shoes.
Do not use nail polish or other cosmetic nail products on treated nails unless directed.
Continue treatment for the full recommended duration, as nail regrowth is slow.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep away from open flame (contains flammable ingredients).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to efinaconazole or other azole antifungals
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe local skin/nail reaction: significant redness, blistering, pain, or swelling around the nail
Signs of allergic skin reaction: widespread rash, itching
otc_and_other_interactions: Minimal systemic absorption, so significant oral drug interactions are not expected; avoid applying other nail/skin products to the same area unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact your prescriber for significant irritation, blistering, or allergic reaction.
Continue routine follow-up to assess treatment response, as visible improvement takes months.
self_monitoring: Track nail appearance over time and take photos to monitor slow regrowth progress.
Report lack of any improvement after several months of consistent use.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered, then resume your regular daily schedule; do not apply twice in one day to make up for a missed application.

description: A two-drug, single-tablet regimen used as a complete treatment for HIV-1 in adults who are already virologically suppressed on a stable antiretroviral regimen.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily, taken with a meal.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as a complete HIV treatment regimen.
directions_for_use: Take with a meal every day - absorption of rilpivirine depends on food.
Take at the same time each day to maintain steady drug levels.
Do not stop or skip doses, as this can lead to drug resistance.
Tell every prescriber and pharmacist you see that you take this medication before starting anything new, including acid reducers.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Coadministration with acid-reducing medications: proton pump inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole) are contraindicated
Coadministration with certain anticonvulsants (e.g., carbamazepine, phenytoin), rifampin, or St. John's Wort
Coadministration with systemic dexamethasone (more than a single dose)
Known hypersensitivity to dolutegravir or rilpivirine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Signs of severe skin/allergic reaction: rash with fever, blistering, mouth sores
New or worsening depression or thoughts of suicide (reported with dolutegravir)
Irregular heartbeat (rilpivirine can affect heart rhythm at high doses/interactions)
otc_and_other_interactions: Proton pump inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole) are contraindicated - they significantly reduce rilpivirine absorption and can cause treatment failure.
H2 blockers (e.g., famotidine) must be timed carefully (well before or after this medication) if used at all - discuss with your HIV specialist.
Calcium, iron, magnesium, or aluminum-containing antacids and supplements can reduce dolutegravir absorption - separate dosing by several hours.
St. John's Wort can drastically reduce drug levels and risk treatment failure - avoid completely.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for signs of liver problems, severe skin reaction, or worsening depression.
Contact your HIV specialist before starting any new prescription or OTC medication, especially acid reducers.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled viral load and CD4 count monitoring.
Take doses consistently with food to maintain effectiveness and prevent resistance.
Report mood changes to your care team.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose with food as soon as remembered if within 12 hours of the scheduled time; if more than 12 hours late, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not double up.

description: An oral medication used to slow kidney function decline in adults at risk of rapidly progressing autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).
dosage_forms: Tablet (various split-dose strengths per REMS program packaging)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your nephrologist - typically a split morning/afternoon dosing regimen, titrated based on tolerability under a required monitoring program (REMS).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed, with mandatory periodic liver function monitoring.
directions_for_use: Take the first (larger) dose upon waking and the second dose 8 hours later, exactly as directed.
Ensure access to water and a bathroom throughout the day, as this medication causes increased urination and thirst.
Avoid taking the second dose too close to bedtime to reduce nighttime urination.
Participate in the required REMS liver monitoring program - this medication is only available through specially certified pharmacies.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Significant liver disease or elevated liver enzymes with symptoms
Inability to sense or respond to thirst
Concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, right upper abdominal pain - seek care immediately (boxed warning for serious liver injury)
Signs of dehydration: excessive thirst, dizziness, very dark urine, confusion
Signs of high sodium levels: confusion, muscle twitching, seizures
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, including clarithromycin and fluconazole - significantly increases tolvaptan levels and liver injury risk.
St. John's Wort can reduce tolvaptan effectiveness and should be avoided.
Stay well hydrated; avoid excessive salt restriction unless directed, given the medication's effect on water balance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of liver injury or severe dehydration.
Contact your nephrologist before starting any new prescription or OTC medication.
self_monitoring: Attend all required liver function tests as part of the REMS program (typically monthly for the first 18 months, then periodically).
Weigh yourself regularly and stay adequately hydrated.
Report excessive thirst, confusion, or reduced urination promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If the morning dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered, but skip it if it is late in the day; skip the second dose if not taken within the recommended window to avoid nighttime urination. Do not double up - contact your nephrologist with questions.

generic_name: Mpox and smallpox vaccine, live non-replicating (MVA-BN)
description: A vaccine used to prevent mpox (formerly monkeypox) and smallpox in adults at high risk of exposure.
typical_dosage: 2 doses given 4 weeks apart; individualized, set by your immunization provider.
typical_duration: 2-dose primary series for full protection.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider, typically in the upper arm.
Complete both doses 4 weeks apart for full protection.
Bring your vaccination record to your second appointment.
storage_instructions: Stored frozen or refrigerated by the administering provider; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component (including chicken/egg protein, gentamicin, or ciprofloxacin residuals)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
Chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations (rare reports of myocarditis/pericarditis after vaccination)
common_side_effects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used as needed for injection site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated.
Immunosuppressive medications (e.g., prednisone, methotrexate, tacrolimus) may reduce vaccine effectiveness; discuss timing with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of anaphylaxis.
Seek prompt care for chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations after vaccination.
self_monitoring: Track your vaccination dates to complete the 2-dose series on schedule.
Watch the injection site and overall symptoms for several days after each dose.
missed_dose_instructions: If the second dose is delayed, it does not need to be restarted from the beginning - schedule it as soon as possible with your provider.

description: A combination antiretroviral medication used with other HIV medications to treat HIV-1 infection; ritonavir is included as a booster to increase lopinavir levels.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your HIV specialist - commonly 400/100 mg (two 200/50 mg tablets) twice daily, taken with or without food depending on formulation.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of a complete antiretroviral regimen.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed with your other HIV medications, at the same times each day.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
Do not skip doses, as this can lead to drug resistance.
storage_instructions: Store tablets at room temperature; oral solution requires refrigeration or room-temperature storage depending on formulation and should be used within the labeled timeframe.
contraindications: Coadministration with numerous drugs highly dependent on CYP3A for clearance, including simvastatin and lovastatin (risk of severe myopathy/rhabdomyolysis)
Coadministration with certain sedatives (e.g., triazolam, oral midazolam)
Known hypersensitivity to lopinavir or ritonavir
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of pancreatitis: severe abdominal pain radiating to the back, persistent nausea/vomiting - seek care immediately
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Irregular heartbeat (PR/QT interval effects) - palpitations, fainting
Signs of high blood sugar or new/worsening diabetes: increased thirst, frequent urination
otc_and_other_interactions: Simvastatin is contraindicated with this medication due to a high risk of severe muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis) - use an alternative statin (e.g., atorvastatin, pravastatin) at a reduced dose under specialist guidance.
St. John's Wort can drastically reduce lopinavir/ritonavir levels and cause treatment failure - avoid completely.
Significantly increases sildenafil levels - risk of prolonged erection and low blood pressure; do not use sildenafil at usual doses without specific guidance from your HIV specialist.
Many other drug interactions are possible via CYP3A4; always check with your HIV specialist or pharmacist before starting any new prescription or OTC medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of pancreatitis, severe allergic reaction, or irregular heartbeat.
Contact your HIV specialist before starting any new medication, including OTC products and supplements.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled viral load, CD4 count, lipid panel, and blood sugar monitoring.
Take doses consistently to prevent drug resistance.
Report new abdominal pain or signs of liver problems promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

drug_class: CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) potentiator
description: An oral targeted medication for cystic fibrosis in patients with specific CFTR gene mutations, used to improve the function of the defective protein responsible for the disease.
dosage_forms: Granules for oral suspension (25 mg, 50 mg, 75 mg packets)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your cystic fibrosis specialist based on age, weight, and genetic mutation - commonly 150 mg every 12 hours with fat-containing food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed, requiring confirmed eligible CFTR mutation.
directions_for_use: Take with fat-containing food (e.g., eggs, butter, cheese, nuts) to ensure adequate absorption.
Take approximately every 12 hours, at the same times each day.
Do not consume grapefruit or grapefruit juice while taking this medication.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, right upper abdominal pain - seek care promptly (liver function monitoring required)
Vision changes (cataracts have been reported in children - periodic eye exams recommended)
Severe abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice - can increase ivacaftor levels.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors including clarithromycin and fluconazole, which can increase ivacaftor levels; dose adjustment may be needed with moderate inhibitors.
St. John's Wort can reduce ivacaftor effectiveness and should be avoided.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your specialist promptly for signs of liver problems or vision changes.
Seek care for severe abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled liver function tests, especially in the first year of treatment.
Attend recommended eye exams, particularly for children.
Track lung function and nutritional status at routine cystic fibrosis clinic visits.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose with fat-containing food as soon as remembered if within 6 hours of the scheduled time; otherwise skip it and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not double up.

description: A combination birth control pill containing the progestin ethynodiol diacetate and the estrogen ethinyl estradiol, available in two estrogen-dose strengths (35 mcg and 50 mcg), used to prevent pregnancy.
dosage_forms: Tablet, 28-day pack (ethynodiol diacetate 1 mg with ethinyl estradiol 35 mcg or 50 mcg)
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth at the same time every day, in the exact order provided in the pack.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing contraception as long as pregnancy prevention is desired.
directions_for_use: Take one pill at the same time every day, following the exact order printed on the pack.
Start a new pack immediately after finishing the previous one.
Use a backup contraceptive method (e.g., condoms) for the first 7 days if starting mid-cycle.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep in original packaging to maintain the correct pill order.
contraindications: History of blood clots (DVT/PE), stroke, or heart attack
Known or suspected breast cancer or estrogen-dependent tumor
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, vision changes, weakness on one side of the body - seek emergency care immediately
Severe abdominal pain (possible liver or gallbladder problem)
Yellowing of skin/eyes (jaundice)
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception if taking this supplement.
Certain antibiotics and antifungals may reduce effectiveness; ask your pharmacist about backup contraception when starting a new medication.
Smoking significantly increases the risk of serious cardiovascular side effects with estrogen-containing contraceptives.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of blood clot, stroke, or heart attack.
Contact your prescriber for persistent or heavy breakthrough bleeding, severe abdominal pain, or jaundice.
self_monitoring: Track your pill-taking to ensure no doses are missed.
Monitor blood pressure periodically as recommended by your prescriber.
Report new severe headaches, vision changes, or leg swelling right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If a pill is missed by less than 24 hours, take it as soon as remembered and continue the pack as normal. If more than 24 hours late, follow the package insert instructions and use backup contraception for 7 days; consider emergency contraception if pills were missed after unprotected sex.

description: An oral medication used to reduce the risk of kidney function decline, kidney failure, and cardiovascular events in adults with chronic kidney disease associated with type 2 diabetes.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber based on kidney function (eGFR) and potassium levels - commonly 10-20 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed, with regular potassium and kidney function monitoring.
directions_for_use: Take once daily, with or without food, at the same time each day.
Swallow tablets whole, or crush and mix with water/apple sauce and use immediately if unable to swallow whole.
Do not use potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high potassium (hyperkalemia): muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, tingling - seek care promptly, this is the most important risk to monitor
Signs of low blood pressure: dizziness, fainting
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium unless directed by your prescriber - risk of dangerous hyperkalemia.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, including clarithromycin - significantly increases finerenone levels and hyperkalemia risk.
Combining with ACE inhibitors/ARBs (e.g., lisinopril, losartan) or other potassium-sparing diuretics increases the risk of high potassium - regular monitoring is required.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) may reduce effectiveness and increase kidney/potassium risks.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or signs of high potassium.
Contact your prescriber before starting any new medication, especially other blood pressure medications or supplements.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled potassium level and kidney function (eGFR) checks, especially after starting or changing the dose.
Avoid high-potassium salt substitutes and report any muscle weakness or heart palpitations.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on the same day; if it is the next day, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A self-injectable biologic medication used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis by targeting and reducing certain immune cells (B-cells).
dosage_forms: Prefilled Sensoready pen or prefilled syringe (20 mg/0.4 mL)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your neurologist - typically weekly loading doses (weeks 0, 1, and 2), then monthly maintenance injections starting week 4.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your neurologist.
directions_for_use: Inject subcutaneously into the abdomen, thigh, or outer upper arm, rotating sites.
Allow the pen/syringe to reach room temperature before injecting, per instructions.
Complete self-injection training with your care team before injecting at home.
Your first injection is typically given under medical supervision.
storage_instructions: Store refrigerated; may be stored at room temperature for a limited time per the package insert. Protect from light. Do not freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, persistent cough, burning with urination - seek care promptly (increased infection risk)
Signs of hepatitis B reactivation: fatigue, yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine
New neurological symptoms: this medication carries a rare risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) - report new confusion, vision changes, or weakness
Signs of injection reaction: fever, chills, rash, especially with the first few doses
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid live vaccines while on this medication and for a period after stopping - discuss vaccination timing with your neurologist.
Increased infection risk when combined with other immunosuppressants (e.g., prednisone, methotrexate) - discuss all medications with your care team.
No significant OTC drug interactions expected, but report all new medications to your neurologist given infection risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for fever, signs of infection, or new neurological symptoms.
Report injection reactions, especially with early doses, to your care team.
self_monitoring: Get hepatitis B screening before starting, as directed.
Monitor for and report any signs of infection promptly.
Attend all scheduled follow-up visits and any recommended blood tests (e.g., immunoglobulin levels).
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible and resume the monthly schedule from that date; contact your neurologist for specific guidance based on how many doses were missed.

description: A self-injectable biologic medication used to treat rheumatoid arthritis and certain rare inflammatory conditions (cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes) by blocking IL-1 activity.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - commonly 100 mg injected subcutaneously once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Inject subcutaneously at approximately the same time each day, rotating sites (abdomen, thigh, upper arm).
Allow the prefilled syringe to warm to room temperature for about 30 minutes before injecting.
Complete self-injection training with your care team before injecting at home.
Do not shake the syringe.
storage_instructions: Store refrigerated; do not freeze. Protect from light.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to E. coli-derived proteins or anakinra components
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serious infection: fever, chills, persistent cough - seek care promptly (increased infection risk)
Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing
Unusual bruising or bleeding (rare low blood count effects)
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions (redness, swelling, itching - very common in the first month)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other biologic immunosuppressants (e.g., other IL-1 blockers or TNF inhibitors) - significantly increased infection risk.
Combining with methotrexate is common in rheumatoid arthritis treatment but requires close infection monitoring.
Avoid live vaccines while on this medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for fever or signs of serious infection.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Watch for and report signs of infection promptly.
Attend scheduled blood count monitoring, especially in the first months of treatment.
Track injection site reactions, which usually improve over the first month.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the normal daily schedule. Do not double up.

generic_name: Diphtheria, tetanus, acellular pertussis, and inactivated poliovirus vaccine (DTaP-IPV)
description: A combination vaccine that protects children against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis (whooping cough), and polio, given as a booster dose.
typical_dosage: A single booster dose given at 4-6 years of age, following completion of the primary DTaP and IPV series; individualized, set by your pediatric provider.
typical_duration: Single booster dose per the routine childhood immunization schedule.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider into the upper arm or thigh muscle.
Given only as a booster after completion of the primary DTaP and IPV vaccine series.
Bring immunization records to confirm eligibility and timing.
storage_instructions: Stored refrigerated by the administering provider; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component (including neomycin or polymyxin B)
Encephalopathy within 7 days of a previous pertussis-containing vaccine not attributable to another cause
Progressive neurological disorder (postpone until condition stabilizes)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
High fever, persistent inconsolable crying, or seizure
common_side_effects: Injection site redness, swelling, or soreness
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen may be used for fever or discomfort after vaccination per pediatrician guidance.
No significant interactions with other routine childhood vaccines given at the same visit at different sites.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or seizure.
Contact the pediatrician for high fever or persistent inconsolable crying.
self_monitoring: Track the child's immunization schedule to confirm all doses are up to date.
Monitor for fever or injection site reactions for 24-48 hours after vaccination.
missed_dose_instructions: If this booster is delayed, it does not need to be restarted - schedule it as soon as possible with the pediatric provider.

description: An oral targeted cancer medication used, in combination with hormone therapy, to treat certain types of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly taken once daily for 21 days followed by 7 days off (28-day cycle), in combination with hormone therapy.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy in repeating cycles as directed by your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take at approximately the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not chew or crush.
Follow the 21-days-on, 7-days-off schedule exactly, or as directed by your oncologist.
Attend all scheduled ECG (heart rhythm) monitoring appointments.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Significant QT interval prolongation or uncontrolled electrolyte abnormalities
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, palpitations, dizziness, or fainting (QT prolongation) - seek care immediately
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Signs of infection: fever, chills (from low white blood cell counts)
New or worsening shortness of breath or cough (rare interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, including clarithromycin and fluconazole - significantly increases ribociclib levels and QT prolongation risk.
St. John's Wort can reduce ribociclib effectiveness and should be avoided.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications, including ondansetron, when possible - discuss with your oncology team.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for irregular heartbeat, fainting, or severe dizziness.
Contact your oncology team for fever, signs of infection, or new breathing symptoms.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled ECGs, especially at treatment start and after dose changes.
Attend all scheduled blood counts and liver function tests.
Report new or worsening cough or shortness of breath promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed or vomited, do not take an extra dose that day - take the next dose at the regular scheduled time. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: An oral targeted medication used in children with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) to treat symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist based on body surface area, typically taken twice daily on an empty stomach.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal.
Swallow capsules whole with water; do not open, crush, or chew.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of heart problems: shortness of breath, swelling, chest pain (reduced heart function/cardiomyopathy has been reported) - seek care promptly
Vision changes, eye pain, or seeing halos around lights (retinal vein occlusion, retinal pigment epithelial detachment) - seek prompt eye evaluation
Severe or persistent diarrhea leading to dehydration
Signs of skin toxicity: severe rash or skin breakdown
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, including clarithromycin and fluconazole - can increase selumetinib levels and toxicity.
St. John's Wort can reduce selumetinib effectiveness and should be avoided.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for shortness of breath, chest pain, or vision changes.
Contact your specialist for persistent vomiting/diarrhea or severe skin reactions.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled heart function tests (echocardiogram) and eye exams.
Track skin changes and diarrhea/vomiting frequency.
Attend all scheduled growth and development monitoring visits.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed or vomited, do not take a replacement dose - wait and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted cancer medication used to treat non-small cell lung cancer and certain colorectal cancers that have a specific KRAS G12C gene mutation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly 600 mg taken twice daily.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy as directed by your oncology team, with regular reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew.
Attend all scheduled ECG (heart rhythm) monitoring appointments.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, palpitations, dizziness, or fainting (QT prolongation) - seek care immediately
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine
New or worsening shortness of breath or cough (possible pneumonitis/interstitial lung disease)
Severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea leading to dehydration
otc_and_other_interactions: Acid-reducing medications, including proton pump inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole), can significantly reduce adagrasib absorption - if an acid reducer is needed, your oncology team will advise on timing or alternatives (e.g., H2 blockers dosed apart, or antacids spaced several hours away).
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, including clarithromycin and fluconazole - can increase adagrasib levels and toxicity.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications, including ondansetron, when possible - discuss with your oncology team.
St. John's Wort can reduce adagrasib effectiveness and should be avoided.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for irregular heartbeat or fainting.
Contact your oncology team for new breathing symptoms, signs of liver problems, or severe GI symptoms.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled ECGs and electrolyte monitoring.
Attend all scheduled liver function tests.
Track hydration status and report persistent vomiting/diarrhea.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by less than 4 hours, take it as soon as remembered; if more than 4 hours late, skip it and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double up.

drug_class: Amino acid therapy for sickle cell disease
description: A prescription oral powder used to reduce the frequency of acute painful crises (sickle cell crises) in patients with sickle cell disease.
dosage_forms: Oral powder for reconstitution (5 g and 10 g packets)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your hematology specialist based on body weight, typically taken twice daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Mix the powder with 8 ounces of cold or room-temperature liquid (water, milk, or juice) or with 4-6 ounces of food, and consume immediately.
Take with meals as directed, twice daily.
Do not use hot liquids, as heat can degrade the medication.
storage_instructions: Store unmixed packets at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing
New or worsening symptoms of liver or kidney problems (rare) - report to your specialist
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC or prescription drug interactions are well established; continue your other prescribed sickle cell medications (e.g., hydroxyurea) as directed alongside this therapy.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your hematology specialist for persistent GI symptoms or any new concerning symptoms.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track the frequency and severity of pain crises to assess treatment response.
Attend all scheduled hematology follow-up visits.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered with food; if close to the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted cancer medication used in combination with other therapies to treat HER2-positive breast cancer.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly taken once daily on an empty stomach, in combination with other cancer therapies.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy as directed by your oncology team, with regular reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 1 hour after eating.
Take at the same time each day.
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or split.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of heart problems: shortness of breath, swelling of legs/ankles, chest pain (reduced heart function) - seek care promptly
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
New or worsening shortness of breath or cough (rare interstitial lung disease)
Severe or persistent diarrhea leading to dehydration
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, including clarithromycin and fluconazole - significantly increases lapatinib levels and toxicity.
St. John's Wort can reduce lapatinib effectiveness and should be avoided.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications, including ondansetron, when possible - discuss with your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for shortness of breath, swelling, or chest pain.
Contact your oncology team for persistent diarrhea, signs of liver problems, or new breathing symptoms.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled heart function tests (echocardiogram/MUGA scan) and liver function tests.
Track diarrhea frequency and hydration status.
Watch for and report hand-foot skin changes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time the next day - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: An oral targeted cancer medication used, typically in combination with amivantamab, to treat non-small cell lung cancer with specific EGFR gene mutations.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - commonly 240 mg once daily, often as part of a combination regimen.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy as directed by your oncology team, with regular reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew.
Take alongside any other prescribed combination cancer medications exactly as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening shortness of breath, cough, or fever (possible interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis) - seek care promptly
Signs of blood clots (common with combination amivantamab therapy): leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath
Signs of heart problems: irregular heartbeat, chest pain (QT prolongation risk)
Numbness, tingling, or vision changes (rare neurologic/ocular effects)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors - can significantly alter lazertinib levels; discuss all new medications with your oncology team.
St. John's Wort can reduce lazertinib effectiveness and should be avoided.
Increased bleeding/clotting risk considerations if combined with anticoagulants (warfarin, apixaban) - discuss with your oncology team, especially when combined with amivantamab.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for new breathing symptoms, chest pain, or signs of blood clots.
Contact your oncology team for severe rash or nail changes affecting daily function.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled imaging and lab monitoring for lung and cardiac status.
Watch for and report new respiratory symptoms right away.
Track skin and nail changes and report if severe.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on the same day; if it is the next day, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

drug_class: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD), pyrimidine synthesis inhibitor
description: An oral medication used to treat rheumatoid arthritis by reducing joint inflammation and slowing disease progression.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber - commonly 10-20 mg once daily, sometimes with an initial loading dose.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for rheumatoid arthritis management.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly without consulting your prescriber - a special drug elimination procedure (cholestyramine) may be needed if you need to stop quickly, especially before pregnancy.
Effective contraception is required during treatment and for a period after stopping, due to risk of birth defects.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Pregnancy (can cause fetal harm - boxed warning)
Women of childbearing potential not using reliable contraception
Severe immunodeficiency or active serious infection
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue - seek care promptly (regular liver monitoring required, boxed warning)
Signs of infection: fever, chills, persistent cough (increased infection risk)
Signs of severe skin reaction: widespread rash, blistering, mouth sores
Numbness or tingling in the hands/feet (peripheral neuropathy)
Unexplained cough or shortness of breath (rare interstitial lung disease)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol - increases the risk of liver damage.
Combining with methotrexate increases the risk of liver toxicity - requires close monitoring if used together.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) may be used cautiously but can add to GI and kidney risks; discuss with your prescriber.
Live vaccines should be avoided during treatment.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber promptly for signs of liver problems, infection, or severe skin reactions.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Attend all scheduled liver function tests and blood pressure checks, especially in the first months of treatment.
Confirm you are using effective contraception if you could become pregnant.
Report new numbness/tingling or persistent cough to your prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted cancer medication used, alone or in combination with other therapies, to treat certain thyroid, kidney, liver, and endometrial cancers.
dosage_forms: Capsule, daily-dose blister packs (4 mg, 8 mg, 10 mg, 12 mg, 14 mg, 18 mg, 20 mg, and 24 mg total daily dose combinations)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist based on the specific cancer type, body weight, and tolerability - your daily dose and capsule combination will be specified exactly by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy as directed by your oncology team, with regular reassessment and possible dose adjustments for side effects.
directions_for_use: Take the full prescribed daily dose at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush.
Take exactly the combination of capsules specified for your prescribed daily dose - do not substitute strengths on your own.
Have your blood pressure checked regularly, including at home if directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe high blood pressure or hypertensive crisis: severe headache, vision changes, chest pain - seek care promptly
Signs of blood clots, heart attack, or stroke: chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side, slurred speech - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of a hole forming in the stomach/intestine (GI perforation) or fistula: severe abdominal pain
Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/urine, coughing up blood
Signs of liver or kidney problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, decreased urination, swelling
Signs of low calcium: muscle cramps, tingling around the mouth
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) when possible - discuss with your oncology team, as dose adjustments may be needed.
St. John's Wort can reduce lenvatinib effectiveness and should be avoided.
NSAIDs may increase bleeding and kidney risks - use acetaminophen for pain when possible, as directed by your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of blood clot, stroke, heart attack, or severe bleeding.
Contact your oncology team promptly for uncontrolled blood pressure, severe abdominal pain, or signs of organ toxicity.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure at home regularly and report elevated readings promptly.
Attend all scheduled blood counts, liver, kidney, thyroid, and calcium level monitoring.
Watch for and report hand-foot skin changes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and it has been less than 12 hours, take it as soon as remembered; if more than 12 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule the next day. Do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

drug_class: Folate analog / chemotherapy rescue and adjunct agent
description: Used to reduce the toxic effects of high-dose methotrexate ('leucovorin rescue') and as an adjunct with certain chemotherapy regimens (such as 5-fluorouracil) to enhance their effect; also used to treat some forms of folate deficiency.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology specialist - dosing and exact timing relative to methotrexate or chemotherapy are precisely scheduled and must be followed exactly.
typical_duration: Short courses timed precisely around chemotherapy cycles, as directed by your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take oral doses at the exact times instructed relative to your methotrexate or chemotherapy dose - timing is critical for effectiveness and safety.
Do not skip or delay doses when used as methotrexate rescue therapy; contact your oncology team immediately if a dose is missed.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
storage_instructions: Store tablets at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Pernicious anemia or other vitamin B12-deficient anemias (should not be used alone for these conditions, as it can mask progression while allowing neurological damage to continue)
Known hypersensitivity to leucovorin or folic acid
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, wheezing, facial swelling - seek care promptly
Signs that methotrexate toxicity is occurring despite rescue therapy: mouth sores, severe fatigue, fever, unusual bruising - contact your oncology team immediately
Seizure activity has been rarely reported, particularly with high doses in combination with certain chemotherapy
common_side_effects: Mouth sores (when used with 5-fluorouracil, can increase this chemotherapy side effect)
otc_and_other_interactions: Leucovorin is specifically used to counteract methotrexate toxicity - never skip or delay a scheduled leucovorin dose after high-dose methotrexate, as this can allow severe, life-threatening toxicity to develop.
May reduce the effectiveness of anti-seizure medications like phenytoin in some cases - discuss with your prescriber if you take anticonvulsants.

May increase the toxicity (including GI side effects) of 5-fluorouracil-based chemotherapy when used together - this is often an intended part of the treatment plan but requires close monitoring by your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncology team immediately if you miss a scheduled dose during methotrexate rescue therapy.
Seek care for signs of allergic reaction or worsening methotrexate toxicity.
self_monitoring: Follow your exact dosing schedule and timing relative to methotrexate or other chemotherapy without deviation.
Attend all scheduled blood level monitoring (e.g., methotrexate levels, kidney function, blood counts).
Report mouth sores, fever, or unusual bruising promptly during rescue therapy.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team or treating facility immediately if a scheduled dose is missed, especially during methotrexate rescue therapy - do not simply take it late or double up without guidance, as timing is critical to safety.

description: An oral chemotherapy drug used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and certain lymphomas by damaging the DNA of cancer cells.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist based on body weight/surface area and blood counts.
typical_duration: Cyclical or continuous courses as directed by your oncologist; length varies by protocol.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed, often on an empty stomach.
Handle tablets with gloves if a caregiver is administering; wash hands after handling.
Do not break or crush tablets unless instructed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original container, away from children and pets; some pharmacies dispense in refrigerated form - follow the pharmacy label.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, chills, or signs of infection (low white blood cell count)
Unusual bruising or bleeding
Severe mouth sores preventing eating/drinking
Seizures (rare, at high doses)
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) and aspirin without checking with your oncology team due to bleeding/low platelet risk.
Avoid live vaccines during treatment.
Check with your pharmacist before starting any new OTC product due to added infection/bleeding risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team immediately for fever, unusual bleeding, or severe mouth sores.
Go to the emergency room for seizures or signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Frequent blood counts (CBC) as scheduled.
Watch for signs of infection and report fever promptly.
Report easy bruising or bleeding.
missed_dose_instructions: Do not double up. Contact your oncology team for guidance on a missed dose - timing is important with chemotherapy.

description: An eye drop that lowers pressure inside the eye to treat glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
typical_dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) once or twice daily as directed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic glaucoma management.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Tilt head back, pull down lower eyelid, instill drop without touching the tip to the eye.
Press gently on the inner corner of the eye (nasolacrimal occlusion) for 1-2 minutes to reduce systemic absorption.
Wait at least 5 minutes between different eye drop products.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep bottle tightly closed.
contraindications: Sinus bradycardia, heart block greater than first degree, cardiogenic shock
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Wheezing or difficulty breathing
Very slow heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting
Signs of heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: Systemic absorption can add to the effects of oral beta-blockers (metoprolol) and blood-pressure medications.
Use caution with other eye drops that lower heart rate or blood pressure.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for breathing difficulty, very slow heart rate, or fainting.
Contact prescriber for persistent eye irritation.
self_monitoring: Follow up eye pressure checks as scheduled.
Monitor pulse if you have heart conditions.
missed_dose_instructions: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the normal schedule.

description: Replaces carnitine to treat primary carnitine deficiency or deficiency associated with certain metabolic or kidney conditions.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist based on the condition being treated and body weight.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic deficiency states.
directions_for_use: Take with plenty of fluids.
May be taken with or without food; if stomach upset occurs, take with food.
Divide doses evenly through the day as directed.
storage_instructions: Store tablets at room temperature; store oral solution as directed on the label (some require refrigeration after opening).
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Seizures (rare, mainly in patients on dialysis)
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; inform your pharmacist of all supplements you take.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for seizures.
Call prescriber for persistent GI upset.
self_monitoring: Follow up carnitine levels as directed by your specialist.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Treats cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection/disease in transplant patients that has not responded to other antiviral treatment.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your transplant/infectious disease specialist; commonly 400 mg twice daily.
typical_duration: Typically an 8-week course, as directed by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food, at consistent times each day.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Concurrent use with ganciclovir or valganciclovir (antagonizes their antiviral activity)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of worsening infection or new symptoms
Significant taste changes affecting eating/nutrition
Irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong interactions with many transplant medications (tacrolimus, cyclosporine, sirolimus) - levels must be monitored closely.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can reduce maribavir effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your transplant team for worsening symptoms or new signs of infection.
Report significant appetite/nutrition changes from taste disturbance.
self_monitoring: Regular CMV viral load monitoring.
Immunosuppressant drug level monitoring (tacrolimus/cyclosporine) as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: An oral chemotherapy combination used to treat metastatic colorectal cancer and gastric cancer that has progressed on other treatments.
dosage_forms: Tablet (15 mg/6.14 mg, 20 mg/8.19 mg trifluridine/tipiracil)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist based on body surface area; taken twice daily on a specific cycle schedule.
typical_duration: Repeating 28-day cycles (5 days on, 2 days off, for 2 weeks, then 14 days off) as directed by your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take within 1 hour after finishing breakfast and dinner.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
Follow the specific calendar/cycle schedule provided by your pharmacy.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
contraindications: Known severe hypersensitivity to trifluridine or tipiracil
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever or signs of infection (low white blood cell count)
Unusual bleeding or bruising
Severe diarrhea or vomiting leading to dehydration
Shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid NSAIDs and aspirin unless approved by your oncology team due to bleeding/low platelet risk.
Check with your pharmacist before taking any new OTC medication or supplement.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team for fever, signs of infection, or uncontrolled diarrhea/vomiting.
Seek emergency care for severe bleeding or breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Regular CBC (blood count) monitoring before each cycle.
Track weight and hydration status, especially with diarrhea.
missed_dose_instructions: Do not take a missed dose later in the day if not taken within the window after a meal; contact your oncology pharmacy for guidance and continue the remaining schedule as directed.

description: An oral targeted therapy for ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 100 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening confusion, mood changes, memory problems, or speech difficulty (CNS effects)
Chest pain, shortness of breath (possible heart or lung effects)
Severe muscle pain or weakness
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces lorlatinib levels.
Many drug interactions via CYP3A4 - check with your pharmacist before starting any new medication, including OTC products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for mood/cognitive changes or new neurologic symptoms.
Seek emergency care for chest pain or severe shortness of breath.
self_monitoring: Regular cholesterol/triglyceride monitoring.
Report cognitive, mood, or speech changes to a caregiver or your care team promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than 4 hours (or vomiting occurs after a dose), skip that dose and take the next one at the regular time. Do not double up.

description: A steroid eye drop/gel used to treat inflammation and allergic conditions of the eye after surgery or due to eye conditions.
typical_dosage: 1-2 drops in the affected eye(s), 2-4 times daily as directed, tapered per prescriber instructions.
typical_duration: Short courses typically 2 weeks or as directed; long-term use requires close monitoring by an eye doctor.
directions_for_use: Shake suspension well before use.
Wash hands before instilling.
Avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or any surface.
Wait at least 5 minutes between different eye drops.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tightly closed.
contraindications: Most viral, fungal, or mycobacterial infections of the eye
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, vision changes, or halos around lights (possible increased eye pressure)
Signs of eye infection: increased redness, discharge, worsening pain
common_side_effects: Increased eye pressure with prolonged use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC oral drug interactions expected; avoid combining with other eye products without prescriber guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your eye doctor promptly for vision changes, eye pain, or signs of infection.
Do not stop abruptly without guidance if used long-term.
self_monitoring: Follow-up eye pressure and exam checks as scheduled, especially with courses longer than 2 weeks.
missed_dose_instructions: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip and resume the normal schedule.

description: Treats symptoms of schizophrenia by altering the effects of certain brain chemicals (dopamine).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically starting around 10 mg twice daily and titrated.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take consistently with or without food.
Do not stop suddenly without talking to your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Severe CNS depression or comatose states
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, muscle rigidity, confusion, irregular heartbeat (neuroleptic malignant syndrome)
Uncontrollable muscle movements of the face/tongue (tardive dyskinesia)
Fainting or irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, or other CNS depressants.
Avoid combining with other drugs that prolong QT interval unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or irregular heartbeat.
Call prescriber for new abnormal movements.
self_monitoring: Report any new involuntary movements promptly.
Track weight and blood sugar periodically.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for non-small cell lung cancer with a specific KRAS G12C gene mutation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 960 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not chew or crush.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine (liver problems)
New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, fever (possible lung inflammation)
Fast or irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid acid-reducing medications (omeprazole and similar) close to dosing without checking with your oncology team - they can reduce absorption.
Many CYP3A4 interactions - check with your pharmacist before starting new medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team for signs of liver problems or new respiratory symptoms.
Seek emergency care for severe breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests as scheduled.
Report new cough or shortness of breath promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than 6 hours, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not double up.

description: An eye drop that lowers pressure inside the eye to treat glaucoma or ocular hypertension by increasing fluid outflow.
typical_dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic glaucoma management.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Instill one drop, avoiding contact between the dropper tip and the eye.
If using more than one eye drop product, wait at least 5 minutes between them.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Significant eye pain or vision changes
Signs of eye infection
common_side_effects: Darkening of the iris (permanent) or eyelid skin
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic OTC drug interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your eye doctor for significant pain, vision change, or infection signs.
self_monitoring: Follow-up eye pressure checks as scheduled.
Note any progressive iris color change and report it.
missed_dose_instructions: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip and resume the normal schedule.

description: Treats excessive daytime sleepiness and cataplexy in people with narcolepsy; taken once nightly at bedtime.
dosage_forms: Extended-release oral suspension (granules for oral suspension, single nightly dose)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your sleep specialist; typically started at a low dose and titrated based on effect.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic narcolepsy management.
directions_for_use: Take only at bedtime, while already in bed - it works quickly and causes sudden sleepiness.
Take on an empty stomach (at least 2 hours after eating).
Mix with water as instructed by the pharmacy and drink promptly.
Do not get out of bed or drive after taking a dose.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; this medication is dispensed through a restricted REMS program pharmacy.
contraindications: Use with alcohol or other sedative-hypnotics
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe difficulty breathing or waking up
Confusion, severe drowsiness the next day
Signs of new depression or suicidal thoughts
Sleepwalking or unusual nighttime behavior
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not combine with alcohol, diphenhydramine, or other sedating OTC sleep aids - risk of severe respiratory depression.
Avoid other CNS depressants (opioids like hydrocodone/acetaminophen, benzodiazepines like alprazolam) unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for difficulty breathing, unresponsiveness, or inability to wake.
Call prescriber for mood changes or unusual nighttime behavior.
