self_monitoring: Monitor for next-day sedation, especially when starting or adjusting dose.
Track sleep quality and cataplexy episodes as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Do not take a missed dose after getting out of bed for the day; wait until the next scheduled bedtime dose. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for BRCA-mutated or other DNA-repair-deficient ovarian, breast, pancreatic, or prostate cancers.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 300 mg twice daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, often as maintenance therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food, at consistent times about 12 hours apart.
Swallow tablets whole; do not chew, crush, or dissolve.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Unusual bruising/bleeding, fatigue with pallor (possible blood disorder including MDS/AML)
New or worsening shortness of breath or cough (possible pneumonitis)
Fever or signs of infection
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can reduce effectiveness.
Many drug interactions via CYP3A4 - check with your pharmacist before starting anything new, including OTC products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for unusual bleeding, persistent fatigue, or breathing changes.
Seek emergency care for severe shortness of breath.
self_monitoring: Regular CBC (blood count) monitoring monthly.
Report new respiratory symptoms promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, do not take an extra dose to make up for it; take the next dose at the regular scheduled time.

description: An oral chemotherapy drug used to treat adrenocortical (adrenal gland) cancer by suppressing adrenal hormone production.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist, with gradual titration based on blood levels and tolerance.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy as directed by your oncologist, with close monitoring.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset, exactly as directed.
You will likely need to take corticosteroid replacement (e.g., hydrocortisone) as directed because this drug suppresses adrenal function.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; handle tablets with care (wear gloves if crushing is ever required by caregivers).
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of adrenal insufficiency: severe weakness, dizziness, low blood pressure, vomiting (especially during illness/stress)
Confusion, difficulty walking, slurred speech (neurotoxicity)
Severe rash
otc_and_other_interactions: May reduce effectiveness of warfarin dose adjustments (monitoring needed) and many other drugs due to strong enzyme induction.
Ask your pharmacist before starting any new OTC medication or supplement.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for signs of adrenal insufficiency, especially during illness.
Seek emergency care for confusion or difficulty walking/speaking.
self_monitoring: Regular mitotane blood level monitoring.
Wear/carry medical alert identification for adrenal insufficiency.
Monitor blood pressure and for symptoms of low cortisol.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team for specific guidance; do not double up doses without direction.

description: An oral targeted therapy for cholangiocarcinoma (bile duct cancer) with an FGFR2 gene fusion or rearrangement.
dosage_forms: Tablet (4 mg, 9 mg, 13.6 mg, 16 mg, 20 mg)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 20 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Vision changes, blurry vision, floaters (possible retinal detachment)
Signs of high phosphate levels (muscle cramps, unusual fatigue)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid phosphate-containing supplements unless directed.
Many CYP3A4 interactions - check with your pharmacist before starting new medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team for vision changes and get scheduled eye exams as directed.
Report signs of liver problems promptly.
self_monitoring: Routine eye exams (retinal detachment risk).
Phosphate level monitoring - a low-phosphate diet or phosphate binder may be needed.
Liver function test monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not double up.

description: A mealtime insulin engineered for faster onset than standard rapid-acting insulins, used to control blood sugar in diabetes.
route: Subcutaneous injection (also used in insulin pumps)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber based on blood sugar, carbohydrate intake, and insulin sensitivity.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for diabetes management.
directions_for_use: Inject within 2 minutes before the start of a meal, or within 20 minutes after starting a meal if needed.
Rotate injection sites (abdomen, thigh, upper arm) to prevent skin changes.
Do not mix with other insulins in the same syringe unless directed.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate unopened pens/vials. Once in use, may be kept at room temperature per the specific product labeling (generally up to 28 days); protect from direct heat and light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe hypoglycemia: confusion, seizure, loss of consciousness
Signs of severe allergic reaction: whole-body rash, difficulty breathing
Low potassium symptoms: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Alcohol can increase the risk of low blood sugar.
Many OTC decongestants can raise blood sugar; check with your pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Treat mild low blood sugar promptly with fast-acting glucose; seek emergency care for severe hypoglycemia (confusion, seizure, unconsciousness).
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Check blood glucose regularly as directed, especially around mealtimes.
Keep a fast-acting glucose source available at all times.
Know the signs and treatment of hypoglycemia.
missed_dose_instructions: If a meal is missed or delayed, adjust timing as directed by your prescriber; do not inject if you are not about to eat, due to hypoglycemia risk.

generic_name: Measles, Mumps, and Rubella Vaccine, Live
description: A vaccine that protects against measles, mumps, and rubella infections.
typical_dosage: A single 0.5 mL dose, with the number of doses in the series set by current immunization guidelines and your provider.
typical_duration: Administered per recommended immunization schedule (typically 2 doses in childhood, or catch-up/booster dosing in adults as indicated).
directions_for_use: Administered by a trained pharmacist or healthcare provider.
Inform your provider of any allergies, pregnancy status, or immune conditions before vaccination.
storage_instructions: Must be refrigerated/frozen per product labeling and protected from light; handled by the administering pharmacy or clinic.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a prior dose or vaccine component (e.g., neomycin, gelatin)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling, difficulty breathing (usually within minutes of the shot)
High fever with seizure
Unusual bruising/bleeding (rare, low platelet reaction)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid other live vaccines within 4 weeks unless given the same day.
Immunosuppressive medications may reduce vaccine effectiveness or increase risk - discuss timing with your provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your provider for high fever or unusual symptoms after vaccination.
self_monitoring: Monitor for fever or rash in the 1-2 weeks after vaccination.
Stay for the recommended observation period after the injection.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose in a multi-dose series is missed or delayed, contact your provider to reschedule - the series generally does not need to be restarted.

description: A topical lotion used to treat head lice infestations by killing lice and their eggs.
typical_dosage: Apply to dry hair and scalp; use enough to thoroughly wet the hair and scalp, as directed on the label.
typical_duration: Single application, left on 8-12 hours, may be repeated in 7-9 days if live lice remain.
directions_for_use: Apply to dry hair, sprinkling on to hair close to the scalp and rubbing in gently.
Allow hair to air dry naturally - do NOT use a hair dryer, curling iron, or other heat source, and avoid open flames and cigarettes (product is flammable while wet).
After 8-12 hours, wash hair with regular shampoo and comb out dead lice/nits with a fine-tooth comb.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from heat and open flame; keep tightly closed.
contraindications: Infants (not established as safe in very young children per label)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of skin irritation that is severe or spreading
Accidental ingestion (seek poison control immediately)
Difficulty breathing after use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic OTC drug interactions expected with correct topical use; avoid combining with other lice treatments applied the same day.
action_if_adverse_effects: Rinse thoroughly and contact prescriber for severe irritation.
Call poison control immediately if swallowed.
self_monitoring: Check hair for live lice/nits after treatment and again in about a week.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as a single treatment course, not a scheduled daily dose; if lice persist, follow the label's retreatment interval (about 7-9 days) or contact your prescriber.

description: An antiretroviral medication used with other HIV medications to treat HIV-1 infection that uses the CCR5 receptor to enter cells (requires tropism testing before use).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your HIV specialist based on other medications you take (dose depends on interacting drugs); commonly 150-600 mg twice daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of a complete antiretroviral regimen.
directions_for_use: Take consistently with or without food, as part of your full HIV regimen.
Do not skip doses - missed doses can lead to resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: CXCR4-tropic or dual/mixed-tropic HIV (requires tropism testing before starting)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe rash preceding liver symptoms
Signs of allergic reaction
Chest pain (rare cardiovascular risk)
otc_and_other_interactions: Many significant interactions via CYP3A4 - your dose depends on other medications; always check with your pharmacist before starting or stopping any medication.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can significantly reduce maraviroc levels and effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your HIV specialist for signs of liver problems or allergic reaction.
Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction or chest pain.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function monitoring.
Routine HIV viral load and CD4 count monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up. Do not stop this medication without talking to your HIV specialist.

description: An antidepressant used for depression, typically reserved for cases that have not responded to other treatments due to its strict dietary and drug restrictions.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically started low and titrated based on response.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy as directed, with close monitoring especially early in treatment.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed.
Follow a strict low-tyramine diet (avoid aged cheeses, cured/fermented meats, tap beer, etc.) to prevent dangerous blood pressure spikes.
Allow required washout periods (often 2 weeks) when switching to or from other antidepressants or serotonergic drugs.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Use within 2 weeks of other antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs), tramadol, or other MAOIs
Use with sympathomimetics (many decongestants) or serotonergic drugs
Elective surgery requiring general anesthesia (needs washout)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe headache, stiff neck, chest pain, sudden high blood pressure (hypertensive crisis) - most often triggered by tyramine-containing foods or interacting drugs
Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, fever, rapid heartbeat, muscle rigidity
Suicidal thoughts, especially early in treatment or in young adults
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid decongestants (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine) - risk of hypertensive crisis.
Avoid diphenhydramine and dextromethorphan-containing OTC cold products unless approved by prescriber.
Never combine with tramadol, other antidepressants, or St. John's Wort - serious risk of serotonin syndrome.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for severe headache with high blood pressure or signs of serotonin syndrome.
Call prescriber promptly for new or worsening mood changes.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure, especially when starting new foods or medications.
Watch closely for mood changes, particularly in the first weeks of treatment.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up. Never stop abruptly without prescriber guidance.

drug_class: Alkylating-like chemotherapy agent with weak MAOI activity
description: An oral chemotherapy drug used in combination regimens (such as MOPP) to treat Hodgkin lymphoma and certain brain tumors.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist as part of a combination chemotherapy protocol.
typical_duration: Given in defined chemotherapy cycles as directed by your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed as part of your chemotherapy protocol.
Avoid alcohol completely - can cause a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, headache, vomiting).
Follow a low-tyramine diet as instructed due to weak MAOI activity.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from children and pets.
contraindications: Concurrent use with other MAOIs or serotonergic drugs
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, chills, signs of infection (low white count)
Unusual bruising or bleeding
Severe headache with high blood pressure (rare, tyramine reaction)
Signs of serotonin syndrome if combined with serotonergic drugs
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol-containing products (including some cough syrups).
Avoid decongestants/sympathomimetics and tyramine-rich foods.
Avoid combining with other serotonergic medications (tramadol, SSRIs) without oncology guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team for fever, unusual bleeding, or severe headache.
Seek emergency care for signs of a severe reaction.
self_monitoring: Regular blood counts as scheduled.
Watch for signs of infection and report fever promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team for guidance on a missed dose - do not double up.

description: A combination antiviral used to cure chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection.
typical_dosage: 3 tablets (300 mg/120 mg) by mouth once daily with food.
typical_duration: Typically 8 weeks (up to 16 weeks in certain patients), as directed by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Take with food - absorption is reduced on an empty stomach.
Take the full course even if you feel well; stopping early can lead to treatment failure.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
contraindications: Concurrent use with atorvastatin or simvastatin
Concurrent use with certain ethinyl estradiol-containing contraceptives (risk of ALT elevation)
Concurrent use with strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue (liver problems)
Signs of hepatitis B reactivation if you have a prior hepatitis B infection
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid atorvastatin and simvastatin during treatment - significantly increased statin levels.
Interacts with many other medications; review your full medication list, including OTC and herbal products, with your pharmacist before starting.
Avoid St. John's Wort.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your prescriber promptly for signs of liver problems.
Do not stop treatment early without medical guidance.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests before and during treatment.
HCV viral load testing to confirm cure after completing therapy.
missed_dose_instructions: If missed and remembered within 18 hours of the usual time, take it with food; if more than 18 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not double up.

description: Used to prevent and treat certain types of malaria.
typical_dosage: For prevention: one tablet once weekly, starting 1-2 weeks before travel and continuing 4 weeks after leaving the malaria area, as directed. For treatment: individualized by prescriber.
typical_duration: Duration depends on travel dates (prophylaxis) or is a short treatment course, as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with food and at least 8 oz of water, on the same day each week if used for prevention.
Continue for the full recommended period after leaving the malaria-risk area.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: History of psychiatric disorders (depression, anxiety, psychosis)
Known hypersensitivity to mefloquine or related compounds
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Anxiety, hallucinations, depression, unusual behavior, or thoughts of self-harm
Seizures
Irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other drugs that can cause seizures or heart rhythm changes unless directed.
Space dosing apart from antacids if directed by your pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop the medication and contact your prescriber immediately for any mood, behavior, or neurologic changes.
Seek emergency care for seizures or severe psychiatric symptoms.
self_monitoring: Monitor your own mood and mental status closely, especially during the first few doses.
Have a travel companion aware of the warning signs if possible.
missed_dose_instructions: If a weekly dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered and resume the normal weekly schedule; do not double up.

description: Used to stimulate appetite and promote weight gain in people with significant unintentional weight loss due to cancer, AIDS, or other conditions.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; commonly 400-800 mg (oral suspension) once daily.
typical_duration: Ongoing as directed, with periodic reassessment.
directions_for_use: Shake oral suspension well before each use.
Take consistently, with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; do not freeze suspension.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Leg swelling or pain, shortness of breath (possible blood clot)
Signs of adrenal insufficiency, especially with abrupt discontinuation after long-term use: weakness, dizziness, nausea
Signs of high blood sugar: excessive thirst, urination
otc_and_other_interactions: May increase blood sugar - monitor closely if you take diabetes medications (metformin, glipizide).
No major OTC interactions expected otherwise; inform your pharmacist of all medications you take.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot (leg swelling/pain, shortness of breath).
Call prescriber for signs of adrenal insufficiency, especially if stopping after long-term use.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood sugar if diabetic.
Track weight and appetite changes.
Do not stop abruptly after prolonged use without prescriber guidance.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for BRAF-mutated melanoma, NSCLC, or thyroid cancer, often used in combination with a BRAF inhibitor.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 2 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal.
Take at the same time each day.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; some pharmacies dispense with a desiccant packet - do not remove it.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Shortness of breath, swelling of legs/ankles (possible heart problems)
Vision changes, eye pain (possible retinal problems)
New cough, fever, difficulty breathing (possible lung inflammation)
Severe skin rash or peeling
otc_and_other_interactions: No major OTC interactions expected; check with your pharmacist before starting new products due to skin and photosensitivity effects.
Use sun protection - increased sun sensitivity.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team for vision changes, new swelling, or breathing changes.
Seek emergency care for severe shortness of breath or chest pain.
self_monitoring: Regular heart function tests (echocardiogram) as scheduled.
Routine eye exams.
Monitor blood pressure.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than 12 hours, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for BRAF-mutated melanoma, typically used in combination with a BRAF inhibitor (encorafenib).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 45 mg twice daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food, about 12 hours apart.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Shortness of breath, swelling (possible heart problems)
Vision changes (possible retinal detachment/vein occlusion)
New cough, fever, breathing difficulty (possible lung inflammation)
Severe muscle pain, dark urine (possible rhabdomyolysis)
otc_and_other_interactions: No major OTC interactions expected; use sun protection due to increased photosensitivity.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team for vision changes, breathing changes, or severe muscle pain.
Seek emergency care for severe shortness of breath.
self_monitoring: Regular heart function tests (echocardiogram) as scheduled.
Routine eye exams.
CPK/muscle enzyme monitoring if muscle symptoms occur.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double up.

generic_name: Meningococcal (Groups A, C, W, Y) Conjugate Vaccine
description: A vaccine that protects against meningococcal disease caused by serogroups A, C, W, and Y.
typical_dosage: A single 0.5 mL dose, per current immunization schedule/booster recommendations.
typical_duration: Administered per recommended immunization schedule, with boosters as recommended for ongoing risk.
directions_for_use: Administered by a trained pharmacist or healthcare provider.
Inform your provider of prior meningococcal vaccination history and any allergies.
storage_instructions: Refrigerated storage handled by the administering pharmacy or clinic.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a prior dose or vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling, difficulty breathing
High fever
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for injection-site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated for you.
May be given with other vaccines at different injection sites.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your provider for high fever or concerning symptoms.
self_monitoring: Monitor injection site and general symptoms for 24-48 hours after vaccination.
missed_dose_instructions: If a booster dose is due, schedule it as soon as possible with your provider; the prior dose remains protective in the interim.

generic_name: Meningococcal (Groups A, C, W, Y) Conjugate Vaccine (CRM197 conjugate)
description: A vaccine that protects against meningococcal disease caused by serogroups A, C, W, and Y, using a different conjugate carrier protein than MenQuadfi.
typical_dosage: A single 0.5 mL dose, per current immunization schedule/booster recommendations.
typical_duration: Administered per recommended immunization schedule, with boosters as recommended for ongoing risk.
directions_for_use: Administered by a trained pharmacist or healthcare provider.
Inform your provider of prior meningococcal vaccination history and any allergies.
storage_instructions: Refrigerated storage handled by the administering pharmacy or clinic; reconstituted per product labeling immediately before use.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a prior dose or vaccine component (including diphtheria toxoid-containing vaccines)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling, difficulty breathing
High fever
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for injection-site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated for you.
May be given with other vaccines at different injection sites.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your provider for high fever or concerning symptoms.
self_monitoring: Monitor injection site and general symptoms for 24-48 hours after vaccination.
missed_dose_instructions: If a booster or second dose is due, schedule it as soon as possible with your provider.

description: An oral chemotherapy drug used mainly for maintenance therapy of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and sometimes for inflammatory bowel disease.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist based on body surface area and genetic testing (TPMT/NUDT15) results.
typical_duration: Often long-term maintenance therapy over months to years, as directed.
directions_for_use: Take consistently, generally on an empty stomach unless your team advises otherwise.
Avoid taking with milk products at the same time if directed (can reduce absorption).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from children and pets.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, chills, or signs of infection (low white blood cell count)
Unusual bruising or bleeding
Yellowing of skin/eyes (liver toxicity)
Severe abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid NSAIDs and aspirin unless approved by your specialist due to bleeding risk.
Avoid live vaccines during treatment.
Check with your pharmacist before starting any new OTC or herbal product.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your care team promptly for fever, unusual bleeding, or jaundice.
Seek emergency care for severe symptoms.
self_monitoring: Regular CBC and liver function monitoring as scheduled.
Report fever or signs of infection immediately.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your care team for specific guidance on a missed dose - do not double up without direction.

description: Used to help prevent bladder toxicity (hemorrhagic cystitis) caused by certain chemotherapy drugs such as ifosfamide and high-dose cyclophosphamide.
route: Oral (tablet, for continuation dosing after an initial IV dose)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology team, timed relative to your chemotherapy doses on a specific schedule.
typical_duration: Given on the days you receive the chemotherapy drug it is protecting against, as directed.
directions_for_use: Take exactly at the scheduled times relative to your chemotherapy infusion - timing is critical for protection.
May be taken with or without food; take with extra fluids and empty your bladder frequently on treatment days.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to mesna or other thiol compounds
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Blood in urine or pain with urination despite taking mesna (report to your oncology team)
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant independent OTC interactions expected; mesna is used specifically alongside chemotherapy per your oncology team's schedule.
action_if_adverse_effects: Report blood in urine or urinary pain to your oncology team right away.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Monitor urine for blood or discoloration on treatment days.
Track fluid intake and urination frequency.
missed_dose_instructions: Because timing relative to chemotherapy is critical, contact your oncology team immediately if a dose is missed rather than taking it late on your own.

description: Used to help prevent and control recurrent urinary tract infections by releasing formaldehyde in acidic urine, which has antibacterial activity.
typical_dosage: 1 g by mouth twice daily.
typical_duration: Often used long-term for chronic UTI prevention, as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Your prescriber may recommend cranberry juice or vitamin C to help keep urine acidic, which improves effectiveness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with sulfonamide antibiotics (reduced effectiveness of both)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe rash or signs of allergic reaction
Blood in urine
Severe stomach pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid antacids and other urine-alkalinizing products (reduce effectiveness).
Avoid combining with sulfa antibiotics (sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim) - can form an insoluble precipitate in urine and reduce effectiveness of both.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for severe stomach pain, rash, or blood in urine.
self_monitoring: Monitor for recurrence of UTI symptoms and report them.
Urine pH may be checked periodically.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used together with controlled UVA light exposure (PUVA therapy) to treat severe psoriasis, vitiligo, and certain skin conditions like cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your dermatologist based on body weight, timed before scheduled UVA treatments.
typical_duration: Given only on days of scheduled phototherapy sessions, as part of an ongoing treatment plan.
directions_for_use: Take with food or milk about 1.5-2 hours before your scheduled UVA light treatment - exact timing matters.
Wear UV-blocking wraparound sunglasses for 24 hours after each dose, even indoors near sunny windows.
Avoid unprotected sun exposure for at least 24 hours after taking a dose.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture.
contraindications: Aphakia (absence of the eye's lens - very high risk of retinal damage)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe sunburn-like reaction or blistering
Eye pain or vision changes
Signs of skin cancer: new or changing moles/lesions over time
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid other photosensitizing drugs and products.
Avoid St. John's Wort - increases photosensitivity.
Check with your pharmacist before using any new OTC product.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your dermatologist for severe burning, blistering, or eye symptoms.
Seek emergency care for severe skin reactions.
self_monitoring: Routine eye exams (cataract risk with long-term use).
Regular skin checks for new or changing lesions.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed before a scheduled light treatment session, contact your dermatology office - the session may need to be rescheduled.

description: Used to control absence (petit mal) seizures, typically when other treatments have not been effective.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your neurologist, generally starting low and titrated based on seizure control.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for seizure control.
directions_for_use: Take consistently with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly - can trigger seizures.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Unusual bruising/bleeding, sore throat, fever (possible blood dyscrasia)
Joint pain, rash, or other signs of lupus-like reaction
Severe skin rash
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased sedation with diphenhydramine or other sedating OTC products.
Alcohol can increase drowsiness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber promptly for unusual bruising, sore throat, fever, or rash.
Do not stop abruptly without medical guidance.
self_monitoring: Periodic blood counts as directed.
Track seizure frequency and report breakthrough seizures.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: An anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive steroid used for a wide range of conditions including allergic reactions, autoimmune flares, and inflammation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; often given as a short tapering course (dose pack) or longer-term at the lowest effective dose.
typical_duration: Short courses (days) for acute flares, or longer-term for chronic conditions under close supervision.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
If using a dose pack, follow the printed tapering schedule exactly - do not stop early or change the schedule.
Take in the morning when possible to mimic natural cortisol rhythm.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Live vaccine administration during high-dose therapy
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat that doesn't improve
Severe mood changes, confusion
Signs of adrenal insufficiency after stopping: severe fatigue, dizziness, nausea
Vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) increase risk of stomach ulcers/GI bleeding when combined.
Can raise blood sugar - monitor closely if taking diabetes medications.
Avoid live vaccines while on higher doses.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for signs of infection, mood changes, or high blood sugar.
Never stop abruptly after more than a few days of use without tapering guidance - can cause adrenal crisis.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood sugar and blood pressure periodically.
Track weight and signs of fluid retention.
Watch for signs of infection.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if on a tapering dose pack, follow the printed schedule and contact your pharmacist if a day was missed rather than guessing.

description: Reduces catecholamine (adrenaline-type hormone) production, used to manage pheochromocytoma, often before surgery.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist, typically starting low and titrated based on response.
typical_duration: Used short-term before surgery, or longer-term for chronic management as directed.
directions_for_use: Take consistently with plenty of fluids.
Drink extra water to reduce the risk of crystal formation in urine.
Avoid tasks requiring alertness until you know how this affects you (sedation is common).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe drowsiness or confusion
Difficulty speaking, tremor, or stiffness (extrapyramidal symptoms)
Blood in urine or difficulty urinating (crystalluria)
Severe diarrhea
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, or other CNS depressants.
Avoid combining with other drugs that cause drowsiness unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your specialist for tremor, stiffness, or urinary symptoms.
Seek emergency care for severe confusion or inability to urinate.
self_monitoring: Maintain high fluid intake to reduce crystalluria risk.
Monitor blood pressure as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat certain life-threatening irregular heartbeats (ventricular arrhythmias).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your cardiologist based on heart rhythm response and blood levels; commonly every 8 hours.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed for arrhythmia control.
directions_for_use: Take with food or antacid to reduce stomach upset.
Take doses evenly spaced as directed - consistency is important for heart rhythm control.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Second- or third-degree heart block without a pacemaker
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening irregular heartbeat, palpitations, or fainting
Tremor, confusion, or difficulty walking (signs of high drug levels)
Signs of liver problems
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other drugs that affect heart rhythm unless directed.
Antacids and acid reducers (omeprazole) can change mexiletine levels - check with your pharmacist.
Smoking can lower mexiletine levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your cardiologist for new palpitations, tremor, or confusion.
Seek emergency care for fainting or severe irregular heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Periodic ECG monitoring as directed.
Blood level monitoring if available/directed.
Track and report palpitations or dizziness.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat symptomatic orthostatic (postural) hypotension - low blood pressure on standing that causes dizziness or fainting.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; commonly 10 mg three times daily during waking hours.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take during the daytime hours when you are upright and active.
Do NOT take within 4 hours of bedtime or when you will be lying down for an extended period - can cause dangerously high blood pressure while supine.
Take doses about 3-4 hours apart, generally upon waking, midday, and late afternoon.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Persistent and excessive supine (lying down) hypertension
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe headache, blurred vision, or chest pain while lying down (supine hypertension)
Very slow heart rate
Difficulty urinating
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other blood-pressure-raising OTC decongestants (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine) unless directed.
Effects may be altered by other blood pressure medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Sit or remain upright and contact your prescriber for severe supine blood pressure elevation symptoms.
Seek emergency care for chest pain or very slow heart rate.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure both lying down and standing as directed.
Report urinary difficulty.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered during waking hours; skip the dose if it is close to bedtime. Do not double up.

description: An eye drop used to treat the signs and symptoms of dry eye disease by forming a layer that reduces tear evaporation.
typical_dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) four times daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use for chronic dry eye disease.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Instill one drop, avoiding contact between the dropper tip and the eye.
If wearing contact lenses, remove them before use and follow your prescriber's guidance on reinsertion.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; do not use if the solution becomes cloudy.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe or worsening eye pain, vision changes, or discharge
otc_and_other_interactions: Wait at least 5-10 minutes between this and other eye drop products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your eye doctor for worsening eye pain, vision changes, or discharge.
self_monitoring: Track symptom improvement and follow up with your eye doctor as scheduled.
missed_dose_instructions: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip and resume the normal schedule.

otc_or_rx: Rx (dispensed under a restricted REMS program)
description: Used either to end an early pregnancy (in combination with misoprostol, under a medical REMS protocol) or, at a different dose/brand, to control high blood sugar caused by Cushing's syndrome.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber depending on the indication and specific product/REMS protocol being used.
typical_duration: Mifeprex is a short single/limited course as part of a defined medical protocol; Korlym is used long-term for Cushing's syndrome as directed.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as directed by your prescriber as part of the specific REMS protocol for your indication.
Follow all program-specific counseling and follow-up appointment instructions.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; dispensed only through certified prescribers/pharmacies under the REMS program.
contraindications: Confirmed or suspected ectopic pregnancy (for the pregnancy-related indication)
Concurrent long-term corticosteroid therapy (for Korlym use, unless directed)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Heavy vaginal bleeding soaking more than 2 pads/hour for 2+ hours (Mifeprex use)
Fever, severe abdominal pain (possible infection)
Signs of low cortisol/adrenal insufficiency: severe weakness, vomiting, low blood pressure (Korlym use)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid NSAIDs around the time of the pregnancy-related protocol unless specifically directed, as they may reduce effectiveness of the accompanying misoprostol.
Korlym is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor with many drug interactions - review your full medication list with your pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Follow the specific emergency instructions given with your REMS program materials.
Seek emergency care for heavy bleeding, fever, or severe abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Attend all required follow-up appointments to confirm treatment success (Mifeprex) or monitor blood sugar/cortisol effect (Korlym).
Track bleeding or symptoms as instructed.
missed_dose_instructions: For Korlym long-term therapy, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose, then skip; for Mifeprex protocol dosing, follow your prescriber's specific instructions exactly - do not adjust the schedule on your own.

description: Used to control blood sugar in type 2 diabetes by slowing the breakdown and absorption of carbohydrates in the gut.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; commonly 25-100 mg three times daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of diabetes management.
directions_for_use: Take with the first bite of each main meal.
If low blood sugar occurs while taking this drug, treat it with glucose tablets or gel, not table sugar - miglitol blocks the breakdown of sucrose.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Bowel obstruction or predisposition to bowel obstruction
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe abdominal pain or bloating
Signs of low blood sugar not responding to glucose
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces effectiveness of other oral medications absorbed with food to some extent; digestive enzyme products (containing amylase) may reduce miglitol's effect.
Increased hypoglycemia risk when combined with other diabetes medications (metformin, glipizide).
action_if_adverse_effects: Treat low blood sugar with glucose tablets/gel immediately.
Call prescriber for severe or persistent GI symptoms.
self_monitoring: Regular blood glucose monitoring.
Periodic A1c checks as scheduled.
missed_dose_instructions: If a meal is missed, skip that dose since this drug is taken with food; do not take it between meals.

description: Used to treat mild-to-moderate type 1 Gaucher disease in patients for whom enzyme replacement therapy is not suitable.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; commonly 100 mg three times daily, adjusted for tolerability and kidney function.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food, at evenly spaced intervals.
Stay well hydrated.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Numbness, tingling, or weakness in hands/feet (possible peripheral neuropathy)
Significant unintended weight loss
Tremor that interferes with daily activities
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; inform your pharmacist of all products you take.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your specialist for numbness/tingling, significant weight loss, or bothersome tremor.
self_monitoring: Regular nerve conduction studies as directed to monitor for neuropathy.
Track weight periodically.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to help prevent stomach ulcers in people who take NSAIDs long-term and are at high risk of ulcer complications.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; commonly 200 mcg up to four times daily with food, taken alongside NSAID therapy.
typical_duration: Continued for as long as the NSAID that requires ulcer prevention is being taken.
directions_for_use: Take with food and at bedtime, as directed, to reduce diarrhea.
Do not share this medication - it can cause pregnancy loss.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy (for the ulcer-prevention indication - can cause miscarriage, premature labor, or birth defects)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe abdominal pain
Heavy vaginal bleeding (in someone who could be pregnant)
Signs of dehydration from severe diarrhea
otc_and_other_interactions: Magnesium-containing antacids can worsen diarrhea - avoid or space apart if possible.
No other significant OTC interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for heavy bleeding or severe abdominal pain, especially if pregnancy is possible.
Call prescriber for diarrhea that doesn't improve.
self_monitoring: Pregnancy status should be confirmed negative before starting if there is any possibility of pregnancy.
Track GI symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to improve wakefulness in people with excessive sleepiness due to narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea, or shift work sleep disorder.
typical_dosage: 100-200 mg by mouth once daily in the morning (or before a shift, for shift work disorder).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed for chronic sleepiness disorders.
directions_for_use: Take in the morning or before your work shift, as directed.
Avoid taking late in the day - can interfere with nighttime sleep.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to modafinil or armodafinil
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe skin rash or blistering (possible Stevens-Johnson syndrome)
Signs of allergic reaction: swelling, difficulty breathing
Chest pain, irregular heartbeat
New or worsening mental health symptoms
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives (birth control pills, patches, rings, and the levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol combination) - use an alternative or backup contraceptive method during use and for one month after stopping.
May increase the effect of warfarin - monitoring may be needed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe rash, chest pain, or allergic reaction.
Call prescriber for new mood or behavior changes.
self_monitoring: Track sleep quality and daytime alertness.
Monitor blood pressure and heart rate periodically.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered in the morning; if it is already afternoon/evening, skip the dose to avoid insomnia. Do not double up.

description: Relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure.
typical_dosage: 7.5-30 mg by mouth daily (may be divided into two doses), titrated to blood pressure response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before meals.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness, especially with the first doses.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: History of angioedema with ACE inhibitors
Concurrent use with aliskiren in diabetic patients
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing/swallowing (angioedema) - seek emergency care immediately
Persistent dry cough that is bothersome
Signs of high potassium: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium unless directed - risk of hyperkalemia.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can blunt blood-pressure-lowering effect and stress the kidneys - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for facial/throat swelling or breathing trouble.
Call prescriber for a persistent cough or signs of high potassium.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure at home if recommended.
Report unusual swelling right away.
Keep scheduled potassium/kidney function labs.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Treats symptoms of schizophrenia by altering the effects of certain brain chemicals (dopamine).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically starting around 50-75 mg/day divided into multiple doses and titrated.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take consistently with or without food.
Do not stop suddenly without talking to your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Severe CNS depression or comatose states
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, muscle rigidity, confusion, irregular heartbeat (neuroleptic malignant syndrome)
Uncontrollable muscle movements of the face/tongue (tardive dyskinesia)
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, or other CNS depressants.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
Call prescriber for new abnormal movements.
self_monitoring: Report any new involuntary movements promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat constipation caused by opioid pain medications in adults with chronic non-cancer pain.
typical_dosage: 25 mg by mouth once daily on an empty stomach (may reduce to 12.5 mg if not tolerated).
typical_duration: Continued for as long as the causative opioid medication is being taken.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after the first meal of the day.
Stop other scheduled laxatives before starting unless directed otherwise; they may still be used as needed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction, or risk of recurrent obstruction
Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe or worsening stomach pain
Signs of opioid withdrawal: sweating, chills, diarrhea, anxiety
Tearing of the stomach or intestine (rare): severe abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (certain antifungals like fluconazole at higher doses, clarithromycin) - can significantly increase naloxegol levels.
St. John's Wort can reduce effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for severe abdominal pain or signs of opioid withdrawal.
Seek emergency care for severe, sudden abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Track bowel movement frequency.
Report if opioid pain medication dose changes, since naloxegol dosing may need adjustment.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose if it is not an appropriate time (empty stomach); take the next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double up.

description: A vaccine that helps prevent lower respiratory tract disease caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), primarily used in older adults.
typical_dosage: A single 0.5 mL dose, per current immunization recommendations for eligible adults.
typical_duration: Currently given as a single dose; revaccination recommendations may be updated over time by public health guidance.
directions_for_use: Administered by a trained pharmacist or healthcare provider.
Inform your provider of any allergies or prior RSV vaccination.
storage_instructions: Frozen/refrigerated storage handled by the administering pharmacy or clinic.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a prior dose or vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling, difficulty breathing
High fever
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for injection-site soreness or fever unless otherwise contraindicated for you.
May be given with other vaccines at different injection sites.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your provider for high fever or concerning symptoms.
self_monitoring: Monitor injection site and general symptoms for 24-48 hours after vaccination.
missed_dose_instructions: Not applicable to a routine repeat schedule at this time; discuss any future dosing recommendations with your provider.

description: Used to help keep a normal heart rhythm in people with a history of atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter.
typical_dosage: 400 mg by mouth twice daily, taken with morning and evening meals.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your cardiologist.
directions_for_use: Take with food (morning and evening meals) to improve absorption.
Do not take with grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Symptomatic heart failure with recent decompensation, or severe heart failure
Second- or third-degree heart block or sick sinus syndrome without a pacemaker
Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Shortness of breath or worsening heart failure symptoms
Fainting or very slow/irregular heartbeat
New or worsening lung symptoms (cough, breathing difficulty)
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly increases levels of simvastatin - dose limits apply; discuss statin choice with your prescriber.
Avoid grapefruit juice.
Many other CYP3A4-related interactions - check with your pharmacist before starting anything new.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your cardiologist promptly for signs of liver problems or worsening heart failure.
Seek emergency care for fainting or severe irregular heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests as scheduled.
Periodic ECG monitoring.
Report new shortness of breath promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat high blood pressure and angina, and sometimes for migraine prevention or portal hypertension.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; commonly 40-80 mg once daily, titrated.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly - can cause rebound high blood pressure or chest pain.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Asthma or severe reactive airway disease
Severe bradycardia or heart block without a pacemaker
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Wheezing or difficulty breathing
Very slow heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting
Signs of worsening heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can blunt the blood-pressure-lowering effect.
Combined with other heart-rate-lowering drugs (e.g., other beta-blockers) can cause excessive bradycardia.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, breathing difficulty, or chest pain.
Never stop abruptly without prescriber guidance - taper is required.
self_monitoring: Check pulse and blood pressure periodically.
Report unusual fatigue or swelling.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: An antifungal eye drop used to treat fungal infections of the eye (fungal keratitis, blepharitis, conjunctivitis).
typical_dosage: 1 drop every 1-2 hours initially, then tapered as directed based on response, often over several weeks.
typical_duration: Typically several weeks, as directed by your eye doctor; do not stop early even if symptoms improve.
directions_for_use: Shake well before use.
Wash hands before instilling.
Continue the full course as directed, even if the eye feels better.
storage_instructions: Store in the refrigerator; protect from light. Do not freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening eye pain, redness, or vision changes despite treatment
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Wait several minutes between this and other eye drop products if multiple are prescribed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your eye doctor promptly if symptoms worsen or do not improve.
self_monitoring: Follow up with your eye doctor as scheduled to confirm the infection is clearing.
missed_dose_instructions: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip and resume the normal schedule.

description: Used to control blood sugar spikes after meals in type 2 diabetes by stimulating rapid, short-acting insulin release.
typical_dosage: 60-120 mg by mouth 1-30 minutes before each main meal.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of diabetes management.
directions_for_use: Take shortly before meals (within 30 minutes).
Skip the dose if you skip a meal, to avoid low blood sugar.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe low blood sugar: confusion, seizure, loss of consciousness
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased hypoglycemia risk when combined with other diabetes medications (metformin, glipizide) or alcohol.
Fluconazole and other CYP2C9 inhibitors can increase nateglinide levels, raising hypoglycemia risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Treat mild low blood sugar promptly with fast-acting glucose; seek emergency care for severe hypoglycemia.
self_monitoring: Check blood glucose regularly, especially around mealtimes.
Keep a fast-acting glucose source available.
missed_dose_instructions: If a meal is skipped, skip that dose. Do not take between meals or double up.

description: A rescue medication used to stop prolonged or repetitive seizure clusters, given by a caregiver when needed, outside of a hospital setting.
dosage_forms: Nasal spray, single-dose device (5 mg per spray)
typical_dosage: One spray (5 mg) into one nostril; a second dose may be given after 10 minutes into the other nostril if seizure activity continues, only if directed by your neurologist's rescue plan.
typical_duration: Used as needed for breakthrough seizure clusters, not on a daily schedule; limited to no more than 1 rescue episode (2 doses) every 3 days and no more than 5 episodes per month, per label guidance.
directions_for_use: Caregivers should be trained in advance on how and when to use this rescue spray.
Insert the tip a short distance into one nostril and press the plunger firmly to release the full dose - it works whether or not the patient inhales.
Position the patient safely (e.g., on their side) after administration due to sedation.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original blister package; keep in a readily accessible, secure location.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to midazolam or benzodiazepines
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe or worsening difficulty breathing
Seizure that does not stop after the rescue doses, or a return to seizures (call emergency services)
Excessive sedation or unresponsiveness
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with alcohol, opioids (hydrocodone/acetaminophen, tramadol), or other sedating OTC products (diphenhydramine) increases the risk of severe sedation and breathing problems.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call emergency services (911) if the seizure does not stop within the expected time, if a new seizure starts, or if breathing becomes difficult or the patient does not wake up as expected.
self_monitoring: Keep a seizure log noting when rescue doses are used.
Ensure device is not expired and caregivers are refreshed on the administration technique periodically.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a rescue medication used only during a seizure cluster, not a scheduled daily dose - there is no missed dose concept.

description: An oral targeted therapy used as extended adjuvant treatment for early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer after completing standard trastuzumab-based therapy.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 240 mg (6 tablets) once daily.
typical_duration: Typically a 1-year course, as directed by your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take with food, at the same time each day.
You will likely be prescribed antidiarrheal medication (such as loperamide) to take proactively during at least the first cycle - follow this schedule closely, as severe diarrhea is very common.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe diarrhea leading to dehydration (dizziness, decreased urination)
Yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine (liver problems)
Severe abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid acid-reducing medications like omeprazole and other PPIs - they significantly reduce neratinib absorption; H2 blockers and antacids also affect absorption and require specific timing - discuss with your pharmacist.
Avoid grapefruit juice and St. John's Wort.
action_if_adverse_effects: Start your antidiarrheal regimen at the first loose stool as instructed and contact your oncology team if diarrhea is severe or persistent.
Call promptly for signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests as scheduled.
Track number of bowel movements per day and report increases promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time the next day. Do not double up.

description: A self-injectable biologic used to reduce the risk of infection from low white blood cell counts (neutropenia) caused by certain chemotherapy regimens.
dosage_forms: On-body injector (Onpro) applied by a healthcare provider that delivers the dose automatically about 27 hours later
typical_dosage: One 6 mg dose per chemotherapy cycle, given approximately 24 hours after chemotherapy (not on the same day).
typical_duration: Given once per chemotherapy cycle, for the duration of your chemotherapy course as directed by your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Do not give on the same day as chemotherapy - timing (about 24 hours after) is important.
If using a prefilled syringe at home, follow your training on proper injection technique and site rotation.
If using the Onpro on-body injector, confirm it is working (you may hear/feel it) and contact your care team if it does not appear to function properly.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; allow to reach room temperature for about 30 minutes before injecting. Do not freeze or shake. Protect from light.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to pegfilgrastim, filgrastim, or E. coli-derived proteins
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden pain in the upper left abdomen or left shoulder tip pain (possible spleen enlargement/rupture)
Difficulty breathing (possible acute respiratory distress)
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling, wheezing
Signs of capillary leak syndrome: sudden swelling, low blood pressure
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or an antihistamine may be used for bone pain/discomfort as directed by your care team; avoid NSAIDs without checking with your oncology team due to bleeding risk during chemotherapy.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe abdominal/shoulder pain, breathing difficulty, or signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Monitor for fever and signs of infection despite treatment and report immediately.
Track bone pain and discuss management options with your care team.
missed_dose_instructions: This is given once per chemotherapy cycle by injection - contact your oncology team if a dose was missed or the on-body injector did not appear to deliver the dose.

description: A transdermal patch used to treat symptoms of Parkinson's disease and restless legs syndrome by stimulating dopamine receptors.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your neurologist; applied once daily and titrated based on response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Apply to clean, dry, intact skin (abdomen, thigh, hip, flank, shoulder, or upper arm) at the same time each day.
Rotate application sites daily to reduce skin reactions - do not reapply to the same spot for 14 days.
Do not use heating pads, saunas, or direct sunlight over the patch - can increase drug release.
Remove the old patch before applying a new one; fold the sticky sides together and dispose of safely (still contains active drug).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original pouch until ready to use.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to rotigotine or patch adhesive components
MRI or cardioversion (patch contains aluminum - remove before these procedures)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden overwhelming sleepiness or falling asleep without warning (especially while driving)
New or worsening compulsive behaviors (gambling, shopping, hypersexuality)
Hallucinations or confusion
Fainting or significant dizziness on standing
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, or other CNS depressants.
Antiemetics like metoclopramide can reduce effectiveness - avoid unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your neurologist for new impulsive behaviors, hallucinations, or significant dizziness.
Do not drive if you experience sudden sleepiness; seek care if this occurs.
self_monitoring: Watch for and report any new compulsive/impulsive behaviors.
Check skin at patch sites for irritation.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply a new patch as soon as remembered and continue with your normal daily patch-change schedule; do not apply an extra patch to make up for a missed one.

description: An antiretroviral medication used with other HIV medications to treat HIV-1 infection.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your HIV specialist; typically started at 200 mg once daily for the first 14 days (lead-in period), then increased to 200 mg twice daily if tolerated.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of a complete antiretroviral regimen.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed, following the lead-in dosing schedule precisely - do not skip the lower starting dose period.
Take consistently with or without food.
Do not skip doses - missed doses can lead to resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Prior discontinuation due to severe rash, hepatotoxicity, or hypersensitivity to nevirapine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, nausea (especially in first weeks)
Severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling (possible Stevens-Johnson syndrome) - most common in the first 6 weeks
Fever with rash
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces nevirapine levels and can lead to treatment failure/resistance.
Many other drug interactions via CYP3A4/2B6 - check with your pharmacist before starting anything new.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your HIV specialist immediately for any new rash, especially with fever, or signs of liver problems.
Seek emergency care for severe skin reactions.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests, especially closely during the first 18 weeks of treatment.
Report any new rash right away, particularly during the first 6 weeks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up. Do not stop this medication without talking to your HIV specialist.

description: An extended-release, once-daily formulation of nevirapine used with other HIV medications to treat HIV-1 infection.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your HIV specialist; typically the immediate-release form is used for the first 14-day lead-in period, then switched to 400 mg extended-release once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of a complete antiretroviral regimen.
directions_for_use: Swallow tablets whole - do not crush, chew, or divide.
Take consistently with or without food, at the same time each day.
Do not skip doses - missed doses can lead to resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Prior discontinuation due to severe rash, hepatotoxicity, or hypersensitivity to nevirapine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, nausea
Severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling (possible Stevens-Johnson syndrome)
Fever with rash
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces nevirapine levels.
Many other drug interactions via CYP3A4/2B6 - check with your pharmacist before starting anything new.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your HIV specialist immediately for any new rash, especially with fever, or signs of liver problems.
Seek emergency care for severe skin reactions.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests, especially closely during the first 18 weeks of treatment.
Report any new rash right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up. Do not stop without talking to your HIV specialist.

description: Used along with diet and other cholesterol medications to lower LDL ("bad") cholesterol in adults with heart disease or high genetic cholesterol risk.
typical_dosage: 180 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of cholesterol management.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Continue taking any other cholesterol medications (such as statins) as directed unless told otherwise.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden pain, swelling, bruising, or weakness near a tendon, especially the Achilles tendon (tendon rupture risk)
Signs of gout: sudden joint pain, redness, swelling (usually the big toe)
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Can increase levels of simvastatin and pravastatin - dose limits may apply; discuss with your prescriber.
No other major OTC interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for tendon pain/swelling or signs of gout.
Stop activity and seek care for sudden tendon pain, especially in the heel.
self_monitoring: Periodic cholesterol (lipid panel) monitoring.
Uric acid level monitoring if you have gout history.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

drug_class: ATP citrate lyase (ACL) inhibitor/cholesterol absorption inhibitor combination
description: A combination tablet used along with diet to lower LDL ("bad") cholesterol in adults with heart disease or high genetic cholesterol risk, combining two complementary mechanisms.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of cholesterol management.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Continue any other cholesterol medications as directed unless told otherwise.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to bempedoic acid or ezetimibe
Concurrent active liver disease (for the ezetimibe component when combined with a statin)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden pain, swelling, or weakness near a tendon, especially the Achilles tendon
Signs of gout: sudden joint pain, redness, swelling
Muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness with dark urine (rare, especially if combined with a statin)
otc_and_other_interactions: Can increase levels of simvastatin and pravastatin if taken together - dose limits may apply.
No other major OTC interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for tendon pain/swelling, signs of gout, or muscle symptoms.
Stop activity and seek care for sudden tendon pain.
self_monitoring: Periodic cholesterol (lipid panel) monitoring.
Uric acid level monitoring if you have gout history.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A small, flexible rod inserted under the skin of the upper arm by a clinician that provides long-acting reversible contraception for up to 3 years.
route: Subdermal implant (inserted in the upper arm)
typical_dosage: One implant inserted by a trained clinician; provides continuous contraception for up to 3 years.
typical_duration: Up to 3 years per implant, then removal and optional replacement.
directions_for_use: Keep the insertion site clean and dry for the first few days as directed.
You should be able to feel the implant under the skin; if you cannot feel it, contact your provider promptly.
Use a backup contraceptive method for the first 7 days if not inserted during the appropriate window of your cycle.
storage_instructions: Handled and stored by the clinic/pharmacy prior to insertion; not stored at home.
contraindications: Current or past history of blood clots
Severe liver disease or liver tumors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Leg swelling/pain, chest pain, or shortness of breath (possible blood clot)
Severe abdominal pain
Signs of infection at the insertion site: increasing redness, warmth, pus
Yellowing of skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort and certain other enzyme-inducing medications can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or severe insertion-site infection.
Contact your provider for irregular bleeding that is bothersome or if you cannot feel the implant.
self_monitoring: Periodically check that you can feel the implant under the skin.
Track bleeding pattern changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Not applicable - this is a continuous long-acting device; schedule removal/replacement with your provider by the 3-year expiration.

description: Used at prescription strength to help lower LDL cholesterol and triglycerides and raise HDL cholesterol.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber, generally starting low (e.g., 500 mg/day) and titrated gradually to reduce flushing.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of cholesterol management.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Taking aspirin (if approved by your prescriber) about 30 minutes before a dose can reduce flushing.
Avoid hot beverages, spicy food, and alcohol around dosing time - can worsen flushing.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue (liver toxicity)
Severe muscle pain or weakness
Signs of high blood sugar: excessive thirst, urination
otc_and_other_interactions: Can raise blood sugar - monitor closely if taking diabetes medications (metformin, glipizide).
Increased muscle toxicity risk when combined with statins (simvastatin, atorvastatin) - report unexplained muscle pain.
Aspirin taken before dosing (with prescriber approval) can reduce flushing.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for signs of liver problems or severe muscle pain.
Do not switch between immediate-release and extended-release niacin products without prescriber guidance - risk of serious liver toxicity.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests.
Periodic blood sugar and uric acid checks.
Track flushing severity and report if intolerable.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A prescription-only, fast-acting nicotine replacement product used to help relieve cravings and withdrawal symptoms as part of a smoking cessation program.
typical_dosage: 1-2 sprays (one in each nostril) per dose, up to 5 doses per hour, not exceeding the maximum daily doses directed on the label, for up to 3 months.
typical_duration: Typically used for up to 3 months as part of a structured quit program, then tapered off.
directions_for_use: Do not sniff, swallow, or inhale through the nose while spraying - this reduces irritation.
Avoid eating or drinking immediately before use.
Do not smoke while using this product.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep out of reach of children and pets - nicotine is toxic if ingested by non-users, especially children.
contraindications: Continued smoking/tobacco use while using this product
Severe or unstable heart disease (recent heart attack, severe arrhythmia)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of nicotine overdose: severe nausea/vomiting, cold sweat, confusion, weakness
Chest pain or irregular heartbeat
Severe or persistent nosebleeds
otc_and_other_interactions: Stopping smoking itself can change the levels of certain other medications (e.g., theophylline) - inform your prescriber when starting a quit attempt.
Avoid combining with other nicotine replacement products unless directed by your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or signs of nicotine overdose.
Call prescriber for persistent nasal irritation or nosebleeds.
self_monitoring: Track cravings and withdrawal symptoms.
Monitor for signs of continued nicotine dependence on the spray itself.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as needed for cravings, not on a fixed schedule; there is no missed dose to make up.

description: An oral targeted therapy used to treat chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) that is Philadelphia chromosome positive.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 300-400 mg twice daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach - no food for at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after each dose.
Swallow capsules whole with water; do not open or crush.
