Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia that is uncorrected
Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (certain antifungals, macrolide antibiotics) or QT-prolonging drugs
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation - a boxed warning; sudden death has occurred)
Yellowing of skin/eyes (liver problems)
Severe abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis)
Signs of high blood sugar
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors including certain antifungals (fluconazole, itraconazole) and macrolide antibiotics (clarithromycin) - can dangerously increase nilotinib levels and QT prolongation risk.
Avoid acid-reducing medications (omeprazole and other PPIs) close to dosing - they reduce nilotinib absorption; H2 blockers and antacids require specific timing per your pharmacist's guidance.
Avoid grapefruit juice and St. John's Wort.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting or irregular heartbeat.
Call your oncology team for signs of liver problems or severe abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Periodic ECG monitoring to check the QT interval.
Regular blood counts, liver function, blood sugar, and electrolyte monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up.

description: Used together with surgical removal of the testicles (orchiectomy) to treat metastatic prostate cancer.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 150-300 mg once daily, started around the time of orchiectomy.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Avoid alcohol - can cause a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, nausea).
Report any vision changes, especially trouble adjusting from light to dark, to your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening shortness of breath or cough (possible interstitial pneumonitis - can be serious)
Yellowing of skin/eyes (liver problems)
Severe vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol-containing products.
May increase levels of other drugs metabolized by the liver - check with your pharmacist before starting anything new.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team immediately for new shortness of breath or cough.
Report vision changes or signs of liver problems promptly.
self_monitoring: Baseline and periodic chest X-rays as directed to monitor for lung changes.
Regular liver function tests.
Report breathing changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to reduce the risk of complications from vasospasm following a subarachnoid hemorrhage (a type of bleeding stroke).
route: Oral (this drug must NEVER be given intravenously - fatal if injected)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; commonly 60 mg by mouth every 4 hours for 21 days.
typical_duration: A defined short course, typically 21 days, starting within 96 hours of the hemorrhage.
directions_for_use: Take exactly on schedule around the clock as directed, generally on an empty stomach.
This medication must only be taken by mouth or given through a feeding tube - it must never be injected.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protected from light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Significant drop in blood pressure: dizziness, fainting
Signs of liver problems
Chest pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit juice - can increase drug levels.
Combined with other blood-pressure-lowering medications can increase risk of hypotension.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for significant dizziness, fainting, or chest pain.
This medication is typically managed in a hospital/rehabilitation setting during the treatment course - report concerns to your care team promptly.
self_monitoring: Blood pressure monitoring, especially when starting or with dose changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your care team promptly for a missed dose given the strict around-the-clock schedule; do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for multiple myeloma, usually used in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 4 mg once weekly on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle.
typical_duration: Continued in cycles as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after food.
Take at the same time each week on the specified days.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open, crush, or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, in the original packaging, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Numbness, tingling, or pain in hands/feet (peripheral neuropathy)
Unusual bruising or bleeding
Signs of infection: fever, chills
New or worsening rash
Severe diarrhea, nausea, or vomiting
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers like St. John's Wort - can reduce effectiveness.
Check with your pharmacist before starting any new OTC medication given bleeding and infection risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team for numbness/tingling, unusual bleeding, or signs of infection.
Seek emergency care for severe reactions.
self_monitoring: Regular blood counts (especially platelets) as scheduled.
Report new numbness or tingling promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by less than 3 days, take it as soon as remembered; if more than 3 days have passed, skip it and resume on the next scheduled day. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat hereditary tyrosinemia type 1 (HT-1), a rare inherited metabolic disorder, in combination with a special low-tyrosine, low-phenylalanine diet.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your metabolic specialist based on body weight and blood levels.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy, generally lifelong.
directions_for_use: Take consistently with or without food, as directed.
Strictly follow the low-tyrosine, low-phenylalanine diet prescribed by your metabolic team - this is essential for the medication to work safely.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, redness, or light sensitivity (corneal changes, usually from high tyrosine levels if diet is not followed)
Easy bruising or bleeding (low platelet count)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes
common_side_effects: Elevated tyrosine levels if diet is not followed
Low platelet or white blood cell counts
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; strict dietary compliance is the main safety factor - discuss any dietary supplement with your metabolic team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your metabolic specialist for eye symptoms or unusual bruising/bleeding.
Report any difficulty maintaining the prescribed diet.
self_monitoring: Regular blood tyrosine level monitoring.
Routine eye exams.
Periodic liver function and blood count monitoring.
Regular alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) monitoring for liver health.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A topical ointment used to prevent chest pain (angina) by relaxing and widening blood vessels; unlike sublingual nitroglycerin, this is used for ongoing prevention, not immediate relief of an angina attack.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically measured in inches using the supplied applicator paper and applied to the skin, with a nitrate-free interval of 10-12 hours daily to prevent tolerance.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use for angina prevention as directed.
directions_for_use: Use the applicator paper (not fingers) to measure and spread a thin, even layer over the marked area, typically on the chest, arm, or thigh - do not rub in.
Rotate application sites to avoid skin irritation.
Follow your prescriber's nitrate-free interval schedule (commonly removing the ointment overnight) to maintain effectiveness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, tightly closed, away from heat.
contraindications: Use with sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, or other PDE5 inhibitors (can cause severe, life-threatening low blood pressure)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe or persistent headache
Fainting, severe dizziness, or very low blood pressure
Chest pain that does not improve with rest (this ointment is not for treating an acute angina attack - use your prescribed sublingual nitroglycerin for that)
otc_and_other_interactions: Never combine with sildenafil or similar erectile dysfunction medications - risk of severe, potentially fatal low blood pressure.
Alcohol can worsen dizziness and low blood pressure.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, severe low blood pressure, or chest pain unrelieved by your rescue nitroglycerin.
Call prescriber for persistent severe headache.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure periodically, especially when starting.
Rotate and inspect application sites for irritation.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered, then resume your normal schedule and nitrate-free interval; do not apply extra ointment to make up for a missed dose.

drug_class: HIV protease inhibitor (used mainly as a pharmacokinetic booster)
description: An antiretroviral medication used with other HIV medications to treat HIV-1 infection; most often used today at low doses to boost (increase) the levels of other HIV protease inhibitors.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your HIV specialist; boosting doses are typically much lower (e.g., 100 mg once or twice daily) than doses used for direct antiviral effect.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of a complete antiretroviral regimen.
directions_for_use: Take with food to improve tolerability and absorption.
Do not skip doses - missed doses can lead to resistance.
Swallow tablets whole; do not chew, crush, or break.
storage_instructions: Store tablets at room temperature; oral solution may require refrigeration - check the pharmacy label.
contraindications: Concurrent use with many drugs that are highly dependent on CYP3A4 for clearance (certain statins, sedatives, ergot medications) - always check with your pharmacist
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis)
Signs of high blood sugar
Irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Potent inhibitor of a liver enzyme (CYP3A4) with extensive drug interactions - dramatically raises levels of many medications including certain statins, sedatives, and erectile dysfunction drugs; always check with your pharmacist before starting or stopping any medication, prescription or OTC.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can significantly reduce ritonavir levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your HIV specialist for signs of liver problems, severe abdominal pain, or irregular heartbeat.
Seek emergency care for severe reactions.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function and blood sugar monitoring.
Routine HIV viral load and CD4 count monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up. Do not stop without talking to your HIV specialist.

description: A self-injectable biologic used to reduce eosinophil-driven inflammation in severe eosinophilic asthma and certain related eosinophilic conditions.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; commonly 100 mg (adults, asthma) injected once every 4 weeks.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed, with periodic reassessment of benefit.
directions_for_use: Allow the prefilled syringe/pen to reach room temperature (about 30-45 minutes) before injecting - do not warm it artificially.
Inject into the thigh, abdomen, or upper arm (with help from another person for the upper arm), rotating sites.
This is not a rescue medication - continue to use your regular quick-relief inhaler for sudden asthma symptoms.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze. May be stored at room temperature for a limited time per the product label if needed - do not put back in the refrigerator once warmed.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing (can occur hours after injection)
Shingles (herpes zoster) - unusual painful rash
Worsening asthma symptoms despite treatment
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; do not stop or reduce other asthma controller medications (including corticosteroids) without your prescriber's guidance, even if you feel better.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Call prescriber for worsening asthma control or a new shingles-like rash.
self_monitoring: Track asthma symptom control and rescue inhaler use, and report worsening control.
Watch for delayed allergic reactions in the hours after injection.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber's office to reschedule as soon as possible; do not double up doses.

description: Used to treat pseudobulbar affect (PBA) - sudden, uncontrollable episodes of laughing or crying that are out of proportion or unrelated to mood - often seen in certain neurologic conditions.
typical_dosage: One capsule once daily for the first 7 days, then one capsule twice daily, as directed by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed for as long as it remains beneficial.
directions_for_use: Take consistently with or without food, about 12 hours apart once on the twice-daily schedule.
Do not take an extra or double dose.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Use with MAOIs (or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI)
Prolonged QT interval, complete heart block, or certain other heart rhythm disorders
Concurrent use with quinidine, quinine, or mefloquine
History of quinidine-induced thrombocytopenia or other quinidine reactions
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation)
Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity (especially if combined with other serotonergic drugs)
Unusual bruising or bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not combine with dextromethorphan-containing OTC cough/cold products - risk of excessive levels/serotonin syndrome.
Increased serotonin syndrome risk when combined with SSRIs (sertraline, escitalopram) or tramadol.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, irregular heartbeat, or signs of serotonin syndrome.
Call prescriber before starting any new medication, including OTC cough/cold products.
self_monitoring: Baseline and periodic ECG monitoring may be recommended, especially if you have heart risk factors.
Track frequency/severity of PBA episodes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat hallucinations and delusions associated with psychosis that can occur in Parkinson's disease.
typical_dosage: 34 mg by mouth once daily, with or without food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly without talking to your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation)
Increased confusion or worsening hallucinations
Signs of a fall or new difficulty walking (elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis are at increased risk of death - discuss risks/benefits with your prescriber)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other QT-prolonging medications.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (certain antifungals like fluconazole, or macrolide antibiotics like clarithromycin) can increase pimavanserin levels and QT prolongation risk - check with your pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting or irregular heartbeat.
Call prescriber for worsening confusion or hallucinations.
self_monitoring: Periodic ECG monitoring may be recommended, especially if you have heart risk factors.
Caregivers should monitor for falls and changes in mental status.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Reduces excess hormone secretion; used for acromegaly, carcinoid syndrome, and certain tumors that cause severe diarrhea/flushing.
typical_dosage: Individualized dose set by your specialist; short-acting form often given 2-3 times daily subcutaneously, or long-acting depot given once monthly by IM injection.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Rotate subcutaneous injection sites to reduce irritation.
Long-acting depot injections must be given by a trained healthcare professional at a clinic, not self-administered.
Allow depot suspension to reach room temperature before injection per pharmacy instructions.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; short-acting vials/ampules may be kept at room temperature for up to 2 weeks once opened per label. Do not freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of gallstones: severe right upper abdominal pain, fever, jaundice - seek care
Severe or persistent abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis) - seek care
Very slow heart rate, dizziness, or fainting - seek care
otc_and_other_interactions: Can raise or lower blood sugar - monitor glucose closely if you take metformin, glipizide, or insulin; dose adjustments may be needed.
May reduce absorption of cyclosporine, requiring dose adjustment in transplant patients.
Can slow heart rate; use caution with other heart-rate-lowering medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for persistent abdominal pain, signs of gallstones, or blood sugar swings.
Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction or fainting.
self_monitoring: Blood glucose checks, especially if diabetic.
Periodic gallbladder ultrasound and thyroid/vitamin B12 monitoring as directed.
Report new abdominal pain promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: For self-injected short-acting doses, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up. Long-acting depot doses should be rescheduled with your clinic as soon as possible.

description: A once-daily single-tablet regimen used to treat HIV-1 infection in appropriate patients.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily with food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day with a meal - food is required for proper absorption.
Do not skip doses; missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original container; keep desiccant in the bottle.
contraindications: Coadministration with proton pump inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole) - significantly reduces rilpivirine absorption
Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue - seek care
Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain with nausea/vomiting - seek emergency care
New or worsening depression, mood changes - contact prescriber
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with omeprazole and other proton pump inhibitors - they drastically lower rilpivirine levels, risking treatment failure and resistance.
St. John's Wort must be avoided - can cause loss of viral control.
H2 blockers (famotidine) must be taken 12 hours before or 4 hours after this medication if needed.
Avoid other NNRTI-containing products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Do not stop or skip doses on your own - contact your HIV specialist about side effects.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe liver problems or lactic acidosis.
self_monitoring: Periodic HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Liver function and kidney function labs as scheduled.
Track adherence closely - missed doses risk resistance.
missed_dose_instructions: If within 12 hours of the usual time, take with food as soon as remembered. If more than 12 hours late, skip the missed dose and resume the next day at the regular time - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for locally advanced basal cell carcinoma that cannot be treated with surgery or radiation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (typically 200 mg by mouth once daily on an empty stomach).
typical_duration: Individualized; continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging, away from moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy (causes severe birth defects/fetal death) - effective contraception required for patients of reproductive potential and their partners
Blood or plasma donation during and for a period after treatment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness with dark urine (possible rhabdomyolysis) - seek care promptly
Signs of pregnancy or missed period while on treatment - contact prescriber immediately
Severe nausea, vomiting, or inability to keep fluids down
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) - can significantly raise sonidegib levels and toxicity risk.
Avoid St. John's Wort and other strong CYP3A4 inducers - can reduce effectiveness.
NSAIDs may add to muscle-related side effect risk when combined with drugs affecting muscle enzymes - discuss with your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncologist for new muscle pain/weakness or severe GI symptoms.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or suspected pregnancy.
self_monitoring: Pregnancy testing before and periodically during treatment as directed.
Creatine kinase (muscle enzyme) monitoring if muscle symptoms occur.
Track weight and nutritional intake.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and resume the next day at the regular time on an empty stomach - do not double up.

description: Slows the decline in lung function in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and other chronic fibrosing interstitial lung diseases.
typical_dosage: 150 mg by mouth twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, with food (individualized/reduced by prescriber if side effects occur).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce nausea.
Swallow capsules whole; do not chew or crush.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep in original blister pack.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, right upper abdominal pain - seek care
Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/vomit - seek care
Chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, or one-sided weakness (possible blood clot/heart attack) - seek emergency care
Severe diarrhea leading to dehydration
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased bleeding risk when combined with warfarin, apixaban, aspirin, or other blood thinners - use caution and report unusual bruising/bleeding.
Strong CYP3A4/P-glycoprotein inhibitors such as clarithromycin can raise nintedanib levels - discuss with your prescriber.
Loperamide is often recommended for diarrhea management - follow prescriber's guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for persistent diarrhea, nausea, or liver-related symptoms; dose may be adjusted.
Seek emergency care for signs of bleeding, blood clot, or severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests before starting and periodically during treatment.
Track weight and signs of dehydration from diarrhea.
Report bruising or bleeding promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for adults with progressing desmoid tumors who require systemic treatment.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (typically 150 mg by mouth twice daily).
typical_duration: Individualized; continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food at consistent times about 12 hours apart.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of ovarian failure (irregular/absent periods) - discuss with prescriber
Severe diarrhea leading to dehydration - seek care
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine - seek care
New rash with blistering or mucous membrane involvement - seek emergency care
common_side_effects: Ovarian dysfunction (in females of reproductive potential)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, clarithromycin) - can raise drug levels.
St. John's Wort and other strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce effectiveness - avoid.
Loperamide may be recommended for diarrhea per your care team's guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncologist for persistent diarrhea, rash, or liver-related symptoms.
Seek emergency care for severe skin reactions or signs of severe dehydration.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests periodically.
Track menstrual changes if applicable.
Monitor hydration during diarrhea episodes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by less than 6 hours, take it as soon as remembered; otherwise skip and resume the next scheduled dose - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for relapsed or refractory pediatric low-grade glioma with a BRAF alteration.
typical_dosage: Individualized weekly dose based on body surface area, set by the treating oncologist.
typical_duration: Individualized; continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Taken once weekly on the same day each week, with or without food.
Follow specialty pharmacy instructions carefully for measuring the oral suspension if prescribed.
storage_instructions: Store tablets at room temperature; oral suspension may require refrigeration - follow pharmacy label.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Vision changes, eye pain, or blurred vision (risk of retinal detachment/vein occlusion) - seek prompt care
Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in urine/stool - seek care
Fever, especially with low blood counts - seek care promptly
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., St. John's Wort) - can reduce drug levels and effectiveness.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, clarithromycin) - can raise drug levels and toxicity risk.
Sun protection recommended - drug can increase photosensitivity.
action_if_adverse_effects: Report any vision changes to the oncology team immediately - a baseline and periodic eye exam is required.
Seek emergency care for fever with low counts or signs of severe bleeding.
self_monitoring: Routine eye examinations as scheduled.
Periodic blood counts and liver function tests.
Watch for and report new vision symptoms right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If a weekly dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is within 3 days of the next scheduled dose - contact your oncology team for guidance rather than doubling up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for myelofibrosis in adults with anemia.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your hematologist/oncologist (typically 200 mg by mouth once daily).
typical_duration: Long-term therapy as directed by your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, cough, burning with urination - seek care promptly (increased infection risk)
Signs of bleeding or easy bruising - seek care
New or worsening abdominal pain, especially with fever (possible bowel perforation) - seek emergency care
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., St. John's Wort, rifampin) - can reduce effectiveness.
Increased infection risk - live vaccines should generally be avoided during treatment; discuss vaccinations with your oncologist.
NSAIDs may add to bleeding/GI risk in patients with low platelet counts - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncologist promptly for signs of infection, bleeding, or new numbness/tingling.
Seek emergency care for severe abdominal pain or signs of bowel perforation.
self_monitoring: Regular complete blood counts.
Liver function monitoring.
Watch for signs of infection and report promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered the same day; if a full day is missed, skip it and resume the next day at the regular time - do not double up.

description: An oral maintenance therapy for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults who achieved remission with chemotherapy.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (typically 300 mg by mouth once daily on days 1-14 of each 28-day cycle).
typical_duration: Individualized; continued cyclically as directed by your oncologist, often for an extended period while in remission.
directions_for_use: Take at approximately the same time each day, with or without food, only on the prescribed days of each cycle.
Swallow tablets whole; do not cut, crush, or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever or signs of infection, especially with low blood counts - seek care promptly (this can be a medical emergency)
Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/urine
Severe nausea/vomiting/diarrhea leading to dehydration
otc_and_other_interactions: Anti-nausea medication (e.g., ondansetron) is often prescribed 30 minutes before each dose - follow your oncologist's instructions.
Increased bleeding risk with NSAIDs, aspirin, warfarin, or clopidogrel when blood counts are low - report unusual bruising/bleeding.
Live vaccines should be avoided during treatment due to immune suppression.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncology team promptly for fever, signs of infection, or bleeding.
Seek emergency care for high fever with low counts (neutropenic fever) - this requires urgent evaluation.
self_monitoring: Regular complete blood counts before and during each cycle.
Liver and kidney function tests as directed.
Take your temperature if feeling unwell.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed or vomited, do not make it up - take the next dose at its regularly scheduled time and contact your oncology team.

description: An emergency nasal spray used to reverse known or suspected opioid overdose, similar in purpose to naloxone but longer-acting.
typical_dosage: One spray (2.7 mg) into one nostril at the first sign of opioid overdose; may repeat every 2-3 minutes in alternating nostrils with additional devices if there is no response, while awaiting emergency help.
typical_duration: Used as needed in an emergency; not a scheduled daily medication.
directions_for_use: Call 911 (or local emergency services) immediately before or after giving the dose.
Tilt the person's head back, insert the tip into one nostril, and press the plunger firmly to release the full dose.
Because this reverses opioid effects, the person needs continued monitoring - the reversal can wear off before the opioid does.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; protect from light; do not freeze. Keep readily accessible with caregivers/household members.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of acute opioid withdrawal (agitation, sweating, rapid heart rate, vomiting) - can occur after use, seek medical follow-up
The person remains unresponsive or stops breathing despite dosing - continue emergency care/CPR and await EMS
otc_and_other_interactions: Will precipitate acute withdrawal in someone taking opioids such as hydrocodone/acetaminophen or tramadol - this is the intended reversal effect but can be distressing.
No significant OTC interactions expected; this is used only in emergency overdose situations.
action_if_adverse_effects: Always seek emergency medical evaluation after any use, even if the person seems to recover, because overdose effects can return.
If severe withdrawal symptoms occur, keep the person calm and get medical care.
self_monitoring: Not applicable for routine self-monitoring; this is a rescue medication for bystanders/caregivers to keep on hand and know how to use.
missed_dose_instructions: Not applicable - this is used only for emergency opioid overdose reversal, not on a schedule.

description: An oral extended-release medication that widens blood vessels in the lungs to improve exercise capacity in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
typical_dosage: Individualized starting dose, gradually titrated upward by your pulmonary hypertension specialist based on tolerability (titration packs are used during dose escalation).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with food at the same times each day, approximately 12 hours apart.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, break, or chew.
Do not stop abruptly - stopping suddenly can cause a dangerous rebound worsening of pulmonary hypertension symptoms.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/vomit - seek care (drug reduces platelet clumping)
Fainting, severe dizziness, or chest pain - seek emergency care
Signs of worsening pulmonary hypertension if a dose is missed or stopped abruptly
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases bleeding risk when combined with aspirin, warfarin, apixaban, clopidogrel, or NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) - use caution and report unusual bruising or bleeding.
Can add to the blood-pressure-lowering effect of other antihypertensives (e.g., amlodipine, lisinopril, losartan) - monitor for dizziness.
Diuretics may worsen dehydration-related dizziness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your specialist if side effects are intolerable rather than stopping on your own.
Seek emergency care for signs of bleeding, fainting, or chest pain.
self_monitoring: Track exercise tolerance and symptoms as directed by your pulmonary hypertension team.
Report new bruising/bleeding.
Home blood pressure checks if advised.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not double up. Never stop this medication abruptly without medical guidance.

description: An oral hormone therapy used to lower testosterone in advanced prostate cancer.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist/urologist (typically a 360 mg loading dose on day one, then 120 mg by mouth once daily).
typical_duration: Long-term therapy as directed by your oncologist/urologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not skip or stop doses without talking to your prescriber - missing doses may reduce effectiveness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong P-glycoprotein inducers unless directed
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, or one-sided weakness (cardiovascular/QT risk) - seek emergency care
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
New or worsening depression or mood changes
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort and other strong P-glycoprotein/CYP inducers can reduce effectiveness - avoid.
May prolong the QT interval - use caution with other QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., ondansetron) and discuss with your prescriber.
May worsen blood sugar/cholesterol control - monitor if taking metformin or glipizide.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for mood changes, liver-related symptoms, or worsening glucose control.
Seek emergency care for chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or fainting.
self_monitoring: Testosterone level checks as directed.
Blood glucose and cholesterol monitoring.
Bone density monitoring for long-term use.
Blood pressure checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered the same day; if not remembered until the next day, skip it and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Contact your prescriber if you miss multiple doses.

description: A combination therapy that improves the function of the defective CFTR protein in people with cystic fibrosis who have two copies of the F508del mutation.
typical_dosage: Individualized by age/weight, set by your CF specialist; typically taken twice daily, 12 hours apart, with fat-containing food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with fat-containing food (eggs, butter, cheese, nuts) to help absorption.
Swallow tablets whole; granules can be mixed with soft food or liquid for young children per pharmacist instructions.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors without dose adjustment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain - seek care
Shortness of breath, chest tightness, or wheezing shortly after starting - seek care
Significant increase in blood pressure
otc_and_other_interactions: Strongly reduces the effectiveness of many other medications, including hormonal contraceptives and statins (e.g., simvastatin, atorvastatin), by inducing drug metabolism - discuss all medications with your CF care team.
Avoid St. John's Wort - combined induction can further reduce effectiveness.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors like fluconazole and clarithromycin unless directed, as levels can be significantly altered in either direction.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your CF care team for breathing difficulty after starting, or liver-related symptoms.
Do not stop abruptly without guidance from your specialist.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests before starting and periodically during treatment.
Blood pressure checks.
Eye exams (cataracts have been reported in children).
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with fatty food if within 6 hours of the missed dose; otherwise skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up.

description: An oral hormone therapy for ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has progressed on prior therapy.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (typically 345 mg by mouth once daily with food).
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take with food at the same time each day.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath - seek emergency care
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe nausea/vomiting affecting ability to eat or drink
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid St. John's Wort and other strong/moderate CYP3A4 inducers - significantly reduce drug levels and effectiveness.
Avoid strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, clarithromycin) - can raise drug levels and toxicity risk.
May affect cholesterol - discuss with prescriber if you take a statin such as atorvastatin or simvastatin.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncologist for persistent nausea or liver-related symptoms.
Seek emergency care for signs of a blood clot.
self_monitoring: Liver function and cholesterol/triglyceride labs periodically.
Track nausea and appetite; report if unable to eat.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: An oral, non-hormonal-acting tablet used to treat moderate to severe painful intercourse (dyspareunia) due to menopause-related vaginal changes.
typical_dosage: 60 mg by mouth once daily with food.
typical_duration: Long-term as needed for symptom control, reassessed periodically by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take with food at the same time each day.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden severe headache, or one-sided weakness - seek emergency care
Vaginal bleeding after starting treatment - contact prescriber promptly
otc_and_other_interactions: May increase the effect of warfarin - closer INR monitoring may be needed.
Fluconazole and other CYP2C9/CYP3A4 inhibitors can raise ospemifene levels - use caution.
Should not be combined with estrogen-containing products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for new vaginal bleeding.
Seek emergency care for signs of a blood clot or stroke.
self_monitoring: Report any vaginal bleeding promptly.
Routine gynecologic follow-up as scheduled.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food; if close to the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not double up.

description: An oral medication used to treat plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and oral ulcers of Behcet's disease.
typical_dosage: Titrated over the first 5-6 days per the starter pack, then a maintenance dose of 30 mg by mouth twice daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic symptom control.
directions_for_use: Follow the titration schedule on the starter pack exactly.
Take with or without food, approximately 12 hours apart.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening depression, anxiety, or suicidal thoughts - seek care immediately
Significant unintended weight loss - contact prescriber
Severe or persistent diarrhea/vomiting
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP450 inducers (e.g., St. John's Wort, rifampin) can reduce effectiveness - avoid.
No significant interaction with common OTC analgesics such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for mood changes or significant weight loss.
Seek emergency/urgent care for suicidal thoughts or severe dehydration from diarrhea.
self_monitoring: Track mood changes.
Monitor weight periodically.
Report persistent GI symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next dose, then skip the missed dose - do not double up.

description: An oral extended-release antipsychotic used to treat schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber (typically 3-12 mg by mouth once daily in the morning).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, typically in the morning, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole - do not crush, chew, or split; the outer shell may appear in the stool, which is normal.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to paliperidone or risperidone
severe_side_effects_seek_care: High fever, muscle rigidity, confusion, irregular heartbeat/sweating (possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care
Uncontrollable muscle movements of face/tongue/limbs (possible tardive dyskinesia) - contact prescriber
Fainting, irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation risk)
New or worsening suicidal thoughts
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with alcohol, diphenhydramine, alprazolam, or tramadol - use caution.
May prolong the QT interval - use caution with other QT-prolonging drugs such as ondansetron.
Can raise blood sugar - monitor if taking metformin or glipizide.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber promptly for tremor, restlessness, or significant sedation.
Seek emergency care for signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or fainting.
self_monitoring: Weight and blood glucose/lipid checks periodically.
Watch for abnormal movements and report them.
Blood pressure checks, especially with position changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next day's dose - do not double up; contact prescriber if multiple doses are missed.

description: A topical gel used to treat cutaneous lesions of AIDS-related Kaposi's sarcoma.
typical_dosage: Apply a generous coat to each lesion 2-4 times daily as directed by your prescriber, increasing frequency gradually as tolerated.
typical_duration: Individualized; continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Apply only to lesions, allowing the gel to dry for 3-5 minutes before covering with clothing.
Avoid applying to normal surrounding skin or mucous membranes.
Wash hands after application unless the hands are being treated.
storage_instructions: Store in refrigerator; keep tube tightly closed; do not freeze.
contraindications: Application to normal (non-lesional) skin or near mucous membranes
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe skin irritation, blistering, or ulceration at application sites - contact prescriber
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid using other topical products (including OTC insect repellents such as DEET) on treated skin - can increase absorption/irritation.
Avoid concurrent use of other topical retinoids or exfoliants on the same area.
Minimize sun exposure on treated areas; use sun protection.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber if irritation is severe; frequency of application may need to be reduced.
Seek care for signs of allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Monitor lesions for response and surrounding skin for irritation.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the next dose at the regular scheduled time; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: A synthetic vitamin D analog used to prevent and treat secondary hyperparathyroidism associated with chronic kidney disease.
route: Oral (also available IV for dialysis administration)
typical_dosage: Individualized based on parathyroid hormone (PTH) level, set by your nephrologist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy, adjusted based on lab results.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food at consistent times as directed.
Do not take with other vitamin D supplements unless approved by your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high calcium: nausea, vomiting, constipation, confusion, muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat - seek care
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid magnesium-containing antacids (e.g., Maalox) - risk of high magnesium levels in kidney disease.
Avoid additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless directed - risk of hypercalcemia.
Digoxin (not in this database) combined with hypercalcemia increases arrhythmia risk - report symptoms of high calcium promptly.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your nephrologist for symptoms of high calcium.
Do not adjust dose without lab-guided direction from your care team.
self_monitoring: Regular calcium, phosphorus, and PTH lab monitoring as scheduled - critical for safe dosing.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up; follow your nephrologist's specific instructions for your dosing schedule.

generic_name: Diphtheria, tetanus, acellular pertussis, hepatitis B, and inactivated poliovirus vaccine
description: A combination childhood vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B, and polio, given as part of the routine infant immunization series.
typical_dosage: 0.5 mL by intramuscular injection, given as a 3-dose series at 2, 4, and 6 months of age, per the pediatric immunization schedule.
typical_duration: Completed as a 3-dose primary series; additional boosters of individual components given later per schedule.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare professional in a clinic or pharmacy setting - not self-administered.
Bring the child's vaccination record to each visit.
Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for post-vaccination discomfort per pediatrician's guidance.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate (36-46F); do not freeze; protect from light. Handled by the administering clinic/pharmacy.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a prior dose or vaccine component
Encephalopathy within 7 days of a previous pertussis-containing vaccine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: High fever (over 105F) or persistent inconsolable crying lasting 3+ hours - seek care
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care
Seizure or limpness/paleness following vaccination - seek emergency care
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen given routinely to prevent fever may slightly blunt the immune response - use only as needed for discomfort per pediatrician's advice.
No significant interactions with other childhood vaccines given at the same visit at different injection sites.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact the pediatrician for high fever or prolonged crying.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or seizure.
self_monitoring: Monitor the child for fever and injection site reaction for 48-72 hours after each dose.
missed_dose_instructions: If a scheduled dose is missed, contact the pediatrician to reschedule as soon as possible - the series does not need to be restarted, just continued.

description: A self-injectable biologic used to treat chronic hepatitis B and C and certain blood disorders by stimulating the immune system's antiviral/antitumor activity.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist (commonly 180 mcg subcutaneously once weekly).
typical_duration: Individualized course, often 24-48 weeks depending on the condition treated.
directions_for_use: Inject subcutaneously into the thigh or abdomen, rotating sites, on the same day each week.
Bring to room temperature before injecting; do not shake the syringe.
Taking acetaminophen before injection may reduce flu-like symptoms - follow your prescriber's guidance.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate (36-46F); do not freeze; protect from light. Keep in original carton until use.
contraindications: Severe psychiatric illness, including active suicidal ideation
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening depression, suicidal thoughts, or severe mood changes - seek care immediately
Signs of infection: fever, chills (interferon suppresses blood counts) - seek care
Vision changes - contact prescriber
Signs of autoimmune problems: new joint pain, rash, or thyroid symptoms
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen is commonly used for flu-like symptoms and is generally compatible - avoid exceeding recommended daily doses.
May increase the effect of warfarin - closer INR monitoring is often needed.
Additive bone marrow suppression with other immunosuppressive/chemotherapy drugs - discuss all medications with your specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your specialist promptly for mood changes, signs of infection, or vision changes.
Seek emergency/urgent care for suicidal thoughts.
self_monitoring: Regular complete blood counts and liver function tests.
Thyroid function tests periodically.
Track mood - use a symptom log if directed.
Eye exams if you have diabetes or hypertension.
missed_dose_instructions: Give the missed dose as soon as remembered if within 2 days of the scheduled time; otherwise skip it and resume the normal weekly schedule - do not double up. Contact your specialist if unsure.

description: An oral targeted therapy for previously treated, unresectable, or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma (bile duct cancer) with an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist, typically taken once daily for 14 days followed by 7 days off, in repeating 21-day cycles.
typical_duration: Individualized; continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food, only on the prescribed days of each cycle.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Vision changes, eye pain, or blurred vision (risk of retinal detachment) - seek prompt eye exam
Signs of high phosphate levels (usually found on labs, may cause soft tissue calcification)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe dry eyes or mouth
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, clarithromycin) and moderate inhibitors when possible - can raise drug levels and toxicity risk.
Avoid St. John's Wort and other strong CYP3A4 inducers - can reduce effectiveness.
Limit phosphate-containing supplements unless directed, given the risk of elevated phosphate levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Report any vision changes to your oncology team immediately - a baseline and periodic eye exam is required.
Contact your oncologist for skin/nail changes or persistent diarrhea.
self_monitoring: Routine eye examinations.
Periodic phosphate, liver, and kidney labs.
Skin and nail care as advised.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than 4 hours, skip it and resume the next scheduled dose - do not double up.

generic_name: Meningococcal groups A, B, C, W, Y vaccine
description: A vaccine that protects against the five most common serogroups of Neisseria meningitidis (meningococcal disease) in a single combination shot for adolescents and young adults.
typical_dosage: 0.5 mL by intramuscular injection, given as a 2-dose series at least 6 months apart, per current immunization guidelines for ages 10-25.
typical_duration: 2-dose primary series; booster timing per current CDC recommendations for ongoing risk.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare professional/pharmacist - not self-administered.
Bring your vaccination record to each visit.
OTC pain relievers (acetaminophen or ibuprofen) may be used for injection site soreness if needed.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate (36-46F); do not freeze. Handled by the administering clinic/pharmacy.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a prior dose or vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care
High fever or fainting shortly after injection
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant interactions with other vaccines given at the same visit at separate injection sites.
Acetaminophen/ibuprofen may be used for post-vaccination discomfort.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your provider for high fever or concerning symptoms.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Monitor for injection site reaction and fever for 48-72 hours after each dose.
missed_dose_instructions: If the second dose is delayed, get it as soon as possible - the series does not need to be restarted; contact your provider to reschedule.

description: An oral medication that binds excess copper and is used to treat Wilson's disease, cystinuria, and (less commonly) severe rheumatoid arthritis.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; typically started at a low dose and titrated based on condition and labs.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic conditions like Wilson's disease.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals and at least 1 hour apart from other drugs, milk, or antacids.
Your prescriber may recommend a pyridoxine (vitamin B6) supplement while on this medication.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: History of penicillamine-related aplastic anemia or agranulocytosis
Pregnancy (in most cases; requires specialist guidance)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood counts: fever, unusual bruising/bleeding, mouth sores - seek care promptly
Signs of kidney problems: swelling, decreased urination, protein in urine
New rash, joint pain, or muscle weakness (possible autoimmune reaction)
Severe shortness of breath (rare lung toxicity)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid iron supplements and antacids within 2 hours of dosing - they reduce absorption.
Avoid taking with dairy products at the same time as absorption is reduced.
NSAIDs and other drugs affecting bone marrow or kidneys should be used cautiously - discuss with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber promptly for signs of low blood counts, kidney problems, or new rash.
Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction or breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Regular complete blood counts and urinalysis (protein) as directed - essential for safe long-term use.
Report fever, bruising, or swelling promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on an empty stomach if possible; if close to the next dose, skip it - do not double up.

generic_name: Diphtheria, tetanus, acellular pertussis, inactivated poliovirus, and Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine
description: A combination childhood vaccine protecting against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, and Haemophilus influenzae type b, given as part of the routine infant immunization series.
typical_dosage: 0.5 mL by intramuscular injection, given as a 4-dose series typically at 2, 4, 6, and 15-18 months of age per the pediatric immunization schedule.
typical_duration: Completed as a 4-dose primary/booster series.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare professional - not self-administered.
Bring the child's vaccination record to each visit.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate (36-46F); do not freeze. Handled by the administering clinic/pharmacy.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a prior dose or vaccine component
Encephalopathy within 7 days of a previous pertussis-containing vaccine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: High fever or persistent inconsolable crying lasting 3+ hours - seek care
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care
Seizure following vaccination - seek emergency care
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant interactions with other routine childhood vaccines given at the same visit at separate injection sites.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact the pediatrician for high fever or prolonged crying.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or seizure.
self_monitoring: Monitor the child for fever and injection site reaction for 48-72 hours after each dose.
missed_dose_instructions: If a scheduled dose is missed, contact the pediatrician to reschedule as soon as possible - the series does not need to be restarted.

description: An oral medication that improves blood flow, used to relieve leg pain/cramping (intermittent claudication) caused by peripheral artery disease.
typical_dosage: 400 mg by mouth 2-3 times daily with meals.
typical_duration: Long-term use; benefit may take up to 8 weeks to become apparent.
directions_for_use: Take with meals to reduce stomach upset.
Swallow tablets whole - do not crush or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to pentoxifylline or methylxanthines (e.g., caffeine, theophylline)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/vomit - seek care
Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or dizziness - seek care
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases bleeding risk when combined with warfarin, apixaban, clopidogrel, aspirin, or NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) - use caution and report unusual bruising or bleeding.
May enhance the blood-pressure-lowering effect of antihypertensives such as lisinopril or amlodipine.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for persistent nausea/dizziness.
Seek care for signs of bleeding or chest pain.
self_monitoring: Track leg pain/walking distance to assess benefit.
Report unusual bruising or bleeding.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: Relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiovascular risk in patients with coronary artery disease.
typical_dosage: 4-16 mg by mouth once daily, titrated to blood pressure response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day, with or without food.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness, especially with the first doses.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: History of angioedema with ACE inhibitors
Concurrent use with aliskiren in diabetic patients
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing/swallowing (angioedema) - seek emergency care immediately
Persistent dry cough that is bothersome
Signs of high potassium: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium unless directed - risk of hyperkalemia.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can blunt blood-pressure-lowering effect and stress the kidneys - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for facial/throat swelling or breathing trouble.
Call prescriber for a persistent cough or signs of high potassium; do not stop abruptly without guidance.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure at home if recommended and keep a log.
Report unusual swelling right away.
Keep scheduled potassium/kidney function labs.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat schizophrenia and severe nausea/vomiting that hasn't responded to other treatments.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically 4-16 mg by mouth 2-4 times daily for psychiatric use.
typical_duration: Individualized; long-term for chronic psychiatric conditions.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed, with or without food.
Avoid prolonged sun exposure - can increase sun sensitivity.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with large doses of CNS depressants
severe_side_effects_seek_care: High fever, muscle rigidity, confusion, irregular heartbeat/sweating (possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care
Uncontrollable muscle movements of face/tongue/limbs (possible tardive dyskinesia) - contact prescriber
Yellowing of skin/eyes (possible liver effect)
Signs of low blood counts: fever, sore throat
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, or tramadol - use caution.
May prolong the QT interval - use caution with other QT-prolonging drugs such as ondansetron.
Can increase sedation and blood-pressure-lowering effects of other medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber promptly for abnormal movements or significant sedation.
Seek emergency care for signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
self_monitoring: Watch for abnormal movements and report them.
Periodic liver function and blood count labs as directed.
Blood pressure checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: Used to control certain types of seizures and, less commonly, for sedation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber based on condition, age, and blood levels (commonly 60-200 mg by mouth daily for seizure control).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic seizure disorders; do not stop abruptly.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time(s) each day, with or without food.
Do not stop suddenly - abrupt discontinuation can cause dangerous withdrawal seizures.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep secure due to controlled-substance/misuse potential.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe drowsiness, slowed/shallow breathing, or confusion (overdose risk, especially with other sedatives) - seek emergency care
Signs of severe skin reaction: rash, blistering, peeling skin - seek emergency care
New or worsening depression or suicidal thoughts
otc_and_other_interactions: Dangerous additive sedation and respiratory depression with alcohol, diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen - avoid combining.
Strongly reduces the effectiveness of warfarin (dose changes often needed), hormonal contraceptives, and many other drugs by inducing liver enzymes.
St. John's Wort may add to sedative effects and complicate seizure control - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe sedation, slowed breathing, or signs of overdose.
Contact prescriber for mood changes; never stop this medication abruptly.
self_monitoring: Periodic blood level monitoring as directed.
Seizure frequency log.
Watch for excessive daytime sedation.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up. Missing doses can trigger seizures; contact your prescriber if you miss more than one dose.

description: An oral antiretroviral used in combination with other medications to treat HIV-1 infection.
typical_dosage: 100 mg by mouth once daily, with or without food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of a combination HIV regimen.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day as part of your complete regimen.
Do not skip doses - missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original container.
contraindications: Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
New or worsening depression, unusual dreams, or mood changes
Signs of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (new infection symptoms shortly after starting therapy)
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort must be avoided - can cause loss of viral control and resistance.
Avoid other strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., phenobarbital); discuss all new medications, including OTC and herbal products, with your HIV specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Do not stop or skip doses on your own - contact your HIV specialist about side effects.
Seek care for signs of severe liver problems.
self_monitoring: Periodic HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Liver function labs as scheduled.
Track adherence closely.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on the same day; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not double up.

description: An oral tablet used to treat dry mouth caused by radiation therapy for head and neck cancer or by Sjogren's syndrome.
typical_dosage: 5-10 mg by mouth 3-4 times daily, individualized by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term as needed for symptom control.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset unless directed otherwise.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe sweating with dizziness or dehydration - seek care
Chest pain, very slow or irregular heartbeat - seek emergency care
Difficulty breathing or wheezing (bronchospasm) - seek emergency care
Significant vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive slowing of heart rate when combined with beta-blockers such as metoprolol - use caution.
May counteract effects of anticholinergic medications (e.g., diphenhydramine); avoid combining unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for excessive sweating or dizziness.
Seek emergency care for chest pain, severe wheezing, or very slow heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Track hydration status due to increased sweating.
Monitor heart rate if you have cardiac history.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: Used to control motor and phonic tics in Tourette's disorder when other treatments have not worked.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber, started at a low dose and slowly titrated (commonly up to 0.2 mg/kg/day, not to exceed 10 mg/day).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy with periodic reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed, at consistent times.
Avoid grapefruit juice - can increase drug levels.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture.
contraindications: Congenital long QT syndrome or history of cardiac arrhythmias
Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or other CYP2D6/QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., macrolide antibiotics, azole antifungals)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation risk) - seek emergency care
High fever, muscle rigidity, confusion (possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care
Uncontrollable muscle movements (possible tardive dyskinesia)
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin and fluconazole - risk of dangerous QT prolongation and arrhythmia.
Avoid combining with other QT-prolonging drugs such as ondansetron.
Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, or tramadol.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, palpitations, or signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
Contact prescriber for abnormal movements.
self_monitoring: Baseline and periodic ECG monitoring as directed - essential given QT risk.
Watch for abnormal movements.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up; contact prescriber if several doses are missed.

description: Used to treat high blood pressure.
typical_dosage: 5-30 mg by mouth twice daily, individualized to blood pressure response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly - can cause rebound high blood pressure or chest pain.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Very slow heart rate, dizziness, or fainting - seek care
Signs of worsening heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath, weight gain - seek care
Chest pain if stopped abruptly - seek emergency care
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can blunt the blood-pressure-lowering effect.
Additive blood-pressure and heart-rate-lowering effects with other antihypertensives (e.g., amlodipine, lisinopril, losartan) or pilocarpine.
May mask symptoms of low blood sugar in patients taking metformin or glipizide.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for excessive dizziness or fatigue; never stop abruptly.
Seek emergency care for chest pain or fainting.
self_monitoring: Home blood pressure and pulse checks.
Blood glucose monitoring if diabetic.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy combined with hormone therapy for PIK3CA-mutated, HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (commonly 300 mg by mouth once daily with food, in combination with hormone therapy).
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per your oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take with food at the same time each day.
Swallow tablets whole - do not crush or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe high blood sugar: excessive thirst/urination, confusion - seek care promptly (very common and can be serious)
Severe skin reaction: widespread rash, blistering, peeling skin (rare but serious - can be life-threatening) - seek emergency care
Severe diarrhea leading to dehydration
Signs of pneumonitis: new cough, shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: Can significantly raise blood sugar - if you take metformin or glipizide, glucose monitoring and dose adjustments are important.
May increase levels of warfarin (via CYP2C9 interaction) - closer INR monitoring may be needed.
Avoid St. John's Wort and other strong CYP3A4 inducers - can reduce effectiveness.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) - can raise alpelisib levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncology team promptly for high blood sugar symptoms or new rash - early treatment can prevent severe reactions.
Seek emergency care for severe skin reactions or breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Frequent blood glucose checks, especially early in treatment.
Skin checks for rash.
Periodic kidney and electrolyte labs.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by less than 9 hours, take it with food as soon as remembered; otherwise skip it and resume the next day at the regular time - do not double up.

description: An oral medication used to slow the progression of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
typical_dosage: Titrated over 2 weeks up to a maintenance dose of 801 mg (3 tablets/capsules) by mouth three times daily with food, per your pulmonologist's titration schedule.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce nausea.
Avoid or minimize sun/UV light exposure and use sunscreen - can cause severe photosensitivity.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue - seek care
Severe sunburn-like reaction after minimal sun exposure - seek care
Signs of allergic reaction: swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Use sunscreen (SPF 50+) and protective clothing - combined with other photosensitizing drugs the risk of severe sunburn increases.
CYP1A2 inhibitors (including certain antidepressants, not on this list) can raise levels - discuss all medications with your prescriber.
No significant interaction with common OTC pain relievers, though liver function should be monitored if using acetaminophen regularly.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for persistent nausea, rash, or liver-related symptoms.
Seek care for severe sun-related skin reactions.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests before starting and periodically during treatment.
Track weight/appetite.
Sun exposure precautions.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take the next dose with food at the regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: A topical solution or gel used to treat external genital and perianal warts.
typical_dosage: Apply to visible warts twice daily for 3 consecutive days, then stop for 4 days; repeat this weekly cycle for up to 4 weeks as directed.
typical_duration: Up to 4 treatment cycles; if warts persist beyond that, contact your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Apply only to the wart tissue using the applicator or a cotton swab, avoiding normal surrounding skin.
Allow to air dry before dressing.
Wash hands thoroughly after application.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep away from flame (solution is flammable). Keep tightly closed.
contraindications: Application to internal/mucosal warts (cervical, vaginal, urethral, or anal canal warts)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe burning, blistering, ulceration, or bleeding at application site - contact prescriber
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic drug interactions expected due to minimal absorption when used as directed on small areas.
Avoid using other topical products on the same area at the same time.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber if local reaction is severe; treatment may need to be paused.
Seek care for signs of allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Monitor treated area for excessive irritation.
Follow up with prescriber if warts do not improve after 4 cycles.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the next dose at the regular scheduled time in the treatment cycle; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: An oral targeted therapy used, usually in combination with dexamethasone, to treat multiple myeloma that has progressed after other treatments; also used for AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (commonly 4 mg by mouth once daily on days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle).
typical_duration: Continued in cycles as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food, only on the prescribed days of each cycle.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open, break, or chew.
Available only through a restricted distribution program (REMS) due to risk of severe birth defects.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original blister packaging.
contraindications: Pregnancy (can cause severe birth defects/fetal death)
Patients unable to comply with the required pregnancy prevention program
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath - seek emergency care (blood clot prophylaxis is often prescribed with this medication)
Fever or signs of infection with low blood counts - seek care promptly
Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/urine
New or worsening shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased blood clot risk when combined with other prothrombotic drugs; anticoagulants such as warfarin or apixaban are often co-prescribed for prevention and require close monitoring since the balance of clotting vs. bleeding risk can shift.
Increased bleeding risk with NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) or aspirin when platelet counts are low.
Live vaccines should be avoided during treatment due to immune suppression.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncology team promptly for signs of infection or bleeding.
Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot.
self_monitoring: Regular complete blood counts.
Monthly pregnancy testing if applicable, per REMS program.
Watch for leg swelling/pain.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time the following day - do not double up.

description: An oral medication that makes the urine less acidic, used to prevent certain types of kidney stones (uric acid and calcium stones) in patients with low urine citrate.
