typical_dosage: Individualized based on 24-hour urine testing, set by your prescriber; commonly 10-20 mEq by mouth 2-3 times daily with meals.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy for chronic kidney stone prevention.
directions_for_use: Take with meals or within 30 minutes after eating to reduce stomach upset.
Swallow tablets whole with plenty of water - do not crush, chew, or suck on them.
Do not lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high potassium: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, tingling - seek care
Severe abdominal pain or GI bleeding (black stools, vomiting blood) - seek emergency care
Difficulty swallowing or feeling that the tablet is stuck
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with potassium-sparing effects of ACE inhibitors (lisinopril) or ARBs (losartan) without monitoring - risk of hyperkalemia.
Avoid NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) when possible - can raise potassium levels and affect kidney function.
Do not take with other potassium supplements unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for signs of high potassium or severe stomach pain.
Seek emergency care for GI bleeding or severe abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Periodic potassium and kidney function labs.
24-hour urine citrate/pH testing as directed to assess effectiveness.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: An oral medication used to treat infections caused by flukes and tapeworms (schistosomiasis, tapeworm infections).
typical_dosage: Individualized based on body weight and the specific parasite being treated, set by your prescriber; often given as 1-3 doses in a single day.
typical_duration: Short-term; typically a 1-day treatment course, sometimes repeated.
directions_for_use: Take with food.
Swallow tablets whole with liquid without chewing - tablets have a bitter taste that can cause gagging if chewed.
Avoid activities requiring alertness (e.g., driving) on the day of treatment, as dizziness/drowsiness can occur.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, difficulty breathing - seek care
Severe abdominal pain or fever after treatment for certain infections (possible inflammatory reaction to dying parasites) - seek care
Seizures (particularly if neurocysticercosis is present) - seek emergency care
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit juice around the time of dosing - may increase drug levels.
No significant interactions with common OTC analgesics such as acetaminophen expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for persistent side effects.
Seek emergency care for seizures or severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Follow-up stool or blood testing as directed to confirm the infection has cleared.
missed_dose_instructions: This is typically a short, supervised treatment course - contact your prescriber if a dose is missed rather than taking it on your own schedule.

description: An oral corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation in conditions such as asthma flares, severe allergic reactions, croup, and autoimmune conditions.
typical_dosage: Individualized based on weight and condition, set by your prescriber; short courses are common (e.g., a several-day burst), tapered if used long-term.
typical_duration: Short courses of a few days for acute flares; longer tapering courses for chronic conditions as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset.
Do not stop a long-term course abruptly - follow the prescribed taper schedule.
Shake oral solution well before measuring with an accurate dosing device.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from light; check specific product label for refrigeration needs.
contraindications: Live vaccine administration during high-dose therapy
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection that seem to be masked or worsening (fever, unusual fatigue)
Severe mood changes, confusion, or agitation
Signs of high blood sugar: excessive thirst/urination
Black, tarry stools or stomach pain (possible GI bleeding)
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) increase the risk of stomach ulcers/GI bleeding when combined - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
Can raise blood sugar - monitor closely if taking metformin or glipizide.
May reduce the effectiveness of some vaccines given during treatment.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for mood changes, high blood sugar symptoms, or signs of GI bleeding.
Never stop a tapering steroid course abruptly.
self_monitoring: Blood glucose checks if diabetic or on a long course.
Track weight and appetite changes.
Monitor for mood changes, especially in children.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, follow your prescriber's specific instructions rather than doubling up, especially on a tapering schedule.

description: A steroid eye drop used to reduce inflammation after eye surgery or from certain inflammatory eye conditions (uveitis).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your ophthalmologist; commonly 1-2 drops in the affected eye(s) 2-4 times daily, tapered as directed.
typical_duration: Short-term to several weeks, tapered gradually per your ophthalmologist's instructions - do not stop abruptly.
directions_for_use: Shake well before each use.
Wash hands before use; tilt head back and instill drop(s) into the lower eyelid pocket without touching the dropper tip to the eye.
Wait at least 5 minutes between this and any other eye drops.
Remove contact lenses before use, if applicable.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; protect from light; discard per the expiration date on the label once opened (often 4 weeks).
contraindications: Most viral, fungal, and mycobacterial eye infections
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, significant vision changes, or worsening redness - contact ophthalmologist promptly
Signs of increased eye pressure (halos around lights, eye pain) - seek care
Signs of eye infection worsening despite treatment
common_side_effects: Increased eye pressure with prolonged use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic drug interactions expected with proper ophthalmic use.
Space out from other eye drops (e.g., artificial tears) by at least 5 minutes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your ophthalmologist for eye pain or vision changes.
Do not stop a tapering course abruptly without guidance.
self_monitoring: Periodic eye pressure checks during use, especially with prolonged treatment.
Follow up as scheduled with your ophthalmologist.
missed_dose_instructions: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: A fast-acting oral liquid/dissolving-tablet corticosteroid used to treat asthma flares, croup, severe allergies, and other inflammatory conditions, especially in children.
typical_dosage: Individualized based on weight and condition, set by your prescriber; often given as a short burst (e.g., several days) for acute flares.
typical_duration: Short courses of a few days for acute flares; longer tapering courses for chronic conditions as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset.
Measure oral solution with an accurate dosing device, not a household spoon.
For the orally disintegrating tablet, place on the tongue and allow it to dissolve without chewing or swallowing whole.
Do not stop a long-term course abruptly - follow the prescribed taper.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; protect from light; do not freeze the oral solution.
contraindications: Live vaccine administration during high-dose therapy
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection that seem to be masked or worsening (fever, unusual fatigue)
Severe mood changes, confusion, or agitation, especially in children
Signs of high blood sugar: excessive thirst/urination
Black, tarry stools or stomach pain (possible GI bleeding)
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) increase the risk of stomach ulcers/GI bleeding when combined - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
Can raise blood sugar - monitor closely if taking metformin or glipizide.
May reduce the effectiveness of some vaccines given during treatment.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for mood changes, high blood sugar symptoms, or signs of GI bleeding.
Never stop a tapering steroid course abruptly.
self_monitoring: Blood glucose checks if diabetic or on a long course.
Track mood changes, especially in children.
Monitor growth in children on repeated courses.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, follow your prescriber's specific instructions rather than doubling up, especially on a tapering schedule.

description: A combination hormone therapy used to treat moderate to severe menopausal symptoms (hot flashes, vaginal changes) in women with an intact uterus; the progestin protects the uterine lining from estrogen-related overgrowth.
dosage_forms: Tablet (sequential regimen, e.g. Premphase - estrogen alone days 1-14, estrogen+progestin days 15-28)
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily, following the specific continuous or sequential regimen prescribed, at the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration needed.
typical_duration: Individualized; typically reassessed with your prescriber at least annually.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Follow the specific tablet sequence on the pack exactly if using the sequential (Premphase) regimen.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known or suspected breast cancer or estrogen-dependent cancer
History of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, vision changes, or one-sided weakness - seek emergency care
New breast lumps or unusual vaginal bleeding - contact prescriber
Yellowing of skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: May alter clotting factors and affect the response to warfarin - closer INR monitoring may be needed.
St. John's Wort can reduce hormone levels via enzyme induction, potentially reducing symptom control.
NSAIDs do not have a major direct interaction but combined clot risk factors should be discussed with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or stroke.
Contact prescriber for new breast lumps or abnormal bleeding.
self_monitoring: Routine mammograms and gynecologic follow-up as scheduled.
Report any new vaginal bleeding.
Blood pressure checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed tablet as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and continue the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: An oral or IV antiviral used to prevent cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection/disease in adults who have had a stem cell or kidney transplant.
route: Oral (tablet form for outpatient/home use) or intravenous
typical_dosage: 480 mg by mouth once daily (dose may be reduced if taken with cyclosporine), individualized and duration set by your transplant specialist.
typical_duration: Individualized course, commonly around 100-200 days post-transplant per your specialist's protocol.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
contraindications: Coadministration with pimozide or certain ergot alkaloids
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe nausea/vomiting affecting oral intake
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly increases levels of cyclosporine and tacrolimus - dose adjustment and closer monitoring of these immunosuppressants is required if co-administered.
Can increase levels of statins such as simvastatin and atorvastatin - increased risk of muscle-related side effects; dose adjustment often needed.
St. John's Wort must be avoided - can reduce letermovir levels and effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your transplant team for persistent nausea or liver-related symptoms.
Report any new muscle pain if also taking a statin.
self_monitoring: Regular CMV viral load monitoring.
Liver function tests.
Immunosuppressant drug level monitoring (cyclosporine/tacrolimus) if co-administered.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and remembered within a few hours, take it as soon as possible; if it is close to the next dose, skip it - do not double up. Contact your transplant team if unsure.

description: A once-daily combination tablet used with other antiretroviral medications to treat HIV-1 infection; cobicistat boosts darunavir levels by inhibiting its breakdown.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily with food, as part of a complete antiretroviral regimen.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day with food - food is required for proper absorption.
Do not skip doses; missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original container.
contraindications: Coadministration with simvastatin or lovastatin (risk of severe myopathy/rhabdomyolysis)
Coadministration with St. John's Wort (loss of virologic control)
Coadministration with rifampin, certain ergot alkaloids, or other drugs highly dependent on CYP3A4 clearance with narrow therapeutic index
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe rash, especially with fever or blistering (rare but serious skin reaction) - seek emergency care
New or worsening diabetes symptoms
Signs of a severe allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with simvastatin - cobicistat markedly raises simvastatin levels, risking severe muscle breakdown; atorvastatin may be used at a reduced dose with monitoring instead.
St. John's Wort must be avoided - dramatically reduces darunavir levels, risking treatment failure and resistance.
Significantly increases sildenafil levels - avoid or use only a reduced dose under medical supervision due to hypotension/priapism risk.
Increases levels of alprazolam and other benzodiazepines - increased sedation risk; use caution.
Omeprazole and other PPIs may be used but should be dose-timed and monitored per your HIV specialist's guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Do not stop or skip doses on your own - contact your HIV specialist about side effects.
Seek emergency care for severe rash, breathing difficulty, or signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Periodic HIV viral load and CD4 count labs.
Liver function and cholesterol/glucose labs.
Track adherence closely.
missed_dose_instructions: If within 12 hours of the usual time, take with food as soon as remembered. If more than 12 hours late, skip the missed dose and resume the next day at the regular time - do not double up.

description: An oral antibiotic used, often with isoniazid, to treat or prevent tuberculosis infection.
typical_dosage: Individualized by weight and regimen, set by your prescriber; often given once weekly for latent TB prevention regimens, or as directed for active TB treatment.
typical_duration: Weeks to months, depending on whether treating latent or active tuberculosis - complete the full course exactly as prescribed.
directions_for_use: Take with food to improve absorption.
May turn urine, sweat, saliva, and tears reddish-orange - this is expected and harmless, but may permanently stain soft contact lenses.
Complete the entire course even if feeling better - stopping early can lead to drug-resistant TB.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, nausea - seek care
Flu-like symptoms with fever/chills, especially with intermittent dosing (hypersensitivity reaction) - seek care
Signs of low blood counts: unusual bruising, bleeding, infection
otc_and_other_interactions: Strongly reduces the effectiveness of warfarin, hormonal contraceptives, and many other drugs by inducing liver enzymes - alternative contraception is needed, and warfarin dose often needs to be increased significantly.
Reduces levels of statins such as simvastatin and atorvastatin - may need dose adjustment.
May reduce effectiveness of sildenafil and many other CYP3A4-metabolized drugs.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber for liver-related symptoms or flu-like reactions.
Do not stop the medication early without medical guidance - complete the full course.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests periodically.
Complete blood counts as directed.
Track adherence - missed doses can lead to treatment failure and resistance.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber or TB treatment program if a dose is missed - do not double up; missed doses in a TB regimen require guidance to keep treatment effective.

description: An oral medication used to prevent relapse of certain types of malaria and, in some regimens, for malaria prevention or treatment of Pneumocystis pneumonia.
typical_dosage: Individualized by weight and indication, set by your prescriber; commonly taken once daily for a defined course (e.g., 14 days for malaria relapse prevention).
typical_duration: Short-term, defined course as prescribed - complete the full course.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Complete the full prescribed course even if feeling well.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: G6PD deficiency (can cause severe hemolytic anemia) - testing is required before starting
Concurrent use with other bone-marrow-suppressing drugs
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of hemolytic anemia: unusual fatigue, pale skin, dark/tea-colored urine, rapid heartbeat, yellowing of skin/eyes - seek care immediately, especially if G6PD deficient
Signs of low blood counts: fever, unusual bruising/bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other drugs that can cause hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals unless directed.
No significant interaction with common OTC pain relievers such as acetaminophen expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for signs of hemolytic anemia (dark urine, unusual fatigue, jaundice).
Contact prescriber for persistent GI upset.
self_monitoring: G6PD testing before starting treatment is essential.
Periodic blood counts if directed during the course.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up; contact your prescriber if multiple doses of this short course are missed.

description: Used to control certain types of seizures and to treat essential tremor.
typical_dosage: Individualized, started at a low dose and gradually increased, set by your prescriber based on condition and response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy; do not stop abruptly.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time(s) each day, with or without food.
Do not stop suddenly - abrupt discontinuation can cause withdrawal seizures.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to primidone or phenobarbital
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe drowsiness, slowed/shallow breathing, or confusion (especially with other sedatives) - seek emergency care
Signs of severe skin reaction: rash, blistering, peeling skin - seek emergency care
New or worsening depression or suicidal thoughts
Uncontrolled eye movements or loss of coordination
otc_and_other_interactions: Dangerous additive sedation with alcohol, diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen - avoid combining.
Reduces the effectiveness of warfarin and hormonal contraceptives by inducing liver enzymes.
St. John's Wort may add to sedative effects and complicate seizure control - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe sedation or signs of overdose.
Contact prescriber for mood changes; never stop this medication abruptly.
self_monitoring: Periodic blood level and complete blood count monitoring as directed.
Seizure/tremor frequency log.
Watch for excessive daytime sedation.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up. Contact your prescriber if you miss more than one dose, as this can trigger seizures.

description: An oral medication used to lower uric acid levels for chronic gout, and sometimes combined with certain antibiotics to increase their blood levels.
typical_dosage: 250-500 mg by mouth twice daily, individualized by your prescriber; not used during an acute gout flare until inflammation subsides.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic gout management.
directions_for_use: Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset.
Drink plenty of water (at least 8 glasses/day) to reduce the risk of kidney stones.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Use during an acute gout attack (can worsen it initially)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe flank/back pain, blood in urine (possible kidney stone) - seek care
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, difficulty breathing - seek care
Signs of low blood counts: fever, unusual bruising/bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly increases and prolongs levels of methotrexate - can cause severe methotrexate toxicity; this combination requires close monitoring or avoidance.
Increases levels of penicillin-type antibiotics (sometimes used intentionally).
Avoid starting during an acute gout flare - NSAIDs or other prescribed anti-inflammatories are used for the acute attack first.
Aspirin can reduce probenecid's uric-acid-lowering effect - avoid regular aspirin use; acetaminophen is preferred for pain.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for signs of kidney stones or allergic reaction.
Seek care for signs of low blood counts.
self_monitoring: Periodic uric acid level checks.
Kidney function monitoring.
Stay well hydrated and report flank pain.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: A systemic immunosuppressant used to prevent organ rejection after kidney, liver, or heart transplant; distinct from topical tacrolimus used for skin conditions.
typical_dosage: Individualized dose based on body weight and blood levels, set by your transplant specialist; typically taken twice daily (immediate-release) or once daily (extended-release), at consistent times relative to meals.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for as long as the transplanted organ is in place.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time(s) every day, consistently either with or without food as instructed - do not change this routine without guidance.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice - can significantly raise drug levels.
Do not switch between brands/formulations without your transplant team's approval, as absorption differs.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors without dose adjustment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, cough, burning with urination - seek care promptly (increased infection risk due to immune suppression)
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
Tremor, seizures, confusion, or severe headache (possible neurotoxicity) - seek care
Signs of high blood sugar: excessive thirst/urination
otc_and_other_interactions: Fluconazole and clarithromycin significantly raise tacrolimus levels - can cause serious toxicity; dose adjustment and closer monitoring needed.
St. John's Wort dramatically lowers tacrolimus levels - risk of organ rejection; must be avoided.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) increase the risk of kidney injury when combined - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
May raise levels of statins such as simvastatin and atorvastatin - increased muscle toxicity risk; dose adjustment often needed.
Live vaccines should be avoided while on this medication due to immune suppression.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your transplant team promptly for tremor, signs of infection, or reduced urination - do not adjust the dose yourself.
Seek emergency care for seizures or severe confusion.
self_monitoring: Regular tacrolimus blood level monitoring - critical for safe dosing.
Kidney function and blood glucose labs.
Blood pressure checks.
Report any new infection symptoms right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If remembered within a few hours, take as soon as possible; if close to the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up. Contact your transplant team promptly about any missed dose.

description: A plasma-derived protein replacement used for chronic augmentation therapy in adults with emphysema due to alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.
typical_dosage: Individualized weight-based dose, commonly 60 mg/kg by IV infusion once weekly, set by your specialist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing weekly therapy.
directions_for_use: Given as a slow IV infusion - many patients are trained for home self-infusion after initial supervised sessions; others receive it at an infusion center.
Bring product to room temperature before infusing per pharmacy instructions.
Use proper aseptic technique for home infusion as trained by your care team.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze; protect from light. Follow pharmacy instructions for reconstitution and use timing.
contraindications: Selective IgA deficiency with known anti-IgA antibodies
History of severe reaction to alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor products
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, throat swelling, wheezing, dizziness - seek emergency care
Fever, chills during or after infusion - contact your care team
Signs of a blood clot
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; this is a protein replacement therapy, not metabolized like typical drugs.
action_if_adverse_effects: Report infusion reactions to your care team immediately so the rate can be slowed or stopped.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track lung function tests as scheduled with your pulmonologist.
Monitor for infusion-related symptoms each session.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your specialist or infusion coordinator to reschedule as soon as possible; do not double the next infusion dose.

description: Used to help restore and maintain a normal heart rhythm in certain types of abnormal heart rhythms (arrhythmias), including atrial fibrillation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your cardiologist; immediate-release commonly 150-300 mg by mouth every 8 hours, or extended-release 225-425 mg every 12 hours.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your cardiologist.
directions_for_use: Take at evenly spaced times as prescribed, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly without your cardiologist's guidance.
Swallow extended-release capsules whole - do not crush or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Significant structural heart disease (e.g., heart failure, prior heart attack) - increased risk of dangerous arrhythmias
Certain conduction disorders without a pacemaker
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening irregular heartbeat, palpitations, fainting, or dizziness - seek emergency care
Chest pain or shortness of breath
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases levels of metoprolol and certain other beta-blockers - can cause excessive slowing of heart rate; dose adjustment may be needed.
Increases the effect of warfarin - closer INR monitoring is needed.
Avoid strong CYP2D6/CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole) - can raise propafenone levels.
Avoid combining with other drugs that slow heart rhythm without cardiologist guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your cardiologist for new dizziness or palpitations; do not stop this medication abruptly.
Seek emergency care for fainting, chest pain, or severe irregular heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Periodic ECG monitoring as directed.
Electrolyte (potassium/magnesium) monitoring.
Track heart rate/rhythm symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up; contact your cardiologist if you miss more than one dose.

generic_name: Measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella vaccine
description: A combination vaccine that protects against measles, mumps, rubella, and chickenpox (varicella), given routinely in childhood.
typical_dosage: 0.5 mL by subcutaneous injection, given as a 2-dose series - typically the first dose at 12-15 months and the second at 4-6 years of age.
typical_duration: 2-dose primary series provides long-lasting protection.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare professional - not self-administered.
Bring your child's vaccination record to each visit.
storage_instructions: Store frozen or refrigerated per specific product label until reconstitution; use promptly after mixing. Handled by the administering clinic/pharmacy.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a prior dose, neomycin, or gelatin
History of febrile seizures or family history of seizures (increased seizure risk with first dose in young children - discuss with pediatrician)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care
High fever with seizure (febrile seizure - slightly more common with this combination vaccine than giving MMR and varicella separately) - seek care
Widespread rash resembling chickenpox
otc_and_other_interactions: Should not be given with other live vaccines unless on the same day - space out live vaccines by at least 4 weeks if not given together.
Recent immunoglobulin/blood product administration may reduce vaccine effectiveness.
Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for fever/discomfort after vaccination.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact the pediatrician for high fever or concerning symptoms.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or seizure.
self_monitoring: Monitor the child for fever and rash for 1-2 weeks after vaccination, as reactions can be delayed with live vaccines.
missed_dose_instructions: If the second dose is delayed, get it as soon as possible - the series does not need to be restarted; contact your provider to reschedule.

description: Used to treat depression; sometimes used off-label for certain sleep-related breathing disorders.
typical_dosage: 15-40 mg by mouth daily in divided doses, individualized by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy with periodic reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed, with or without food.
Avoid abrupt discontinuation - taper as directed by your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or fainting - seek emergency care
New or worsening suicidal thoughts, especially in young adults - seek care immediately
Severe confusion, hallucinations, or difficulty urinating
otc_and_other_interactions: Dangerous interaction (serotonin syndrome and cardiac risk) with MAOIs - must not be combined.
Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, or tramadol; tramadol also raises serotonin syndrome risk.
Can prolong the QT interval - use caution with other QT-prolonging drugs such as ondansetron.
Anticholinergic effects add up with diphenhydramine (dry mouth, constipation, confusion, especially in older adults).
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for bothersome side effects; do not stop abruptly.
Seek emergency care for chest pain, fainting, or suicidal thoughts.
self_monitoring: Periodic ECG monitoring, especially in those with cardiac risk factors.
Monitor mood, especially early in treatment.
Blood pressure and heart rate checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: An inhaled enzyme medication used in cystic fibrosis to thin mucus and improve lung function by breaking down extracellular DNA in thick airway secretions.
typical_dosage: 2.5 mg (one ampule) inhaled once daily via a nebulizer, some patients use twice daily per their pulmonologist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing daily therapy.
directions_for_use: Use only with the specific nebulizer type recommended by your prescriber/pharmacist - not all nebulizers are compatible.
Do not dilute or mix with other medications in the nebulizer.
Store ampules in the refrigerator and protect from light; a small number may be kept at room temperature for daily use.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; protect from strong light; do not freeze. Unopened foil pouches may be kept at room temperature for up to 24 hours.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to dornase alfa or Chinese hamster ovary cell products
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, difficulty breathing - seek care
Worsening shortness of breath or chest pain after use - contact prescriber
Significant voice changes or sore throat that persist
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic drug interactions expected due to local action in the lungs and minimal systemic absorption.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your pulmonologist for persistent voice changes or chest discomfort.
Seek care for signs of allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track lung function (spirometry) as scheduled with your CF care team.
Monitor for changes in mucus/cough patterns.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if close to the next scheduled dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: An oral antibiotic used in combination with other drugs as part of standard treatment for active tuberculosis.
typical_dosage: Individualized by weight, set by your prescriber as part of a multi-drug TB regimen, typically once daily.
typical_duration: Usually used for the first 2 months of a standard 6-month TB treatment regimen, as part of a combination protocol.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food, at the same time each day, exactly as prescribed with your other TB medications.
Complete the full prescribed course - stopping early can lead to drug-resistant TB.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, nausea - seek care promptly (this medication requires liver monitoring)
Signs of gout flare: joint pain and swelling, especially in the big toe
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol - significantly increases the risk of liver toxicity.
NSAIDs and other drugs that raise uric acid may worsen gout risk in combination with this medication.
Acetaminophen should be used cautiously and in the lowest effective dose given the shared liver metabolism/toxicity risk during TB treatment - discuss with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your TB treatment team promptly for liver-related symptoms or joint pain.
Do not stop the medication early without medical guidance.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests periodically throughout treatment - essential for safety.
Uric acid level checks if joint symptoms occur.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber or TB treatment program if a dose is missed - do not double up; consistent adherence is critical to prevent drug-resistant TB.

description: Used to improve muscle strength in myasthenia gravis, a condition causing muscle weakness.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your neurologist; immediate-release commonly 60 mg every 3-4 hours during waking hours, adjusted to symptom control. Extended-release forms are typically dosed once or twice daily, often at bedtime for overnight coverage.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your neurologist.
directions_for_use: Take at evenly spaced times to maintain consistent muscle strength throughout the day.
Swallow extended-release tablets whole - do not crush or chew.
Take with food if stomach upset occurs.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Mechanical bowel or urinary tract obstruction
Known hypersensitivity to pyridostigmine or other cholinesterase inhibitors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe muscle weakness that worsens after dosing (possible cholinergic crisis) - seek emergency care
Difficulty breathing or swallowing - seek emergency care
Very slow heart rate or fainting
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive slowing of heart rate when combined with beta-blockers such as metoprolol - use caution.
Effects may be reduced by certain antibiotics; discuss any new prescription with your neurologist.
Avoid anticholinergic OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine) which can counteract this medication's effect and worsen myasthenia symptoms.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your neurologist for increasing weakness or excessive cholinergic symptoms (drooling, cramping) - dose may need adjustment.
Seek emergency care for severe breathing/swallowing difficulty, which can indicate either worsening myasthenia or overdose and requires urgent evaluation.
self_monitoring: Track muscle strength and symptom patterns throughout the day to help guide dose timing.
Report new or worsening weakness promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up, as this can cause excess cholinergic side effects.

description: Used, typically combined with sulfadiazine and leucovorin, to treat toxoplasmosis.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber based on the condition being treated and body weight; usually combined with other medications.
typical_duration: Individualized course, often several weeks, as directed by your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Take exactly as prescribed along with any companion medications (e.g., leucovorin, sulfadiazine).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light.
contraindications: Megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood counts: fever, unusual bruising/bleeding, sore throat - seek care promptly
Signs of severe skin reaction: rash, blistering - seek emergency care
Seizures (rare, with high doses)
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with methotrexate significantly increases the risk of severe bone marrow suppression (both are folate antagonists) - requires close monitoring or avoidance.
Folic acid/folinic acid (leucovorin) supplementation is often prescribed alongside this medication to reduce bone marrow toxicity - follow your prescriber's specific instructions.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber promptly for signs of low blood counts.
Seek emergency care for severe skin reactions or seizures.
self_monitoring: Regular complete blood counts throughout treatment - essential for safety.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food unless close to the next dose - do not double up; contact your prescriber if a dose is missed on a combination regimen.

description: An oral medication used to treat hemolytic anemia in adults with pyruvate kinase (PK) deficiency.
typical_dosage: Individualized starting dose, gradually titrated upward by your hematologist based on hemoglobin response (a titration/taper pack is used during the initial dose-adjustment period).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food, exactly per the titration schedule provided by your hematologist.
Do not change your dose on your own - follow the titration pack schedule exactly.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain - seek care
Signs of worsening anemia: severe fatigue, shortness of breath, rapid heartbeat - seek care
otc_and_other_interactions: This drug is a moderate inducer of certain liver enzymes and may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives and other CYP3A4-metabolized drugs, including some statins (atorvastatin) - discuss all medications, including OTC and herbal products, with your hematologist.
St. John's Wort should be avoided - combined enzyme induction could further reduce effectiveness of other medications you take.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your hematologist for liver-related symptoms or worsening anemia.
Do not stop or adjust the dose without medical guidance.
self_monitoring: Regular hemoglobin and liver function labs, especially during dose titration.
Track energy levels and symptoms of anemia.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up; contact your hematologist if a titration dose is missed.

description: An oral targeted therapy for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) after prior treatment with other kinase inhibitors.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist (commonly 150 mg by mouth once daily).
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening rash, especially with skin peeling (can be serious) - contact prescriber promptly
Signs of heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain - seek care
Palpitations or fainting (QT prolongation risk) - seek emergency care
Signs of a blood clot
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers, including St. John's Wort - can significantly reduce ripretinib levels and effectiveness.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) - can raise drug levels and toxicity risk.
Use caution with other QT-prolonging drugs such as ondansetron.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your oncologist for new rash, palpitations, or swelling.
Seek emergency care for fainting or signs of heart failure.
self_monitoring: Baseline and periodic echocardiogram (heart function) monitoring.
ECG monitoring for QT interval.
Skin checks and blood pressure monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed and remembered within 12 hours, take it as soon as possible; if more than 12 hours have passed, skip it and resume the next day at the regular time - do not double up.

description: Used to help restore and maintain a normal heart rhythm in certain abnormal heart rhythms (arrhythmias).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your cardiologist; commonly 324-648 mg by mouth every 8-12 hours.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your cardiologist.
directions_for_use: Take at evenly spaced times as prescribed, with food if stomach upset occurs.
Swallow extended-release tablets whole - do not crush or chew.
Do not stop abruptly without your cardiologist's guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Complete heart block without a pacemaker
History of drug-induced long QT syndrome or torsades de pointes
Known hypersensitivity to quinidine or quinine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat (risk of dangerous arrhythmia/torsades de pointes) - seek emergency care
Ringing in the ears, vision changes, confusion (signs of cinchonism/toxicity) - seek care
Signs of low blood counts: fever, unusual bruising/bleeding
Severe diarrhea
otc_and_other_interactions: Use caution with other QT-prolonging drugs such as ondansetron - additive risk of dangerous arrhythmia (torsades de pointes).
Increases the effect of warfarin - closer INR monitoring is needed.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, fluconazole) - can raise quinidine levels and toxicity risk.
Antacids that alkalinize urine can increase quinidine levels - discuss any regular antacid use with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your cardiologist for ringing in the ears, vision changes, or persistent diarrhea.
Seek emergency care for fainting, palpitations, or signs of severe arrhythmia.
self_monitoring: Periodic ECG monitoring - essential given QT prolongation risk.
Electrolyte (potassium/magnesium) monitoring.
Quinidine blood level checks if directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up; contact your cardiologist if you miss more than one dose.

description: Controls certain irregular heart rhythms (arrhythmias) by slowing electrical signals in the heart.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your cardiologist based on the arrhythmia being treated and response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for rhythm control.
directions_for_use: Take at evenly spaced times as prescribed to keep blood levels steady.
Take with food if stomach upset occurs.
Do not stop suddenly without talking to your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Complete heart block without a pacemaker
History of drug-induced long QT syndrome or torsades de pointes
Known hypersensitivity to quinidine or quinine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting, severe dizziness, or racing/irregular heartbeat (possible dangerous rhythm)
Ringing in the ears, hearing loss, vision changes, confusion (cinchonism)
Unusual bruising or bleeding, fever, sore throat (rare blood disorders)
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases warfarin's blood-thinning effect - bleeding risk; INR must be monitored closely.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., ondansetron, azithromycin, clarithromycin) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
Quinidine strongly inhibits CYP2D6 and can raise levels of metoprolol and reduce the pain relief from tramadol.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, chest pain, or a racing/irregular heartbeat.
Call your prescriber for ringing in the ears, vision changes, or confusion.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled ECG and blood level checks.
Report new palpitations, dizziness, or fainting promptly.
Periodic blood counts as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip the missed dose. Do not double up.

description: Treats uncomplicated malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum, usually combined with another antimalarial drug.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your prescriber based on body weight and the malaria treatment regimen.
typical_duration: Short course, typically 3-7 days as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with food or a full glass of water to reduce stomach upset.
Complete the full course exactly as prescribed even if you feel better.
Take at the same times each day as directed with any companion antimalarial drug.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: History of thrombocytopenia (low platelets) from quinine
History of blackwater fever or optic neuritis from quinine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Unusual bruising, bleeding, or blood in urine (possible severe low platelets)
Ringing in the ears, hearing loss, vision changes, confusion (cinchonism)
Fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases warfarin's blood-thinning effect - bleeding risk; INR should be monitored.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (azithromycin, clarithromycin, ondansetron) raises risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
Avoid combining with other quinine-containing products (including some tonic water in large amounts).
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for irregular heartbeat, fainting, or signs of severe bleeding.
Call your prescriber for hearing changes, vision changes, or unusual bruising.
self_monitoring: Watch for unusual bruising or bleeding and report it right away.
Keep scheduled blood counts if on repeated or prolonged courses.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Helps people with insomnia fall asleep and stay asleep by blocking wake-promoting orexin signals in the brain.
typical_dosage: 25-50 mg by mouth once nightly, within 30 minutes of going to bed, on an empty stomach.
typical_duration: Used nightly as needed for insomnia; re-evaluate need for continued use periodically with your prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take only when you can devote a full 7 or more hours to sleep before you need to be active again.
Do not take with or right after a meal - it works more slowly.
Do not take more than once per night.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in original packaging.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Daytime drowsiness or impaired alertness/driving ability the morning after use
Sleep paralysis, hallucinations while falling asleep or waking, or temporary leg weakness (cataplexy-like symptoms)
New or worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm
Complex sleep behaviors (walking, driving, or eating while not fully awake)
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with alcohol, diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, hydrocodone/acetaminophen, or other CNS depressants - avoid combining.
Do not combine with St. John's Wort, which can lower daridorexant levels and reduce effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Do not drive or operate machinery if you feel drowsy the next morning.
Call your prescriber if you experience sleepwalking, hallucinations, or worsening mood.
Seek care immediately for thoughts of self-harm.
self_monitoring: Track how rested you feel in the morning and any unusual sleep-related behaviors.
Report new or worsening depression.
missed_dose_instructions: Only take this medicine if you are going to bed and can stay in bed for a full night; if you missed bedtime, skip the dose and resume the next night. Do not take during the day to make up for a missed dose.

description: Prevents and treats osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and reduces risk of invasive breast cancer in certain high-risk women.
typical_dosage: 60 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at any time of day, with or without food.
Take calcium and vitamin D supplements as recommended by your prescriber.
Stand and move periodically during long trips to reduce blood clot risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: History of blood clots (DVT, PE, retinal vein thrombosis)
Pregnancy or women who could become pregnant
Prolonged immobilization (e.g., upcoming surgery, extended bed rest)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of stroke: sudden weakness, slurred speech, vision changes - seek emergency care immediately
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases risk of blood clots; use caution with estrogen-containing products.
May reduce the blood-thinning effect of warfarin slightly - monitor INR if used together.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, or stroke symptoms.
Stop the medicine and call your prescriber right away if a clot is suspected.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled bone density (DEXA) scans.
Report new leg swelling or breathing changes immediately.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Treats symptoms of Parkinson's disease by slowing the breakdown of dopamine in the brain.
typical_dosage: 0.5-1 mg by mouth once daily, individualized by your neurologist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly without talking to your neurologist.
Avoid large amounts of tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, cured meats, tap beer) - discuss dietary limits with your provider.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Use with meperidine, tramadol, methadone, or St. John's Wort
Use with most antidepressants (SSRIs/SNRIs) without prescriber guidance - serotonin syndrome risk
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity, tremor - seek emergency care immediately
Severe headache, especially with a hypertensive crisis (rare with dietary tyramine excess)
New or worsening uncontrolled movements (dyskinesia)
New or worsening impulse control problems (gambling, compulsive behaviors)
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with tramadol and with St. John's Wort - risk of serotonin syndrome.
Contraindicated (or requires strict avoidance) with SSRIs such as sertraline or escitalopram - risk of serotonin syndrome.
Avoid dextromethorphan-containing cough/cold products - serotonin syndrome risk.
Caution with over-the-counter decongestants (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine) - risk of elevated blood pressure.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of serotonin syndrome or severe headache with vision changes.
Call your neurologist for new impulse-control changes or worsening movements.
self_monitoring: Report new depression, unusual urges, or mood changes.
Monitor blood pressure if directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time the next day - do not double up.

description: Treats secondary hyperparathyroidism in adults with stage 3-4 chronic kidney disease and low vitamin D levels.
typical_dosage: 30 mcg by mouth once daily at bedtime, adjusted by your prescriber based on lab results.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy with periodic lab-based dose adjustments.
directions_for_use: Take at bedtime as directed.
Do not take with high doses of other vitamin D supplements unless approved by your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep in original container.
contraindications: Evidence of vitamin D toxicity or hypercalcemia
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high calcium: nausea, vomiting, constipation, confusion, excessive thirst/urination - contact prescriber promptly
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid additional over-the-counter vitamin D or calcium supplements unless your prescriber approves - risk of hypercalcemia.
Thiazide diuretics can increase risk of high calcium levels when combined.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your prescriber promptly for symptoms of high calcium.
Do not increase the dose on your own.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled calcium, phosphorus, PTH, and vitamin D level checks.
Report new nausea, confusion, or excessive thirst.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular bedtime - do not double up.

description: Applied to certain diabetic foot/leg ulcers to help stimulate healing when used with good wound care.
typical_dosage: individualized amount based on wound size, applied once daily as directed by your prescriber or wound care team.
typical_duration: Up to 20 weeks; re-evaluate with your wound care team if the ulcer has not improved.
directions_for_use: Clean the wound as instructed before each application.
Apply a thin, even layer only to the ulcer surface; do not rub in.
Cover with a saline-moistened gauze dressing as directed; do not use occlusive dressings.
Wash hands before and after application.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze. Discard remaining product per the expiration date after first use as directed on the label.
contraindications: Known malignancy at the application site
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Increasing redness, warmth, swelling, or pus at the wound (possible infection)
Wound that worsens or fails to improve
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected with topical use; avoid applying other topical products to the wound unless directed by your care team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your wound care team for signs of infection or worsening wound.
Stop use and call your prescriber for severe irritation or rash.
self_monitoring: Track wound size/appearance with photos if recommended.
Report any fever or spreading redness immediately.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered that day; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: Treats or helps prevent influenza (flu) A and B by blocking the virus's ability to spread in the body.
typical_dosage: 10 mg (two inhalations) twice daily for 5 days for treatment, started within 2 days of symptom onset; prevention dosing set by prescriber.
typical_duration: 5 days for treatment; longer courses may be used for prevention as directed.
directions_for_use: Use the Diskhaler device exactly as demonstrated by your pharmacist.
Do not use with a nebulizer or ventilator - can clog the device.
Complete the full course even if you feel better.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: History of asthma or COPD with bronchospasm risk from inhaled powder (use caution)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Wheezing, difficulty breathing, or chest tightness after use - seek care promptly, especially if you have asthma or COPD
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, facial swelling, trouble breathing
Unusual behavior or confusion (rare, more reported in children/teens)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected.
Avoid live attenuated influenza nasal spray vaccine within 2 weeks of use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care right away for breathing difficulty or wheezing.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track fever and flu symptoms; call your prescriber if symptoms worsen instead of improving.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered, then continue the regular twice-daily schedule; do not double up doses.

description: Lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes by quickly stimulating the pancreas to release insulin around mealtimes.
typical_dosage: 0.5-4 mg by mouth within 30 minutes before each meal, individualized by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for blood sugar control.
directions_for_use: Take shortly before meals; skip the dose if you skip a meal.
Do not take if you are not going to eat, to avoid low blood sugar.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe low blood sugar: confusion, sweating, shakiness, fainting - treat immediately and seek care if severe
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Clarithromycin, fluconazole, and other strong CYP3A4/CYP2C8 inhibitors can significantly raise repaglinide levels and increase low-blood-sugar risk - avoid or adjust dose under prescriber guidance.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) and alcohol can increase the blood-sugar-lowering effect and hypoglycemia risk.
Always carry a fast-acting sugar source in case of low blood sugar.
action_if_adverse_effects: Treat low blood sugar right away with fast-acting sugar; seek emergency care if confusion or loss of consciousness occurs.
Call your prescriber for signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed, especially before meals.
Keep scheduled A1C checks.
missed_dose_instructions: If a meal is skipped, skip the dose for that meal; do not take a dose if you are not eating. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted cancer therapy for certain lung, thyroid, and other tumors with a specific RET gene alteration.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team based on body weight - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as scheduled, with or without food, at consistent times.
Swallow capsules whole with water; do not open or crush.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
High blood pressure symptoms: severe headache, vision changes
Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/urine
Irregular heartbeat, fainting, chest pain (QT prolongation risk)
Signs of infection: fever, chills
New or worsening shortness of breath, cough (rare lung inflammation)
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, clarithromycin) can raise selpercatinib levels and increase toxicity/QT prolongation risk.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., ondansetron, azithromycin) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
Avoid acid-reducing medications (omeprazole) close to dosing - discuss timing with your oncology team, as absorption may be affected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, fainting, or irregular heartbeat.
Call your oncology team promptly for signs of liver problems, bleeding, or infection.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled liver function tests, blood pressure checks, and ECGs.
Monitor blood pressure at home if recommended.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is close to the next dose; do not double up. Contact your oncology team if you miss multiple doses or vomit after a dose.

description: Replaces missing adenosine deaminase enzyme in patients with ADA-deficient severe combined immunodeficiency (ADA-SCID).
route: Intramuscular injection (given by a caregiver or healthcare provider after training)
typical_dosage: individualized, set by the treating specialist based on body weight and enzyme activity levels.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy, often continued indefinitely unless transitioned to another treatment (e.g., gene therapy, transplant).
directions_for_use: Give injections exactly on the schedule set by the specialist - missed or delayed doses can allow toxic metabolites to build up.
Rotate injection sites as instructed.
Only caregivers trained by the treatment team should administer injections at home.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate (2-8°C); do not freeze; protect from light.
contraindications: Known severe hypersensitivity to elapegademase or PEGylated products
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
Fever, signs of infection (patients remain at risk for infection during treatment)
Unusual bruising or bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; avoid live vaccines unless specifically approved by the treatment team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Call the treatment team promptly for fever or signs of infection.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled immune function and enzyme activity labs.
Watch for and report any signs of infection immediately.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact the treatment team immediately if a dose is missed or delayed - do not simply skip or double a dose, as this therapy requires strict scheduling.

description: An oral targeted therapy for certain relapsed or refractory acute leukemias with specific genetic alterations (e.g., KMT2A rearrangement).
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team based on body weight and concurrent medications - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as scheduled, at consistent times as directed.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
Attend all scheduled monitoring visits, especially early in treatment (differentiation syndrome risk).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, cough, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain, or swelling (possible differentiation syndrome) - seek care immediately, this can be life-threatening
Irregular heartbeat, fainting, chest pain (QT prolongation risk)
Signs of infection or low blood counts: fever, unusual bruising/bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) can raise revumenib levels and increase toxicity/QT risk.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce drug levels and effectiveness - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency/urgent care for fever with breathing trouble, chest pain, or fainting.
Call your oncology team promptly for any new fever or signs of infection.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled ECGs, electrolyte checks, and blood counts.
Report new shortness of breath or rapid weight gain right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team for guidance if a dose is missed - do not double up without their instruction.

description: Treats schizophrenia and is used with antidepressants for major depressive disorder, and to manage agitation associated with Alzheimer's dementia.
typical_dosage: individualized, typically 1-4 mg by mouth once daily, titrated by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop suddenly without talking to your prescriber.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Increased mortality risk in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening depression, agitation, or thoughts of self-harm - seek help immediately
Fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, sweating (possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care immediately
Uncontrollable muscle movements (tardive dyskinesia)
New uncontrollable urges (gambling, shopping, eating, sexual urges)
Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst/urination
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen.
Combined with sertraline or escitalopram may increase serotonin-related side effects; dose adjustment may be needed with strong CYP2D6/3A4 inhibitors such as fluconazole.
May reduce blood-pressure response and increase dizziness with antihypertensives (lisinopril, losartan, amlodipine).
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fever with muscle stiffness/confusion, or for thoughts of self-harm.
Call your prescriber for new uncontrollable movements or urges.
self_monitoring: Track weight, blood sugar, and cholesterol as directed.
Report mood changes or new compulsive behaviors.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it. Do not double up.

description: Treats adults with noncirrhotic nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH/MASH) with moderate to advanced liver scarring, used with diet and exercise.
typical_dosage: individualized based on body weight, typically 60-100 mg by mouth once daily, set by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy with periodic liver monitoring to confirm ongoing benefit.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before the first meal of the day, or as directed.
Continue recommended diet and exercise changes alongside this medicine.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, abdominal pain
Signs of gallbladder problems: severe right upper abdominal pain, especially after fatty meals
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases levels of statins such as simvastatin and atorvastatin - your prescriber may need to lower your statin dose to reduce muscle injury risk.
May affect levothyroxine requirements - thyroid function should be monitored.
Avoid other potentially liver-toxic OTC products (e.g., high-dose acetaminophen) unless approved by your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your prescriber promptly for yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, or severe abdominal pain.
Seek care for signs of gallbladder attack.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled liver function tests.
Report new abdominal pain or jaundice right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and resume your normal once-daily schedule the next day - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a susceptible IDH1 mutation.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at consistent times, as directed.
Attend all scheduled monitoring visits, especially in the first months (differentiation syndrome risk).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, cough, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain, or swelling (possible differentiation syndrome) - seek care immediately, this can be life-threatening
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Irregular heartbeat, fainting (QT prolongation)
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) can raise olutasidenib levels - dose adjustment may be needed.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce effectiveness - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency/urgent care for fever with breathing trouble or fainting.
Call your oncology team promptly for jaundice or new fever.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled liver function tests and ECGs.
Report new shortness of breath or rapid weight gain right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team for guidance if a dose is missed - do not double up without their instruction.

description: Lowers eye pressure in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension by increasing fluid outflow from the eye.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use to control eye pressure.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use; avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface.
Apply gentle pressure to the inner corner of the eye for 1-2 minutes after each drop to reduce systemic absorption.
If wearing contact lenses, remove before applying and wait 15 minutes before reinserting.
If using other eye drops, space them at least 5 minutes apart.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light; discard per the labeled in-use period after opening.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, significant vision change, or worsening redness that does not improve
Signs of allergic reaction: eyelid swelling, severe itching
common_side_effects: Small deposits on the cornea (corneal verticillata)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic OTC drug interactions expected due to minimal absorption; avoid using with other eye products without spacing doses.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your eye care provider for persistent redness, pain, or vision changes.
Seek care for signs of a significant allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled eye pressure checks and eye exams.
Report any vision changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed drop as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: Used in combination with other antiviral drugs to treat chronic hepatitis C infection.
typical_dosage: individualized based on body weight and the companion antiviral regimen, set by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Course length (often 12-24 weeks) is set by your prescriber as part of a combination hepatitis C regimen.
directions_for_use: Take with food as directed.
Take exactly as prescribed together with your other hepatitis C medicine(s) - do not take ribavirin alone.
Both partners must use two effective forms of contraception during treatment and for 6 months after (risk of severe birth defects).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy, and male partners of pregnant women (significant birth defect/fetal risk)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe anemia: extreme fatigue, shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness
New or worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm
Signs of pancreatitis: severe abdominal pain
Chest pain (rare cardiac events, especially with pre-existing heart disease)
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not combine with didanosine or other drugs known to worsen ribavirin's toxicity (discuss all medicines with your specialist).
NSAIDs and other drugs affecting blood counts may add to anemia risk - discuss pain relief options with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain or severe shortness of breath.
Call your prescriber promptly for signs of severe anemia, depression, or self-harm thoughts.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled blood counts (especially hemoglobin) and pregnancy tests if applicable.
Report new mood changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule - do not double up. Contact your specialist about missed doses of a hepatitis C regimen.

description: Treats and helps prevent Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infections and is used as part of some tuberculosis regimens, especially in patients on HIV therapy.
typical_dosage: individualized, commonly 150-300 mg by mouth once daily, adjusted based on other medicines you take (especially HIV protease inhibitors).
typical_duration: Course length set by your prescriber based on the infection being treated or prevented.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Complete the full course exactly as prescribed.
Expect harmless orange-red discoloration of urine, tears, and skin - soft contact lenses may become permanently stained.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Severe rash, joint pain and eye pain/redness (uveitis, more common at higher doses or with interacting drugs)
Signs of low white blood cells: fever, frequent infections
Signs of low platelets: unusual bruising or bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly reduces effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives (birth control pills) - use a backup method.
Reduces levels of tacrolimus and cyclosporine, risking organ transplant rejection - close monitoring required.
Reduces warfarin's effect - INR monitoring required.
Levels are increased when combined with atazanavir or other protease inhibitors - dose must be adjusted by your specialist.
Reduces effectiveness of azole antifungals like fluconazole, and vice versa fluconazole can raise rifabutin levels - monitor for uveitis.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your prescriber promptly for eye pain/redness, jaundice, or unusual bruising.
Seek care for signs of infection with fever.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled liver function tests and blood counts.
Report new eye symptoms (pain, redness, blurred vision) right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: Slows disease progression in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, Lou Gehrig's disease) by reducing glutamate activity in the nervous system.
typical_dosage: 50 mg by mouth twice daily, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by your neurologist.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach at consistent times each day.
Do not stop without talking to your neurologist.
Avoid alcohol - increases risk of liver toxicity.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: History of severe hypersensitivity reaction to riluzole
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue - liver enzymes are monitored closely, especially in the first months
Signs of lung problems: unexplained cough, shortness of breath (rare interstitial lung disease)
Fever (may signal low white blood cell counts)
otc_and_other_interactions: Ciprofloxacin significantly increases riluzole blood levels (CYP1A2 inhibition), raising toxicity risk - use another antibiotic if possible or use with caution and monitoring.
Avoid alcohol and other potentially liver-toxic substances, including high-dose acetaminophen, unless approved by your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your neurologist promptly for jaundice, unexplained cough, or fever.
Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled liver function tests, especially during the first several months.
Report new cough or breathing changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: Used to prevent or treat influenza A infection (not effective against influenza B).
typical_dosage: 100 mg by mouth twice daily, or as adjusted for kidney/liver impairment or older adults, set by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Treatment typically 5-7 days; prevention courses may last several weeks as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food.
Start treatment as early as possible after symptoms begin for best effect.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to rimantadine or amantadine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Seizures (rare, more common with high levels or in patients with seizure history)
Severe dizziness, confusion, or hallucinations
