Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive dizziness/CNS effects with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, or other sedating drugs.
Acetaminophen and aspirin can modestly reduce rimantadine blood levels - not usually clinically significant but note if response seems reduced.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for seizures or severe allergic reaction.
Call your prescriber for severe confusion or hallucinations.
self_monitoring: Track flu symptoms and fever; contact your prescriber if symptoms worsen or do not improve.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up.

description: Reduces inflammation in conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, atopic dermatitis, and ankylosing spondylitis by blocking JAK enzyme signaling.
typical_dosage: individualized, typically 15-45 mg by mouth once daily depending on the condition being treated, set by your specialist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not crush, split, or chew.
Do not stop without talking to your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, cough, burning with urination - increased risk of serious infections including tuberculosis and shingles
Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath (boxed warning)
Chest pain, signs of heart attack or stroke (boxed warning for increased cardiovascular risk)
Unusual bruising, bleeding, or signs of low blood counts
Signs of a new skin cancer or unusual lump (increased malignancy risk)
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other immunosuppressants (tacrolimus, cyclosporine, methotrexate) increases infection risk - only combined under close specialist supervision.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) can raise upadacitinib levels and side effect risk.
Live vaccines should be avoided while on this medicine - discuss vaccination timing with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, heart attack, or stroke.
Call your prescriber promptly for any signs of infection or unusual bruising/bleeding.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood counts, liver function tests, and cholesterol checks.
Watch for and report any signs of infection immediately.
Report new lumps or skin changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

drug_class: Rho kinase inhibitor/prostaglandin analog combination (ophthalmic, glaucoma agent)
description: Lowers eye pressure in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension using two combined mechanisms to increase fluid outflow from the eye.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use to control eye pressure.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use; avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface.
Apply gentle pressure to the inner corner of the eye for 1-2 minutes after each drop.
Remove contact lenses before applying and wait 15 minutes before reinserting.
If using other eye drops, space them at least 5 minutes apart.
storage_instructions: Store in the refrigerator before opening; after opening, may be stored at room temperature and protected from light for the labeled in-use period.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to netarsudil, latanoprost, or other prostaglandin analogs
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, significant vision change, or worsening redness that does not improve
Gradual change in eye color (increased brown pigment in the iris) - notify your eye doctor
Signs of allergic reaction: eyelid swelling, severe itching
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic OTC drug interactions expected due to minimal absorption; avoid using other prostaglandin eye drops at the same time.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your eye care provider for persistent redness, pain, or vision changes.
Report any gradual eye color change to your eye doctor.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled eye pressure checks and eye exams.
Report any vision changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed drop as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) when surgery would not improve function or cause worsening disability.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as scheduled, at consistent times as directed.
Attend all scheduled liver function monitoring visits.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Signs of infection: fever, chills
Unusual bruising or bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) can raise vimseltinib levels and increase toxicity risk.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce effectiveness - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for jaundice, dark urine, or new fever.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled liver function tests and cholesterol checks.
Report new fatigue or swelling around the eyes.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team for guidance if a dose is missed - do not double up without their instruction.

description: Protects infants against rotavirus infection, a common cause of severe diarrhea and dehydration in young children.
typical_dosage: Two-dose series given at approximately 2 and 4 months of age, per the pediatric immunization schedule.
typical_duration: Series completed by 24 weeks of age per CDC guidance.
directions_for_use: Complete both doses of the series on schedule.
Tell the provider about any immune system problems or prior intussusception before each dose.
Caregivers should practice careful hand hygiene after diaper changes for about 1-2 weeks after vaccination, as the vaccine virus can be shed in stool.
storage_instructions: Refrigerated at the pharmacy/clinic; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of intussusception: severe abdominal pain/crying, vomiting, bloody stool, lethargy - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Immunosuppressant medicines in the household should not handle soiled diapers without good hand hygiene due to viral shedding.
Other live vaccines can generally be given at the same visit; discuss timing of any other vaccines with the provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of intussusception or severe allergic reaction.
Call the pediatrician for high fever or symptoms that worsen.
self_monitoring: Track which doses in the series have been given and watch for abdominal symptoms in the days after each dose.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact the pediatrician to reschedule as soon as possible - the series must be completed by the recommended age cutoff.

description: Protects infants against rotavirus infection, a common cause of severe diarrhea and dehydration in young children.
typical_dosage: Three-dose series given at approximately 2, 4, and 6 months of age, per the pediatric immunization schedule.
typical_duration: Series completed by 32 weeks of age per CDC guidance.
directions_for_use: Complete all three doses of the series on schedule.
Tell the provider about any immune system problems or prior intussusception before each dose.
Caregivers should practice careful hand hygiene after diaper changes for about 1-2 weeks after vaccination, as the vaccine virus can be shed in stool.
storage_instructions: Refrigerated at the pharmacy/clinic; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of intussusception: severe abdominal pain/crying, vomiting, bloody stool, lethargy - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Immunosuppressant medicines in the household should not handle soiled diapers without good hand hygiene due to viral shedding.
Other live vaccines can generally be given at the same visit; discuss timing of any other vaccines with the provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of intussusception or severe allergic reaction.
Call the pediatrician for high fever or symptoms that worsen.
self_monitoring: Track which doses in the series have been given and watch for abdominal symptoms in the days after each dose.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact the pediatrician to reschedule as soon as possible - the series must be completed by the recommended age cutoff.

description: An oral targeted therapy for certain solid tumors with an NTRK gene fusion, and for ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team based on body surface area and age - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take once daily with or without food, at a consistent time.
Swallow capsules whole; do not chew or open.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers without dose adjustment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Confusion, mood changes, dizziness, or difficulty with balance/coordination (CNS effects)
Irregular heartbeat or fainting (QT prolongation)
Signs of heart failure: swelling, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain
Bone fractures with minimal trauma
Vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) significantly raise entrectinib levels and toxicity risk - dose adjustment required.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce effectiveness - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, chest pain, or severe confusion.
Call your oncology team for new dizziness, mood changes, or vision changes.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled ECGs and liver function tests.
Report new falls, confusion, or coordination problems right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is close to the next dose; if vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take an extra dose - contact your oncology team for guidance.

description: An oral targeted therapy for certain ovarian, fallopian tube, primary peritoneal, or prostate cancers, often with a BRCA mutation.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood counts: unusual fatigue, bruising, bleeding, fever, frequent infections (risk of myelodysplastic syndrome/acute leukemia with long-term use)
Chest pain, shortness of breath, coughing up blood (rare blood clots)
Signs of high blood pressure: severe headache, vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: May increase the blood-thinning effect of warfarin - INR should be monitored closely.
Increases levels of CYP1A2 and CYP3A4-metabolized drugs; discuss all new OTC/prescription medicines with your oncology team.
Avoid strong CYP1A2 inducers such as smoking, which can reduce effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for signs of low blood counts, unusual bleeding, or infection.
Seek emergency care for chest pain or shortness of breath.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled complete blood counts and blood pressure checks.
Report new fatigue, bruising, or bleeding right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If more than 12 hours have passed since a missed dose, skip it and take the next scheduled dose; do not double up.

description: An add-on treatment for seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
typical_dosage: individualized based on body weight, set by your neurologist, typically given in two divided doses with food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with food - food increases absorption.
Do not stop suddenly - can increase seizure frequency; taper only under medical supervision.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening seizures
Signs of severe allergic/skin reaction: widespread rash, blistering, fever (rare DRESS syndrome)
New or worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm
Fainting or irregular heartbeat (QT shortening)
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with alprazolam, diphenhydramine, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen.
Can reduce blood levels of hormonal contraceptives - use a backup method.
May affect levels of other anticonvulsants and warfarin - dose adjustments may be needed with specialist guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for a seizure that does not stop or for a severe skin reaction.
Call your neurologist for mood changes or thoughts of self-harm.
self_monitoring: Keep a seizure diary.
Report new rash or mood changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it. Do not double up. Contact your neurologist if you miss multiple doses.

description: Used with other antiretroviral drugs to treat HIV infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV.
typical_dosage: 600 mg by mouth twice daily as part of a combination HIV regimen, set by your HIV specialist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of HIV treatment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, split, or chew.
Take exactly with your other HIV medicines as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort, carbamazepine)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome: new infection symptoms shortly after starting treatment
Irregular heartbeat or fainting (QT prolongation)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort and rifabutin/rifampin significantly reduce fostemsavir levels and can cause treatment failure and drug resistance - avoid.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin, clarithromycin) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting or irregular heartbeat.
Call your HIV specialist for jaundice or new infection symptoms.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled liver function tests and HIV viral load/CD4 checks.
Report new symptoms after starting treatment right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. Do not stop any part of your HIV regimen without talking to your specialist.

description: Relieves nasal allergy symptoms (sneezing, itching, congestion, runny nose) by combining an antihistamine with an anti-inflammatory steroid.
typical_dosage: Two sprays in each nostril twice daily.
typical_duration: Used seasonally or long-term for allergy control, as directed.
directions_for_use: Shake gently before use and prime the pump if it hasn't been used recently.
Blow your nose gently before use; tilt head slightly forward and spray away from the nasal septum.
Avoid spraying directly into the eyes.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from freezing; discard after the labeled number of sprays or expiration.
contraindications: Recent nasal surgery or trauma (use with caution)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Nosebleeds that are frequent or severe, or a whistling sound with breathing (rare septal perforation with long-term steroid nasal use)
Vision changes or eye pain (rare glaucoma/cataract risk with prolonged steroid exposure)
Signs of allergic reaction: facial swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive drowsiness with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, or other sedating medicines.
Long-term combined use with other nasal or inhaled corticosteroids increases total steroid exposure - discuss with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your prescriber for frequent nosebleeds or vision changes.
Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Report worsening nasal symptoms, recurrent nosebleeds, or vision changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Use as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy used with chemotherapy for FLT3-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and alone for certain mast cell diseases.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team based on the treatment protocol - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Duration set by the treatment protocol (combined with chemotherapy cycles, or continuous for mastocytosis).
directions_for_use: Take with food, at consistent times as directed.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, cough, shortness of breath (risk of serious lung inflammation/pulmonary toxicity)
Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat
Signs of severe nausea/vomiting affecting ability to keep fluids down
Signs of heart problems: chest pain, irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) can significantly raise midostaurin levels and toxicity risk.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce effectiveness - avoid.
Anti-nausea medicines like ondansetron are often used together for treatment-related nausea - your oncology team will guide this.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for fever, cough, or shortness of breath.
Seek emergency care for chest pain or severe breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled blood counts and monitoring visits during treatment.
Report new cough or breathing changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team for guidance if a dose is missed - do not double up without their instruction.

description: Prevents nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy given over several days, using a patch that delivers medicine through the skin.
typical_dosage: One patch applied to the upper outer arm at least 24 hours (up to 48 hours) before chemotherapy; remove at least 24 hours after chemotherapy ends, up to 7 days of wear, as directed.
typical_duration: Applied per chemotherapy cycle, as directed by your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Apply to clean, dry, intact skin on the upper outer arm; do not apply to irritated or damaged skin.
Do not cut the patch.
Avoid exposing the patch site to direct sunlight; cover with clothing if outdoors.
Remove and dispose of the patch as directed, folding it in half with the sticky sides together.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original pouch until ready to use.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to granisetron or other 5-HT3 antagonists
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, fainting, or chest pain (QT prolongation)
Signs of severe allergic/skin reaction at the patch site
Severe constipation or abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other serotonergic drugs (e.g., tramadol, sertraline, escitalopram) increases risk of serotonin syndrome - report any agitation, rapid heartbeat, or muscle rigidity.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (azithromycin, clarithromycin) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, chest pain, or signs of serotonin syndrome.
Call your oncology team for a skin reaction at the patch site.
self_monitoring: Track nausea control and bowel movements; report severe constipation.
missed_dose_instructions: If a patch falls off early, apply a new one to a different site and contact your oncology team for guidance on timing; do not use more than one patch at a time.

description: Applied to chronic wounds (such as pressure ulcers or diabetic ulcers) to break down dead tissue and help promote healing.
typical_dosage: Applied once daily (or as directed) directly to the wound as part of a wound care regimen.
typical_duration: Continued until debridement is complete, per your wound care team's assessment.
directions_for_use: Clean the wound as instructed before each application.
Apply directly to the wound; if the wound is deep, apply into the crevices of the wound.
Cover with an appropriate dressing as directed by your wound care team.
Avoid use with certain antiseptic solutions (e.g., those containing heavy metals like silver) that can reduce enzyme activity - ask your wound care team before using other wound products.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; may be kept at room temperature for a limited time per the label - do not freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Increasing redness, warmth, swelling, odor, or pus at the wound (possible infection)
Wound that worsens or fails to improve
New pain at the wound site
common_side_effects: Mild redness or warmth at wound site
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with topical antiseptics containing metals (e.g., silver sulfadiazine) or acidic solutions unless directed by your wound care team, as they can inactivate the enzyme.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your wound care team for signs of infection or a worsening wound.
Stop use and call your prescriber for a significant allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track wound size/appearance as instructed and report any fever or spreading redness immediately.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered that day; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: Used with a phenylalanine-restricted diet to lower blood phenylalanine levels in people with phenylketonuria (PKU) who are responsive to this therapy.
typical_dosage: individualized based on body weight and phenylalanine response, set by your metabolic specialist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy alongside dietary management.
directions_for_use: Take with food at the same time each day to improve absorption and consistency.
Dissolve tablets or powder in water or juice as directed; take within 15-20 minutes of mixing.
Continue your prescribed low-phenylalanine diet - this medicine does not replace dietary management.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep the bottle tightly closed.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
Signs of significantly low phenylalanine (if diet is not adjusted): irritability, poor growth
otc_and_other_interactions: May enhance the effects of levodopa-containing products through effects on neurotransmitter pathways - discuss any Parkinson's medications with your specialist.
No significant common OTC interactions expected; always coordinate diet and supplement changes with your metabolic specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact your metabolic specialist for questions about dietary phenylalanine adjustments.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled blood phenylalanine level checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered that day; if it is the next day, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in the chronic phase.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal, twice daily approximately 12 hours apart.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of pancreatitis: severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting
Irregular heartbeat or fainting (QT prolongation at higher doses)
Signs of high blood pressure: severe headache, vision changes
Unusual bruising or bleeding, signs of low blood counts
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) can raise asciminib levels and increase toxicity risk.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
May increase levels of simvastatin and other sensitive CYP3A4/OATP substrates - discuss all medicines with your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, fainting, or severe abdominal pain.
Call your oncology team promptly for signs of bleeding or infection.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled blood counts, pancreatic enzyme checks, and ECGs.
Report new abdominal pain right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than a few hours, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time; do not double up.

description: Treats schizophrenia in adults using a once-daily patch that delivers medicine through the skin.
typical_dosage: One patch applied once daily, worn for 24 hours, then replaced; strength individualized by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Apply to clean, dry, intact skin on the upper arm, upper back, abdomen, or hip; rotate sites and avoid reapplying to the same spot for 2 weeks.
Remove the old patch before applying a new one - only wear one patch at a time.
Avoid exposing the patch to heat sources (heating pads, saunas) - can increase drug release.
Do not stop suddenly without talking to your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the sealed pouch until ready to use.
contraindications: Increased mortality risk in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, sweating (possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care immediately
Uncontrollable muscle movements (tardive dyskinesia)
New or worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm
Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst/urination
Irregular heartbeat or fainting
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (azithromycin, clarithromycin, ondansetron) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
May increase serotonin-related side effects when combined with sertraline or escitalopram.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fever with muscle stiffness/confusion, fainting, or thoughts of self-harm.
Call your prescriber for new uncontrollable movements or a skin reaction at the patch site.
self_monitoring: Track weight, blood sugar, and cholesterol as directed.
Check the patch site daily for irritation.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply a new patch as soon as remembered and resume the regular daily schedule from that point - do not apply an extra patch to make up for a missed one.

description: Provides long-term control of asthma and COPD symptoms by relaxing airway muscles; not for treating sudden breathing attacks.
typical_dosage: One inhalation (50 mcg) twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as part of an asthma/COPD control plan; usually combined with an inhaled corticosteroid for asthma.
directions_for_use: Use exactly as directed twice daily - do not use for sudden shortness of breath; keep a fast-acting rescue inhaler (e.g., albuterol) on hand for that.
Rinse mouth after use if also using an inhaled steroid together.
Do not exceed the prescribed frequency.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep the Diskus closed except when in use.
contraindications: Use as monotherapy for asthma without an inhaled corticosteroid (boxed warning for increased risk of asthma-related death)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening asthma or COPD symptoms, or increased use of a rescue inhaler - contact prescriber, do not simply add more salmeterol
Chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat (rare cardiovascular effects)
Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling, difficulty breathing (paradoxical bronchospasm)
otc_and_other_interactions: Beta-blockers (e.g., metoprolol) can blunt salmeterol's bronchodilating effect and worsen bronchospasm - use cautiously together.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, fluconazole) can raise salmeterol levels, increasing cardiovascular side effect risk.
Additive cardiovascular stimulation with other stimulant-type OTC decongestants (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine).
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or worsening breathing difficulty.
Call your prescriber if you are using your rescue inhaler more often than usual.
self_monitoring: Track symptom frequency and rescue inhaler use.
Keep scheduled lung function tests.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular twice-daily schedule - do not double up.

description: Protects adults age 50 and older (and certain younger immunocompromised adults) against shingles (herpes zoster) and its complications.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or other healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: Two-dose series, given 2-6 months apart (as close as 1-2 months apart for immunocompromised patients).
typical_duration: Two doses complete the series; long-lasting protection after completion.
directions_for_use: Complete both doses of the series for full protection.
Bring your vaccination record to each visit.
You may still get shingles after vaccination, but symptoms are typically milder.
storage_instructions: Refrigerated at the pharmacy/clinic (2-8°C); not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, trouble breathing - seek emergency care immediately
otc_and_other_interactions: Immunosuppressant drugs (e.g., prednisone, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, methotrexate) may reduce the immune response - this vaccine is still generally recommended for immunocompromised patients as it is not a live vaccine.
OTC acetaminophen or ibuprofen can be used for injection-site soreness or fever if approved by your provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Call your provider for fever or side effects that last more than a few days.
self_monitoring: Track which dose in the series you have received and when the second dose is due.
missed_dose_instructions: If the second dose is delayed, there is no need to restart the series - get it as soon as possible.

description: Treats Cushing's disease (when surgery is not an option or has not worked) and acromegaly by reducing excess hormone production.
route: Subcutaneous injection (short-acting) or intramuscular injection (long-acting, given by a provider)
dosage_forms: Long-acting injectable suspension (monthly, given by a provider)
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your endocrinologist based on hormone levels and response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy with periodic lab-based dose adjustments.
directions_for_use: If self-injecting the short-acting form, rotate injection sites (thigh or abdomen) as trained by your care team.
Attend all scheduled visits for the long-acting monthly injection.
Do not adjust the dose on your own.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; short-acting injections may be kept at room temperature briefly before use - protect from light; do not freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high blood sugar: increased thirst/urination, blurred vision (very common, often requires diabetes medication)
Signs of gallstones: severe right upper abdominal pain
Slow heart rate, fainting, irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation/bradycardia)
Signs of adrenal insufficiency: severe fatigue, dizziness, low blood pressure
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: Can raise blood sugar, requiring adjustment of diabetes medicines such as metformin or glipizide.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin, clarithromycin) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
May reduce the effectiveness of, or require dose changes to, other hormone-affecting medicines - discuss all medicines with your endocrinologist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, severe irregular heartbeat, or signs of adrenal crisis.
Call your endocrinologist promptly for severe abdominal pain or high blood sugar symptoms.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar regularly as directed.
Keep scheduled ECGs, gallbladder ultrasounds, and hormone level checks.
missed_dose_instructions: For self-injected doses, take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it - do not double up. Contact your care team to reschedule a missed long-acting injection appointment.

drug_class: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor/alpha-2 agonist combination (ophthalmic, glaucoma agent)
description: Lowers eye pressure in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension by reducing fluid production in the eye through two combined mechanisms.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use to control eye pressure.
directions_for_use: Shake well before use.
Wash hands before use; avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface.
Apply gentle pressure to the inner corner of the eye for 1-2 minutes after each drop to reduce systemic absorption.
Remove contact lenses before applying and wait 15 minutes before reinserting.
If using other eye drops, space them at least 5 minutes apart.
storage_instructions: Store upright at room temperature, protect from light.
contraindications: Use in infants/neonates (brimonidine component can cause serious CNS depression in young children)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, significant vision change, or worsening redness
Signs of allergic reaction: eyelid swelling, severe itching, rash
Unusual drowsiness, slow heartbeat, or low blood pressure (rare systemic absorption effects, especially in children)
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not use with MAO inhibitors.
Additive drowsiness/blood pressure lowering with CNS depressants (diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol) and with antihypertensives (lisinopril, losartan, amlodipine, metoprolol).
Sulfonamide-related allergy: brinzolamide is a sulfonamide - tell your prescriber if you have had reactions to sulfa drugs (e.g., sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim).
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your eye care provider for persistent redness, pain, or vision changes.
Seek emergency care for signs of a significant allergic reaction or fainting.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled eye pressure checks and eye exams.
Report drowsiness or dizziness, especially in children who may be accidentally exposed.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed drop as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: Used as part of a combination regimen to treat multidrug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis when other options are not available.
typical_dosage: individualized multi-phase regimen set by your TB specialist, typically starting with a loading dose then a reduced maintenance dose several times weekly.
typical_duration: Typically a 24-week course as part of a longer multidrug TB regimen, set by your specialist.
directions_for_use: Take with food to improve absorption.
Take exactly as scheduled together with your other TB medicines - never take bedaquiline alone.
Complete the entire course exactly as prescribed, even if you feel better, to prevent resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin, St. John's Wort)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, fainting, or palpitations (boxed warning for QT prolongation and risk of death)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe nausea
Chest pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin, clarithromycin, fluconazole) significantly increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms - avoid where possible.

Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) raise bedaquiline levels and toxicity risk; strong inducers (rifabutin, St. John's Wort) reduce effectiveness - avoid combining without specialist guidance.
Alcohol should be avoided due to added liver stress.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, palpitations, or chest pain.
Call your TB specialist promptly for jaundice or severe nausea.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled ECGs and liver function tests.
Report new palpitations or dizziness right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your TB specialist for guidance if a dose is missed - do not double up or stop the regimen without their instruction, as this can promote drug resistance.

description: Treats Friedreich's ataxia, a rare inherited neurological disorder, in adults and adolescents.
typical_dosage: individualized, typically 150 mg (three capsules) by mouth once daily on an empty stomach, set by your neurologist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal.
Swallow capsules whole.
Do not stop without talking to your neurologist.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, facial swelling, trouble breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit juice and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin), which can raise drug levels.
Avoid combining with other potentially liver-toxic products (e.g., high-dose acetaminophen, excess alcohol) unless approved by your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your neurologist promptly for jaundice, dark urine, or severe fatigue.
Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled liver function tests.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and resume your normal once-daily schedule the next day - do not double up.

description: Reduces inflammation in plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's disease, and ulcerative colitis by blocking IL-23, a protein involved in inflammation.
route: Subcutaneous injection (self-administered after training, or by a caregiver); some regimens include an initial IV infusion
dosage_forms: Intravenous infusion (for induction in some conditions)
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your specialist - typically given every 8 or 12 weeks after an initial induction phase.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Allow the prefilled syringe/pen to warm to room temperature for about 15-45 minutes before injecting, as instructed.
Inject into the thigh or abdomen (or upper arm if given by a caregiver); rotate injection sites.
Do not shake the syringe or pen.
Follow your specialist's exact dosing schedule - do not skip or delay doses without guidance.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate (2-8°C); do not freeze. May be stored at room temperature for a limited time per the label if needed. Protect from light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, cough, burning with urination, wounds that won't heal - increased infection risk
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing
Signs of liver problems (Crohn's/UC use): yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other immunosuppressants (methotrexate, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, prednisone) increases infection risk - only combined under specialist supervision.
Live vaccines should be avoided while on this medicine - discuss vaccination timing with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
Call your specialist promptly for any signs of infection.
self_monitoring: Watch for and report any signs of infection immediately.
Keep scheduled tuberculosis screening and any labs your specialist orders.
missed_dose_instructions: Give the missed dose as soon as remembered, then resume your regular schedule from that date; contact your specialist if you are unsure how to adjust the schedule.

description: Helps remove excess nitrogen (as ammonia) from the body in patients with urea cycle disorders who cannot fully break down protein normally.
typical_dosage: individualized based on body weight and dietary protein intake, set by your metabolic specialist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy alongside a protein-restricted diet.
directions_for_use: Take with meals/snacks in evenly divided doses as directed, spread throughout the day.
Continue the prescribed protein-restricted diet - this medicine works together with diet, not instead of it.
Mix powder formulations with food or liquid as directed; do not swallow powder dry.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep container tightly closed.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high ammonia (a metabolic crisis): vomiting, lethargy, confusion, irritability, refusal to eat - seek emergency care immediately, this can be life-threatening
Signs of low blood counts: unusual bruising, bleeding, fever
Irregular heartbeat (rare, related to associated electrolyte changes)
otc_and_other_interactions: Corticosteroids (e.g., prednisone) can increase protein breakdown and raise ammonia levels, counteracting this medicine's effect - report steroid use to your specialist.
Probenecid and certain other drugs affecting kidney excretion may affect phenylbutyrate clearance - discuss all medicines with your specialist.
Valproic acid (a common anticonvulsant) can raise ammonia levels and is generally avoided in urea cycle disorders.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for any signs of a metabolic/hyperammonemia crisis.
Call your metabolic specialist for any illness, as illness can trigger high ammonia even with good adherence.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled ammonia and plasma amino acid level checks.
Learn to recognize early signs of high ammonia and have an emergency action plan.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered with food; if it is almost time for the next dose, contact your metabolic specialist for guidance rather than skipping, since missed doses can raise ammonia levels.

description: Lowers high blood potassium levels (hyperkalemia) by binding potassium in the gut so it is removed in the stool.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your prescriber based on potassium levels; oral doses are often mixed in a small amount of water or sorbitol as directed.
typical_duration: Short-term for acute high potassium, or intermittent/ongoing use for chronic management, as directed.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as directed, usually 1-4 times daily or as a single dose for acute treatment.
Take other oral medicines at least 3 hours apart from this medicine, as it can bind and reduce absorption of other drugs.
For rectal use, retain the enema for the time directed before evacuating.
storage_instructions: Store suspension at room temperature; do not freeze; shake well before use.
contraindications: Bowel obstruction or abnormal bowel motility
Should not be used with sorbitol due to risk of intestinal necrosis (per FDA warning)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe abdominal pain, distension, bloody stools, or vomiting (rare but serious bowel injury/necrosis) - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of low potassium from overuse: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
Signs of fluid retention: swelling, shortness of breath (some products contain significant sodium)
otc_and_other_interactions: Can bind and reduce the absorption of many oral medicines, including levothyroxine - separate dosing by at least 3 hours.
Avoid combining with magnesium- or aluminum-containing antacids, which can reduce potassium-binding effectiveness and increase risk of bowel problems.
Do not take with sorbitol-containing products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for severe abdominal pain, bloody stools, or vomiting.
Call your prescriber for constipation that does not improve or signs of low potassium.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled potassium and electrolyte level checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up. Contact your prescriber if you have ongoing high-potassium symptoms.

description: Combines a long-acting basal insulin with a GLP-1 receptor agonist in one injection to control blood sugar in type 2 diabetes.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your prescriber, injected once daily within 1 hour before the first meal of the day.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for blood sugar control.
directions_for_use: Inject under the skin of the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm; rotate injection sites.
Take within the hour before your first meal, at roughly the same time each day.
Never share your pen with another person, even with a new needle.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate unused pens (2-8°C); once in use, store at room temperature (below 86°F/30°C) and discard after the labeled number of days - do not freeze.
contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2 syndrome
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe low blood sugar: confusion, sweating, shakiness, fainting - treat immediately and seek care if severe
Signs of pancreatitis: severe abdominal pain radiating to the back, persistent vomiting
A lump or swelling in the neck, hoarseness, trouble swallowing (rare thyroid tumor risk seen in animal studies)
Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Other diabetes medicines (metformin, glipizide) increase the risk of low blood sugar when combined.
NSAIDs and alcohol can enhance the blood-sugar-lowering effect and mask symptoms of low blood sugar.
Beta-blockers (metoprolol) can mask the warning signs of low blood sugar such as rapid heartbeat.
Always carry a fast-acting sugar source in case of low blood sugar.
action_if_adverse_effects: Treat low blood sugar right away with fast-acting sugar; seek emergency care if confusion or loss of consciousness occurs.
Seek care immediately for signs of pancreatitis or a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed.
Keep scheduled A1C checks.
Report a neck lump or hoarseness right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and resume your normal schedule with the next meal - do not double up or take extra to make up for a missed dose.

description: An oral targeted therapy for certain liver, kidney, and thyroid cancers by blocking growth signals and blood vessel formation in tumors.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal), or as directed by your oncologist.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/urine, coughing up blood
Chest pain, shortness of breath (risk of heart problems)
Severe high blood pressure: severe headache, vision changes
Signs of a hole in the stomach/intestine: severe abdominal pain
Severe rash, peeling skin, especially on hands and feet (hand-foot skin reaction)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly increases warfarin's blood-thinning effect - increased bleeding risk; INR must be monitored closely.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) and aspirin can add to bleeding risk.
St. John's Wort can reduce sorafenib levels and effectiveness - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, severe bleeding, or signs of a perforated bowel.
Call your oncology team promptly for severe hand-foot skin reaction, high blood pressure symptoms, or jaundice.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure regularly as directed.
Keep all scheduled liver function tests and blood counts.
Inspect hands and feet for skin changes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up.

description: Treats moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults by selectively blocking an enzyme involved in inflammatory signaling.
typical_dosage: 6 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop without talking to your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, cough, burning with urination
Signs of a new skin cancer or unusual lump (increased malignancy risk)
Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other immunosuppressants (methotrexate, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, prednisone) increases infection risk - only combined under specialist supervision.
Live vaccines should be avoided while on this medicine - discuss vaccination timing with your prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
Call your prescriber promptly for any signs of infection.
self_monitoring: Watch for and report any signs of infection immediately.
Report any new skin lesions or lumps.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: A combination maintenance inhaler for long-term control of COPD symptoms; not for sudden breathing attacks.
dosage_forms: Inhalation spray (Respimat device, 2.5 mcg/2.5 mcg per actuation)
typical_dosage: Two inhalations once daily, at the same time each day.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use for COPD maintenance.
directions_for_use: Use exactly as directed once daily - do not use for sudden shortness of breath; keep a rescue inhaler on hand for that.
Avoid spraying in or near the eyes - can cause blurred vision or eye pain.
Prime the inhaler before first use and if not used for more than a few days, per the instructions.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from freezing; discard 3 months after first use or when the dose indicator reads zero, whichever comes first.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to atropine or its derivatives
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden worsening of breathing right after use (paradoxical bronchospasm) - stop use and seek care
Eye pain, blurred vision, halos around lights, or red eyes (possible narrow-angle glaucoma)
Difficulty urinating or worsening urinary symptoms (can worsen enlarged prostate/urinary retention)
Chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Beta-blockers (e.g., metoprolol) can blunt the bronchodilating effect and should generally be avoided in COPD.
Additive anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention) with diphenhydramine and other anticholinergic OTC products.
Other LAMA or LABA inhalers should not be used at the same time - risk of overdose-related side effects.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care right away for sudden worsening breathing, eye pain, or urinary retention.
Call your prescriber for chest pain or irregular heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Track symptom control and rescue inhaler use.
Report new eye pain or urinary difficulty.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it - do not double up or use more than one dose in 24 hours.

description: An oral targeted therapy for certain colorectal cancers, gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), and liver cancer that have progressed on other treatments.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team, typically taken once daily for 21 days followed by 7 days off, in 28-day cycles.
typical_duration: Continued in cycles as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take with a low-fat meal at the same time each day.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue (boxed warning for severe/fatal liver toxicity)
Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/urine, coughing up blood
Severe high blood pressure: severe headache, vision changes
Chest pain, sudden weakness (heart attack/stroke risk)
Severe rash, peeling skin, especially on hands and feet (hand-foot skin reaction)
Signs of a hole in the stomach/intestine: severe abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Significantly increases warfarin's blood-thinning effect - increased bleeding risk; INR must be monitored closely.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) and aspirin can add to bleeding risk.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers (fluconazole, clarithromycin, St. John's Wort) affect regorafenib levels - avoid without oncology guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, severe bleeding, or signs of a perforated bowel.
Call your oncology team promptly for jaundice, severe hand-foot skin reaction, or high blood pressure symptoms.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled liver function tests and blood pressure checks.
Inspect hands and feet for skin changes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time the next day - do not double up or take two doses on the same day.

drug_class: Complete HIV antiretroviral regimen (integrase inhibitor/booster/NRTI combination)
description: A complete single-tablet regimen to treat HIV-1 infection in appropriate adults, combining an integrase inhibitor with a booster and two NRTIs.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily with food, as set by your HIV specialist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for HIV treatment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day with food to improve absorption.
Do not stop or skip doses - missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
Kidney function is monitored regularly due to the tenofovir disoproxil fumarate component.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep in the original container with the desiccant.
contraindications: Concurrent use with simvastatin or lovastatin
Concurrent use with rifampin, St. John's Wort, or other strong CYP3A4 inducers
Significant kidney impairment (not recommended below a certain kidney function threshold)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of lactic acidosis or severe liver problems: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain with nausea/vomiting, yellowing skin/eyes (boxed warning)
Worsening kidney function: decreased urination, swelling, bone pain (tenofovir DF can affect kidneys and bone density)
Signs of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome: new infection symptoms shortly after starting treatment
Sudden worsening of hepatitis B if you also have that infection and stop this medicine
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with simvastatin (and generally avoided with atorvastatin at higher doses) - the cobicistat booster markedly raises statin levels, risking severe muscle injury.
St. John's Wort and rifampin significantly reduce drug levels and can cause treatment failure and resistance - avoid.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can add to kidney stress when combined with the tenofovir component - use acetaminophen when possible and discuss with your specialist.
Cobicistat increases levels of many other drugs (e.g., sildenafil) - review all medicines with your HIV specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of lactic acidosis or severe liver problems.
Call your HIV specialist promptly for decreased urination, bone pain, or new infection symptoms.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled kidney function tests, bone density checks if recommended, and HIV viral load/CD4 checks.
Report new muscle pain, breathing trouble, or abdominal pain right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. Contact your specialist about missed doses, as adherence is critical to prevent resistance.

description: Replaces a missing digestive enzyme to treat genetic sucrase-isomaltase deficiency, improving digestion of table sugar (sucrose).
typical_dosage: individualized based on body weight, taken with each meal or snack, set by your gastroenterologist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy taken with meals.
directions_for_use: Mix the dose with water, milk, or infant formula (not fruit juice) immediately before taking, as directed.
Take with every meal and snack that contains sucrose.
Do not heat the solution - heat can destroy the enzyme's activity.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze. May be kept at room temperature for a limited time per the label once opened.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to yeast, yeast products, papain, or glycerin (product components)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
Severe abdominal pain unresponsive to dose adjustment
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; effectiveness depends on avoiding heating the solution and taking it with sucrose-containing food.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
Call your gastroenterologist for abdominal symptoms that do not improve with dose adjustment.
self_monitoring: Track digestive symptoms and growth (in children) to help guide dose adjustments with your care team.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed before a sucrose-containing meal, take it as soon as remembered before eating; if the meal is finished, take the next dose with the next meal/snack as scheduled.

description: Cleanses the bowel before a colonoscopy so the colon lining can be clearly seen.
typical_dosage: Two doses of dissolved solution (typically about 16 oz each, followed by additional clear liquid) taken the evening before and the morning of the colonoscopy, exactly per your prescriber's split-dose instructions.
typical_duration: One-time use for bowel preparation before the procedure.
directions_for_use: Follow the exact split-dose timing given by your prescriber's office - this affects how clean and safe your prep is.
Drink each dose over the time period directed, followed by the recommended amount of additional clear liquids.
Stay near a bathroom once you begin - expect frequent, loose bowel movements.
Follow the clear liquid diet instructions provided before your procedure.
Stop drinking clear liquids at the time specified before your procedure (usually a few hours before).
storage_instructions: Store the powder at room temperature; use the mixed solution within the time frame specified on the label.
contraindications: Galactose-restricted diets (product may contain sugars requiring caution in rare metabolic conditions)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe abdominal pain, distension, or rectal bleeding
Signs of dehydration or electrolyte imbalance: severe dizziness, irregular heartbeat, confusion, seizures
Signs of allergic reaction: hives, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Take other oral medicines (including OTC drugs) at least 1 hour before starting or wait until the prep is finished, since rapid bowel evacuation can reduce their absorption - ask your prescriber about timing of essential daily medicines such as levothyroxine or seizure medicines.
Diuretics and other drugs affecting electrolytes (e.g., some blood pressure medicines) may need to be held the day of prep - follow your prescriber's specific instructions.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe abdominal pain, signs of dehydration, or an allergic reaction.
Call your prescriber's office if you cannot tolerate the prep or are unable to complete it.
self_monitoring: Track fluid intake and hydration; contact your prescriber's office with questions about completing the prep.
missed_dose_instructions: If you have trouble completing a dose, contact your prescriber's office promptly - do not simply skip the second dose, as an incomplete prep may require rescheduling the colonoscopy.

description: Treats bacterial acne and certain eye infections (conjunctivitis) by stopping bacterial growth.
typical_dosage: Applied to affected skin areas 1-2 times daily, or eye drops instilled several times daily as directed.
typical_duration: Course length set by your prescriber based on the condition treated.
directions_for_use: Wash and dry the affected skin area before applying (for topical use).
For eye use, wash hands before instilling; avoid touching the applicator tip to the eye.
Complete the full course as directed even if symptoms improve.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a significant allergic reaction: widespread rash, blistering, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
Increased eye pain, redness, or vision changes (for ophthalmic use)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid use with other topical products containing silver (e.g., silver sulfadiazine) - can reduce effectiveness.
Tell your prescriber about any prior reaction to sulfa antibiotics like sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim before starting.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of a significant allergic reaction.
Call your prescriber for worsening irritation or eye symptoms.
self_monitoring: Track skin or eye symptoms and report if they worsen instead of improving.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply/use as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next application, skip the missed one - do not double up.

description: Treats bacterial eye infections with associated inflammation by combining an antibiotic with an anti-inflammatory steroid.
typical_dosage: individualized, typically instilled several times daily, tapered as directed by your eye care provider.
typical_duration: Short-term use only, as directed - not for long-term use due to the steroid component.
directions_for_use: Shake suspension well before use.
Wash hands before use; avoid touching the applicator tip to the eye.
Do not stop early or extend use beyond what is prescribed - stopping steroid eye drops abruptly or using them too long can cause problems.
Remove contact lenses before use.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light; discard per the labeled in-use period after opening.
contraindications: Most viral eye infections (e.g., herpes simplex keratitis)
Fungal or untreated bacterial/tubercular eye infections
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Increased eye pain, vision changes, or worsening redness - report promptly, especially with prolonged steroid use (risk of increased eye pressure, cataracts, or delayed healing/infection)
Signs of allergic reaction: eyelid swelling, severe itching
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic OTC drug interactions expected due to minimal absorption; avoid using other eye products without spacing doses and discuss any other eye drops with your eye care provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your eye care provider promptly for increased pain, vision changes, or worsening redness.
Seek emergency care for a significant allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled eye pressure checks if using longer than a few weeks, as directed by your eye care provider.
missed_dose_instructions: Use the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: A long-acting antiretroviral used with other HIV medicines to treat multidrug-resistant HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults.
route: Oral (loading doses) and subcutaneous injection (given by a healthcare provider, twice yearly for maintenance)
typical_dosage: individualized loading regimen (oral and injectable) followed by maintenance injections roughly every 6 months, set by your HIV specialist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of HIV treatment.
directions_for_use: Take oral loading tablets exactly on the schedule provided, with or without food.
Attend all scheduled injection appointments - missed injections can lead to loss of viral control and drug resistance.
Continue your complete HIV regimen exactly as prescribed.
storage_instructions: Store oral tablets at room temperature, protect from moisture; injections are stored and administered at the clinic/pharmacy.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin, St. John's Wort, carbamazepine)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome: new infection symptoms shortly after starting treatment
Significant injection site reactions: swelling, lumps, or ulceration that worsen or do not resolve
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions (pain, swelling, redness, nodules)
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort and rifabutin/rifampin significantly reduce lenacapavir levels and can lead to treatment failure and drug resistance - avoid.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can raise lenacapavir levels - discuss all medicines with your HIV specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your HIV specialist promptly for a worsening injection site reaction or new infection symptoms.
Seek care for signs of jaundice or a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled injection appointments and HIV viral load/CD4 checks.
Check injection sites periodically as directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your HIV specialist immediately if you are going to miss a scheduled injection - the dosing window is important to maintain effective drug levels and prevent resistance.

generic_name: Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate bowel preparation tablets
description: Cleanses the bowel before a colonoscopy so the colon lining can be clearly seen, using a tablet-based (non-liquid) preparation.
typical_dosage: 12 tablets taken with 16 oz of water the evening before, and 12 tablets with 16 oz of water the morning of the colonoscopy, each followed by additional clear liquids, exactly per your prescriber's split-dose instructions.
typical_duration: One-time use for bowel preparation before the procedure.
directions_for_use: Follow the exact split-dose timing given by your prescriber's office.
Take each tablet with a sip of water, over about 15-20 minutes, followed by the additional clear liquids required.
Stay near a bathroom once you begin - expect frequent, loose bowel movements.
Follow the clear liquid diet instructions provided before your procedure.
Stop drinking clear liquids at the time specified before your procedure.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe abdominal pain, distension, or rectal bleeding
Signs of dehydration or electrolyte imbalance: severe dizziness, irregular heartbeat, confusion, seizures
Signs of allergic reaction: hives, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Take other oral medicines (including OTC drugs) at least 1 hour before starting or wait until the prep is finished - ask your prescriber about timing of essential daily medicines such as levothyroxine or seizure medicines.
Diuretics and other drugs affecting electrolytes may need to be adjusted the day of prep - follow your prescriber's specific instructions.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe abdominal pain, signs of dehydration, or an allergic reaction.
Call your prescriber's office if you cannot tolerate the prep or are unable to complete it.
self_monitoring: Track fluid intake and hydration; contact your prescriber's office with questions about completing the prep.
missed_dose_instructions: If you have trouble completing a dose, contact your prescriber's office promptly - do not simply skip the second dose, as an incomplete prep may require rescheduling the colonoscopy.

drug_class: Complete HIV antiretroviral regimen (protease inhibitor/booster/NRTI combination)
description: A complete single-tablet regimen to treat HIV-1 infection in appropriate adults, combining a protease inhibitor with a booster and two NRTIs.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily with food, as set by your HIV specialist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for HIV treatment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day with food to improve absorption.
Do not stop or skip doses - missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep in the original container with the desiccant.
contraindications: Concurrent use with simvastatin or lovastatin
Concurrent use with rifampin, St. John's Wort, or other strong CYP3A4 inducers
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Signs of severe skin reaction: widespread rash, blistering, fever
Signs of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome: new infection symptoms shortly after starting treatment
Sudden worsening of hepatitis B if you also have that infection and stop this medicine
Worsening kidney function: decreased urination, swelling
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with simvastatin/lovastatin (and generally avoided with higher-dose atorvastatin) - the cobicistat booster markedly raises statin levels, risking severe muscle injury.
St. John's Wort and rifampin significantly reduce drug levels and can cause treatment failure and resistance - avoid.
Cobicistat increases levels of many other drugs (e.g., sildenafil) - review all medicines with your HIV specialist.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can add to kidney stress - use acetaminophen when possible and discuss with your specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of a severe skin reaction or breathing difficulty.
Call your HIV specialist promptly for jaundice, decreased urination, or new infection symptoms.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled liver and kidney function tests and HIV viral load/CD4 checks.
Report new rash or reduced urination right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. Contact your specialist about missed doses, as adherence is critical to prevent resistance.

description: Combines two mechanisms in one tablet to lower blood sugar in type 2 diabetes - reducing sugar reabsorption by the kidneys and decreasing sugar production by the liver.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your prescriber based on kidney function and blood sugar control.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for blood sugar control.
directions_for_use: Take with meals to reduce stomach upset.
Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not crush, split, or chew.
Stay well hydrated, especially in hot weather or with illness causing vomiting/diarrhea.
Temporarily stop before procedures using IV contrast dye, as directed by your prescriber, due to the metformin component.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Conditions predisposing to dehydration or low blood pressure
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, feeling cold - seek emergency care immediately, this is rare but serious
Signs of ketoacidosis even with normal-looking blood sugar: nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fatigue, trouble breathing
Signs of a genital or urinary tract infection: pain/burning with urination, genital itching/odor
Signs of dehydration or low blood pressure: dizziness, fainting
otc_and_other_interactions: Corticosteroids (prednisone) raise blood sugar and may reduce this medicine's effectiveness - monitoring and dose adjustment may be needed.
Other diabetes medicines (glipizide) increase the risk of low blood sugar when combined.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can affect kidney function and increase metformin accumulation risk.
Excess alcohol increases risk of lactic acidosis - avoid heavy alcohol use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of lactic acidosis or ketoacidosis.
Call your prescriber promptly for signs of a urinary/genital infection or dehydration.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed.
Keep scheduled kidney function tests and A1C checks.
Stay well hydrated.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it. Do not double up.

description: An oral chemotherapy drug used mainly for acute leukemias, interfering with cancer cell DNA production.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team based on body surface area and blood counts - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued per the specific chemotherapy protocol, as directed by your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as scheduled, at a consistent time, with or without food.
Avoid crushing tablets and handle with care; caregivers who are pregnant should avoid handling this medicine.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep away from children and pets.
contraindications: Prior resistance to thioguanine or mercaptopurine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood counts: unusual fatigue, bruising, bleeding, fever, frequent infections
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal swelling (risk of liver toxicity with prolonged use)
Signs of infection: fever, chills, sore throat
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other chemotherapy agents such as methotrexate can increase risk of liver toxicity and low blood counts - your oncology team monitors this closely as part of your protocol.
Avoid NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) and aspirin, which can add to bleeding risk when blood counts are low.
Avoid alcohol - additional liver stress.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for fever, unusual bruising/bleeding, or jaundice.
Seek emergency care for signs of serious infection or bleeding.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled blood counts and liver function tests.
Report fever or signs of infection immediately - avoid crowds/sick contacts when counts are low.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team for guidance if a dose is missed - do not double up without their instruction.

description: An oral targeted therapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with a MET exon 14 skipping alteration.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (risk of serious lung inflammation/pneumonitis)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Nausea, vomiting, decreased urination (risk of pancreatitis or kidney effects)
Signs of severe skin reaction: peeling, blistering
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) can significantly raise capmatinib levels and toxicity risk - dose adjustment may be needed.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce effectiveness - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for new cough, shortness of breath, or fever - lung inflammation can be serious.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe skin reaction or liver problems.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled liver function tests and monitoring visits.
Report new swelling, cough, or breathing changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than 4 hours, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time; do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for certain melanomas, non-small cell lung cancers, and thyroid cancers with a BRAF V600 mutation, often combined with trametinib.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal, twice daily approximately 12 hours apart.
Swallow capsules whole with water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever (can be high and require dose interruption) - report any fever to your oncology team promptly
New skin lesions or changes (risk of new skin cancers)
Signs of severe allergic/skin reaction: widespread rash, blistering
Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath
Vision changes (rare eye problems)
