Signs of high or low blood sugar in diabetics (can affect blood sugar control)
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives - use a non-hormonal backup method.
May reduce warfarin's blood-thinning effect - INR should be monitored.
Strong CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors can significantly affect dabrafenib levels - avoid St. John's Wort and discuss all new medicines with your oncology team.
Can affect blood sugar levels in patients on metformin or glipizide - monitor blood sugar closely.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for fever, new skin lesions, or vision changes.
Seek emergency care for chest pain or a severe skin reaction.
self_monitoring: Check temperature regularly, especially in the first months.
Keep scheduled skin exams and blood sugar checks if diabetic.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than 6 hours, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for certain BRCA-mutated breast cancers and, in combination with enzalutamide, for certain prostate cancers.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take once daily at a consistent time, with or without food.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood counts: unusual fatigue, bruising, bleeding, fever, frequent infections (risk of myelodysplastic syndrome/acute leukemia with long-term use)
Signs of new/worsening lung symptoms: cough, shortness of breath
Signs of severe allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: P-glycoprotein inhibitors can raise talazoparib levels; discuss all new medicines, including OTC products, with your oncology team.
Avoid combining with other bone marrow-suppressing drugs unless directed, as this can worsen low blood counts.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for signs of low blood counts or new breathing problems.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled complete blood counts.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time the next day; if vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take an extra dose - contact your oncology team for guidance.

description: Treats Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder, most often in people who are totally blind, by helping regulate the body's internal clock.
typical_dosage: 20 mg by mouth once daily at the same time each night, 1 hour before bedtime.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every night, about 1 hour before bed, without food (avoid taking after a high-fat meal).
Take consistently every night, even on nights with less structured schedules, for the best effect.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine (rare)
New or worsening depression or unusual thoughts/behavior
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not combine with melatonin supplements - additive/overlapping effect with no added benefit.
Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or other CNS depressants.
Fluvoxamine and other strong CYP1A2 inhibitors significantly raise tasimelteon levels - avoid combination.
Smoking can reduce tasimelteon levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your prescriber for jaundice, dark urine, or new mood changes.
Avoid driving or hazardous activities until you know how this medicine affects you the next morning.
self_monitoring: Keep a sleep diary to track response; keep scheduled liver function tests if recommended.
missed_dose_instructions: Only take this medicine if you are about to go to bed for the night; if bedtime has passed, skip the dose and resume the next night at the regular time.

description: An oral targeted therapy for certain epithelioid sarcomas and follicular lymphomas with an EZH2 gene mutation.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, night sweats, unexplained bruising/bleeding, or swollen lymph nodes (rare risk of secondary blood cancers, including T-cell lymphoma and myelodysplastic syndrome/leukemia)
New or worsening cough, shortness of breath (rare lung inflammation)
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) can raise tazemetostat levels and increase toxicity risk.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce effectiveness - avoid.
May reduce effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives - use a backup method.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for unusual bruising/bleeding, fever, or new lymph node swelling.
Seek emergency care for severe breathing difficulty or allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled blood counts and monitoring visits.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time; do not double up.

generic_name: Tetanus and diphtheria toxoids adsorbed vaccine (Td)
description: Protects adolescents and adults against tetanus (lockjaw) and diphtheria, typically given as a booster every 10 years or after a wound.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or other healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: A single booster dose, repeated approximately every 10 years, or sooner after a significant wound if more than 5 years since the last dose.
typical_duration: Booster given as a single dose; repeat per the recommended schedule.
directions_for_use: Tell your provider about the date of your last tetanus-containing vaccine.
Keep a record of your vaccination for future reference.
storage_instructions: Refrigerated at the pharmacy/clinic (2-8°C); do not freeze; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component
History of encephalopathy within 7 days of a prior pertussis-containing vaccine (relevant if considering Tdap instead)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, trouble breathing - seek emergency care immediately
Severe pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site that worsens
otc_and_other_interactions: Immunosuppressant drugs (e.g., prednisone, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, methotrexate) may reduce the immune response but do not prevent vaccination - discuss timing with your provider.
OTC acetaminophen or ibuprofen can be used for injection-site soreness or fever if approved by your provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Call your provider for a severe or worsening injection site reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep track of your vaccination date for future booster planning.
missed_dose_instructions: If a booster is overdue, get it as soon as possible - there is no need to restart any series.

description: An oral targeted therapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with a MET exon 14 skipping alteration.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take once daily with food, at a consistent time.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (risk of serious lung inflammation/pneumonitis)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Significant swelling of the face, limbs, or elsewhere
otc_and_other_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) can raise tepotinib levels and increase toxicity risk.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce effectiveness - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your oncology team promptly for new cough, shortness of breath, or fever.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe swelling or breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled liver function tests and monitoring visits.
Report new swelling or breathing changes right away.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time with food; do not double up.

description: Reduces relapses in relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis by modulating the immune system.
typical_dosage: 7-14 mg by mouth once daily, set by your neurologist.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Effective contraception is required during treatment and for a period after stopping, for both men and women, due to birth defect risk - discuss with your prescriber.
A medicine (accelerated elimination procedure) may be needed to clear this drug from your body quickly if needed - discuss with your neurologist.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy or women/men not using effective contraception
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue - liver enzymes are monitored closely
Signs of infection: fever, chills, cough (immune-modulating effect increases infection risk)
Numbness, tingling, or weakness in hands/feet (possible peripheral neuropathy)
Signs of severe skin reaction: widespread rash, blistering, fever
Significant increase in blood pressure
otc_and_other_interactions: May increase warfarin's blood-thinning effect - INR monitoring recommended.
Increases risk of liver toxicity when combined with other hepatotoxic drugs, including methotrexate - avoid combining unless closely supervised by your neurologist.
Live vaccines should be avoided while on this medicine.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your neurologist promptly for jaundice, numbness/tingling, or signs of infection.
Seek emergency care for a severe skin reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled liver function tests and blood pressure checks.
Report new numbness, tingling, or weakness right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: Builds new bone and reduces fracture risk in people with severe osteoporosis at high risk of fracture.
typical_dosage: 20 mcg injected under the skin once daily.
typical_duration: Treatment is generally limited to a maximum of 2 years over a patient's lifetime, per your prescriber's guidance.
directions_for_use: Inject into the thigh or abdomen at about the same time each day; rotate injection sites.
Give the first few injections while sitting or lying down in case of dizziness.
Take calcium and vitamin D supplements as recommended by your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate at all times, including between uses; do not freeze. Discard the pen after 28 days from first use even if medicine remains.
contraindications: Increased baseline risk of osteosarcoma (e.g., Paget's disease of bone, prior radiation involving the skeleton, open epiphyses, unexplained elevated alkaline phosphatase)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Dizziness or fainting shortly after injection (transient low blood pressure)
Signs of high calcium: nausea, constipation, confusion, excessive thirst/urination
New unexplained bone pain (rare osteosarcoma risk seen in animal studies)
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid additional over-the-counter calcium or vitamin D supplements beyond what your prescriber recommends - risk of hypercalcemia.
Digoxin toxicity risk may be increased if high calcium develops - report palpitations if you take digoxin.
action_if_adverse_effects: Sit or lie down if dizzy after an injection; call your prescriber if fainting occurs.
Call your prescriber for symptoms of high calcium or new bone pain.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled bone density (DEXA) scans and calcium level checks.
Report new bone pain right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and resume your normal once-daily schedule the next day - do not double up.

description: Reduces chorea (involuntary movements) associated with Huntington's disease.
typical_dosage: individualized, started low and titrated slowly by your neurologist based on response and side effects.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with food, at consistent times as directed.
Do not stop suddenly without talking to your neurologist.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Untreated or inadequately treated depression, or actively suicidal (boxed warning for depression and suicidality in Huntington's disease patients)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening depression, agitation, or thoughts of self-harm - seek help immediately (boxed warning)
Fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, sweating (possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome-like reaction) - seek emergency care immediately
Irregular heartbeat or fainting (QT prolongation)
Difficulty swallowing or worsening balance/falls
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with sertraline or escitalopram can increase serotonin-related and QT-prolongation risks - monitor closely.
Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (azithromycin, clarithromycin, ondansetron) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for thoughts of self-harm, fainting, or fever with muscle stiffness.
Call your neurologist for worsening mood, swallowing difficulty, or new falls.
self_monitoring: Track mood changes and report them right away.
Keep scheduled ECGs if directed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: Treats multiple myeloma (with other medicines) and a serious skin complication of leprosy (erythema nodosum leprosum).
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your specialist - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Duration set by your treatment protocol.
directions_for_use: Take at bedtime, at least 1 hour after the evening meal, as directed.

This medicine is only available through a restricted distribution program (REMS) due to severe birth defect risk - both male and female patients must follow strict contraception and monitoring requirements.
Never share this medicine with anyone else.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture; keep in original blister packaging, out of reach of others.
contraindications: Pregnancy (severe, life-threatening birth defects - boxed warning)
Women who could become pregnant unless enrolled in and fully compliant with the REMS program
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath (boxed warning for significant risk of DVT/PE)
Numbness, tingling, or pain in hands/feet (peripheral neuropathy) - may be irreversible if not caught early
Severe dizziness or fainting on standing
Signs of severe allergic/skin reaction: widespread rash, blistering, fever
Signs of low white blood cells: fever, frequent infections
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases blood clot risk; combining with estrogen-containing contraceptives further raises this risk - non-hormonal or specific approved contraception is required per REMS.
Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen.
Your specialist may prescribe a blood thinner (such as low-dose aspirin or another anticoagulant) alongside thalidomide to reduce clot risk - follow their instructions exactly.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting.
Call your specialist promptly for numbness/tingling in hands or feet.
self_monitoring: Keep all REMS program requirements, including pregnancy tests if applicable.
Report new tingling or numbness right away.
Keep scheduled blood counts.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and resume your normal bedtime schedule the next night - do not double up. Contact your specialist about missed doses.

description: Treats schizophrenia in patients who have not responded to other antipsychotic treatments, used at the lowest effective dose due to significant heart rhythm risk.
typical_dosage: individualized, started low and titrated by your prescriber based on response and ECG monitoring.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy only after other options have failed, with ongoing ECG monitoring.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food.
Do not stop suddenly without talking to your prescriber.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Known reduced CYP2D6 activity (poor metabolizers) - boxed warning
Concurrent use with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors or other drugs that prolong QT interval - boxed warning for dangerous/fatal heart rhythms
Severe CNS depression or comatose states
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, fainting, palpitations - seek emergency care immediately (boxed warning for QT prolongation and sudden death)
Fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, sweating (neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care immediately
Uncontrollable muscle movements (tardive dyskinesia)
Vision changes (rare pigmentary retinopathy with high doses)
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with other QT-prolonging drugs, including azithromycin and clarithromycin - risk of fatal heart rhythms.
Combining with ondansetron significantly increases QT prolongation risk - avoid.
Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen.
Fluoxetine and other strong CYP2D6 inhibitors significantly raise thioridazine levels - contraindicated combination per labeling.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for irregular heartbeat, fainting, or fever with muscle stiffness.
Call your prescriber for new uncontrollable movements or vision changes.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled ECGs and eye exams.
Report new palpitations or fainting right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: Treats symptoms of schizophrenia by blocking dopamine activity in the brain.
typical_dosage: individualized, typically 5-30 mg by mouth daily in divided doses, titrated by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food.
Do not stop suddenly without talking to your prescriber.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Severe CNS depression or comatose states
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, sweating (neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - seek emergency care immediately
Uncontrollable muscle movements (tardive dyskinesia)
Irregular heartbeat, fainting
Signs of low white blood cells: fever, sore throat, frequent infections
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alprazolam, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen.
Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (azithromycin, clarithromycin, ondansetron) increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
May blunt the blood-pressure-lowering effect of some antihypertensives and add to dizziness with lisinopril, losartan, or amlodipine.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fever with muscle stiffness/confusion or fainting.
Call your prescriber for new uncontrollable movements.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood counts if directed.
Report new movements, palpitations, or fainting right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.

description: An add-on treatment for partial seizures in patients with epilepsy.
typical_dosage: individualized, started low and titrated by your neurologist, taken with food in divided doses.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce the risk of dizziness.
Do not stop suddenly - can increase seizure frequency; taper only under medical supervision.
Do not use for conditions other than epilepsy unless specifically directed (risk of seizures in patients without epilepsy).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Use in patients without epilepsy (increased risk of new seizures/status epilepticus)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening seizures, or a seizure that does not stop
Confusion, extreme drowsiness, or difficulty speaking
New or worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm
Signs of severe skin reaction: widespread rash, blistering, fever
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with alprazolam, diphenhydramine, tramadol, or hydrocodone/acetaminophen.
Strong CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors can affect tiagabine levels - discuss all medicines with your neurologist.
Avoid alcohol - increases sedation and seizure risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for a seizure that does not stop or for severe confusion.
Call your neurologist for mood changes or a skin reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep a seizure diary and report new or worsening seizures.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it. Do not double up.

description: An oral targeted therapy for certain acute myeloid leukemias and cholangiocarcinomas (bile duct cancer) with a susceptible IDH1 mutation.
typical_dosage: individualized, set by your oncology team - never change your dose or schedule without their guidance.
typical_duration: Continued as long as it is effective and tolerated, per your oncology team.
directions_for_use: Take once daily on an empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal), at a consistent time.
Swallow tablets whole with water.
Attend all scheduled monitoring visits, especially in the first months (differentiation syndrome and QT prolongation risks).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, cough, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain, or swelling (possible differentiation syndrome) - seek care immediately, this can be life-threatening
Irregular heartbeat, fainting, chest pain (boxed warning for QT prolongation)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin, clarithromycin, fluconazole) significantly increases risk of dangerous heart rhythms - avoid where possible.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, clarithromycin) raise ivosidenib levels and increase QT/toxicity risk.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce effectiveness - avoid.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency/urgent care for fever with breathing trouble, chest pain, or fainting.
Call your oncology team promptly for jaundice or any new fever.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled ECGs, electrolyte checks, and liver function tests.
Report new shortness of breath or rapid weight gain right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on the same day unless less than 12 hours remain before the next dose, then skip it - do not double up. Contact your oncology team if you vomit after a dose.

description: Protects against tick-borne encephalitis (TBE), a viral infection spread by tick bites in parts of Europe and Asia, typically given to travelers to endemic areas.
route: Intramuscular injection (administered by a pharmacist or other healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: A 3-dose primary series, with the first two doses typically 1-3 months apart and a third dose 5-12 months later; accelerated schedules are available for travelers with limited time before departure.
typical_duration: Series completed over several months to a year; booster doses may be recommended for ongoing exposure risk.
directions_for_use: Complete the full series on schedule, ideally starting well before travel to an endemic area.
Bring your vaccination record to each visit and to your travel medicine follow-up.
Continue standard tick-bite prevention (repellent, protective clothing, tick checks) even after vaccination.
storage_instructions: Refrigerated at the pharmacy/clinic (2-8°C); do not freeze; not for home storage.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose, egg protein, or vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, trouble breathing - seek emergency care immediately
High fever or neurologic symptoms after vaccination (rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: Immunosuppressant drugs (e.g., prednisone, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, methotrexate) may reduce the immune response - antibody testing may be recommended before travel.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Call your provider for high fever or unusual neurologic symptoms.
self_monitoring: Track which doses in the series you have received and plan timing around travel dates.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your travel medicine provider to reschedule as soon as possible - timing relative to travel is important for protection.

description: Treats chronic lung infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis, delivered directly to the lungs by inhalation.
dosage_forms: Inhalation powder capsules with handheld inhaler device (28 mg/capsule)
typical_dosage: Four capsules (112 mg) inhaled twice daily, in alternating 28-day cycles of 28 days on and 28 days off, as directed by your pulmonologist/CF specialist.
typical_duration: Used in repeating on/off cycles long-term as directed.
directions_for_use: Use the specific Podhaler device provided - do not swallow the capsules.
Take the two doses each day about 12 hours apart.
Use a bronchodilator before this medicine if part of your regular CF treatment routine, as directed.
Clean the inhaler device as instructed.
storage_instructions: Store capsules at room temperature in the original blister, protect from moisture; keep capsules in the blister until immediately before use.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to tobramycin or other aminoglycosides
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Significant hearing changes, ringing in the ears, or dizziness/balance problems (aminoglycosides can affect hearing/balance with prolonged use)
Decreased urination or swelling (rare kidney effects, more likely with prior kidney problems or other nephrotoxic drugs)
Coughing up blood, or significant new shortness of breath/wheezing after a dose
Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Systemic absorption is low, but combining with other drugs affecting hearing/kidney function should be discussed with your CF care team.
No significant common OTC drug interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call your CF care team promptly for hearing changes, decreased urination, or coughing up blood.
Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction or severe wheezing after a dose.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled hearing tests and kidney function checks if directed.
Track lung function and report worsening breathing.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular twice-daily schedule - do not double up.

description: Combination eye drop/ointment used short-term to treat bacterial eye infections with inflammation, such as after eye surgery.
typical_dosage: 1-2 drops in affected eye(s) every 4-6 hours, or apply ointment 1-3 times daily, as directed by prescriber; do not use longer than 2 weeks without re-evaluation.
typical_duration: Short-term (typically 1-2 weeks); requires follow-up eye exam if longer.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Shake suspension well before each use.
Tilt head back, pull down lower lid, instill drop, avoid touching tip to eye.
Wait 5-10 minutes between different eye medications.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; discard per label after opening (usually 28 days).
contraindications: Viral, fungal, or mycobacterial eye infections
Known hypersensitivity to aminoglycosides or corticosteroids
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, vision changes, or worsening redness - may indicate increased eye pressure or infection
Signs of allergic reaction: swelling, severe itching
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; avoid using other eye products at the same time without spacing doses by 5-10 minutes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact prescriber for worsening eye pain, vision changes, or signs of allergic reaction.
Do not continue beyond prescribed duration due to steroid-related eye pressure risk.
self_monitoring: Monitor for improvement within a few days; report no improvement or worsening symptoms.
If used more than 10 days, eye pressure should be checked by prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Use as soon as remembered; if close to next dose, skip the missed dose and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat metastatic breast cancer in postmenopausal women with estrogen-receptor-positive tumors.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; commonly 60 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, until disease progression or as directed by oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Keep all lab and imaging follow-up appointments.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture.
contraindications: QT-prolongation risk with certain heart conditions or electrolyte abnormalities
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Leg swelling/pain or sudden shortness of breath (blood clot)
Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, fainting (QT prolongation)
Vaginal bleeding, vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased bleeding risk when combined with warfarin - monitor INR closely.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications and correct low potassium/magnesium before use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or irregular heartbeat.
Report vaginal bleeding to prescriber promptly.
self_monitoring: Periodic eye exams (cataracts reported with long-term use).
Electrolyte and ECG monitoring if at risk for QT prolongation.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: A concentrated, long-acting basal insulin used once daily to control blood sugar in diabetes; U-300 concentration provides a flatter, longer-lasting profile than standard U-100 glargine and is not interchangeable unit-for-unit with it.
dosage_forms: Prefilled U-300 injector pen (SoloStar, Max SoloStar)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber based on blood sugar monitoring; injected once daily at the same time each day.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Inject subcutaneously into abdomen, thigh, or upper arm; rotate injection sites.
Do not mix with other insulins in the same syringe.
Dial the exact dose on the pen; discard needle after each use.
storage_instructions: Unopened pens: refrigerate. In-use pen: store at room temperature, use within the labeled in-use period (typically up to 6 weeks), do not refrigerate once in use, protect from direct heat/light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe low blood sugar: confusion, sweating, seizure, loss of consciousness - treat immediately and seek care
Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Alcohol can increase hypoglycemia risk.
NSAIDs and aspirin can enhance glucose-lowering effect; monitor blood sugar closely.
action_if_adverse_effects: Treat low blood sugar per sick-day/hypoglycemia plan; seek emergency care for severe or unresponsive episodes.
Contact prescriber if blood sugars are persistently high or low.
self_monitoring: Regular blood glucose checks as directed.
Periodic A1C testing.
Keep a hypoglycemia treatment source available at all times.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on the same day; do not double the next dose. Contact prescriber if unsure, since this is a basal insulin with a long duration of action.

description: Lowers blood pressure and helps protect the heart after a heart attack by relaxing blood vessels.
typical_dosage: 1-4 mg by mouth once daily, titrated to response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day, with or without food.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: History of angioedema with ACE inhibitors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Swelling of face/lips/tongue/throat or trouble breathing (angioedema) - emergency
Signs of high potassium: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid potassium supplements/salt substitutes unless directed.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can blunt blood-pressure-lowering effect and stress kidneys - prefer acetaminophen for pain.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for facial/throat swelling or breathing trouble.
Call prescriber for persistent cough or signs of high potassium.
self_monitoring: Home blood pressure checks.
Periodic kidney function and potassium labs.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used for depression that has not responded to other antidepressants; requires strict dietary and medication restrictions due to serious interaction risks.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically started low and titrated slowly.
typical_duration: Long-term, with periodic reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed; do not stop or change dose without prescriber guidance.
Avoid tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, cured meats, tap beer, soy sauce) - risk of hypertensive crisis.
Requires a 2-week washout when switching to/from most other antidepressants.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture.
contraindications: Use with other antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs), tramadol, or other MAOIs
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden severe headache, stiff neck, chest pain, or vomiting after eating tyramine foods (hypertensive crisis) - emergency
Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, fever, rapid heartbeat, muscle rigidity - emergency
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid all decongestants (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine) and cough/cold products containing dextromethorphan - risk of hypertensive crisis/serotonin syndrome.
Avoid St. John's Wort and other serotonergic supplements.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of hypertensive crisis or serotonin syndrome.
Do not take any new medication, herbal product, or OTC drug without checking with pharmacist/prescriber first.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure regularly.
Report mood changes or suicidal thoughts immediately.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Eye drop used once daily to lower elevated eye pressure in glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
typical_dosage: 1 drop in affected eye(s) once daily in the evening.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Instill 1 drop in affected eye(s) each evening.
Wait at least 5 minutes before using other eye drops.
Remove contact lenses before use; wait 15 minutes before reinserting.
storage_instructions: Store unopened bottle refrigerated or at room temperature per label; once opened, may be stored at room temperature and discarded after 6 weeks.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to travoprost or benzalkonium chloride
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain or vision changes
Signs of eye infection
common_side_effects: Gradual darkening of iris color and eyelash growth
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; avoid using other eye drops within 5 minutes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for persistent eye redness/irritation or vision changes.
self_monitoring: Periodic eye pressure checks with eye care provider.
Note any progressive change in eye/eyelash color.
missed_dose_instructions: Use as soon as remembered that day; if near the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double up.

description: Once-daily inhaler combining a steroid and two bronchodilators to control symptoms of COPD and, in some patients, asthma.
typical_dosage: 1 inhalation once daily, same time each day; not a rescue inhaler.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing maintenance therapy.
directions_for_use: Inhale once daily at the same time each day.
Rinse mouth with water (do not swallow) after each use to reduce thrush risk.
Not for acute symptom relief - use a rescue inhaler for sudden breathing problems.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep the inhaler cover closed when not in use; discard 6 weeks after opening the foil tray or when counter reads 0.
contraindications: Primary treatment of acute bronchospasm/status asthmaticus
Severe milk protein allergy (device contains lactose)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening breathing right after use (paradoxical bronchospasm) - seek care
Signs of pneumonia: fever, chills, worsening cough
Vision changes/eye pain (glaucoma), difficulty urinating (anticholinergic effect)
Fast/irregular heartbeat, chest pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Use caution with other anticholinergic OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine) - additive dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention.
MAOIs and tricyclic antidepressants can increase cardiovascular effects of the LABA component.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for worsening breathing, chest pain, or signs of infection.
Rinse mouth after each dose to reduce thrush; report white patches in mouth.
self_monitoring: Track symptom control and rescue inhaler use.
Report frequent rescue inhaler use to prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if almost time for next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not use two doses at once.

description: Removes excess copper from the body in patients with Wilson's disease who cannot tolerate penicillamine.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; typically divided into 2-4 doses per day on an empty stomach.
typical_duration: Long-term, lifelong therapy for Wilson's disease.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals, and separated from other drugs/supplements/minerals.
Do not open capsules; swallow whole.
Do not take iron supplements at the same time - separate by at least 2 hours.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; protect from heat and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of worsening neurological symptoms (tremor, difficulty speaking)
Signs of iron deficiency (fatigue, pallor)
Severe rash
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid taking with mineral supplements (iron, zinc, calcium) or antacids - reduces absorption.
Separate from other medications by at least 1 hour.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for new or worsening neurologic symptoms or severe rash.
Do not stop abruptly without medical guidance.
self_monitoring: Periodic copper and iron level labs.
Neurological symptom tracking.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered if still away from food; if a meal is due, skip and resume the empty-stomach schedule at the next dose. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat schizophrenia and short-term for severe anxiety not controlled by other treatments.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically 2-20 mg by mouth daily in divided doses.
typical_duration: Long-term for schizophrenia; short-term for anxiety.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as directed.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
Avoid prolonged sun exposure - use sunscreen (photosensitivity).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, muscle rigidity, confusion, irregular heartbeat (neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - emergency
Uncontrollable muscle movements of face/tongue (tardive dyskinesia)
Fainting, irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation)
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, or other sedating OTC sleep aids.
Avoid combining with other QT-prolonging medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or irregular heartbeat.
Report new abnormal movements to prescriber promptly.
self_monitoring: Periodic monitoring for abnormal movements.
Blood pressure and weight checks.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Eye drop used to treat herpes simplex viral infections of the eye (herpetic keratitis).
typical_dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye every 2 hours while awake (max 9 drops/day) until the eye surface heals, then reduced frequency; do not use for more than 21 days.
typical_duration: Short-term, until healing is confirmed by an eye care provider (generally up to 21 days).
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Instill drop into the affected eye as directed; avoid touching the tip to the eye.
Do not wear contact lenses during treatment.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; protect from light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening eye pain, redness, or vision changes
Signs of allergic reaction: eyelid swelling, severe irritation
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber if the eye is not improving in 7-14 days or worsens.
Seek care for severe pain or vision loss.
self_monitoring: Follow-up eye exams as scheduled to confirm healing.
Watch for signs the infection is not clearing.
missed_dose_instructions: Use as soon as remembered; resume the regular dosing interval. Do not double up.

description: Used to reduce tremor, stiffness, and muscle spasm in Parkinson's disease and drug-induced movement disorders.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically started at 1 mg/day and gradually titrated.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy, reassessed periodically.
directions_for_use: Take with food if stomach upset occurs.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
Stay well hydrated and avoid overheating - can reduce sweating.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain or vision changes (possible glaucoma)
Inability to urinate
Confusion, hallucinations, especially in older adults
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive anticholinergic effects (confusion, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention) with diphenhydramine and other sedating antihistamines.
Increased CNS depression with alcohol.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for eye pain, inability to urinate, or confusion/hallucinations.
Contact prescriber if constipation or dry mouth become severe.
self_monitoring: Watch for confusion, especially in older adults.
Monitor bowel and urinary function.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Combination extended-release tablet used with diet and exercise to improve blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically once daily with the evening meal.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, split, or chew.
Take with food to reduce GI upset.
Stay well hydrated; stop before procedures requiring contrast dye or surgery as directed by prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of ketoacidosis: nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, unusual fatigue, rapid breathing (can occur even with normal blood sugar) - seek emergency care
Signs of urinary tract or genital infection
Signs of dehydration/low blood pressure
Severe joint pain (DPP-4 inhibitors)
Signs of lactic acidosis: muscle pain, trouble breathing, unusual tiredness
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid excess alcohol - increases risk of lactic acidosis and low blood sugar.
NSAIDs may affect kidney function and increase metformin accumulation risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop and seek care for signs of ketoacidosis or lactic acidosis.
Contact prescriber for recurrent genital/urinary infections.
self_monitoring: Regular blood glucose monitoring.
Periodic kidney function and vitamin B12 levels.
Stay alert for dehydration, especially in hot weather or illness.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used in people with cystic fibrosis who have at least one F508del mutation (or other responsive mutation) to improve the function of the defective CFTR protein.

typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with fat-containing food.
Swallow tablets whole.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original blister pack.
contraindications: Not for use in patients without at least one responsive CFTR mutation
Severe liver impairment (dose adjustment or avoidance needed)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain, loss of appetite - seek care promptly
Rash
Vision changes (cataracts reported in children)
High blood pressure

Do not stop abruptly without medical guidance.

Periodic eye exams in children.
Blood pressure checks.
missed_dose_instructions: If within 6 hours of the scheduled dose, take it with fat-containing food; otherwise skip and take the next dose at its regular time. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat depression, sometimes with associated anxiety or sleep disturbance.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically 50-150 mg by mouth daily, often at bedtime.

directions_for_use: Take at bedtime if drowsiness occurs.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
Do not stop abruptly - taper as directed by prescriber.

contraindications: Use with or within 14 days of an MAOI
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, chest pain, fainting
Signs of serotonin syndrome (with other serotonergic drugs): agitation, fever, tremor
Suicidal thoughts, especially early in treatment or in young adults
Seizures
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation and anticholinergic effects with diphenhydramine.
Combining with tramadol increases seizure and serotonin syndrome risk.
Avoid alcohol - increases sedation.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for irregular heartbeat, seizures, or signs of serotonin syndrome.
Report any worsening mood or suicidal thoughts immediately.
self_monitoring: Monitor mood and report suicidal thoughts.
Periodic ECG if cardiac risk factors present.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used in combination with fulvestrant to treat certain types of hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer with specific gene alterations.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically taken on a 4-days-on/3-days-off cycle.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per oncologist.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food at approximately the same times each day.
Follow the specific on/off treatment schedule exactly as prescribed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high blood sugar: excessive thirst/urination, confusion
Severe diarrhea or dehydration
New or worsening skin rash
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - can alter drug levels.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers can significantly change drug exposure - report all new medications to your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact oncology team promptly for severe diarrhea, rash, or high blood sugar symptoms.
Do not adjust dose or schedule without guidance.
self_monitoring: Regular blood glucose checks.
Report new rash or diarrhea promptly.
Keep all oncology follow-up visits and labs.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than a few hours, skip it and resume the normal schedule at the next scheduled time - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: Used in combination with other therapies to treat HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, including cases with brain metastases.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically taken twice daily, about 12 hours apart.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food at consistent times, about 12 hours apart.
Swallow tablets whole.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain
Severe diarrhea leading to dehydration
Signs of infection
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels significantly.
Report all new medications to your oncology team due to numerous drug interactions.
action_if_adverse_effects: Start antidiarrheal treatment as directed and contact oncology team for severe or persistent diarrhea.
Seek care for signs of liver injury.
self_monitoring: Periodic liver function tests.
Track bowel movements/diarrhea.
Keep oncology follow-up appointments.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up. Vomited doses are not replaced.

description: Used to treat symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) that cannot be treated with surgery; available only through a restricted REMS program due to liver injury risk.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; typically twice daily on an empty stomach.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, with regular liver monitoring.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal).
Enrollment in the manufacturer's REMS program is required.
Avoid grapefruit products.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serious liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, abdominal pain - seek care immediately
Hair color changes
Eye/vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit juice and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels.
Avoid other medications known to cause liver injury unless approved by your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for signs of liver injury.
Report any new symptoms to your oncology team promptly.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function blood tests as required by the REMS program.
Track for jaundice or unusual fatigue.
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time on an empty stomach - do not double up.

generic_name: Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B vaccine (combined)
description: Combination vaccine that helps protect against both hepatitis A and hepatitis B infection.
typical_dosage: A 3-dose series (0, 1, 6 months) or accelerated schedule, as recommended by your immunization provider.
typical_duration: Completed vaccination series.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider or pharmacist in the upper arm.
Complete the full series for adequate protection.
storage_instructions: Refrigerated storage handled by the administering pharmacy/clinic; do not freeze.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component (including yeast)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing
High fever
Fainting shortly after injection
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for injection-site discomfort or fever as directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact provider for high or persistent fever.
self_monitoring: Wait for observation as directed after injection.
Track doses completed in the series.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is delayed, contact your pharmacy/provider to resume the series as soon as possible - it generally does not need to be restarted.

description: Taken with certain HIV protease inhibitors (such as atazanavir or darunavir) to increase and prolong their blood levels; has no antiviral activity on its own.
typical_dosage: 150 mg by mouth once daily, taken with food at the same time as the boosted HIV medication.
typical_duration: Long-term, taken continuously as part of an HIV treatment regimen.
directions_for_use: Take with food, at the same time each day as the boosted medication.
Do not stop or change without prescriber guidance - can affect levels of other HIV medications.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Use with many drugs metabolized by CYP3A (e.g., certain statins, sedatives, ergot derivatives) due to serious interaction risk - review full medication list with prescriber/pharmacist
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
Signs of a serious drug interaction: unusual muscle pain, extreme sedation, irregular heartbeat
common_side_effects: Jaundice-like yellowing of eyes (benign, from bilirubin change)
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with simvastatin and lovastatin - risk of severe muscle toxicity.
Can significantly increase levels of sildenafil, alprazolam, and many other drugs - always check before starting any new OTC or prescription medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber before starting any new medication, supplement, or OTC product.
Seek care for signs of kidney problems or severe interaction symptoms.
self_monitoring: Periodic kidney function tests.
Report all medication changes to your HIV care team.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food, along with the boosted medication; if close to the next dose, skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: A biologic used to reduce inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis and other inflammatory conditions by blocking IL-6 signaling; suppresses the immune system.
dosage_forms: Solution for IV infusion (administered in clinic)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; subcutaneous injections are typically given every 1-2 weeks.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for chronic inflammatory conditions.
directions_for_use: If self-injecting, rotate injection sites (thigh or abdomen) and let the syringe warm to room temperature before use.
Do not inject into bruised, red, or hard skin.
Keep all lab monitoring appointments.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze; protect from light; do not shake.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, persistent cough, wound that won't heal - seek care promptly
Signs of bowel perforation: severe abdominal pain, fever
Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: May reduce effectiveness of live vaccines - avoid live vaccines while on therapy.
Can alter the metabolism of drugs processed by the liver (e.g., statins) as inflammation improves - report all medications to your care team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for signs of infection, severe abdominal pain, or liver injury.
Report any new infection to your prescriber before your next dose.
self_monitoring: Regular labs: complete blood count, liver enzymes, cholesterol.
Watch for early signs of infection, which may be blunted by this medication.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber's office if a dose is missed to reschedule - do not double up or self-adjust the schedule.

description: A self-injectable bone-building medication used to treat osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and men at high risk of fracture.
typical_dosage: 80 mcg subcutaneously once daily, into the periumbilical area of the abdomen.
typical_duration: Limited to a maximum of 2 years of lifetime use (per product labeling), followed by an antiresorptive agent.
directions_for_use: Inject once daily into the abdomen, rotating injection sites.
The first few doses should be given while seated or lying down due to risk of orthostatic hypotension/dizziness.
Dispose of used pens in a sharps container.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze. May be stored at room temperature for limited time per pen instructions once in use.
contraindications: Increased baseline risk of osteosarcoma (e.g., Paget's disease of bone, prior skeletal radiation)
Pediatric patients or those with open epiphyses
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Dizziness or fainting, especially after the first few doses
Signs of high calcium: nausea, constipation, confusion
Rapid heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; use caution with calcium/vitamin D supplements - follow prescriber's recommended intake to avoid high calcium levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Sit or lie down if dizzy after injection.
Contact prescriber for symptoms of high calcium or persistent dizziness.
self_monitoring: Periodic calcium level checks.
Bone density monitoring as scheduled.
Track total lifetime duration of use (2-year maximum).
missed_dose_instructions: Skip the missed dose and resume with the next scheduled daily injection. Do not double up.

description: Vaccine that helps protect against typhoid fever, typically given before travel to areas where typhoid is common.
typical_dosage: A single 0.5 mL injection at least 2 weeks before potential exposure; a booster is recommended every 2 years with continued/repeated exposure.
typical_duration: Single dose with booster every 2 years if ongoing risk continues.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider or pharmacist in the upper arm.
Complete vaccination at least 2 weeks before travel for full protection.
storage_instructions: Refrigerated storage handled by the administering pharmacy/clinic; do not freeze.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
High fever
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen may be used for injection-site discomfort or fever as directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact provider for high or persistent fever.
self_monitoring: Wait for observation as directed after injection.
Note the date for booster timing if travel risk continues.
missed_dose_instructions: If the booster is delayed, get it as soon as possible before further exposure; contact your travel clinic/pharmacy with questions.

drug_class: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor agonist (ophthalmic/nasal, for dry eye)
description: A nasal spray used to increase natural tear production in patients with dry eye disease; distinct from oral varenicline used for smoking cessation.
typical_dosage: 1 spray in each nostril twice daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use for chronic dry eye disease.
directions_for_use: Prime the spray before first use per package instructions.
Tilt head slightly forward and spray once into each nostril.
Do not spray into the eyes.
storage_instructions: Store upright at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe or persistent nosebleeds
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; distinct from oral varenicline (Chantix) - do not confuse dosing or indications with the smoking-cessation product.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for persistent nosebleeds or severe throat/nasal irritation.
self_monitoring: Track improvement in dry eye symptoms.
Report any worsening nasal symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Use as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular twice-daily schedule.

drug_class: PARP inhibitor/androgen synthesis inhibitor combination (oral oncology)
description: Combination tablet used with prednisone to treat certain types of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with BRCA gene alterations.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; taken once daily, typically on an empty stomach, together with prednisone.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day as directed (fasting state typically required for the abiraterone component).
Take prednisone as co-prescribed - do not stop prednisone abruptly.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Pregnancy (can cause fetal harm; not indicated in women but partners should use contraception)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain
Signs of high blood pressure or fluid retention: severe headache, swelling, rapid weight gain
Signs of low blood counts: unusual bruising/bleeding, fatigue, infection
Signs of low adrenal function if prednisone is stopped abruptly: severe weakness, dizziness
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels.
NSAIDs may increase fluid retention/blood pressure effects; use acetaminophen preferentially unless approved otherwise.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact oncology team promptly for signs of liver injury, severe hypertension, or low blood counts.
Never stop the co-administered prednisone abruptly without guidance.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests, blood pressure checks, and complete blood counts as scheduled.
Report swelling or rapid weight gain.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and resume the normal schedule at the next scheduled time - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions.

description: Used to dissolve certain gallstones without surgery or to treat primary biliary cholangitis by improving bile flow.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber based on body weight and indication; typically taken in divided doses with food.
typical_duration: Long-term for primary biliary cholangitis; up to 24 months for gallstone dissolution with periodic imaging to assess response.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Take consistently as prescribed - missed doses reduce effectiveness for gallstone dissolution.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Calcified gallstones or radiopaque stones (for gallstone dissolution indication)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Right upper abdominal pain or biliary colic
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Aluminum-based antacids and cholestyramine can reduce absorption - separate dosing by several hours.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for worsening abdominal pain or signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Periodic liver function tests and imaging (ultrasound) as directed to assess gallstone response.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: A topical gel chemotherapy used to treat skin lesions of early-stage cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides).
typical_dosage: Apply a thin film once daily to affected skin areas as directed by oncology/dermatology team; avoid unaffected skin.
typical_duration: Long-term application as directed, with periodic skin assessment.
directions_for_use: Wear disposable nitrile gloves to apply; wash hands after removing gloves.
Allow gel to dry fully before covering with clothing.
Avoid contact with eyes, mucous membranes, and unaffected skin; wash unintended contact areas immediately with water.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; discard tube 90 days after opening even if product remains.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe skin irritation, blistering, or ulceration
Signs of allergic contact dermatitis
Accidental eye exposure - flush and seek care immediately
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid applying other topical products to treated skin unless approved by prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for severe skin reactions, blistering, or accidental eye/mucous membrane exposure.
Report worsening or spreading skin irritation.
self_monitoring: Regular skin exams by dermatology/oncology team.
Photograph and track lesion changes if instructed.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered that day; if it is almost time for the next application, skip the missed dose. Do not apply extra to make up.

description: Used to treat and prevent cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection, particularly in transplant recipients and people with weakened immune systems.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist based on kidney function and indication; typically once or twice daily with food.
typical_duration: Varies by indication - from several weeks (treatment) to months (prevention post-transplant).
directions_for_use: Take with food.
Swallow tablets whole - do not crush or break (hazardous drug); caregivers should avoid direct contact with crushed tablets or the oral solution and use gloves if handling.
Use precise dosing device for oral solution.
storage_instructions: Store tablets at room temperature; oral solution should be refrigerated and discarded after the labeled use period.
contraindications: Severe neutropenia, anemia, or thrombocytopenia at baseline (caution/dose adjustment)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood counts: unusual bleeding/bruising, fever, infection, severe fatigue
Seizures
Decreased urination (kidney effects)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other bone-marrow-suppressing medications unless directed by specialist, due to additive risk of low blood counts.
NSAIDs may increase risk of kidney effects when combined.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for signs of low blood counts, seizures, or decreased urination.
Keep all scheduled lab appointments.
self_monitoring: Frequent complete blood counts, especially early in treatment.
Kidney function monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: A nasal spray used as needed ('rescue therapy') to stop prolonged or repetitive seizure clusters in patients with epilepsy; distinct from oral/rectal diazepam formulations.
dosage_forms: Nasal spray (5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg, 20 mg single-use devices)
typical_dosage: Individualized dose (5-20 mg) set by prescriber based on age/weight; a second dose may be given after 4-12 hours only if directed by the seizure action plan. Do not use more than 2 doses per episode or more than one episode every 5 days without contacting a prescriber.
typical_duration: Used as needed per seizure action plan; not for daily/scheduled use.
directions_for_use: Use only for seizure clusters as described in the patient's seizure action plan.
Spray into one nostril; the device requires no priming.
Caregivers should be trained in advance on when and how to use it, and should call for emergency help if seizures continue as instructed in the action plan.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original packaging until ready to use.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Slowed or difficulty breathing - seek emergency care
Seizure that does not stop after the second dose, or a new type of seizure - call emergency services
Excessive sedation or unresponsiveness
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation and respiratory depression risk with diphenhydramine, alcohol, opioids (e.g., hydrocodone/acetaminophen, tramadol), and other sedatives.
Avoid combining with other benzodiazepines unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call emergency services if breathing becomes slow/shallow or the patient does not wake up.
Follow the individualized seizure action plan; contact the prescriber after each use.
self_monitoring: Track number of doses/episodes used per month.
Confirm caregivers are current on training for administration.
missed_dose_instructions: This is an as-needed rescue medication, not a scheduled daily dose - use only when a seizure cluster occurs, per the seizure action plan.

description: A higher-dose combination birth control pill (norethindrone 1 mg/mestranol 50 mcg) used to prevent pregnancy and regulate menstrual cycles.
typical_dosage: 1 tablet by mouth daily at the same time each day, following the 21- or 28-day pack sequence.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as long as contraception/cycle control is desired.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day, with or without food.
Use backup contraception (e.g., condoms) for the first 7 days when starting.
Follow pack sequence exactly; placebo/reminder pills (if 28-day pack) still count in the sequence.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: History of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Leg pain/swelling or sudden shortness of breath (blood clot)
Chest pain, sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness on one side (stroke/heart attack)
Severe abdominal pain, jaundice
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception.
Certain antibiotics and antifungals may reduce effectiveness; discuss with pharmacist when starting new medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, stroke, or heart attack.
Contact prescriber for severe abdominal pain or jaundice.
self_monitoring: Track cycle regularity and any missed pills.
Report new severe headaches or leg swelling.
missed_dose_instructions: If one pill is missed, take it as soon as remembered and take the next pill at the regular time (may mean taking two in one day); if two or more are missed, follow package instructions and use backup contraception. Consider emergency contraception if pills were missed around unprotected intercourse.

description: Used in combination with chemotherapy, and as maintenance therapy, for FLT3-ITD-positive acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically once daily, with ECG monitoring due to QT-prolongation risk.
typical_duration: Per oncology treatment protocol, including induction, consolidation, and maintenance phases.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day as directed.
Requires baseline and periodic ECG monitoring and electrolyte correction (potassium, magnesium) before and during treatment.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers without dose adjustment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, fainting, dizziness (QT prolongation/Torsades de Pointes) - emergency
Signs of infection or low blood counts
Signs of differentiation syndrome: fever, difficulty breathing, rapid weight gain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid other QT-prolonging medications.
Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels significantly.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for irregular heartbeat or fainting.
Report fever or breathing difficulty to oncology team immediately.
self_monitoring: Regular ECGs and electrolyte panels as scheduled.
Frequent complete blood counts.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team for guidance on any missed dose - do not double up without instruction.

description: Vaccine that helps protect against chickenpox (varicella) infection.
typical_dosage: A 2-dose series, as recommended by your immunization provider (typically ages 1 and 4-6 for children; 2 doses 4-8 weeks apart for eligible adults).
typical_duration: Completed 2-dose series.
directions_for_use: Administered by a healthcare provider or pharmacist.
As a live vaccine, avoid pregnancy for 1 month after vaccination and avoid close contact with severely immunocompromised individuals if a rash develops.
storage_instructions: Frozen/refrigerated storage handled by the administering pharmacy/clinic; protect from light.
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component (including gelatin/neomycin)
Recent blood product/immune globulin administration (timing restrictions apply)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
High fever
Widespread rash
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid aspirin/salicylates for 6 weeks after vaccination due to a theoretical risk of Reye's syndrome.
Acetaminophen may be used for fever/discomfort as directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact provider for high fever or widespread rash.
self_monitoring: Wait for observation as directed after injection.
Schedule the second dose per recommended timing.
missed_dose_instructions: If the second dose is delayed, get it as soon as possible - the series does not need to be restarted.

description: A single-dose oral vaccine that helps protect travelers against cholera caused by Vibrio cholerae serogroup O1.
typical_dosage: A single oral dose, taken at least 10 days before potential exposure/travel.
typical_duration: Single dose; protection duration and need for boosters should be discussed with a travel medicine provider.
directions_for_use: Do not eat or drink for 60 minutes before and after dosing.
Prepared and administered by a healthcare provider or pharmacist.
Complete at least 10 days before travel to an area with cholera risk.
storage_instructions: Frozen storage handled by the administering pharmacy/clinic prior to reconstitution.
contraindications: Chronic GI conditions in some cases (discuss with provider)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction
Severe diarrhea or vomiting
High fever
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid antibiotics for at least 14 days before dosing, as they can reduce vaccine effectiveness by killing the live vaccine strain.
Avoid taking within 10 days of antimalarial medications when possible - discuss timing with travel provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for severe or persistent GI symptoms or high fever.
Report any signs of allergic reaction promptly.
self_monitoring: Confirm at least 10 days between vaccination and travel departure.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a single-dose vaccine; contact your travel clinic if the dose was not completed as directed before travel.

drug_class: Nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (antiviral, for hepatitis B)
description: Used to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adults with compensated liver disease.
typical_dosage: 25 mg by mouth once daily with food.
typical_duration: Long-term; stopping treatment can cause severe flares of hepatitis B and requires close monitoring.
directions_for_use: Take with food at the same time each day.
Do not stop without prescriber guidance - abrupt discontinuation can cause serious liver flares.
Get tested for HIV before starting, as this drug alone is not a complete HIV treatment.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original container; keep the desiccant in the bottle.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe worsening of hepatitis after stopping the medication - seek care immediately if stopping
Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, severe fatigue
Signs of kidney problems
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid St. John's Wort - can reduce drug levels and effectiveness.
Discuss all new medications with prescriber, as this drug is often combined with HIV therapy considerations.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber immediately before stopping this medication for any reason.
Seek care for signs of lactic acidosis or worsening liver disease.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests and hepatitis B viral load monitoring.
Kidney function monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up. Do not run out of medication without a refill plan, as stopping can cause a serious hepatitis flare.

description: Used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML), often in combination with other therapies; dose is gradually increased (ramp-up) to reduce tumor lysis syndrome risk.
dosage_forms: Tablet (dose titration 'Starting Pack' and maintenance strengths)
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; started at a low dose and increased weekly over 4-5 weeks (ramp-up schedule) to the target maintenance dose.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per oncology protocol.
directions_for_use: Take with a meal and water at the same time each day.
Follow the exact ramp-up schedule provided - do not skip titration steps.
Drink plenty of fluids, especially during the ramp-up phase, to reduce tumor lysis syndrome risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors during initiation/ramp-up (tumor lysis syndrome risk)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of tumor lysis syndrome: nausea, vomiting, confusion, decreased urination, irregular heartbeat, muscle cramps - seek emergency care especially during the first weeks of treatment
Signs of infection or low blood counts
Signs of severe allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - significantly alter drug levels.

Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, clarithromycin) can dangerously increase levels, especially during dose ramp-up - report all medications to your oncology team before starting anything new.
