action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of tumor lysis syndrome (especially during ramp-up).
Report fever or signs of infection promptly.
self_monitoring: Frequent blood chemistry and blood count checks, especially during dose ramp-up.
Stay well hydrated as instructed.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than 8 hours, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up. Contact your oncology team with questions, especially during the ramp-up phase.

description: A non-hormonal oral medication used to treat moderate-to-severe hot flashes (vasomotor symptoms) associated with menopause.
typical_dosage: 45 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term as needed for symptom control; liver function should be checked periodically.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not take with certain CYP1A2 inhibitor medications - review your full medication list with your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known cirrhosis or severe kidney impairment
Concurrent use with strong or moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g., certain antidepressants, some antibiotics)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, right upper abdominal pain, unusual fatigue - seek care promptly
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid excessive caffeine intake, as fezolinetant can increase caffeine levels/effects.
Discuss all new medications with your pharmacist due to liver enzyme interactions.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber promptly for signs of liver injury.
Report severe or worsening abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Baseline and periodic liver function blood tests.
Track hot flash frequency/severity for symptom response.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used with other heart failure medications to reduce the risk of hospitalization and cardiovascular death in adults with symptomatic chronic heart failure and reduced ejection fraction.
typical_dosage: Started at 2.5 mg once daily with food and doubled approximately every 2 weeks as tolerated, up to a target of 10 mg once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with food at the same time each day.
Swallow tablets whole.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness, especially when starting or increasing dose.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Concurrent use with other soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators or PDE5 inhibitors (e.g., sildenafil, tadalafil) - risk of severe low blood pressure
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Symptoms of low blood pressure: dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting - seek care if severe or persistent
Signs of anemia: unusual fatigue, pale skin
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not combine with sildenafil or other PDE5 inhibitors - risk of severe hypotension.
Avoid nitrates unless specifically directed by prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Sit or lie down and contact prescriber for significant dizziness/lightheadedness.
Seek emergency care for fainting.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure, especially during dose increases.
Periodic blood counts.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used, often with hormone therapy, to treat hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly taken twice daily, continuously (no rest period between cycles for this agent).
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole.
Report diarrhea promptly - early treatment with antidiarrheal medication may be needed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe diarrhea leading to dehydration
Signs of blood clots (leg swelling/pain, sudden shortness of breath)
Signs of infection/low blood counts
Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Signs of lung inflammation: new or worsening cough, shortness of breath
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - significantly alter drug levels.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, clarithromycin) can markedly increase levels and toxicity - report all new medications to oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Start antidiarrheal treatment as directed for diarrhea and notify oncology team.
Seek care for signs of blood clot, infection, or liver injury.
self_monitoring: Regular complete blood counts and liver function tests.
Track bowel movements for diarrhea management.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed or vomited, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: Used to treat infantile spasms and, as add-on therapy, refractory complex partial seizures; available only through a restricted REMS program due to permanent vision loss risk.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist based on weight/indication; typically given in divided doses twice daily.
typical_duration: Long-term for refractory epilepsy; individualized short course for infantile spasms, reassessed regularly for vision risk versus benefit.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed, with or without food.
Enrollment in the manufacturer's REMS program (with regular vision testing) is required.
Do not stop abruptly - taper as directed to avoid seizure worsening.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Vision changes or loss of peripheral vision - report immediately (may be permanent even after stopping)
Suicidal thoughts or behavior
Signs of severe drowsiness or coordination problems (MRI changes reported in infants)
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, and other CNS depressants.
No major metabolic (CYP) interactions, but review all medications with prescriber given seizure-medication complexity.
action_if_adverse_effects: Report any vision changes to prescriber and ophthalmologist immediately.
Seek care for mood changes or suicidal thoughts.
self_monitoring: Regular vision field testing per REMS program (baseline, every 3 months during treatment, and after stopping).
Monitor mood and behavior.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up. Missing doses can increase seizure risk - contact prescriber if doses are frequently missed.

description: An older oral antiretroviral used as part of combination therapy to treat HIV infection; largely replaced by newer agents but may still appear on some formularies.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your HIV specialist; taken with food as part of a combination antiretroviral regimen.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of HIV treatment.
directions_for_use: Take with food to improve absorption.
Take every dose of every HIV medication as prescribed - missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
Do not stop or change without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture.
contraindications: Use with numerous drugs metabolized by CYP3A4 (e.g., certain statins, sedatives, ergot derivatives) - review full medication list with prescriber/pharmacist
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Signs of high blood sugar
Severe or persistent diarrhea
otc_and_other_interactions: Contraindicated with simvastatin and lovastatin - risk of severe muscle toxicity.
Numerous interactions with other medications; always check with pharmacist before starting anything new, including OTC and herbal products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber before starting any new medication or supplement.
Seek care for signs of liver problems or severe diarrhea.
self_monitoring: Regular HIV viral load and CD4 count monitoring.
Periodic blood glucose and liver function tests.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, take the missed dose anyway and continue the regular schedule - do not skip HIV medication doses without discussing with your prescriber, as missed doses risk resistance.

description: Used alone for chronic hepatitis B, or as part of combination therapy for HIV infection.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; commonly 300 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term; stopping treatment for hepatitis B can cause severe flares and requires close monitoring.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop without prescriber guidance, particularly for hepatitis B.
Get tested for HIV before starting if being used for hepatitis B alone.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original container; keep the desiccant in the bottle.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe worsening of hepatitis after stopping - seek care immediately if stopping
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling
Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, severe fatigue
Bone pain (long-term bone density loss)
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs may increase risk of kidney problems when combined.
Avoid St. John's Wort - can reduce drug levels.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber immediately before stopping this medication for any reason.
Seek care for signs of kidney problems or lactic acidosis.
self_monitoring: Regular kidney function tests.
Periodic bone density monitoring with long-term use.
Hepatitis B viral load or HIV viral load monitoring as applicable.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up. Do not run out of medication, as stopping can cause a serious hepatitis flare if used for hepatitis B.

description: Used to treat solid tumors of any type that carry an NTRK gene fusion, in patients without a satisfactory alternative treatment.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically taken twice daily, with or without food.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at consistent times about 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Swallow capsules whole; use the provided dosing device for the liquid solution.
storage_instructions: Capsules: room temperature. Oral solution: refrigerate.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain
New confusion, dizziness, or difficulty walking (nervous system effects)
Signs of low blood counts
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels significantly.
Report all new medications to oncology team due to CYP3A4-mediated interactions.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact oncology team promptly for signs of liver injury or new neurological symptoms.
Do not adjust dose without guidance.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests.
Report new dizziness, confusion, or gait changes promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: An oral capsule vaccine series that helps protect travelers against typhoid fever.
typical_dosage: One capsule taken every other day for a total of 4 doses, completed at least 1 week before potential exposure/travel.
typical_duration: Full 4-dose series; a booster is recommended every 5 years with continued/repeated exposure.
directions_for_use: Take each capsule about 1 hour before a meal with a cool or lukewarm drink.
Swallow capsules whole - do not chew.
Keep capsules refrigerated until taken; complete all 4 doses on schedule.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze.
contraindications: Concurrent antibiotic use (can inactivate the vaccine)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
High fever
Severe abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid taking antibiotics during the vaccine series, as they can kill the live vaccine strain and reduce effectiveness.
Avoid antimalarial medications (e.g., mefloquine) at the same time when possible - space doses as directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for severe allergic reaction or high fever.
Contact your travel clinic if a dose is missed or an antibiotic is needed during the series.
self_monitoring: Track that all 4 doses are taken on the every-other-day schedule.
Confirm completion at least 1 week before travel.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered and continue the every-other-day schedule; contact your travel clinic/pharmacy if this affects completing the series before travel.

description: Used as first-line treatment for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with specific EGFR gene mutations.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly 45 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening shortness of breath or cough (possible lung inflammation) - seek care promptly
Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe diarrhea or skin reactions
Signs of corneal/eye problems
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole - they reduce absorption and effectiveness; if acid reducers are needed, discuss timing/alternatives (like antacids taken several hours apart) with your oncology team.
Avoid St. John's Wort - may reduce effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for new breathing problems, signs of liver injury, or severe skin reactions.
Report diarrhea that does not improve with recommended management.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests.
Monitor skin, nails, and for respiratory symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: Used to treat myelofibrosis in adults with severely low platelet counts (thrombocytopenia).
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist/hematologist; commonly taken twice daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at consistent times, with or without food.
Swallow capsules whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/urine, severe headache
Signs of infection: fever, chills
Irregular heartbeat, fainting (QT prolongation)
Signs of blood clots
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid other QT-prolonging medications.
Increased bleeding risk if combined with NSAIDs, aspirin, or anticoagulants - report all medications to your care team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for unusual bleeding, signs of infection, or irregular heartbeat.
Report new bruising or bleeding promptly.
self_monitoring: Frequent complete blood counts, especially platelets.
Periodic ECG monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: Used to treat certain grade 2 gliomas (brain tumors) with an IDH1 or IDH2 mutation following surgery.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically taken once daily on an empty stomach.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal) at the same time each day.
Avoid grapefruit products.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain - seek care promptly
New seizures or worsening neurological symptoms
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels significantly.
Report all new medications to oncology team due to CYP3A4-mediated interactions.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact oncology team promptly for signs of liver injury or new neurological symptoms.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests.
Periodic brain imaging as scheduled by oncology team.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time on an empty stomach - do not double up.

description: Used to treat chronic hepatitis C virus infection, particularly in patients who have failed prior direct-acting antiviral treatment.
typical_dosage: 1 tablet by mouth once daily with food, for a course set by your specialist (commonly 12 weeks).
typical_duration: A defined treatment course, typically 12 weeks, as prescribed.
directions_for_use: Take with food at the same time each day.
Complete the full course even if feeling well.
Get tested for hepatitis B before starting - reactivation risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original container.
contraindications: Concurrent use with rifampin or certain other strong P-gp/CYP inducers (reduces effectiveness)
Known hepatitis B co-infection without appropriate monitoring
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of hepatitis B reactivation or liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Slow heart rate if combined with amiodarone (not typically co-prescribed)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid St. John's Wort - significantly reduces drug levels/effectiveness.
Can increase levels of statins (e.g., simvastatin) - increased muscle toxicity risk; dose adjustment or statin switch may be needed.
Acid-reducing medications (like omeprazole) may reduce absorption - timing/spacing may be required per specialist guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for signs of liver problems.
Do not stop treatment early without guidance.
self_monitoring: Liver function tests and hepatitis C viral load monitoring during and after treatment.
Hepatitis B monitoring if co-infected.
missed_dose_instructions: If within 18 hours of the scheduled time, take the missed dose with food; if more than 18 hours have passed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time - do not double up.

description: An oral capsule therapy used after antibiotic treatment to help prevent recurrence of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) infection by restoring healthy gut bacteria.
typical_dosage: 4 capsules by mouth once daily for 3 consecutive days, started 2-4 days after completing antibiotic treatment for C. diff.
typical_duration: A single 3-day course.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach when possible, as directed.
Swallow capsules whole with water - do not crush or open.
Start within the specific window after finishing antibiotics as directed by prescriber.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze.
contraindications: Severe food allergies to ingredients in the product
Severely immunocompromised state without specialist guidance
Active severe inflammatory bowel disease flare
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, severe abdominal pain
Severe or worsening diarrhea
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid taking antibiotics during the treatment course, as they can reduce effectiveness.
Do not take other antidiarrheal products at the same time without checking with prescriber, as they may affect how the product works.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for fever, severe abdominal pain, or signs of allergic reaction.
Report if diarrhea recurs after treatment.
self_monitoring: Watch for recurrence of C. diff symptoms (watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping) after treatment.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber if a dose within the 3-day course is missed, since this is a short defined course - do not simply extend or double doses on your own.

description: Used to treat schizophrenia, bipolar disorder (manic, mixed, and depressive episodes), and as an add-on treatment for major depressive disorder.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically started at a low dose once daily and titrated based on response.
typical_duration: Long-term, with periodic reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Effects on mood/psychosis may take several weeks to become fully apparent - continue as directed even if improvement is gradual.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fever, muscle rigidity, confusion, irregular heartbeat (neuroleptic malignant syndrome) - emergency
Uncontrollable muscle movements (tardive dyskinesia)
Signs of high blood sugar
Suicidal thoughts, especially in young adults
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine and other sedating OTC sleep aids.
Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels.
CYP3A4 inhibitors like fluconazole can increase drug levels - dose adjustment may be needed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
Report any new abnormal movements or suicidal thoughts to prescriber promptly.
self_monitoring: Monitor for abnormal movements periodically.
Blood glucose and weight checks.
Monitor mood and report suicidal thoughts.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat the cardiomyopathy of transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), a condition in which an abnormal protein builds up in the heart.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your cardiologist; typically taken once daily. Vyndamax and Vyndaqel are different formulations/strengths of the same active drug and are not interchangeable milligram-for-milligram - use only the specific product and strength prescribed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow capsules/tablets whole - do not break, crush, or dissolve.
Do not switch between Vyndamax and Vyndaqel without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of worsening heart failure: increasing swelling, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain - report to cardiologist
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; tafamidis can affect certain lab test-based drug transport interactions - inform your care team of all medications, including OTC products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact cardiologist for worsening heart failure symptoms.
Report severe or persistent diarrhea.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled cardiology follow-up visits, including heart function assessments.
Track weight and swelling at home if instructed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Eye drop used once daily to lower elevated eye pressure in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
typical_dosage: 1 drop in affected eye(s) once daily in the evening.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Instill 1 drop in affected eye(s) each evening.
Wait at least 5 minutes before using other eye drops.
Remove contact lenses before use; wait 15 minutes before reinserting.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate unopened bottles; once opened, store at room temperature and discard after 8 weeks.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain or vision changes
Signs of eye infection
common_side_effects: Gradual darkening of iris color and eyelash growth
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; avoid using other eye drops within 5 minutes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for persistent eye redness/irritation or vision changes.
self_monitoring: Periodic eye pressure checks with eye care provider.
Note any progressive change in eye/eyelash color.
missed_dose_instructions: Use as soon as remembered that day; if near the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat certain tumors (including renal cell carcinoma) associated with von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease, and advanced renal cell carcinoma after other treatments.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically taken once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe anemia: unusual fatigue, pale skin, shortness of breath
Signs of low oxygen: shortness of breath, bluish lips/fingertips
Signs of allergic reaction with infusion-related symptoms if co-treated with other agents
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid strong CYP2C19 inhibitors/inducers and combined hormonal contraceptives may be less effective - use non-hormonal backup contraception.
Report all new medications to your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for signs of severe anemia or low oxygen levels.
Contact oncology team for any new or worsening symptoms.
self_monitoring: Regular hemoglobin/blood count checks.
Oxygen saturation monitoring if directed.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: A self-injectable biologic used with other therapies to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), helping to improve exercise capacity and reduce disease progression.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your pulmonary hypertension specialist; typically given once every 3 weeks.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by specialist.
directions_for_use: Injection is prepared and given by or under supervision of a healthcare provider, or self-administered after training.
Rotate injection sites.
Keep all scheduled lab monitoring appointments (blood counts required before each dose).
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; protect from light; do not freeze.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of bleeding: unusual bruising, nosebleeds, blood in stool
Signs of high red blood cell count: severe headache, dizziness, flushing
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Increased bleeding risk when combined with aspirin, NSAIDs, warfarin, apixaban, or clopidogrel - discuss any bleeding-risk medications with your specialist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for unusual bleeding or symptoms of high red blood cell count.
Report any new bruising or nosebleeds to your care team.
self_monitoring: Blood counts (hemoglobin/hematocrit and platelets) checked before each dose.
Track any signs of bleeding.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your specialist's office to reschedule if a dose is missed or delayed - do not double up or self-adjust timing.

description: Used to treat non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with ALK or ROS1 gene rearrangements, and certain other ALK-positive cancers.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly taken twice daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at consistent times about 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Swallow capsules whole.
Avoid grapefruit products.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening shortness of breath or cough (possible lung inflammation) - seek care promptly
Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Irregular heartbeat, fainting (QT prolongation)
Vision changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels significantly.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, clarithromycin) can increase drug levels - report all new medications to oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for new breathing problems, irregular heartbeat, or signs of liver injury.
Report vision changes to your oncology team.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests and ECGs.
Periodic eye exams for vision changes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than 6 hours, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: Used as add-on treatment for focal (partial-onset) seizures in adults.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your neurologist; started at a low dose and slowly titrated upward over several weeks to reduce serious rash risk.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Follow the slow titration schedule exactly - do not increase dose faster than directed.
Do not stop abruptly - taper as directed to avoid seizure worsening.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a serious skin reaction: rash, blistering, peeling skin, fever, swollen lymph nodes (DRESS syndrome) - seek care immediately
Suicidal thoughts or behavior
Irregular heartbeat (QT shortening)
Extreme drowsiness or difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, and other CNS depressants.
May reduce effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives - use backup contraception.
Can affect levels of other seizure medications - report all medications to prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of a serious skin reaction or severe drowsiness.
Report suicidal thoughts immediately.
self_monitoring: Watch closely for rash during the titration period and report any rash immediately.
Monitor mood/behavior changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Eye drop used to treat Demodex blepharitis, an inflammation of the eyelids caused by Demodex mites.
typical_dosage: 1 drop in each eye twice daily for 6 weeks.
typical_duration: A defined 6-week course, as directed by eye care provider.
directions_for_use: Instill 1 drop in each eye, morning and evening, 6-8 hours apart.
Remove contact lenses before use; wait 30 minutes before reinserting.
Wait at least 5 minutes before using other eye drops.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe eye pain or vision changes
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for severe eye pain, vision changes, or lack of improvement after the 6-week course.
self_monitoring: Track symptom improvement (eyelid redness, crusting) over the 6-week course.
Follow-up eye exam as scheduled.
missed_dose_instructions: Use as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the twice-daily schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ulcerative colitis, and polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis by reducing immune-driven inflammation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist; immediate-release is typically taken twice daily, extended-release once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at consistent times each day, with or without food.
Swallow extended-release tablets whole - do not split, crush, or chew.
Do not switch between immediate-release and extended-release without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection: fever, chills, cough, wound that won't heal - seek care promptly
Signs of blood clots: leg swelling/pain, sudden shortness of breath, chest pain - seek emergency care
Signs of heart attack or stroke
Signs of a tear in the stomach or intestines: severe abdominal pain, fever
Unusual bruising/bleeding, signs of low blood counts
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other immunosuppressants (e.g., long-term prednisone) without close monitoring - increased infection risk.
Avoid live vaccines while on therapy.
Strong CYP3A4/2C19 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole) can increase drug levels - dose adjustment may be needed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, heart attack, or stroke.
Contact prescriber promptly for signs of infection or severe abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Regular labs: complete blood count, liver enzymes, cholesterol.
Watch for early signs of infection.
Report any new lumps or skin changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used in combination with somatostatin analog therapy to reduce severe diarrhea caused by carcinoid syndrome.
typical_dosage: 250 mg by mouth three times daily with food, or as adjusted by prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy alongside somatostatin analog treatment.
directions_for_use: Take with food.
Continue somatostatin analog therapy as co-prescribed unless directed otherwise.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Severe constipation or bowel obstruction risk (use caution)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe constipation or abdominal pain
Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Signs of depression or mood changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Use caution combining with other constipating medications (e.g., loperamide) - monitor bowel function.
Report all new medications to your oncology/GI team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for severe constipation, abdominal pain, or signs of liver injury.
Report mood changes.
self_monitoring: Track bowel movement frequency to gauge symptom control.
Periodic liver function tests.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food; if close to the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Combination extended-release tablet used with diet and exercise to improve blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your prescriber; typically once daily with the evening meal.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, split, or chew.
Take with food to reduce GI upset.
Stay well hydrated; stop before procedures requiring contrast dye or surgery as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of ketoacidosis: nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, unusual fatigue, rapid breathing (can occur even with normal blood sugar) - seek emergency care
Signs of urinary tract or genital infection
Signs of dehydration/low blood pressure
Signs of lactic acidosis: muscle pain, trouble breathing, unusual tiredness
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid excess alcohol - increases risk of lactic acidosis and low blood sugar.
NSAIDs may affect kidney function and increase metformin accumulation risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop and seek care for signs of ketoacidosis or lactic acidosis.
Contact prescriber for recurrent genital/urinary infections.
self_monitoring: Regular blood glucose monitoring.
Periodic kidney function and vitamin B12 levels.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: A single-dose oral antiviral used to treat influenza (flu) in patients who have had symptoms for no more than 48 hours, and to prevent flu after known exposure.
typical_dosage: A single oral dose based on body weight, taken as soon as possible after flu symptoms begin (within 48 hours).
typical_duration: Single dose treatment (or single dose for post-exposure prevention).
directions_for_use: Take as a single dose as soon as possible after diagnosis.
Do not take with dairy products, calcium-fortified beverages, or antacids/supplements containing calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, aluminum, or selenium - these reduce absorption.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Unusual behavior or confusion (rare neuropsychiatric events reported with flu itself and antivirals, especially in children/adolescents)
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not take with dairy, calcium-fortified juices, or antacids/mineral supplements (calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc) - separate by several hours as these significantly reduce absorption and effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for signs of allergic reaction or unusual behavior changes.
Contact prescriber if flu symptoms worsen or do not improve.
self_monitoring: Monitor for symptom improvement over the following days.
Watch for worsening breathing or high fever that doesn't improve.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a one-time single dose; if it was not taken as directed, contact your prescriber for guidance rather than taking it late without checking.

description: A self-injectable or in-office biologic used to treat moderate-to-severe allergic asthma, chronic idiopathic urticaria (hives), chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, and IgE-mediated food allergy.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your allergist/specialist based on body weight and IgE level; typically given every 2-4 weeks.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy, reassessed periodically for response.
directions_for_use: If self-injecting, rotate injection sites (thigh or abdomen, avoiding a 2-inch area around the navel).
First doses are often given in a healthcare setting to monitor for allergic reaction.
Do not stop other asthma/allergy medications abruptly without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze; protect from light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of anaphylaxis: hives, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing, dizziness - can occur even after previous doses without reaction; seek emergency care immediately and carry emergency epinephrine if prescribed
Signs of heart or blood vessel problems (chest pain, unusual bruising) - rare
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; continue prescribed asthma/allergy medications as directed unless told to reduce them.
action_if_adverse_effects: Use emergency epinephrine and seek emergency care immediately for signs of anaphylaxis.
Report any delayed allergic-type reactions to prescriber.
self_monitoring: Remain in the office for observation after injections as directed, especially for the first several doses.
Track asthma/hive symptom control.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your prescriber's office to reschedule a missed dose - do not double up or significantly delay without guidance, as this can affect the dosing interval.

description: Used to increase circulating white blood cells (neutrophils and lymphocytes) in patients with WHIM syndrome, a rare primary immunodeficiency.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your specialist based on body weight; typically taken once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food, as directed.
Report any new infections promptly, as this medication modifies immune cell counts.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers without dose adjustment
Certain heart rhythm conditions (QT prolongation risk) - caution advised
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Irregular heartbeat, fainting, dizziness (QT prolongation) - seek care
Signs of infection despite treatment
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for irregular heartbeat or fainting.
Report any signs of infection to your specialist promptly.
self_monitoring: Regular blood counts to monitor white blood cell response.
Periodic ECG monitoring if at cardiac risk.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a FLT3 gene mutation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically taken once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Requires baseline and periodic ECG monitoring due to QT-prolongation risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of differentiation syndrome: fever, difficulty breathing, rapid weight gain, swelling - seek emergency care
Irregular heartbeat, fainting (QT prolongation)
New muscle weakness or nerve symptoms (posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome - headache, seizure, vision changes, confusion)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid other QT-prolonging medications.
Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels significantly.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors like fluconazole can increase drug levels - report all new medications to oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of differentiation syndrome or irregular heartbeat.
Report new neurological symptoms immediately.
self_monitoring: Regular ECGs and liver function tests.
Frequent complete blood counts.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: Used in combination with other therapies to treat relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically taken once or twice weekly on specific days.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, per oncology protocol.
directions_for_use: Take on the specific days of the week directed by your oncologist - not a daily medication.
Take with food to reduce nausea.
Anti-nausea medication is often prescribed preventively - take as directed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe nausea/vomiting or dehydration
Confusion or dizziness (can affect ability to drive)
Signs of infection or low blood counts
Significant unintentional weight loss
otc_and_other_interactions: Use caution combining with other sedating medications (e.g., diphenhydramine, alprazolam) - additive dizziness/confusion risk.
Stay well hydrated; report all new medications to your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact oncology team promptly for severe nausea, confusion, or signs of infection.
Use anti-nausea medication as prescribed at the first sign of nausea.
self_monitoring: Frequent complete blood counts.
Track weight and appetite.
Monitor for dizziness/confusion, especially with activities like driving.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your oncology team for guidance if a scheduled dose is missed, since this medication is taken on specific days rather than daily - do not double up.

description: A once-weekly transdermal patch used to prevent pregnancy by releasing estrogen and progestin through the skin.
typical_dosage: Apply 1 new patch once weekly for 3 weeks, followed by 1 patch-free week, then repeat the cycle.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as long as contraception is desired.
directions_for_use: Apply to clean, dry skin of the buttock, abdomen, upper outer arm, or upper torso (not breasts); rotate sites.
Change the patch on the same day each week.
Use backup contraception for the first 7 days when starting.
Do not use lotion/oils near the application site, which may affect adhesion.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original pouch until use.
contraindications: History of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Leg pain/swelling or sudden shortness of breath (blood clot)
Chest pain, sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness on one side
Severe abdominal pain, jaundice
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce contraceptive effectiveness - use backup contraception.
Certain antibiotics/antifungals may reduce effectiveness; discuss with pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, stroke, or heart attack.
Contact prescriber for severe abdominal pain, jaundice, or if the patch repeatedly falls off.
self_monitoring: Check that the patch stays adhered; replace promptly if it falls off per instructions.
Track weekly patch-change schedule.
Report new severe headaches or leg swelling.
missed_dose_instructions: If a patch change is missed or a patch falls off for less than 24 hours, reapply/replace it and continue the normal schedule; if off for more than 24 hours or the timing is unclear, apply a new patch, start a new 4-week cycle, and use backup contraception for 7 days.

description: Vaccine required or recommended for travel to certain countries with risk of yellow fever transmission; may be required for entry documentation (International Certificate of Vaccination).
dosage_forms: Injectable suspension (administered only at authorized yellow fever vaccination centers)
typical_dosage: A single 0.5 mL subcutaneous injection, given at least 10 days before travel.
typical_duration: Single dose; considered to provide long-lasting protection for most travelers.
directions_for_use: Must be administered at a certified yellow fever vaccination center.
Obtain the International Certificate of Vaccination documentation as needed for travel.
storage_instructions: Frozen storage handled by the administering travel clinic/pharmacy.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
High fever
Signs of severe neurological or organ-related reaction (rare but serious) - severe headache, confusion, muscle weakness
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen may be used for injection-site discomfort or fever as directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction or neurological symptoms.
Contact provider for high or persistent fever.
self_monitoring: Wait for observation as directed after injection.
Keep the International Certificate of Vaccination for travel documentation.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a single-dose vaccine; contact your travel clinic if timing before travel is a concern.

description: Used for short-term treatment of insomnia, specifically to help with falling asleep.
typical_dosage: 5-10 mg by mouth immediately before bedtime, only when able to get a full night's sleep (at least 4 hours).
typical_duration: Short-term use, generally 1-2 weeks; longer use should be reassessed by prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take immediately before bedtime, not with or right after a high-fat meal (delays onset).
Only take if able to stay in bed for at least 4 hours.
Do not take with alcohol.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sleep-related activities with no memory of the event (sleep-walking, sleep-driving, sleep-eating) - stop and contact prescriber
Signs of severe allergic reaction: facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing
Severe drowsiness, confusion, or difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, and other CNS depressants - avoid combining.
Use caution with other sedatives like alprazolam - increased risk of excessive sedation/respiratory depression.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact prescriber for sleepwalking/complex sleep behaviors.
Seek emergency care for severe allergic reaction or breathing difficulty.
self_monitoring: Track sleep quality and daytime drowsiness.
Reassess need for continued use with prescriber after short-term course.
missed_dose_instructions: Only take when going to bed and able to get a full night's sleep; if not taken at bedtime, skip the dose - do not take later in the night or double up.

description: A self-injectable biologic used to reduce the risk of infection by boosting white blood cell (neutrophil) production, commonly after chemotherapy or bone marrow transplant, or in chronic neutropenia.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncology/hematology team; often given once daily for a defined number of days per cycle, based on blood counts.
typical_duration: Course length varies by indication and cycle; often several days per chemotherapy cycle or ongoing for chronic neutropenia.
directions_for_use: Let the syringe warm to room temperature before injecting.
Rotate injection sites (abdomen, thigh, upper arm).
Do not shake the syringe.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate; do not freeze; protect from light; may sit at room temperature for a limited time before use per product instructions.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to filgrastim or E. coli-derived proteins
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Sudden severe pain in the upper left abdomen or shoulder tip (possible spleen enlargement/rupture) - seek emergency care
Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing (possible lung inflammation) - seek emergency care
Signs of severe allergic reaction
Signs of sickle cell crisis in patients with sickle cell disease
otc_and_other_interactions: Acetaminophen or NSAIDs may be used for bone pain as directed, though NSAIDs may need to be used cautiously during chemotherapy - confirm with oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for severe abdominal/shoulder pain or trouble breathing.
Contact care team for bone pain not controlled by recommended OTC relief.
self_monitoring: Regular complete blood counts as scheduled by the care team.
Watch for fever, which should still be reported urgently.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact your care team promptly if a scheduled dose is missed, as this medication is often given on a specific cycle-based schedule.

description: Used as maintenance therapy after chemotherapy response, or for treatment of certain recurrent ovarian, fallopian tube, or peritoneal cancers.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist based on body weight and platelet count; typically taken once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Taking at bedtime may help reduce nausea.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high blood pressure: severe headache, vision changes
Signs of low blood counts: unusual bleeding/bruising, fever, severe fatigue
Signs of a new blood cancer (rare): unusual bruising, prolonged fatigue - report promptly
Signs of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome: severe headache, seizures, vision loss, confusion
otc_and_other_interactions: Monitor blood pressure if using decongestants like pseudoephedrine, which can raise blood pressure further.
Report all new medications to your oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for severe headache with vision changes or signs of low blood counts.
Contact oncology team for uncontrolled nausea or new bruising/bleeding.
self_monitoring: Regular complete blood counts, especially platelets.
Regular blood pressure checks.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: Used to treat melanoma and certain other cancers with a BRAF V600 gene mutation.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly taken twice daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at consistent times about 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Use sun protection (SPF 30+, protective clothing) - significant photosensitivity risk.
Swallow tablets whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New skin lesions or growths (risk of new skin cancers) - have skin checked regularly
Irregular heartbeat, fainting (QT prolongation)
Signs of severe skin reaction: rash, blistering, peeling
Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
Severe sunburn-like reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Use sunscreen and avoid excess sun exposure - significant photosensitivity.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications.
Report all new medications due to CYP-mediated interactions.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for new skin growths, irregular heartbeat, or severe skin reactions.
Report severe sunburn-like reactions.
self_monitoring: Regular skin exams by dermatology (during and for months after treatment).
Periodic ECGs and liver function tests.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed by more than 4 hours, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: An antiretroviral used as part of combination therapy to treat HIV infection, and to help prevent mother-to-child transmission during pregnancy/delivery.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your HIV specialist; typically taken multiple times daily as part of a combination regimen.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as part of HIV treatment (or a defined short course for perinatal prevention).
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed, at evenly spaced intervals.
Take every dose of every HIV medication as prescribed - missed doses can lead to drug resistance.
Do not stop or change without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature away from moisture.
contraindications: Severe neutropenia or anemia at baseline (caution/dose adjustment)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood counts: unusual fatigue, pale skin, easy bruising, fever - seek care promptly
Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, severe fatigue, nausea
Signs of muscle weakness/myopathy with long-term use
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with other bone-marrow-suppressing drugs (e.g., valganciclovir) without close monitoring - additive risk of low blood counts.
NSAIDs and acetaminophen at high doses may increase toxicity risk; use per prescriber guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for signs of low blood counts or lactic acidosis.
Keep all scheduled lab appointments.
self_monitoring: Frequent complete blood counts, especially early in treatment.
Regular HIV viral load and CD4 count monitoring.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if close to the next dose, take the missed dose anyway and continue the regular schedule - do not skip HIV medication doses without discussing with your prescriber, as missed doses risk resistance.

description: Eye gel used to treat herpes simplex viral infections of the eye (acute herpetic keratitis).
typical_dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye 5 times daily until the corneal ulcer heals, then 3 times daily for 7 days.
typical_duration: Course guided by healing of the eye surface, typically several weeks, as directed by eye care provider.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Instill 1 drop into the affected eye as directed; avoid touching the tip to the eye.
Vision may be temporarily blurred after application - wait before driving.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening eye pain, redness, or vision changes
Signs of allergic reaction: eyelid swelling, severe irritation
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber if the eye is not improving or worsens.
Seek care for severe pain or vision loss.
self_monitoring: Follow-up eye exams as scheduled to confirm healing.
missed_dose_instructions: Use as soon as remembered; resume the regular dosing interval. Do not double up.

description: Used to treat cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) that persists, has progressed, or recurred during or after other treatments.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically 400 mg by mouth once daily with food.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take with food at the same time each day.
Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush.
Stay well hydrated - at least 2 liters of fluid daily unless fluid-restricted.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clots: leg swelling/pain, sudden shortness of breath, chest pain - seek emergency care
Signs of severe dehydration or high blood sugar
Signs of low blood counts: fever, unusual bleeding/bruising
Irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: May potentiate the effect of warfarin - increased INR/bleeding risk reported; monitor INR closely if combined.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot or irregular heartbeat.
Contact oncology team for dehydration, high blood sugar symptoms, or unusual bleeding.
self_monitoring: Regular blood counts, blood sugar, and electrolyte checks.
INR monitoring if also taking warfarin.
Track fluid intake.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: A topical cream/foam used to treat plaque psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis, or atopic dermatitis, depending on the specific product; distinct from oral roflumilast used for COPD.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to affected skin areas once daily.
typical_duration: Ongoing as directed; reassess with prescriber if no improvement after several weeks.
directions_for_use: Apply a thin layer to affected areas once daily; wash hands after application unless hands are being treated.
Avoid application to the eyes, mouth, and vagina.
Can be used on sensitive areas like the face and skin folds as directed by prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Mood changes (rare, mainly reported with oral form but caution advised)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected; avoid applying other topical products to the same area at the same time without spacing.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for signs of allergic reaction or if the skin condition worsens.
Report new mood changes.
self_monitoring: Track skin symptom improvement over several weeks.
Report lack of improvement to prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered that day; if it is almost time for the next application, skip the missed dose. Do not apply extra to make up.

description: Used to treat seizures associated with CDKL5 deficiency disorder in patients 2 years of age and older.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your neurologist based on body weight; typically given three times daily with food.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Shake the oral suspension well before each use and use the provided dosing device.
Take with food.
Do not stop abruptly - taper as directed to avoid seizure worsening.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking
Suicidal thoughts or behavior
Signs of severe allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, and other CNS depressants.
Report all medications to prescriber given complexity of seizure management.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for extreme sedation or difficulty waking.
Report mood changes or suicidal thoughts immediately.
self_monitoring: Track seizure frequency for treatment response.
Monitor alertness/sedation level, especially after dose changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume schedule. Do not double up. Missing doses can increase seizure risk - contact prescriber if doses are frequently missed.

description: A short 14-day oral course used to treat postpartum depression in adults.
typical_dosage: 50 mg by mouth once daily in the evening with a fat-containing meal, for 14 days, as directed by prescriber.
typical_duration: A defined 14-day course.
directions_for_use: Take in the evening with a fat-containing meal, at the same time each day.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery for at least 12 hours after each dose due to drowsiness/impaired alertness.
Use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Suicidal thoughts or worsening depression - seek care immediately
Extreme sedation, confusion, or difficulty staying awake
Signs of severe allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Additive sedation with diphenhydramine, alcohol, and other CNS depressants - avoid combining, especially given driving restriction.
Use caution with other sedatives like alprazolam - increased sedation risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for worsening depression or suicidal thoughts.
Do not drive or perform activities requiring alertness for at least 12 hours after each dose.
self_monitoring: Track mood symptoms daily during the 14-day course.
Have a support person aware of the treatment course given sedation risk.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it the next evening with food at the regular time - do not double up or extend the course beyond 14 days without prescriber guidance.

description: Used in combination with other therapies to treat certain types of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), follicular lymphoma, and small lymphocytic lymphoma.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; commonly taken twice daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated, with close monitoring for serious toxicities.
directions_for_use: Take at consistent times about 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Report diarrhea, cough, or shortness of breath promptly.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain - seek care promptly
Severe diarrhea/colitis: severe abdominal pain, blood in stool
New or worsening cough, shortness of breath (possible lung inflammation/infection, including serious opportunistic infections)
Signs of a tear in the intestine: severe abdominal pain, fever
Signs of severe skin reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels significantly.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor - can markedly increase levels of statins (e.g., simvastatin) and other CYP3A4-metabolized drugs, increasing toxicity risk; report all medications to oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for signs of liver injury, severe diarrhea, or breathing problems.
Report fever immediately due to infection risk.
self_monitoring: Frequent liver function tests, especially early in treatment.
Regular monitoring for infection symptoms and blood counts.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at its regular scheduled time - do not double up.

description: Used to treat non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with an ALK gene rearrangement.
typical_dosage: Individualized, set by your oncologist; typically taken once daily.
typical_duration: Continued as long as beneficial and tolerated.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day; take with food per current product labeling to reduce GI side effects (confirm formulation-specific food instructions with your pharmacist).
Swallow capsules/tablets whole.
Avoid grapefruit products.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain
New or worsening shortness of breath or cough (possible lung inflammation)
Irregular heartbeat, fainting (QT prolongation)
Signs of high blood sugar
Severe diarrhea, nausea, or vomiting
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit products and St. John's Wort - alter drug levels significantly.
Avoid other QT-prolonging medications.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, clarithromycin) can increase drug levels - report all new medications to oncology team.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for signs of liver injury, breathing problems, or irregular heartbeat.
Report persistent GI symptoms to your oncology team.
self_monitoring: Regular liver function tests, ECGs, and blood glucose monitoring.
Track GI symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, and it is more than 12 hours until the next dose, take it as soon as remembered; otherwise skip it and take the next dose at its regular time - do not double up. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take an extra dose.

description: An immunosuppressant taken by mouth to prevent organ transplant rejection, and sometimes used for severe autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis or psoriasis.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized based on body weight, blood drug levels, and the specific transplant/condition, and is set and adjusted by the transplant or specialist team - never change the dose or brand without their guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term, often lifelong for transplant recipients.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times every day, consistently either with or without food.
Do not switch between brands/formulations (e.g., Sandimmune vs. Neoral/Gengraf) without your transplant team's approval - they are not interchangeable dose-for-dose.
Mix oral solution with room-temperature orange or apple juice and drink immediately if using the liquid form; avoid grapefruit juice.
storage_instructions: Store capsules at room temperature; refrigerate oral solution if directed and use within the labeled time after opening.
contraindications: Uncontrolled high blood pressure (for some uses)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection (fever, chills, sore throat) - immunosuppression increases infection risk
Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling, unusual fatigue
Significant increase in blood pressure
Signs of a new or worsening skin lesion (increased skin cancer risk with long-term use)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit juice - significantly raises cyclosporine levels and toxicity risk.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can increase kidney toxicity risk when combined.
St. John's Wort significantly reduces cyclosporine levels and can cause transplant rejection - avoid entirely.
Many antibiotics/antifungals raise cyclosporine levels - always tell your pharmacist before starting any new medication, including OTC products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact your transplant team promptly for signs of infection, kidney problems, or significant blood pressure changes.
Do not stop this medication without guidance - stopping can cause organ rejection.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled blood level (trough), kidney function, and blood pressure monitoring appointments.
Check blood pressure at home if recommended.
Watch for and report signs of infection promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if it is close to the next dose, contact your transplant team for guidance rather than guessing, since missed doses can risk organ rejection.

description: A potent, long-acting steroid used to reduce inflammation and swelling in a wide range of conditions, and sometimes to prevent chemotherapy-related nausea.
typical_dosage: Highly variable depending on the condition being treated (often 0.5-9 mg/day), and may be tapered - follow the specific prescribed schedule exactly.
typical_duration: Often a short course; longer courses require a slow taper under medical guidance.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Take in the morning when possible to mimic the body's natural cortisol rhythm.
Follow the exact taper schedule provided - do not stop abruptly after prolonged use.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of adrenal insufficiency if stopped abruptly after prolonged use: severe fatigue, low blood pressure, nausea
High blood sugar symptoms (increased thirst/urination)
Signs of infection (steroids can mask fever)
Severe mood changes or stomach pain/black stools
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen, aspirin) increase risk of stomach ulcers/GI bleeding when combined.
Can raise blood sugar - monitor closely if also taking diabetes medications.
Can increase warfarin's effect - monitor INR.
action_if_adverse_effects: Never stop abruptly after a course longer than about 2-3 weeks - follow the taper exactly.
Seek care for severe mood changes, high blood sugar symptoms, or GI bleeding.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood sugar closely if diabetic.
Watch for mood changes, swelling, and signs of infection.
Follow the taper schedule precisely.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on a multi-dose schedule; follow your written taper instructions or call your pharmacist rather than doubling up.

description: A corticosteroid taken by mouth to replace a hormone the body isn't making enough of (adrenal insufficiency) or to reduce inflammation in various conditions.
typical_dosage: Individualized based on the condition being treated - replacement therapy for adrenal insufficiency uses a specific daily schedule set by an endocrinologist; anti-inflammatory dosing varies by condition.
typical_duration: Often lifelong for adrenal insufficiency; variable/short-term for anti-inflammatory use.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
For replacement therapy, take at the specific times of day prescribed to mimic natural cortisol rhythm.
Never stop or skip doses without medical guidance - can cause a life-threatening adrenal crisis.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of adrenal crisis if a dose is missed or during illness/stress: severe weakness, vomiting, low blood pressure, confusion - this is a medical emergency
High blood sugar symptoms
Signs of infection
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs increase risk of stomach irritation/GI bleeding when combined.
Can raise blood sugar - monitor closely if also taking diabetes medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: If you have adrenal insufficiency, you may need a higher "stress dose" during illness, injury, or surgery - discuss a sick-day plan with your endocrinologist in advance.
Seek emergency care for signs of adrenal crisis.
self_monitoring: Carry medical alert identification noting you take hydrocortisone for adrenal insufficiency, if applicable.
Monitor blood sugar closely if diabetic.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered. If you have adrenal insufficiency and miss a dose, contact your endocrinologist promptly, especially if you are ill - missed doses can be dangerous.

description: A beta blocker taken by mouth to lower blood pressure, prevent migraines, and reduce the risk of a repeat heart attack.
typical_dosage: 10-30 mg by mouth twice daily, individualized to the condition and response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at consistent times each day, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly - must be tapered by prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Severe bradycardia or heart block without a pacemaker
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Very slow heart rate, fainting, or severe dizziness
Difficulty breathing or wheezing
Signs of worsening heart failure
otc_and_other_interactions: Can mask symptoms of low blood sugar in patients on insulin/sulfonylureas.
NSAIDs may reduce blood-pressure-lowering effect.
Decongestants (pseudoephedrine) may raise blood pressure/heart rate.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for resting heart rate under 50 bpm, fainting, or worsening breathing.
Never stop abruptly.
self_monitoring: Check pulse/blood pressure at home if recommended.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose, then skip it. Do not double up.
